issue:420.body:
## Problem and user outcome

Researchers need to retrieve domain-specific scientific data through MCP and use it in traceable ScienceDiscovery workflows. Literature search alone does not satisfy this need: the objects are expression datasets, bioactivity measurements, variant assertions, and protein structures.

Provide supported, discoverable connections to **GEO, ChEMBL, ClinVar, RCSB PDB, and AlphaFold Protein Structure Database**, with reliable retrieval, explicit data boundaries, and provenance that survives downstream analysis.

## Context and existing implementation

Request inspired by this article: https://x.com/servasyy_ai/article/2112052770287284550
Related project documentation: https://aipoch.com/docs/guides/connectors/

Source inspection of ScienceDiscovery at baseline `0d31e155` found existing MCP implementations for GEO, ChEMBL, ClinVar, and PDB in `services/gateway/src/sciencediscovery_gateway/public_biomed_mcp.py`, plus manifests in `packages/mcp-sources/src/public-biomed.ts`. UniProt, Ensembl, and Reactome provide additional reusable patterns. No built-in AlphaFold DB adapter was found in that inspection.

This is a request to complete and validate domain database support, reusing existing adapters. It does not assume these databases are entirely unsupported. The baseline assessment was static inspection, not a live end-to-end availability test; recheck the target version before implementation.

## Requested scope

| Database | Required user-facing capabilities | Domain details to preserve |
| --- | --- | --- |
| GEO | Search studies, retrieve study/sample metadata, discover actual processed/supplementary files, and download selected analysis-ready data | GSE/GSM/GPL identifiers, organism, sample conditions, platform, and whether data are raw counts, normalized values, or other processed data |
| ChEMBL | Search molecules/targets, retrieve bioactivity measurements with useful filters, and perform similarity searches | Molecule/target/assay IDs, assay type, organism, relation, value, units, confidence, and source references |
| ClinVar | Search/lookup variants and retrieve individual clinical assertions | VCV/RCV/SCV identifiers where applicable, assembly, condition, review status, dates, and conflicting submissions |
| RCSB PDB | Search/lookup experimental structures and download supported structure files | PDB ID, experimental method, resolution where applicable, chains/entities, ligands, and source/version metadata |
| AlphaFold DB | Retrieve available predictions by protein accession and download model/confidence files when available | UniProt accession, model identifier/version, source URLs, and confidence information |

AlphaFold DB retrieval is separate from running AlphaFold prediction software. New prediction compute infrastructure is outside this request. PubMed and other literature databases are also outside this scope.

## Integration requirements

- Reuse the MCP client, connector selection, permission/audit, and artifact download mechanisms. Prefer official provider APIs behind MCP adapters; do not require providers to expose MCP themselves.
- Make supported sources and operations discoverable, with setup instructions and any credential requirements. Enable the source for the intended Session and support both Inspector validation and Agent use.
- Return structured domain data and standard evidence records with stable identifiers, source links, retrieval time, and provider version/release when available. Retain source caveats and attribution.
- A generic custom MCP connection currently preserves raw/structured content but produces empty standardized `records`; calling a tool successfully alone must not count as complete evidence integration.
- Transfer large datasets and structure files through governed artifact jobs, with source metadata and integrity checks. Keep file bytes out of model context and distinguish a proposed download from a completed, verified artifact.
- Handle pagination, provider rate limits, timeouts, invalid identifiers, missing records/files, and partial failures explicitly. Do not silently present a capped subset as the complete dataset.
- Document scientific limits: GEO standard matrix/SOFT candidate paths do not enumerate all supplementary files; not every expression matrix is suitable for count-based analysis; ClinVar submissions can conflict; experimental and predicted structures must remain distinguishable.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] On the target version, document the existing capability and remaining gap for each of the five databases.
- [ ] All five sources can be configured/enabled and successfully called from the intended Session; tool inputs and results are inspectable and audited.
- [ ] Each database has a representative live provider validation with recorded identifiers, commands/steps, expected results, and actual results. Record unavailable-provider cases as blocked rather than passed.
- [ ] GEO: discover actual files for a public study, retrieve relevant sample annotations, and download/verify a real selected matrix. Validate its data type and dimensions before downstream analysis; report when count-based analysis is inappropriate.
- [ ] ChEMBL: retrieve a target/molecule-linked activity set with explicit assay/measurement constraints, preserving units and relations, and verify pagination or clearly disclosed limits.
- [ ] ClinVar: retrieve assertions and preserve conflicting classifications/review status without reducing them to one unsupported consensus.
- [ ] PDB: retrieve an experimental structure, complete a verified CIF/PDB download, and demonstrate that a downstream analysis step can read the artifact and inspect its metadata.
- [ ] AlphaFold DB: retrieve a known available prediction by accession, verify a model download and available confidence metadata, and clearly identify it as predicted.
- [ ] Returned evidence and downloaded artifacts retain their source identifiers/URLs and retrieval metadata in subsequent analysis outputs.
- [ ] Automated tests cover domain result normalization and representative missing-record, malformed-input, rate-limit, and download-failure paths. Product-level validation covers connector selection, Inspector/Agent execution, and completed artifacts; mocked success alone is insufficient.
- [ ] User documentation describes supported operations, limitations, configuration, and reproducible examples for each source.

Implementation may be split into linked changes, but this feature remains open until the full five-database acceptance scope is verified.

## Child work item — PDB entity and chemical-component identity verification (migrated from #448)

The PDB connector must let researchers verify a structure’s protein target and ligand identity against a ChEMBL record without relying on structure titles or compound names. This is a bounded sub-item of the PDB acceptance scope above, not a separate database integration.

### Required MCP operations

- Expose discoverable polymer and nonpolymer entity identifiers from an entry lookup (or an equivalent bounded entry expansion).
- `pdb_get_polymer_entity(pdb_id, entity_id)`: entity description/type, organism, UniProt/reference mappings, label/auth chain identifiers, sequence/coverage and construct/mutation information where available.
- `pdb_get_nonpolymer_entity(pdb_id, entity_id)`: ligand/component identity, label/auth chain mappings and provider cross-references.
- `pdb_lookup_chemical_component(component_id)`: CCD name, formula/charge, InChI, complete InChIKey, available SMILES and mapped external identifiers with provenance. Extended CCD IDs such as five-character `A1CEA` are valid.

All results must provide structured domain fields and nonempty standardized evidence records with stable identifiers, canonical URLs, retrieval time, attribution and provider version/revision where available. Missing UniProt/InChIKey mappings must remain missing; do not replace them with name-based identity assertions. Preserve salt/parent relationships, stereochemistry-aware complete identifiers, covalent/modified-component qualifications, and label versus author chain IDs.

### Required validation cases

- Positive chain: through MCP, enumerate `9OS6` entities; verify polymer entity `1` maps to UniProt `P00533`, nonpolymer entity `2` maps to CCD `A1CEA`, and `A1CEA` has complete InChIKey `OMZCMEYTWSXEPZ-UHFFFAOYSA-N`, matching ChEMBL free Canertinib `CHEMBL31965`. Preserve the distinct dihydrochloride `CHEMBL545315` and its parent relation. Display protein label/auth chain `A/A` and ligand `B/A` without conflation.
- Negative chain: retrieve `5VCW` polymer entity `1` and show UniProt `Q99640`; it must not be reported as an EGFR complex merely because Pelitinib has EGFR activity elsewhere.
- Complete a selected mmCIF artifact download using the governed artifact path, verify its checksum, read the file downstream and retain the linked cross-database evidence in saved outputs.
- Complete an Agent journey using MCP metadata tools without direct HTTPS/web-fetch fallback; separately record Inspector, stub-model and real-model evidence.
- Cover extended CCD IDs; invalid/missing entities; missing protein/chemical mappings; timeout/rate-limit/partial failure feedback; and label/auth-chain distinctions.
- Add English and Chinese documentation with the positive and negative identity-matching examples and limits.

Official reference endpoints: `/rest/v1/core/polymer_entity/9OS6/1`, `/rest/v1/core/nonpolymer_entity/9OS6/2`, `/rest/v1/core/chemcomp/A1CEA`, and `/rest/v1/core/polymer_entity/5VCW/1` at `data.rcsb.org`.

issue:422.body:
## Problem
The `CodeCheck (GitCode)` check run on GitHub PRs only says "GitCode labelled the merge request `ci-failed`" and links to the GitCode MR. It doesn't name the failing rule or file. The GitCode MR page/API is not reachable for every contributor or reviewer (WAF/login). So authors end up writing "CodeCheck is ignored" (e.g. #421, also failing on #412 and #391), and reviewers can't tell whether a failure comes from the PR.

## Expected
When CodeCheck fails, the GitHub check-run output lists the failing checker/rule, file:line and message (or a stable public log link), so authors and reviewers can act without GitCode access.

## Verification cases
1. **Failure details mirrored**
   - Preconditions: a PR whose head introduces a known CodeCheck violation (e.g. a lint rule the GitCode pipeline enforces).
   - Steps: push; wait for the sync; open the `CodeCheck (GitCode)` check run on GitHub.
   - Expected / pass: `output.summary` or `output.text` names the rule, file:line and message; conclusion `failure`.
2. **Clean head**
   - Preconditions: a PR with no violations.
   - Steps: push; open the check run.
   - Expected / pass: conclusion `success`; no stale failure text from an earlier head.
3. **Infra failure isn't shown as a code failure (negative)**
   - Preconditions: the GitCode pipeline fails for an infra reason (timeout/sync error).
   - Steps: trigger; open the check run.
   - Expected / pass: output says it's an infra/sync failure, not a code violation, and links to a retry path.
4. **No secret leakage (security)**
   - Preconditions: a pipeline log that contains tokens/env.
   - Steps: mirror the failure details.
   - Expected / pass: mirrored text contains no tokens, cookies or internal URLs with credentials.

## Context
Refs #421, Refs #385. Seen at #421 head f494792 (GitCode MR !296) and #412 head 29e724a.

issue:436.body:
## 背景 / 输入

NatureBench 复现会话在 run 前已通过 API 将 `approvalMode` 设为 `always_allow`：

```http
PATCH /api/sessions/{sessionId}
{"approvalMode":"always_allow"}
```

随后 Agent 大量调用工具（读文件、装依赖、跑 python、写报告等）。日志：`jiuwenswarm.log`。

## 问题是什么

即便会话级 `always_allow`，运行中仍出现大量 **`allow_once` 且 `persisted=False`** 风格的授权记录（约百余次量级），审批噪声大、不粘滞。长复现任务的可观测性被权限流水淹没；也与用户对「Always allow = 本会话不再追问」的心智模型不符。

（权限文案/网络同意相关体验另见 #392、#393。）

## 我们怎么规避的

- 仍设 `always_allow`，减少 UI 卡死概率。
- 监控与成功判据改看 workspace 文件与 run 状态，不依赖权限流水是否「干净」。

## 期望应该是什么样

1. `always_allow` 应对该 session（或同 permission epoch）的同类工具调用真正粘滞，而不是每次 `allow_once` + `persisted=False`。
2. 日志/UI 在 always_allow 下折叠或汇总授权，避免百级噪音。
3. 文档写清：哪些动作仍会突破 always_allow（若有硬例外），并与设置文案一致。

## 相关

- #392 Permission card: "Allow same type" is unclear
- #393 Resume after a sandbox network block needs three consecutive approvals

issue:437.body:
## 背景 / 输入

NatureBench 论文复现任务包（设计上）**不含**论文 PDF/MD（reproduce vs discovery 防火墙）。ScienceDiscovery 会话里仅有：

- `NATUREBENCH_TASK_BRIEF.md` / `data_description.md` / `metadata.json`
- DOI：`10.1038/s43588-024-00689-2`
- 作者代码：`github.com/pachterlab/CGP_2023`

外部获取：Nature 付费墙；bioRxiv 遇 Cloudflare；PMC 预印本偶发可得。

## 问题是什么

「忠实复现论文方法」需要方法细节，但工作区默认**没有**可读全文。Agent 只能靠 brief + GitHub notebook/Monod API 拼方法，复现保真度与可审计性下降；与产品「读论文 → 做事」叙事有缝。

（上传 PDF 解析另见 #333。）

## 我们怎么规避的

- 写入 `REPRODUCE_INSTRUCTIONS.md`：DOI、bioRxiv、作者仓库、Monod `mminference`。
- 浅克隆 `CGP_2023` 进 workspace 作方法参考；用作者实现而非另起无关聚类。

## 期望应该是什么样

1. 复现类会话：支持一键「附着论文」（DOI → OA PDF / 用户上传），并进入 Paper reader 可检索上下文。
2. 若上游 benchmark 故意不带 PDF：产品应引导用户补论文，并在报告里强制记录「方法来源（PDF 页码 / 仓库 commit）」。
3. 对 paywall / bot 墙：明确失败态与人工粘贴摘要的入口，而不是静默只用 brief。

## 相关

- #333 [Bug]: PDF uploaded via Drop files is not parsed by Paper reader
- #98 artifact / provenance / CAS（含 papers）方向

issue:438.body:
## 背景 / 输入

在 ScienceDiscovery 沙箱 / science-env 中复现 meK-means（Monod `mminference`）：

- 环境：`/opt/science-env/bin/python`
- 依赖：`monod==0.2.9.0`、`loompy`、`anndata`、较新的 `numpy`（≥2）

Case：`s43588-024-00689-2`；驱动脚本 `run.py`。

## 问题是什么

Monod 0.2.9.0 与 **numpy 2** 组合需要额外 shim 才能跑通作者路径，例如：

- `np.meshgrid` 返回值按 list 使用的兼容
- float bounds / `gridsize=[1,1]` 等调用约定修补

否则 Agent 卡在依赖/兼容调试，而不是论文复现本身。预装科学栈「开箱可跑作者代码」的承诺打折。

## 我们怎么规避的

在会话内自建/修补 `mekmeans-cpu` 路径与 shim（详见会话 `REPRODUCTION_REPORT.md` §3），再跑真实 loom。

## 期望应该是什么样

1. science-env（或官方 skill）对常见复现栈给出**钉死且测过的** monod/numpy/loompy 组合，或提供已知 shim 文档。
2. Agent 首次导入失败时，表面友好的「已知兼容问题 + 推荐 pin」提示，而不是长 traceback 试错。
3. 可选：NatureBench / 论文复现模板预装最小可跑镜像，与 brief 中的计算提示对齐。

issue:439.body:
## 背景 / 输入

长 EM 任务 `mop_sc`（约 26.5 min）通过重定向写入 `logs/mop_sc.log`。进程全程 ~100% CPU，但日志在 gene select 附近长时间停在很小体积（约 623 B），直到进程退出才刷出大量内容。

## 问题是什么

Python/`print` **块缓冲**（非 TTY）导致：

- 用户与监控误判「卡住」
- Agent 更容易用墙钟定时器提前结束 turn（加剧孤儿作业问题）

## 我们怎么规避的

不以日志增长为唯一心跳；改看 `ps` CPU、RSS、以及最终 `predictions.npy` 是否落盘。事后用 `[TIMED]` 行核对 wall/cpu/RSS。

## 期望应该是什么样

1. 产品拉起的长时间命令默认 `python -u` / `PYTHONUNBUFFERED=1`，或对重定向日志做行缓冲。
2. Session/job UI 提供进程级心跳（CPU、RSS、最近输出时间），不单靠日志文件 mtime。
3. 文档提示 Agent：长任务应用 unbuffered 或显式 `flush`。

issue:455.body:
## 背景

Codex/Claude Specialist（Phase2/3）体验中，配置与运维仍偏「懂进程 env + 懂 API」：

- 设置页**没有** runtime/SDK 选择器；UI 保存不发 `runtime`（只能 API 带 `runtime` 创建）。
- `SCIENCE_AGENT_CODEX_BASE_URL` **只能**写进 API 进程环境，改完需重启；主 Agent 工具 `configure_specialist_runtime` 只能改已有外部 runtime 的非密钥项，**不能**设 base URL、代填 key、引导 device-code，也不能把 native 改成 codex/cc。
- 有任务内配密卡（`CodexConfigCard` / `runtime-config`），但**没有**右侧 Specialist CLI 卡片，也**没有**「重启 specialist runtime」。

产品口径（维护者确认）：配置页保持简；复杂鉴权进主对话；保底是用户可直连 specialist，且可重启。

## 目标（三块合一，完整产品面）

### A. 配置页：选 runtime + 拉 SDK

- 配置页增加 **runtime 选择**（至少 `codex` / `claude-code` 等已支持 kind）。
- 选定后，系统下载/安装对应 SDK（失败有明确提示与可重试）。
- 表单保持简：**runtime + Skills + 描述**（名称可保留）；旁侧短文案提示：鉴权 / base URL / device-code 等在主对话由主 Agent 完成。
- 保存时 UI **必须**把所选 `runtime` 写入 create/update API（与现有 schema 对齐）。

### B. 主对话代配：加密输入 + device-code 引导

放开当前限制，主 Agent 在对话中可协助完成：

- **base URL / API key**：向用户发出**加密输入框**；用户把 key 填进输入框，**key 不进入对话正文**。
- **device-code**：主 Agent 把 code 交给用户，并说明如何在外部完成配置。
- 完成后写入平台侧安全存储 / `runtime-config` 路径，供后续委派使用（具体存储形态实现自定，验收看行为）。

### C. 右侧 Specialist 卡片 + CLI + 重启

- 会话右侧增加 **Specialist 卡片**。
- 点击后打开 **CLI 页**：展示主 Agent ↔ 该 specialist 的对话记录；用户也可在此页直接与 specialist 交互。
- 该页左侧提供 **「重启 specialist runtime」**（换 endpoint/凭证或进程异常后可重新拉起，无需整站重启 API）。

## 验收标准

- [ ] **A**：设置页可选 runtime；选定后触发 SDK 拉取；保存后 GET specialist 可见对应 `runtime.kind`；有「剩余配置在主对话完成」提示。
- [ ] **B**：主对话可走加密输入完成 base URL 与 key（正文日志/历史中不可见明文 key）；device-code 流程有用户可见引导；无需手改进程 env 即可完成常见第三方 endpoint 配置（至少覆盖当前 Codex→DeepSeek Responses 类场景的一条端到端路径）。
- [ ] **C**：右侧卡片可打开 CLI 页；可见主 Agent–specialist 记录且用户可交互；「重启 specialist runtime」可用，重启后可再次委派/交互。
- [ ] 不降低现有安全底线：Always Allow 不得代填密钥；密钥不进 specialist 元数据白名单。
- [ ] 有对应自动化或可重复手工验收步骤（可与 `test(specialist): HTTP runtime 契约` 姊妹 issue 互补，不重复）。

## 非目标

- 不在本 issue 只补 HTTP 静默丢 `runtime` 的测试（另开测试 issue）。
- 不要求设置页做成「覆盖所有鉴权形态的巨型表单」。
- 不要求提供完全脱离平台的独立 Codex CLI 产品面；本 issue 的「CLI 页」是平台内嵌的 specialist 交互面。

## 现状锚点（便于实现对照）

- UI 表单：`apps/web/src/Orchestration.tsx`（无 runtime 选择器）
- 主 Agent 工具：`configure_specialist_runtime`（`main-config.ts`）
- 配密卡：`CodexConfigCard` / `POST .../subagents/:id/runtime-config`
- Base URL：`SCIENCE_AGENT_CODEX_BASE_URL` 进程 env

issue:462.body:
## User request

When I switch the model in a conversation, I want the next new conversation to start with that model automatically. I should not have to select it again or separately visit settings to make that choice stick.

Example: the configured default is model A. In session 1, I explicitly select model B in the conversation model picker. Every new conversation should initially use model B rather than returning to model A: this includes another session in the same project, a session in a different project, and the first session of a newly created project, even if the target project has a different default. If I later explicitly select model C, the next new session should start with C.

## Current behavior

The conversation picker changes a session override. New sessions inherit the project default model, falling back to the system default, so a choice made in the previous conversation is not automatically reused.

This is a request to change that behavior, rather than only explain it with a tooltip.

## Expected behavior and acceptance criteria

- [ ] After an explicit, successfully saved model selection in a conversation, every new conversation starts with that selected model, across all projects and including the first session of a newly created project, without an extra confirmation or a trip to settings.
- [ ] A remembered explicit selection takes precedence over project and system model defaults when initializing any new conversation.
- [ ] A later explicit selection becomes the remembered choice for subsequent new sessions. Merely opening an older conversation does not replace the remembered choice.
- [ ] The remembered choice survives page refresh and application restart.
- [ ] Existing conversations retain their own model selection; creating a conversation does not change other conversations or an in-flight run's model.
- [ ] If there is no remembered selection, normal project-default → system-default inheritance continues to work.
- [ ] If the remembered model has been removed or is no longer selectable, creation falls back to a valid configured default, or shows actionable model configuration feedback if none exists. It must not retain a dangling model selection.
- [ ] The model shown in the new conversation matches its effective saved model. Any scope hint accurately describes the new behavior in both English and Chinese.
- [ ] Repeatable browser regression coverage verifies A → select B → create session → B within the same project, across projects with different defaults, and in a newly created project; a subsequent selection of C; persistence after reload/restart, unchanged existing conversations, and missing-model fallback.

## Selection policy

Use one last explicitly selected model for new conversations, independent of project boundaries. The user requests a Codex-style experience: choose a model once and keep using that choice when starting new conversations. This is the requested interaction policy, rather than a claim about Codex implementation details.

Project boundaries must not reset the remembered selection. Merely viewing an older conversation must not count as choosing its model. Existing conversations retain their own selection. This specifies the initialization behavior; it does not require rewriting every project's settings or changing other users' preferences. The persistence mechanism should follow the product's user/preference model.

## Related issues and current PRs

- #44 describes the same source of confusion, but its proposed solution explicitly retains session-only switching and adds a scope hint. This issue requests remembered selection for new sessions instead. Keep the two acceptance contracts distinct; a hint-only change does not satisfy this request.
- PR #289 is currently an open draft for #44. Its description explicitly says persistence/configuration/selection callbacks are unchanged. It does not implement remembered selection; its hint wording will need to be reconciled if this feature lands.
- #278 concerns configuration from within a conversation and task continuation. It does not require new sessions to reuse the last selected model.
- Closed #336 is an analogous usability request about remembering approval mode/defaults, rather than model selection.

At filing time, a search of open/closed issues and current open PRs found no exact duplicate or open PR implementing this remembered-model behavior.

issue:48.body:
## Context

Since July 2026 an open-source "science workbench" category has formed, triggered by Anthropic's Claude Science launch (2026-06-30). Three direct open-source alternatives appeared the same week and are now at scale: [synthetic-sci/openscience](https://github.com/synthetic-sciences/openscience) (~3.6K★), [aipoch/open-science](https://github.com/aipoch/open-science) (~4.2K★), and [ai4s-research/open-science](https://github.com/ai4s-research/open-science) (~1.7K★). Having compared ScienceDiscovery against them (and against the autonomous-scientist systems: Sakana AI-Scientist, InternScience/InternAgent + MLEvolve), here is a strengths/gaps assessment in the hope it helps prioritization. Facts below are from public repo data collected 2026-09-15.

## Strengths (keep — and communicate)

1. **Sandbox-first security model.** Fail-closed Bubblewrap/Seatbelt execution, operator-scoped NPU chip passthrough, opt-in Broker with fixed entry points and `shell: false`. None of the three competitors communicates a default-isolation story; the highest-engagement technical question on a competitor's launch thread was literally *"are the skills executed within a secure, containerized sandbox by default, or does the user manage isolation?"* — this repo already answers that question, but almost nobody knows it does.
2. **Provenance depth.** CAS with pinned-asset drift rejection, review checks, cross-session/SubAgent citation chains. The strongest provenance story in the category.
3. **Search-camp RSI engine.** The evolve sidecar (flat-PUCT tree + OpenEvolve MAP-Elites, discriminability probe, explicit "no model training, no search-rule modification") is a clean, honest scope with a real cousin in [InternScience/MLEvolve](https://github.com/InternScience/MLEvolve) (#1 on MLE-Bench).
4. **Ascend NPU path.** 910B sandbox passthrough + allowlisted workloads (Protenix/MindScience) is unique in the category and extends machine-verifiable research to device-scale workloads.
5. **Engineering discipline beyond repo age.** Bilingual doc set, CI tiers (UT/ST/mocked E2E), self-documented limitations (e.g., Idea Tree scores are model judgments, not experimental evidence).

## Gaps (ordered by leverage)

1. **Installation/onboarding.** No binaries in Releases — #1 (open since 08-19, rated 1/5) is the only organic user feedback this repo has received, and it is someone who *could not install the product*. All three competitors ship desktop installers and a <10-minute quickstart. This pairs directly with the first-experience goal in #22.
2. **No community surface.** All merged PRs are bots; there are zero human external PRs. For comparison: aipoch merges 6+ human PRs/day; ai4s-research power users file bugs *and* land the fixes (e.g., their stall-guard for looping agents came from a user). A "good first issue" ladder + a contributor guide + weekly maintainer RFC triage would start the flywheel.
3. **Category invisibility + an unverifiable benchmark claim.** 58★ vs 1.7–4.2K for peers; one promotion event found (Sina Finance 2026-08-16) whose headline claim (BiomniBench-DA "业界SOTA") is dual-claimed by aipoch's README badge on the same benchmark. Without published methodology/splits, the claim reads as marketing and hurts credibility with scientists — either publish the eval or drop the superlative.
4. **Adoption levers validated by competitors, still missing here:** headless CLI / task API (repeated cross-repo demand — researchers want CI and agent-to-agent use, not only a GUI), model-provider onboarding (subscription reuse, connectivity-test friction), Windows parity.
5. **Cross-model skill consistency.** The single most-validated complaint in the category: *"one flag switches the model, not whether the skill actually works"* (prompts tuned on one model degrade on smaller/local models). A per-skill model-compatibility matrix or a cross-model smoke-test suite for the 300+ skills would directly differentiate.

## Suggested next steps

- [ ] Ship Linux binaries + a 10-minute quickstart (pairs with #22)
- [ ] Publish evolve/idea-tree efficiency metrics (per-node token cost, CAS reuse rate, surviving-node quality on an independent benchmark) — the pruning+reuse efficiency story is genuinely differentiating and no competitor tells it
- [ ] Benchmark-claim triage: methodology for BiomniBench-DA or remove the SOTA wording
- [ ] Community ladder: CONTRIBUTING good-first-issues + a maintainer-reserved RFC-triage day

Happy to help flesh any of these out.

issue:482.body:
## Problem

On Windows, killing a runner child with POSIX-style signals does not tear down the full process tree. Desktop Windows work needs a platform adaptation that terminates the child **and** its grandchildren (e.g. `taskkill /T /F`).

PR #478 (`Closes #477` / F3.1 CAS) already embeds `terminateTree` under `services/runner/src/platform/`. That belongs to **F3.2**, not F3.1 — track and accept it here (or split it out of #478).

## Expected

- `services/runner` (and any required API call sites) obtain tree-kill via `platform/index.ts` only.
- POSIX path remains signal-based; Windows uses an explicit tree terminate.
- Unit tests tagged `os:windows` cover child + grandchild cleanup.

## Verification cases

### Case 1 — Windows tree kill
- **Preconditions:** Windows host; spawn a Node/cmd child that itself spawns a grandchild that stays alive.
- **Steps:** Call `terminateTree(child)`; wait briefly; inspect process list for child and grandchild PIDs.
- **Expected / pass:** Both PIDs are gone; helper returns success/true.

### Case 2 — POSIX unchanged
- **Preconditions:** Linux or macOS.
- **Steps:** Run existing runner process-lifecycle / posix platform tests.
- **Expected / pass:** No behaviour change vs `main`; suite green.

### Case 3 — Facade only
- **Preconditions:** PR diff for this issue.
- **Steps:** Grep runner call sites for raw `taskkill` / `process.platform === \"win32\"` outside `platform/`.
- **Expected / pass:** No direct platform branches in consumer code; all go through `platform/index.ts`.

## Related

- Split from / Follow-up for PR #478 and #477 (F3.1)
- Parent: #400

issue:483.body:
## Problem

POSIX `chmod 0600` only toggles the read-only bit on Windows NTFS and does **not** strip inherited group/world access. Secrets, bootstrap tokens, and similar owner-only files need an ACL adaptation (`icacls` inheritance strip + grant current user).

PR #478 embeds `restrictToOwner` / `restrictToOwnerSync` under `services/api` and `services/runner` platform layers while claiming only F3.1 (#477). Track **F3.3** here so scope and AC are explicit (or split out of #478).

## Expected

- Sensitive write sites that previously `chmod`'d to owner-only use `restrictToOwner` via `platform/os` (api) / `platform` (runner).
- POSIX keeps `chmod`; Windows uses icacls with inheritance removed.
- Highest-sensitivity stores (e.g. master key / SSH private key paths) are included or explicitly deferred with rationale.

## Verification cases

### Case 1 — Windows ACL tightened
- **Preconditions:** Windows host; create a temp file that inherits group-readable ACLs.
- **Steps:** Call `restrictToOwner(file)`; run `icacls <file>` and inspect DACL.
- **Expected / pass:** Inheritance removed; current user has access; unintended group/world ACE gone (or equivalent owner-only outcome documented in the test).

### Case 2 — POSIX unchanged
- **Preconditions:** Linux or macOS.
- **Steps:** Run posix platform + existing secrets/bootstrap unit tests.
- **Expected / pass:** Mode bits still applied as on `main`; suite green.

### Case 3 — Sync path at startup
- **Preconditions:** Windows; data dir owned by another principal (or simulated failure).
- **Steps:** Exercise `restrictToOwnerSync` on bootstrap/token paths.
- **Expected / pass:** Failure mode is explicit (error message), not a silent weaken; documented in PR/issue notes.

## Related

- Split from / Follow-up for PR #478 and #477 (F3.1)
- Parent: #400
- Note from #478 review: `store/secrets.ts` / `store/ssh-config.ts` may still rely on raw `chmod` — include or call out as residual risk.

issue:495.body:
## Problem

`win-desktop-client/` is an independent pnpm workspace (not listed in the root `pnpm-workspace.yaml` packages: `config / apps/* / services/* / packages/*`). Architecture checks and `tsconfig.tests.json` also skip it. As a result, install / typecheck / unit-test failures under this tree are invisible to GitHub Actions (see #486: missing patch and empty `tsconfig` include were only found by local runs).

## Expected

A CI job (or matrix entry) runs on changes under `win-desktop-client/**` and exercises at least:

- `pnpm install` (lockfile present)
- `pnpm typecheck` (when sources exist)
- `pnpm test` for portable Node tests

## Verification cases

### Case 1 — install gate
- **Preconditions:** PR that only touches `win-desktop-client/` and references a missing `patchedDependencies` file (or otherwise breaks install).
- **Steps:** Open the PR; wait for CI.
- **Expected / pass:** The new job fails with a clear install error; root jobs that ignore this tree may still be green.

### Case 2 — typecheck / test gate
- **Preconditions:** PR adds a TypeScript error under `win-desktop-client/src/` or a failing `test/*.test.ts`.
- **Steps:** Open the PR; wait for CI.
- **Expected / pass:** typecheck or test step fails; merge is blocked by the required check once wired.

### Case 3 — no-op on unrelated paths
- **Preconditions:** PR only changes `apps/web/` (or another root package).
- **Steps:** Open the PR.
- **Expected / pass:** The win-desktop-client job is skipped or stays green without installing Electron unnecessarily.

## Context

Refs #486, #485. Non-blocking Follow-up from HongyeZhou review of shell.01.

issue:496.body:
## Problem

#494 adds `scripts/lib/venv-launchers.mjs` (trampoline replace + runtime DLL copy) with portable unit tests, but:

1. Nothing in-tree calls `replaceVenvTrampolines` / `copyVenvRuntimeDlls` (`assemble-backend.mjs` / bootstrap not present yet).
2. Comments claim a closed loop with `fixVenvHome`, but that helper does not exist — after swapping the launcher, `pyvenv.cfg` `home` can still point at the build machine, so the real `python.exe` still fails off-machine.
3. Tests only compare bytes; they do not spawn `Scripts\python.exe`, so the field failures (entity not found / `0xC0000135`) are not covered.

## Expected

- Call sites in assemble-backend (pack-time) and bootstrap (first-run repair) invoke the module.
- `fixVenvHome` (or equivalent) rewrites `pyvenv.cfg` `home` to the bundled interpreter root.
- A Windows smoke test builds a uv venv, relocates it, spawns `Scripts\python.exe -c "..."`, and asserts exit 0 with `sys.prefix` at the new path.

## Verification cases

### Case 1 — pack-time wiring
- **Preconditions:** Payload contains a uv-created venv whose `Scripts\python.exe` is a trampoline; assemble-backend runs.
- **Steps:** Inspect `Scripts\python.exe` and `pyvenv.cfg` after assemble.
- **Expected / pass:** Launcher is a real CPython stub (no `uv trampoline` marker); `home` points at the bundled python root; runtime DLLs sit beside the launcher.

### Case 2 — first-run bootstrap repair
- **Preconditions:** `dataDir\envs` still has pre-fix trampolines (reinstall with valid unpack stamp).
- **Steps:** Start the shell once on a clean machine without system Python.
- **Expected / pass:** Bootstrap replaces trampolines, copies DLLs, fixes `home`; each venv `python.exe -c "import sys; print(sys.prefix)"` exits 0.

### Case 3 — Windows spawn smoke (CI or labeled job)
- **Preconditions:** `os:windows` (or equivalent) test runner with a bundled/minimal CPython + uv.
- **Steps:** Create uv venv → move tree → `spawn(Scripts/python.exe, ["-c", "import sys; print(sys.prefix)"])`.
- **Expected / pass:** Exit code 0; printed prefix equals the relocated venv path. Byte-only unit tests alone do not satisfy this case.

## Context

Refs #494, #493. Non-blocking Follow-up from HongyeZhou review of shell.04. #494 should use `Refs #493` until this loop lands (or fold wiring into the same PR).

issue:50.body:
## Summary

Both long-running engines — the evolution search and the Idea Tree — can be **started** from the command line but cannot be **observed, controlled, or stopped** from it. Their progress is designed to land on a frontend card, so a terminal user gets a run id and then nothing. I would like `evolve` and `idea` subcommands that reuse the HTTP endpoints the Web UI already calls.

## What happens today

Starting works. `ScienceDiscovery run "/evolve-design --algorithm puct …"` reaches the same control plane as the browser, the agent loads the `evolve-design` skill, and it calls `create_evolve_run`. Then the turn ends — deliberately. The tool's own result text instructs the model:

> The search runs for minutes to hours and its card streams live progress on its own — do not wait for it here, and do not poll `get_evolve_run`.

`create_idea_research` says the same thing:

> After success, report the handoff and end this turn; the existing tree card streams progress. Do not poll or start another research to wait for completion.

That is the right call for the agent loop — polling would burn the budget the search itself needs. But it means **the card is the only progress surface**, and the CLI has no equivalent. `ScienceDiscovery run` prints `Search created: <uuid>` and exits while the search keeps running server-side for hours.

`services/launcher/src/cli-options.ts` has no evolve or idea-tree subcommand and no related flag. So from a terminal today you cannot:

- list the searches or researches that exist;
- see how far one has got;
- fetch a candidate;
- stop one, or pause and resume it.

The only workaround is starting another `run` in the same session and hoping the model calls `get_evolve_run` / `get_idea_research` — a whole model turn spent reading a status field, using tools whose descriptions explicitly tell the model not to poll them.

## The endpoints already exist

The Web UI drives all of this over plain HTTP:

**Evolve**
- `GET /api/evolve/runs`
- `GET /api/evolve/runs/<id>/events?after=<cursor>`
- `GET /api/evolve/runs/<id>/candidates/<codeHash>`
- `POST /api/evolve/runs/<id>/stop`

**Idea Tree**
- `GET /api/sessions/<sid>/idea-tree/research`
- `POST /api/sessions/<sid>/idea-tree/research` — `pause`, `continue`, `stop`, `defaults`
- `GET /api/sessions/<sid>/idea-tree/research/<rid>/events`
- `GET /api/sessions/<sid>/idea-tree/graph`

## The client plumbing also already exists

`services/launcher/src/control-plane-client.ts` has an authenticated generic `request<T>(path, init)` and `subscribeRunEvents()`, a working SSE consumer that "mirrors the Web frontend's `subscribeRunEvents`: fetch with `accept: text/event-stream`, split frames". The launcher also already resolves the bearer token from the data directory. A `watch` subcommand is that SSE reader pointed at a different path — this is wiring, not new infrastructure.

## Proposal

```
ScienceDiscovery evolve list
ScienceDiscovery evolve get <run-id> [--candidate <hash>]
ScienceDiscovery evolve watch <run-id>
ScienceDiscovery evolve stop <run-id>

ScienceDiscovery idea list --session <id>
ScienceDiscovery idea get <research-id> --session <id>
ScienceDiscovery idea watch <research-id> --session <id>
ScienceDiscovery idea pause|continue|stop <research-id> --session <id>
```

Conventions, matching what `run` already does:

- **text on a TTY, JSONL when piped.** `run` already switches output mode this way; these commands should not invent a second convention.
- **`watch` resumes rather than replays.** The evolve event endpoint already takes `?after=<cursor>`; a dropped connection should continue from the last event seen.
- **Token and data-dir handling identical to `run`** — sharing a `--data-dir` with `serve` should mean no extra configuration.

One asymmetry to decide: evolve exposes only `stop`, while Idea Tree has `pause` / `continue` / `stop`. Either the CLI mirrors each engine's real capabilities, or evolve gains pause/resume — worth an explicit choice rather than an accident.

## Why it matters

- **Unattended and batch use.** Starting a search from a job script is pointless if the same script cannot poll it, stop it when a budget is spent, or collect the winning candidate.
- **Headless and remote machines.** On a workstation reached over SSH there is no browser to hold the card open. Today that machine can start a multi-hour search it cannot then observe.
- **Consistency.** The CLI is already positioned as the scriptable twin of the Web UI; the two most expensive operations in the product are exactly the ones it cannot drive.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] Evolve searches and Idea Tree researches can be listed, inspected, watched, and stopped from the CLI.
- [ ] `watch` streams live and resumes from a cursor after a dropped connection.
- [ ] Output follows the existing TTY/pipe convention, so `| jq` works.
- [ ] No new authentication path: the token comes from the data directory as `run` already does.
- [ ] Commands and options appear in `help` and in the CLI reference.
- [ ] Stopping from the CLI has the same effect as stopping from the UI card.

## Open questions

- Should `run` gain an optional `--wait` that blocks until a started engine finishes? Useful in scripts, but these runs last hours — probably better served by `watch`.
- Should `watch` exit non-zero when the run ends in failure, so a script can branch on it?
- Does `evolve list` need session/project scoping, given `GET /api/evolve/runs` is global today?

Related: [#30](https://github.com/openJiuwen-ai/sciencediscovery/issues/30) (introduce the CLI in the README) — that issue is about making the CLI discoverable; this one is about the two workflows it cannot reach.

issue:54.body:
## Summary

ScienceDiscovery can already evolve the things a user brings it — a program, a prompt, a protocol. It cannot evolve **itself**. I would like RSI support: given a dataset of tasks, search over the agent's own harness — system prompt fragments, specialist instructions, skill methodology, tool and skill selection — score each variant by running it against that dataset, and surface the winner for a human to adopt.

The search machinery for this already exists in `services/evolve`. What is missing is the candidate being the harness, the evaluation being an agent run, and a reviewed promotion step.

## What is already there

This is deliberately an extension, not a new engine.

- **The search sidecar**, `services/evolve`, runs on `agentdescent>=0.4.6` — `evolve()` / `async_evolve()`, `FlatPuct`, the ledger, the verifier and the policies — behind two engines: flat-PUCT tree search (`puct_engine.py`) and MAP-Elites islands with ring migration (`openevolve_engine.py`).
- **Non-program candidates are first class.** `text_candidate.py` exists precisely because "a prompt or an abstract has no docstring", and `judge_domain.py` states its purpose plainly: it "is what makes `/evolve` work on things that are not programs over tables: a prompt, an abstract, a protocol, a plan". Evolving prompt text is not a new capability — it is the existing one pointed at a different file.
- **Four scoring seams**, already cut: `scorecard_domain` (a metric over a dataset), `test_gate_domain` (a suite's pass rate), `script_domain` (a scorer the drafting model writes), `judge_domain` (a rubric read by a model).
- **Anti-reward-hacking is already solved once.** `test_gate_domain` freezes in two layers — a proposal filter over `frozen` globs in the prompt, and enforcement below it — with the upstream note this issue should quote rather than restate: *"without it the shortest path to a high score is to weaken the thing measuring it."* That is the single most important property RSI needs, and the pattern is in the tree.
- **Held-out splitting exists.** `create_evolve_run` already accepts `caseSplit` with `gateGroups`, `rolloutGroups` and `testGroups`, which is the shape needed to keep a harness from overfitting the tasks it was tuned on.
- **Trajectories are recorded.** `packages/trajectory` captures per-session entries with the context blocks that were actually sent, which is the raw material for judging whether a harness change helped.
- **Parts of the harness are already frozen.** Built-in specialists reject edits to `instructions` / `description` / `name` / `connectorIds` / `enabledSkillIds`; only `enabled` is user-mutable. RSI has to open that door deliberately rather than by accident.

## What is missing

1. **The candidate is never the harness.** Today a candidate is one text-shaped artifact the user owns. The agent's own scaffolding lives elsewhere and is not reachable by a search: prompt assembly (`packages/context/src/prompt-renderer.ts`, `assembler.ts`), specialist instructions (`packages/specialist/src/builtins.ts`), skill methodology (`skills/*/SKILL.md`), and the skill/connector selection for a run.

2. **There is no task-dataset scoring mode.** `scorecard_domain` scores a *program* over a table. RSI needs to score a *harness* over a set of tasks, where each evaluation is a full agent run with its own tool calls, sandboxed execution and artifacts. That is a different cost class and needs its own domain.

3. **There is no promotion path.** An improved harness must be diffable, reviewable, versioned and revertible. Nothing should ever be self-applied.

## Proposal

### 1. A harness candidate

A bundle rather than a single blob: prompt fragments, one or more specialist instruction sets, selected skills, and the run settings that go with them. The mutation prompt sees the bundle and rewrites part of it; the ledger records which part changed, so a win is attributable to something specific.

### 2. A `task_dataset` domain

A dataset entry is a task plus whatever the existing four modes need to score its outcome — a metric, a test suite, a scoring script, or a rubric. Evaluating one candidate means running the agent over the split and aggregating. Reuse `caseSplit` so the reported number comes from tasks the search did not tune against.

The honest problem here is cost: one candidate equals N agent runs, each with model calls and sandboxed execution. The design needs a budget per generation and an early-abandon policy, not just a score.

### 3. Freeze the things a self-improving search must not touch

Same two-layer shape `test_gate_domain` already uses, with a wider frozen set:

- the task dataset and its expected outcomes;
- the scorer, whichever mode it is;
- the permission, sandbox and approval layers — a harness that scores better by asking for fewer confirmations is not better;
- the evolve sidecar's own code and the freeze list itself.

A candidate that edits any of these is rejected at the proposal filter, not merely penalized.

### 4. Promotion is a human step

The winner lands as a reviewable proposal: a diff against the current harness, the score with its held-out number, and the trajectory evidence behind it. Adoption is explicit, versioned and revertible. The skill review flow and the built-in specialists' read-only rules already establish that shape; RSI should reuse it rather than invent a second one.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] A search can take the agent's harness as its candidate, not only a user artifact.
- [ ] A task dataset can be supplied, and a candidate is scored by running the agent over it.
- [ ] The reported score comes from a held-out split.
- [ ] The dataset, the scorer, and the permission/sandbox layers are frozen against modification by the search, enforced at the proposal filter.
- [ ] An improved harness appears as a reviewable, versioned proposal and is never self-applied.
- [ ] Reverting to the previous harness is one action.
- [ ] A run states its budget and stops at it.

## Open questions

- Should a run evolve one specialist at a time, or the whole bundle? One at a time attributes wins more cleanly; the whole bundle can find interactions.
- Where does a task dataset live — a repository artifact, a workspace file, or a first-class store object?
- Which engine fits better? PUCT refines one starting point; OpenEvolve's islands keep diversity, which may matter more when a prompt change can be good in one dimension and harmful in another.
- What is the minimum dataset size where a win is believable rather than noise, given the non-determinism the judge mode already documents?
- Should this reuse `/evolve-design`'s checkpointed design conversation, or have its own entry point?

Related: [#50](https://github.com/openJiuwen-ai/sciencediscovery/issues/50) — the engines can be started but not observed or stopped from the CLI, which matters more for a search whose evaluations are full agent runs.

## Summary

On 2026-10-26 every GitHub issue in `openJiuwen-ai/sciencediscovery` was classified against the nine requirement rows in #249. Pull requests were excluded. The three counts agreed: `gh issue list --state all`, REST pagination of 100 items per page, and the issue search counter. The total is **232** issues, **116 open** and **116 closed**.

Whether an issue is developed was judged from `origin/main` at `65eddde1`, not from the open or closed flag. An open issue can already be on `main`. A closed issue can still be undeveloped when it was closed as a duplicate or as not planned, or when the change never reached `main`.

This issue records that snapshot. It does not close, retitle, or implement any of the issues below.

## Counts

| | |
| --- | --- |
| bug / feature / other | 73 / 151 / 8 |
| bug severity P0 / P1 / P2 / P3 | 1 / 24 / 44 / 4 |
| mapped to a #249 row / unmapped | 139 / 93 |
| developed / partial / not developed / not applicable | 103 / 39 / 82 / 8 |
| marked complex | 122 |

Severity is the impact of the defect itself. It is not lowered because a later commit fixed it. "Not applicable" is used only for the eight items in **other**, which have no defect or feature to build. "Complex" means the work crosses modules, depends on an external system, or packs several independent pieces into one issue.

## Rules

1. An issue maps to one of the nine names in the #249 table, or to **unmapped**.
2. Issues already closed before the 2026-10-10 v0.3.0 kickoff stay unmapped, even when the topic matches a row. An issue closed on 2026-10-10 counts as inside the cycle. This rule sets aside 20 topic matches: CI engineering refactor 4, componentized architecture 10, documentation and website 5, routine bug fixes 1. Those four counts are part of the snapshot. The 20 issue numbers are not listed separately.
3. A feature maps by topic and never lands in Routine bug fixes.
4. A bug in behavior that a requirement row delivers maps to that row. Other bugs inside the release cycle map to Routine bug fixes.
5. A defect in the test or CI harness (a wrong gate, lost end-to-end evidence, broken test discovery) maps to CI engineering refactor. A product defect that CI happened to catch still maps to Routine bug fixes.
6. **Other** is a calendar, a call for release-note feedback, a discussion, or a usage question. #249 itself is other and unmapped: it is the calendar that holds the table.
7. Developed means the requested behavior is on `origin/main` at `65eddde1`. Evidence is a merge that is an ancestor of that commit, or a path on that commit. Early pull requests, roughly #3 through #111, were rewritten out of that ancestry and were checked by subject or by path. A number in an older write-up that is actually a GitCode id was not treated as a GitHub pull request.

   - #327 was closed as not planned and superseded by #330. The behavior landed with #330 in pull request #356. #327 stays not developed.

## Original specification (preserved for traceability)

> Cross-tracking: [GitCode #90](https://gitcode.com/openJiuwen/sciencediscovery/issues/90) (Chinese counterpart of this issue).

## What I was trying to do

Enter the app for the first time and figure out how to start my first analysis.

## What I saw instead

With no projects yet, the home screen shows a centered empty-state card listing three steps:

1. Configure a model (go to system settings → model registry, then save a provider token);
2. Create a project (its first session opens automatically);
3. Drop a CSV and ask (analyze the CSV and plot charts).

These are plain static list items (empty-state rendering in `apps/web/src/App.tsx`) with no click handlers: clicking "Configure a model" does nothing, and so does "Create a project". There is no composer, no upload area, no sample-data button, and no guided tour.

## Why this is confusing

New users have no idea where to click; the three steps are signposts, but every one of them requires the user to find the destination on their own.

## Suggested user-observable outcome

- Turn each step into a real action: "Configure a model" opens the matching settings section directly; "Create a project" opens the creation dialog directly.
- Add a prominent primary button "Load sample data and try it now": automatically create an initial project and session, load a bundled sample CSV, and prefill a ready-to-send example prompt, so a new user sees their first chart within seconds.
- Open question (needs a product decision): the theme of the bundled sample CSV and its expected chart types are not decided yet — a public, license-clean scientific dataset should be picked first.

Design notes: making the empty-state steps interactive is low-risk frontend routing/dialog work; the one-click sample needs decisions on data source (bundled vs. downloaded on first run) and topic, which is why it is registered as an open question here.

Reviewed against upstream main `65eddde1` on 2026-10-27. Historical PR test results apply to their recorded candidate revisions only; no new product acceptance tests were run in this triage.

## Remaining work

Audit all original documentation criteria against the reorganized current docs, restore missing operational how-to/index/reference coverage if needed, and record an actual supplied-example tutorial run and bilingual parity/link results. Do not recreate pages that already exist.

## Release

## Completion rule

- [ ] Account for every original criterion: delivered evidence, remaining implementation, explicit approved alternative, or separately linked follow-up.
- [ ] Run matching acceptance checks on the final candidate and retain actual results; do not treat workflow presence, merged status or historical green CI as full acceptance.
- [ ] Reconcile still-open PRs and original dependencies with the successor issue before merge.

## Original specification (preserved for traceability)

## Summary

`/evolve` is one of the largest features in the product and has **no user documentation in either language**. A researcher cannot learn what it does, when to reach for it, or how to drive it, without reading the source. I would like an explanation page, a how-to, and a tutorial — in English and Chinese — plus the existing Chinese architecture note fixed up and made reachable.

## What ships versus what is documented

What ships:

| Surface | Size |
|---|---|
| `services/evolve` Python sidecar | 23 modules, two search engines — flat-PUCT (`puct_engine.py`) and MAP-Elites islands with ring migration (`openevolve_engine.py`) |
| Scoring modes | four domain seams: `scorecard_domain` (dataset metric), `test_gate_domain` (test suite), `script_domain` (a scorer the model writes), `judge_domain` (LLM rubric) |
| Agent tools | `create_evolve_run`, `get_evolve_run` |
| Skill | `evolve-design`, a four-checkpoint design conversation with an algorithm choice |
| Web UI | 13 components — panel, algorithm picker, candidate stream, score chart, search graph canvas and table, budget bar, cell grid |
| UI strings | 188 `evolve.*` message keys |
| HTTP API | `/api/evolve/runs`, `/runs/<id>/events`, `/runs/<id>/candidates/<hash>`, `/runs/<id>/stop` |

What is documented:

| Language | Coverage |
|---|---|
| Chinese | **one** file, `docs/zh/explanation/evolve-standalone.md` (252 lines) |
| English | **zero** — the word "evolve" appears in exactly one English file, `docs/en/reference/web-frontend.md`, in passing |

And the single Chinese file has two problems of its own:

1. **It is unreachable.** `docs/zh/explanation/README.md` does not link it. The index lists `skill-library-management.md` and `skill-self-evolution.md` but not `evolve-standalone.md`, so the only way to find it is to list the directory. (Raised as an orphan page in [#25](https://github.com/openJiuwen-ai/sciencediscovery/issues/25).)
2. **It answers a different question.** Its own opening says it covers the two engines' differences and what it would take to run the sidecar as a standalone backend. That is an architecture note for a maintainer. Nothing in it tells a researcher what a search is for, when scoring will actually discriminate, or how to start one.

## What to write

### 1. `explanation/evolve.md` (EN + ZH)

What an evolution search is, and the honest limits: it rewrites a candidate dozens of times and keeps what scores higher, so it succeeds or fails on whether the scoring can tell a good candidate from a bad one — a scoring function that cannot shows up as a flat run, not as an error. Cover the four scoring modes and when each applies, the two engines and when to pick which, and the frozen-scorer rule that `test_gate_domain` enforces, whose upstream note is worth quoting: *"without it the shortest path to a high score is to weaken the thing measuring it."*

### 2. `how-to/run-an-evolution-search.md` (EN + ZH)

The operational path: preparing a starting point and a dataset or test suite, what `--algorithm puct` versus `--algorithm openevolve` changes, reading the score chart and the search graph, budgets and stopping, retrieving the winning candidate, and what the approval card asks for before a run starts.

### 3. `tutorial/…-evolve-a-solution.md` (EN + ZH)

One short end-to-end run a reader can actually complete: a small starting program, a dataset with a metric, the `/evolve-design` conversation answered checkpoint by checkpoint, then what to look at while it runs and how to tell a real improvement from noise. This is the piece [#26](https://github.com/openJiuwen-ai/sciencediscovery/issues/26) asks for in general, applied here.

### 4. Fix what exists

Link `evolve-standalone.md` from the Chinese explanation index, give it an English counterpart, and retitle it so its scope is obvious — it is the engine-internals and standalone-deployment note, not the feature's documentation.

### 5. Reference the surface

The four HTTP endpoints belong in `reference/rest-api.md`, and the two agent tools in `reference/builtin-tools.md`, so the feature is reachable from the reference tree as well as the prose.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] An English reader can learn what `/evolve` is, when to use it, and how to run one, without reading source code.
- [ ] Explanation, how-to and tutorial pages exist in both languages and are linked from their indexes.
- [ ] The four scoring modes and the two engines are each documented with the case they suit.
- [ ] The frozen-scorer rule is stated where a user designing a search will meet it.
- [ ] The tutorial runs end to end on a supplied example, and says how to judge whether the result is real.
- [ ] `evolve-standalone.md` is linked, translated, and scoped by its title.
- [ ] The evolve endpoints and agent tools appear in the reference documents.

## Open questions

- Should the tutorial evolve a program (dataset metric) or a prompt (LLM judge)? The program case is more convincing; the prompt case is cheaper to run and needs no dataset.
- Can a small example — a starting program plus a labelled dataset — be committed for the tutorial, as [#26](https://github.com/openJiuwen-ai/sciencediscovery/issues/26) proposes generally?
- Does the Idea Tree engine want the same treatment in the same pass? It has the same shape of gap: `idea-tree-engine.md` is also Chinese-only.

Related: [#25](https://github.com/openJiuwen-ai/sciencediscovery/issues/25) (documentation completeness and the orphan pages), [#26](https://github.com/openJiuwen-ai/sciencediscovery/issues/26) (the tutorial series), [#54](https://github.com/openJiuwen-ai/sciencediscovery/issues/54) (RSI, which builds directly on this engine and will be much harder to explain if the engine itself is undocumented).

## Cross-check needed

cc @zhaozhaozz @zy95-12 @HongyeZhou

### Three-layer defaults (important)
These coexist and are easy to conflate:

1. **Schema fallback**: `DEFAULT_SKILL_SELECTION_MODE = "all"` when unset (`packages/schema/src/runtime-settings.ts`).
2. **New Project product default**: `withDefaultProjectSkillSettings` writes `skillSelectionMode: "selected"` + empty `enabledSkillIds` / libraries (Skill Library intent: avoid silently expanding capability).
3. **JiuwenSwarm force-all**: on start, `http/index.ts` calls `store.useEverySkillEverywhere()` so the **effective** mode is `all` while Swarm is the backend (stored `selected` is kept and applies again when switching back to native).

Box smoke on Swarm therefore seeing `all` is **expected**, not accidental.

### Observation (box smoke, 2026-10-24 Asia/Shanghai)
- SHA: `main@9eb45d75`
- Backend: **JiuwenSwarm** (force-all path)
- Model: Zhipu `glm-5.3-flash`
- ~17 shipped skills effective, `thinkingEffort: high`
- Trivial user prompt → **~38k input tokens** (chat/history ≈ **165 bytes**)
- First visible assistant text ≈ **20s** wall

Progressive disclosure is **already implemented** (`docs/en/developer-docs/skill-progressive-disclosure.md`: metadata/path in prompt, body on demand). It does **not** prevent metadata/tool-surface growth when the effective selected set is the whole catalog under `all` / Swarm force-all.

### Questions for maintainers
1. Should end-user UX optimize for **Project `selected`** or accept **Swarm force-all** as the primary path?
2. Is there appetite to change schema DEFAULT, Swarm force-all, or both?
3. Have you seen the same **TTFT / cost** under Swarm vs native?

### Proposed performance watch split (do not mix into one Nightly bucket)
1. **UX / API latency lane** — queue → context → **TTFT** → run wall; short daily probe (`live.mjs ttft` + one real short chat), measure under **both** native and JiuwenSwarm, and under `all` vs `selected`.
2. **Correctness lane (existing L3 ×9)** — tool/files/cancel/etc.; keep **out of** TTFT gates.
3. **Research quality lane (L4 Nightly)** — DRB/Biomni/etc. as quality signal, **not** first-token UX.

### Possible directions (not proposing a fix yet)
- Keep progressive disclosure; also shrink **effective set** under Swarm (or stop force-all)
- Align schema DEFAULT with new-Project `selected`
- Cap / warn when resolved skill metadata size exceeds a threshold
- Surface skill-token cost in Usage / composer

### Non-goals
- Nightly research-bench red streak root-cause (separate)
- Tool-call accuracy eval (separate)

### Test coverage gap
- Unit coverage exists for settings semantics (`store.test.ts`: selected / all / `useEverySkillEverywhere`).
- **No CI gate** on TTFT or skill-token size; `live.mjs ttft()` logs only.
- Progressive disclosure tests do not cap catalog size under `all`.

Cross-check so far: skills-side review agrees the three-layer story; DigitalMate has no parallel issue. Nearby: #508, #93, #141.

> Converted from bug → feature per HongyeZhou (2026-10-27): this is a product/UX presentation improvement, not a hard defect.

## Feature request
When tool calls fail then recover mid-run, the default timeline narrative shows raw **failed** tool cards before a later success. #335 expected a clearer “retrying with fixed args” (or equivalent) presentation for the same logical operation. PRs #345 / #551 addressed missing required `prompt` on `task` before a deep createSubagent throw; they did **not** deliver the general failure→retry UI narrative (S6).

## Expected
When there is clear association evidence that a later call is a bounded correction of the same logical tool operation, the UI updates in place (or equivalent merged presentation): default view is a concise result; attempt count / errors / recovery detail are available on demand. Unrecoverable failures keep a clear reason. Real execution history and audit evidence are not rewritten as pure success. Do not blindly replay side-effecting operations to reduce cards.

## Verification cases

1. **In-place recovery presentation**
   - **Preconditions:** A recoverable invalid-argument or soft-fail path that retries within one logical operation (browser or hermetic UI fixture).
   - **Steps:**
     1. Trigger a tool call that fails then succeeds on a bounded correction.
     2. Inspect the timeline/card for that operation.
   - **Expected result / pass criteria:** Default view is not a stack of contradictory failed+success cards for the same operation; recovery state/result is shown in place; history of attempts remains inspectable; independent operations are not wrongly merged.

2. **Side-effect boundary**
   - **Preconditions:** A tool invocation that may have already executed with side effects before observation failed.
   - **Steps:**
     1. Observe recovery/UI merge behavior.
   - **Expected result / pass criteria:** No blind resubmit of committed side-effecting work solely to tidy the timeline; audit/failure records stay consistent.

## Context
- Env: _not provided_ for a fresh UI journey this filing; scope from #335 expected narrative and product phase-3 note on that Issue.
- Refs: Parent #335; PRs #345 / #551 (merged) for prompt-path only.
- Notes: Related UX umbrella #330 is adjacent (timeline hierarchy) but not a substitute for this recovery-presentation bug.

issue:618.body:
Follow-up to #245, criterion 3. PR #617 delivers the measurement harness and the per-request wire diagnostics, but the real relay-vs-direct measurement is **not** delivered: the team's bot host has no relay or model endpoint credentials.

## What is missing

Criterion 3 of #245 asks for a comparison of a relay endpoint against a direct endpoint with the same model alias, the same request body bytes, the same workload and the same concurrency, with wire latency reported separately from agent duration and token counts. The harness exists (`scripts/model-endpoint-compare.mjs`, delivered in #617 and covered by `scripts/model-endpoint-compare.test.mjs` against local stub endpoints). What does not exist is a run against real endpoints, so #245 stays open as partially delivered.

## Who can run it

Someone on an owner-hosted machine that has both endpoint URLs and their credentials. The team's bot host cannot: it has no model credentials, and this is not a code problem.

## Command (fill the placeholders)

```bash
node scripts/model-endpoint-compare.mjs \
  --model <model-alias> \
  --prompt-file <one-prompt.txt> \
  --a-name relay  --a-base-url <relay-base-url>  --a-token-env A_TOKEN \
  --b-name direct --b-base-url <direct-base-url> --b-token-env B_TOKEN \
  --requests 20 --concurrency 2 --timeout-ms 300000 \
  --out compare.json
```

`--body-file <identical-body.json>` may be used instead of `--prompt-file` when the exact request body must be reused. The script refuses two different model aliases and refuses a workload where the two bodies would differ, so a latency delta cannot come from a body change.

## What to do with the result

Paste the comparison table the script prints (p50/p90/p95 per endpoint, failures, tokens) and attach or link `compare.json` in #245. That closes criterion 3.

## Notes

- Endpoint tokens are read from the environment variables named by `--a-token-env` / `--b-token-env`; they are never written into the report.
- No repository change is expected from this issue: it is a measurement task, not a code task.

Related: #245, #617.

issue:623.body:
## Motivation

Long-running offline computations and Agent conversations have different lifecycles. An Agent turn can finish while a training, simulation, or batch-processing task continues running. After evaluation, this is a feature-design topic about coordination between offline tasks and Agents, rather than a defect in turn completion.

This issue replaces #434 and preserves its motivating scenario.

## Motivating scenario

In the NatureBench reproduction session `93f897ca-cefe-4e7b-932d-8339cbef1459`, run `84d71b8a-77dd-42a7-bc81-15e326b14cb1` completed while a background `python run.py --instances mop_sc` computation continued. The final computation took approximately 1,587.7 seconds and produced `predictions.npy` with shape `(5693,)`.

The user had to inspect host processes and wait for the output manually. Starting another Agent run could also launch duplicate work. An Agent promising to return after a wall-clock delay is not a reliable scheduling mechanism.

## Feature scope

Design how long-running offline tasks collaborate with Agents across turns:

- Give supported offline tasks a queryable identity and lifecycle, with ownership linked to the originating session/run.
- Make ongoing computation visible even after the initiating Agent turn finishes.
- Let a later turn inspect, await, or resume coordination with the same task without starting duplicate computation.
- Define how task completion, failure, cancellation, and results become available to the user and Agent.
- Define the default turn-completion policy when a task is still running, including whether explicit detachment is required.
- Document lifecycle limits, including runtime/service restarts and the treatment of processes launched outside the supported task mechanism.

## Design decisions before implementation

- Turn completion: wait for the task, require explicit detach, or register it in the background and notify.
- Ownership and persistence: session-level versus run-level handles, and restart behavior.
- Minimum user interface: how users discover active tasks, inspect progress, and retrieve results.
- Agent continuation: explicit user-driven await/resume versus automatic completion notification or continuation.
- Delivery decomposition: build on existing execution/query/wait capabilities and split implementation into reviewable changes.

These are open design questions; this issue does not select a policy.

## Acceptance criteria

- A user starts a representative long-running computation and can distinguish Agent-turn completion from task completion.
- The same supported task remains discoverable and queryable across turns according to the documented lifecycle.
- The Agent can inspect or await that task and retrieve its final result without launching a duplicate.
- Completion, failure, and cancellation have defined, verifiable user-visible outcomes.
- The chosen turn-completion and restart policies are documented and covered by matching end-to-end scenarios.

## Related work

- #434: original report and evidence; superseded by this feature proposal.
- #439: redirected output buffering. Log buffering is a separate concern; coordinate where progress reporting intersects.

issue:647.body:
## Reproduction

On a clean checkout of `main` @ `69f40c9f` where workspace packages have not been built:

```bash
cd apps/web
node_modules/.bin/tsx --test tests/*.test.ts tests/*.test.tsx
```

Result on this machine: **448 tests, 385 pass, 63 fail**, and every failure is the same module resolution error from the `.tsx` files:

```
Error [ERR_MODULE_NOT_FOUND]: Cannot find module
'.../apps/web/node_modules/@sciencediscovery/operational-logging/dist/diagnostics.js'
imported from .../apps/web/src/ErrorDiagnosticActions.tsx
```

Single-test repro: `node_modules/.bin/tsx --test tests/AuthTokenPrompt.test.tsx` → exit 1, same error.

It goes away only after `packages/operational-logging` is built (`tsc -p packages/operational-logging/tsconfig.json`), i.e. the web suite silently depends on a build step that its own `test` script does not perform.

## Current behaviour vs expected

`packages/operational-logging/package.json` maps the runtime entry to a build artifact:

```json
"exports": {
  ".":             { "types": "./src/index.ts",       "default": "./dist/index.js" },
  "./diagnostics": { "types": "./src/diagnostics.ts", "default": "./dist/diagnostics.js" }
}
```

Types resolve to `src/`, but the runtime entry resolves to `dist/`, so an unbuilt tree makes `apps/web` (which depends on this package as `workspace:*`, `apps/web/package.json:13`) fail at import time. `apps/web`'s `test` script is plain `tsx --test tests/*.test.ts tests/*.test.tsx` and has no build step; CI passes only because the pipeline builds first.

Expected: `apps/web` tests run on a clean checkout without a manual build of the workspace dependency — either the in-repo runtime entry points at the TS source (tsx/vite compile it) or the test script builds what it needs.

## Code evidence

- `packages/operational-logging/package.json` — `exports["./diagnostics"].default` = `./dist/diagnostics.js` while `types` = `./src/diagnostics.ts`; no `dist/` in the repository.
- `apps/web/package.json:13` — `"@sciencediscovery/operational-logging": "workspace:*"`.
- `apps/web/package.json` scripts — `"test": "tsx --test tests/*.test.ts tests/*.test.tsx"` (no build).
- Failure site: `apps/web/src/ErrorDiagnosticActions.tsx` imports `@sciencediscovery/operational-logging/diagnostics`.

## Suggested red test / acceptance

No new unit test is needed — the red state is the suite itself:

```bash
rm -rf packages/operational-logging/dist
cd apps/web && node_modules/.bin/tsx --test tests/*.test.ts     # ts files pass today
cd apps/web && node_modules/.bin/tsx --test tests/*.test.tsx    # 63 ERR_MODULE_NOT_FOUND today
```

Acceptance: with `dist/` absent, `tsx --test tests/*.test.tsx` reports **0 `ERR_MODULE_NOT_FOUND`** and the same pass count as with a built tree (448/448 on the tree where this was measured).

## Duplicate check (open + closed)

- `"operational-logging"` → no issue about its `exports` map or the missing build step.
- `ERR_MODULE_NOT_FOUND` → 0 hits in issues.
- `apps/web test` / web suite build → no open issue; `#467` is a UI fix, `#632` a feature.
- No open PR changes `packages/operational-logging/package.json` or the `apps/web` test script.

Found and measured by ScienceDiscovery while prewarming the web worktree for the `#646` sprint (448 tests, 63 `ERR_MODULE_NOT_FOUND` failures, worktree unmodified).

issue:668.body:
## Goal

Track the remaining external-agent interoperability work after PR #424 merged the initial Specialist runtime slice. This issue deliberately keeps two protocol directions separate while coordinating their shared safety, session and artifact requirements.

## Delivered baseline

PR #424 merged support for explicit Specialist tasks using Codex, Claude Code and ACP executables, normalized task/event/handoff behavior, independent concurrent Workspace/Runner execution, configuration cards and thin runtime diagnostics. It does **not** complete either original Issue’s full acceptance criteria.

## Workstream A — ScienceDiscovery hosts external Specialist runtimes (remaining from #385)

Keep the existing Specialist model and require explicit `task(specialistId=…)` targeting for non-native execution. The platform remains the authority for Workspace, permissions, secrets, artifacts, audit and cancellation.

- [ ] Validate and document a successful live-auth matrix for supported Codex, Claude Code and ACP providers, including task completion, cancellation, timeout and declared-artifact handoff. Report unavailable credentials/providers as blocked, never passed.
- [ ] Decide and implement the supported iCode adapter path, or explicitly defer it with product rationale.
- [ ] Complete the Skills/MCP/tool bridge so an external runtime can request platform-governed tools without gaining undeclared native permissions.
- [ ] Finish the product configuration surface aligned with #278: persisted/this-run/alternate credential choices, usable error recovery and no secret leakage to catalog bodies, argv, logs or artifacts.
- [ ] Add the deferred UX: runtime picker/probe, fallback controls and handoff/diagnostics visibility.
- [ ] Add the deferred reliability coverage: multi-SDK stress, escape/isolation regressions, protocol backpressure/error bounds and process-crash recovery semantics.
- [ ] Evaluate deferred orchestration/operations separately: quota/priority/dependency graphs, shared pools only with an isolation design, and fuller metrics/cluster/multi-tenant monitoring.

## Workstream B — ScienceDiscovery is an ACP v1 Agent for editors (remaining from #64)

Editors are ACP Clients; ScienceDiscovery is the spawned ACP Agent. This is not the same as Workstream A, where ScienceDiscovery drives an external agent.

- [ ] Provide a supported ACP v1 stdio JSON-RPC entry point and `initialize` capability negotiation; do not multiplex it with MCP stdio or require a browser first.
- [ ] Implement session lifecycle mapping: `session/new`, `session/prompt`, streaming `session/update`, `session/cancel`, recoverable Project/Session/Run context and absolute workspace mapping.
- [ ] Map ACP permission requests to the existing governance and sandbox path; the ACP route must not be less restrictive than the Web UI.
- [ ] Return standards-compliant JSON-RPC errors and advertise only implemented capabilities; document any research-specific extensions.
- [ ] Verify against an actual ACP Client (for example Zed or a VS Code ACP extension): launch, prompt, streamed text, at least one tool call and denied permission behavior.
- [ ] Add unit, conformance and isolated E2E coverage for version negotiation, cancellation, authentication if enabled, sandbox equivalence and secret/session-body log redaction.
- [ ] Publish editor configuration documentation. ACP Registry publication is a separate product decision and must not block local interoperability.

## Shared boundaries

- Secrets never enter Specialist catalog bodies, argv, artifacts or unauthenticated ACP traffic.
- Existing sandbox, artifact provenance and permission controls remain authoritative.
- ACP v2 remains non-default until it is stable and separately accepted.

Supersedes the remaining scope of #385 and #64. PR #424 is delivered baseline, not proof that the above acceptance is complete.

issue:669.body:
## Goal

Make literature reports and review outcomes honestly verifiable: readers should see the evidence supporting material claims, know when evidence could not be verified, and never mistake a partial Quick review for full claim-fidelity verification.

## Workstream A — claim-to-evidence excerpts (from #415)

- [ ] For each material quantitative or clinical claim in a literature report, retain a short source excerpt or structured claim-to-evidence table with stable identifier and usable locator (for example PMID/DOI plus abstract/full-text location where available).
- [ ] Include the evidence in saved report/review artifacts without flooding model context; preserve source provenance and retrieval metadata.
- [ ] When an excerpt cannot be obtained, record an explicit evidence gap rather than silently presenting the claim as fully supported.

## Workstream B — visible unverifiable states (from #560)

- [ ] Extend the evidence/review schema with a visible `UNVERIFIABLE` status (or equivalent reasoned states such as identity unresolved and provider unavailable).
- [ ] Preserve the reason, affected claim/citation and review coverage in reports and review summaries. Do not silently discard identity-resolution or provider-availability findings.
- [ ] Keep the existing policy distinction: provider failure is not proof that a citation is false; it is an explicit limitation on verification.
- [ ] Align reviewer Skill instructions and runtime normalization so emitted states are representable and auditable.

## Workstream C — truthful automatic-review scope (follow-up to closed #414)

- [ ] A format/provenance-only Quick review must present itself as partial/format-only and disclose skipped claim checks with a reason.
- [ ] A claim-checked literature review must identify which claims were checked, supported, unsupported or unverifiable.
- [ ] Add regressions for stale report reviews, missing primary deliverables and the prior false-looking `ACCEPT_AND_PROCEED` Quick outcome.

## Validation

- [ ] Reproduce the CRISPR base-editing literature-report scenario from #415 and verify human-readable claim evidence or explicit gaps.
- [ ] Cover identifier mismatch, unresolved identity, unavailable provider, conflicting evidence, missing locator and provider timeout paths.
- [ ] Test Quick/Deep UI and saved artifact semantics independently; mocked provider success alone is insufficient.
- [ ] Document the distinction among supported, unsupported, unverifiable and not-reviewed claims.

Consolidates the unfinished scope of #415 and #560 and retains the relevant transparency regression from closed #414.
