issue:909.body:
## Summary

`ST` fails on a clean `main` because the pinned Python runtime is fetched from `astral-sh/python-build-standalone` and that download either answers `504` or streams at 9–31 KB/s, far past the 5-minute `execFile` cap in the test. It fails before any code under test runs, so it is not attributable to the PR whose run turns red — but it does turn `merge-gate` red, which is the one required check in this repository, so it blocks merges.

Current instance: `#678` (tip `5ad9b21b6aeb5d7f30556de8ddafc07d1246d85e`) is approved and otherwise green except `ST`.

## Where

- Test: `test/api/evolve-distribution.test.ts::a user initializes the pinned release into an empty installation and completes a real Evolve task@linux/amd64`
- Downloader: `scripts/binary-release/fetch-runtime.mjs`
- Asset: `https://github.com/astral-sh/python-build-standalone/releases/download/20260805/cpython-3.12.13+20260805-x86_64-unknown-linux-gnu-install_only_stripped.tar.gz` — `34,184,519` bytes

## CI evidence

Run [`41999191976`](https://github.com/openJiuwen-ai/sciencediscovery/actions/runs/41999191976), job `ST` `127150383484` (`2026-11-05T09:04:19Z` → `09:09:17Z`): `{"status":"FAIL","planned":51,"executed":51,"passed":50,"failed":1}`, the only red identity is the test above, first line:

```
Download failed (504): https://github.com/astral-sh/python-build-standalone/releases/download/20260805/cpython-3.12.13+20260805-x86_64-unknown-linux-gnu-install_only_stripped.tar.gz
```

## Control: the same case on a clean `main`

`main` at `7057aaf65f2c81d0b0af64a449d9259c62128673`, tracked tree clean, dependencies installed and built the same way, no branch of `#678` present:

- `node scripts/binary-release/fetch-runtime.mjs --runtime python --arch x86_64 --output … --cache …` → **exit 124** (killed at a 300 s cap; it had written 0 bytes to disk, because the script reads the whole archive into memory before writing).
- `node --import tsx --test --test-name-pattern "pinned release" test/api/evolve-distribution.test.ts` → **exit 1** after **301 s** (`duration_ms: 300128`), i.e. it hit the same `execFile` 5-minute cap with the same command and the same URL.

So the same case fails on `main` without the change under review.

## Observed throughput for that asset

| Reading | Result |
| --- | --- |
| `curl -sI` (same URL) | `HTTP/2 302` |
| `curl -sL -r 0-1048575` (1 MiB range) | `206`, `1,048,576` bytes in `33.48 s` → `31,322 B/s` |
| `curl -L` (full, 45 s cap) | `200`, `818,498` of `34,184,519` bytes in `45 s` → `18,185 B/s` |
| bare `node fetch` | `status 200` in `1.1 s`, then 0 bytes for 60 s before abort |
| independent samples of the same URL, three machines | `9,445` / `25,735` / `18,312` B/s |

At `9–31 KB/s` the `34 MB` asset needs roughly **18 to 60 minutes**, while the test allows 5.

## It is not deterministic

Fifteen minutes before the red run, the same case passed in merge-group run [`41997396390`](https://github.com/openJiuwen-ai/sciencediscovery/actions/runs/41997396390) (`2026-11-05T08:52:58Z` → `08:53:41Z`, `42.6 s`). `main`'s own `ST` was green in run [`41997392457`](https://github.com/openJiuwen-ai/sciencediscovery/actions/runs/41997392457) (`08:52Z`). So the failure tracks the download path degrading, not a fixed defect in the test.

## Why this is worth a fix rather than a retry

`merge-gate` is the only required status check here, and `ST` is one of the jobs it aggregates, so any PR can be blocked for a reason that has nothing to do with its diff, and a re-run only helps if the CDN happens to recover. Retries also cost a full `ST` cycle (≈5 minutes each time) and cannot be triggered by contributors: `POST /actions/jobs/{id}/rerun` and `POST /actions/runs/{id}/rerun-failed-jobs` both answer `403 Must have admin rights to Repository` for a non-member token.

## Options, in the order we would pick them

1. **Cache the pinned runtime between runs** (keyed by the asset version), so the network is used once per version instead of on every `ST` run.
2. **Verify against a mirror first** and fall back to the GitHub release, or honour `fetch-runtime.mjs`'s resume/cache path when a partial download exists instead of restarting from byte 0.
3. **Fail fast and name the cause**: if the download cannot reach a minimum rate within N seconds, fail with a message that says "external asset download too slow", so the red check is self-explanatory.
4. If none of the above is wanted now, an explicit **retry/exemption policy for `ST` on this identity** would at least stop it blocking unrelated PRs.

If the project prefers that this be reported differently, say so and we will follow that shape instead.

issue:910.body:
## Summary

`packages/data-source/src/source-health.test.ts` gives its fault injection a wall-clock budget of about `200 ms` (`200` iterations at `1 ms`). On a busy runner that budget is exhausted before the injected fault lands, the case fails with `Timed out waiting for local fault injection`, and because `UT` is one of the jobs `merge-gate` aggregates, an unrelated pull request turns red on the only required status check in this repository.

Two pull requests were hit by the same identity in two different time windows today, and the same file passes in a normal run.

## Failing identity

```text
packages/data-source/src/source-health.test.ts::parallel 429 callers share cooldown, drain their queue and do not retry inside one slot@linux/amd64
message: "Timed out waiting for local fault injection"
```

## Evidence

**Hit 1 — `#872`**, `UT` job `126735548839`, run [`41875320473`](https://github.com/openJiuwen-ai/sciencediscovery/actions/runs/41875320473), read from the job's uploaded `ut-results` artifact (`group-227/worker-1-events.jsonl`; the job log itself only carries `Run`/`Done` lines). Group summary `planned 16 / executed 16 / passed 15 / failed 1`; whole layer `planned 6279 / executed 6279 / passed 6278 / failed 1`.

**Hit 2 — `#878`**, `UT` job `126741018427`, same identity, another window.

**Control — the same file passing**, `UT` job `126822084143` (`2026-11-04T19:54:21Z`): `Run 229/555: packages/data-source/src/source-health.test.ts (16)` → `Done (6210ms)`, layer `{"status":"PASS","planned":6281,"passed":6281,"failed":0}`.

Neither pull request touches `packages/data-source`: `#872` changes four files under `apps/web`, `#878` changes `apps/web` only. So the failing identity is unreachable from either diff.

## Cause

`packages/data-source/src/source-health.test.ts:98-101` polls for the first of 12 concurrent callers to observe the injected fault:

```ts
// ~200 iterations × 1 ms ≈ 200 ms total
```

When the event loop is loaded (parallel `UT` workers, coverage instrumentation), `200 ms` is not enough for the fault to be observed, and the wait falls through to `assert.fail("Timed out waiting for local fault injection")`. The product behaviour is correct; the budget is what fails.

## Effect

Any pull request can be blocked by this, and a re-run only helps if the runner happens to be less loaded. Contributors cannot re-run: `POST /actions/jobs/{id}/rerun` and `POST /actions/runs/{id}/rerun-failed-jobs` answer `403 Must have admin rights to Repository` to a non-member token. So the only currently available recovery is asking a maintainer.

## Options

1. **Replace the fixed budget with a deadline** (for example `waitFor` with a `10 s` timeout and a short poll interval), so a loaded runner still passes and a genuinely missing fault still fails quickly enough.
2. **Wait on the event rather than polling** — if the injection can expose a promise or an emitter, awaiting it removes the timing assumption entirely.
3. If the current budget is deliberate, document the expected runner load and treat the red as a known flake; then it should not be able to block `merge-gate` for unrelated changes.

We can prepare option 1 as a pull request if that is the preferred shape; tell us which option you want and we will follow that instead of choosing for you.

issue:916.body:
## 问题背景

Windows 直接执行模式提供托管 Bash，但既有的 starter 环境可能没有安装 Agent 调用 `run_shell` 时依赖的常用 Unix 工具（如 `head`、`tail`、`wc`、`sort`、`grep`、`sed`）。同一条命令在不同 Windows 设备或历史安装环境中表现不一致；缺少明确的能力探测和诊断时，Agent 可能反复重试不可用的命令。

此外，Windows 的 `.cmd` / `.bat` 启动入口不能完全按原生可执行文件的方式处理，带空格和特殊字符的参数也需要正确传递。

## 预期行为

- 托管 Windows Bash 明确提供并能解析约定的基础 Unix 工具，不依赖用户机器碰巧安装了 Git Bash。
- 首次创建及历史 starter 环境升级后，工具集合保持一致；升级保留审计记录，重复启动不会无意义地迁移。
- Runner readiness 能暴露实际平台与 Shell 能力，Agent 的工具说明不再假设主机有某个命令。
- 对 Bash 标准的 command-not-found 失败给出准确、有限长度、可操作的诊断；保留原始 stderr，不将所有 exit 127 错误误判为命令缺失。
- 正确启动 Windows `.cmd` / `.bat` shim，且参数中的空格和特殊字符不被意外解释或丢失。

## 建议修复范围

1. 在 Windows 托管 starter 环境中提供 MSYS2 Bash 与必要的 coreutils / grep / sed，配置正确的工具查找路径。
2. 增加托管 Shell 的能力探测及 setup 后的状态刷新。
3. 为持久化 starter 增加按缺失项增量升级和幂等处理。
4. 完善 `run_shell` / `check_runner` 工具说明及缺失命令诊断。
5. 针对 Windows 脚本 shim 的启动与参数传递提供兼容路径。

## 验收标准

- [ ] 新安装 Windows 环境可通过真实 `run_shell` 调用使用约定的基础工具
- [ ] 历史环境可升级且保留原修订，重复启动不产生多余修订
- [ ] Runner 能力探测和 Agent 工具说明反映实际可用能力
- [ ] 缺失命令有准确、可恢复的提示，不破坏 stderr 和其他错误语义
- [ ] `.cmd` / `.bat` 启动及含空格、元字符的参数传递通过测试
- [ ] 相关 Runner / workspace 测试及 Windows 端到端流程验证

## 实现 PR

- #716 — `fix(runner): provide a managed Windows shell toolchain`

关联版本计划：#718（Windows Shell 工具链与能力诊断）。
## #716 验收范围澄清（2026-11-07）

本 Issue 的关闭范围是 **Windows `none` 直接执行模式**的托管 Shell 工具链、starter 增量升级、能力诊断与 Windows `.cmd` / `.bat` shim 兼容。`Runner.ready` 不应因独立 Shell 不可用而阻断 Python；对于 Shell 不可用，API 派发前应明确返回 `dispatched: false`，托管提交后的拒绝应有确定的 `not_started`/失败状态，不能错误产生 `unknown` 而持续阻塞工作区。这些是 #716 自身行为正确性要求，不属于可被范围调整豁免的回归。

Shell 能力报告以 starter 环境为基础，并不保证所有旧的、自定义或克隆的目标环境都具有相同工具集合；目标环境执行时仍需给出正确的失败结果。跨全部环境版本的工具链一致性与通用执行准入协议重设计不纳入本 Issue。原有 Windows 实机流程为提交者报告的验证，不能等同于独立的全平台测试；GitHub Actions `merge-gate` 仍须实际执行，不因本澄清而豁免。

issue:917.body:
## 问题背景

Agent 工具调用结果直接进入模型上下文时，Shell 执行、环境、文件传输、Skill、MCP 等工具可能返回冗长原始数据、敏感字段或与当前推理无关的内容，导致上下文浪费并增加信息泄露风险。

仅对返回内容做简单截断也不够：MCP 的 `structuredData`、`crossReferences` 等结构化业务数据可能被意外遗漏；真正发生截断后，如果没有可读取的引用，Agent 就无法恢复所需证据，影响后续分析。

## 预期行为

- 模型看到的是有边界、与任务相关的结果摘要，而不是无约束的原始工具输出。
- 敏感凭据、下载源 URL 等不必要信息不进入模型视图或长期保存的审计元数据；合法的下载候选 ID、许可证、归属信息及文件大小等业务字段仍被保留。
- MCP 输出保留 `structuredData`、`crossReferences` 和分析摘要中的有效业务数据，并在限制大小时优先维持可解释性。
- 真实业务数据因截断丢失时，若持久化成功，应返回可通过 `read_tool_output` 获取完整证据的引用；若不可恢复，要明确告知，不能静默假装完整。
- 小结果无需不必要的持久化；深层嵌套、循环引用及存储失败等边界情况应可控。
- arXiv 工具结果提供可用的分页和论文获取路径。

## 建议修复范围

1. 针对 Shell、执行管理、环境、NPU、传输与 Skill 工具定义适用的模型可见结果字段。
2. 对审计元数据中的敏感数据与原始大载荷做防御性清理，并限制递归深度。
3. 为 MCP 结果构造大小受限的投影，覆盖 JSON 文本、结构化记录、交叉引用与分析摘要。
4. 对发生信息损失的结果建立可恢复的 `read_tool_output` 引用与明确的失败回退提示。
5. 在下载、文献检索及 PDF 读取等真实链路中核对关键字段和结果语义。

## 验收标准

- [ ] 工具输出遵守模型上下文大小约束，不包含不必要的敏感字段
- [ ] MCP 结构化结果及交叉引用不被静默丢弃
- [ ] 截断导致业务信息损失时有可读取引用，或明确标识恢复不可用
- [ ] 小结果不产生不必要的证据持久化
- [ ] 深层嵌套、循环引用、存储失败等场景可预测且不泄露原始载荷
- [ ] 下载候选、许可证/来源信息、arXiv 分页及论文获取链路不回归
- [ ] 覆盖相关单元测试与端到端执行 / MCP 场景

## 实现 PR

- #717 — `fix(tools): bound model-facing execution and MCP results`

关联版本计划：#718（工具输出与结果投影优化）。
## #717 验收范围澄清（2026-11-07）

本 Issue 验收 **第一阶段的有界模型视图与证据恢复契约**：现有 Shell/执行管理等工具的必要字段投影、MCP 结构化业务数据可见、实际投影损失的显式标记与可用的 `read_tool_output` 恢复、安全边界、文献工具分页和指定论文查询。对文献搜索，应优先削减重复的 provider `structuredData`，再缩短模型需要阅读的摘要；对于结构化查询，应保护其业务 payload。#717 中相应的 F6 顺序问题仍按此标准验收，不能通过范围变更予以忽略。

不要求 #717 提供适用于所有 MCP Server 和未来工具的通用语义投影框架、自动识别跨字段重复、全局 token 最优预算分配或基于任务完成率的系统评测。这些属于后续独立架构设计和增量迁移工作。原始安全/恢复/边界测试不可因此放松；缺失的 CI、版权或第三方服务实测证据也不因本澄清视为通过。

issue:918.body:
## What

`services/gateway/tests/test_architecture_boundaries.py:156` (`GeneratedWorkspaceBoundaryTests`, added by #915) pins only one direction of the walk: both new cases assert that something is **not** reported. Nothing asserts that a violation still **is** reported after the ignore list changed.

## Trigger

`IGNORED_DIRECTORIES` is widened again, or `_files()` is narrowed, so that a real source root (`services/api`, `packages`, `apps/web`, `test/api`) stops being walked. Every current case still passes:

- `test_a_generated_workspace_is_not_walked` and `test_a_workspace_file_removed_after_listing_is_skipped` assert absence only;
- `test_node_and_browser_sources_use_only_product_names` asserts `failures == []`, which a walk that sees nothing also satisfies.

The boundary test then silently stops policing the Gateway boundary with no red test anywhere.

## Fix

Add the mirror case in `GeneratedWorkspaceBoundaryTests`, reusing the `mock.patch.object(sys.modules[__name__], "_files", ...)` plumbing already present at `:162`:

- have the patched walk yield a path under `services/api/src` (for example `services/api/src/probe-boundary-<pid>.ts`) whose content contains a vendor token;
- assert `_node_boundary_failures()` returns that path, as `path: <relative>` or `content: <relative>`.

Three lines in the test file. No production code changes.

## Why it is worth a line

Measured at `f99cc8a24495544988045699b9e5c2429553e332` (review comment on #915): a fabricated `services/api/src/probe-zz-deerflow-boundary.ts` does produce `['path: services/api/src/probe-zz-deerflow-boundary.ts']`, and with the pre-change ignore set a probe in `services/api/.tmp` produces `['content: services/api/.tmp/probe-manual-537457.ts']`. The guard works today; only its regression direction is untested.

Found while reviewing #915 and tracked here so the review thread can be closed without losing the gap.

Written-by: ScienceDiscovery Product Claimed-by: ScienceDiscovery Product Claim-Id: 8c2885cfabeb4ba4ba2f1b4c6db60f65 Branch: dev/925-bug-activity-panel-prints-raw-english-st Base: 2908e9e8bb4f At: 2026-11-05T13:37:29Z ## What happens The Session activity panel (`Executions & reminders`) is fully translated except for the two values it takes from server data, which are printed as the raw API token even when the UI language is Chinese: - the status badge on every execution, transfer and reminder record renders `item.state` verbatim, so a running execution shows `running`; - the execution meta line renders `provenance` verbatim, so it reads `工作区 ws_a · 溯源 pending`, and the record's accessible label (fold summary, focus label) reads `local · main · running`. Chinese is the product default, so this is what a default-locale user sees. ## What is expected The badge keeps the state as its CSS class (styling must not change) but names the state in the UI language: `排队中`, `运行中`, `已完成`, `失败`, `已取消`, `未知`. The provenance reads `待提交` / `已提交`. Under English the labels stay the words the rest of the UI already uses: `Queued`, `Running`, `Completed`, `Failed`, `Cancelled`, `Unknown`, and `Pending` / `Committed`. ## Where it comes from - `apps/web/src/AgentActivityPanel.tsx:97`, `:111`, `:122` — `{item.state}`; the class must keep `item.state`, only the child text needs a label. - `apps/web/src/AgentActivityPanel.tsx:98` — `t("activity.executionMeta", { provenance: item.provenance, workspace: item.workspaceId })` passes the raw token into the sentence. - `apps/web/src/AgentActivityPanel.tsx:96`, `:110`, `:121` — the `label` prop of `ProcessRecord` interpolates `item.state`. - `apps/web/src/i18n/messages.ts` carries 25 `activity.*` keys in both catalogues (en `2738-2759`, zh `5757-5778`) but none for these values, which is why this is the one activity surface that still shows English. Value domains, for whoever writes the keys: `packages/schema/src/execution.ts:45` (`queued|running|completed|failed|cancelled|unknown`), `apps/web/src/api/runs.ts:40` (timers: `pending|fired|cancelled`), `packages/schema/src/execution.ts:101` (provenance: `pending|committed|unconfirmed`). The other surfaces already do exactly this, so the pattern is in-tree: `apps/web/src/WakeNotice.tsx:72` maps wake states through `chat.wakeNoticeState.*`, `apps/web/src/GovernedDownloadCards.tsx:50` does the same for download states. ## Failing test (reproduce before the fix) Render the panel under the Chinese locale with one running execution and assert the tree does not carry the English token. The probe below is a temporary file — it is not part of the branch, it exists to prove the failure: ```tsx // apps/web/tests/zz-activity-badge-probe.test.tsx (temporary, not committed) const activity = { executions: [{ id: "job", agentId: "main", runnerId: "local", workspaceId: "ws_a", state: "running", provenance: "pending" }], transfers: [], timers: [], agents: [], }; const client = { getAgentActivity: async () => activity } as unknown as ApiClient; let view: ReactTestRenderer; await act(async () => { view = create(createElement(LocaleProvider, { initialLocale: "zh-CN" }, createElement(AgentActivityPanel, { client, sessionId: "session" }))); }); const tree = JSON.stringify(view!.toJSON()); assert.match(tree, /执行/); assert.doesNotMatch(tree, /running/); ``` Command and observed output: ``` $ cd apps/web && node --import tsx --test tests/zz-activity-badge-probe.test.tsx not ok 1 - zh-CN badge names the state in Chinese error: |- The input was expected to not match the regular expression /running/. rendered fragment: {"type":"span","props":{"className":"activity-badge running"},"children":["running"]} # tests 1 # pass 0 # fail 1 ``` The same render shows the second half of this issue: `"工作区 ws_a · 溯源 pending"` — `provenance` is untranslated in the sentence produced by `activity.executionMeta`, and the process record's label is `local · main · running`. ## Environment - `main` @ `7057aaf65f2c81d0b0af64a449d9259c62128673` - node `v22`; from `apps/web`: `node --import tsx --test tests/` - default locale zh-CN; the probe forces it with `LocaleProvider initialLocale="zh-CN"`, and the panel's own chrome in the same render is Chinese (`执行与提醒`, `查看日志`, `取消执行`), so the locale is applied and the English tokens are not a locale-detection artifact. ## Smallest mergeable slice Two files, about 30 lines, no logic change: 1. `apps/web/src/i18n/messages.ts` — add `activity.state.{queued,running,completed,failed,cancelled,unknown}` and `activity.provenance.{pending,committed}`, one entry per key in the en block beside `activity.resumeAgentScope` and one in the zh block beside its counterpart. 2. `apps/web/src/AgentActivityPanel.tsx` — a `stateLabel(state)` / `provenanceLabel(provenance)` helper that calls `t()` and falls back to the raw value for any value the catalogues do not carry (a newer API can add a state), used in the three badge children, the `executionMeta` call and the three `label` props. Boundaries: the `activity-badge ${item.state}` class, the `live`/`cancellable` predicates and the `progress.length` accounting stay exactly as they are; no assertion migration in existing tests; no change to any other badge or badge format in the app. ## Coverage note `#876` (merged today, `dev2/fix/874-activity-unknown-terminal`) is the only recent change to this file and it touched neither the badge text nor the `executionMeta` call — it moved `unknown` out of `live()` and switched `filesCommitted` to `progress.length`. There is no open pull request against `AgentActivityPanel.tsx`. ## Acceptance - The probe passes: under zh-CN the badge text is `运行中` while `className` is still `activity-badge running`, and the execution meta line no longer contains `pending`. - Under `initialLocale="en"` the visible text is unchanged from `main` apart from the badge/provenance wording, so `apps/web/tests/AgentActivityPanel.test.tsx` keeps passing. - A state or provenance value the catalogues do not know renders its raw token rather than an empty string or a missing-key placeholder. - Scope stays at the eight keys above; a transfer's `partial`, a reminder's `fired` and provenance `unconfirmed` are deliberately out of scope and keep rendering their raw token.

Branch: dev/930-bug-a-length-rejection-answers-500-inter
Base: 2908e9e8bb4f
At: 2026-11-05T13:49:58Z

## What happens

A provider form accepts a pasted API token of any length, and the API answers an over-long one with a bare internal error instead of naming the field:

```
POST /api/providers/preview-models
{"name":"Probe provider","baseUrl":"https://example.test/v1","apiProtocol":"openai-chat-completions","apiToken":"<20 000 chars>"}

HTTP 500 {"error":"Internal server error"}
```

The very same validator rejects the empty-token case correctly, so one form gets two different failure shapes for two client mistakes:

```
POST … {"apiToken":""}      → 400  "The LLM API token cannot be empty"
POST … {"apiToken":"k"×20000} → 500  "Internal server error"
```

The `500` also reaches the user as the generic error surface, so the form cannot say which field to shorten.

## What is expected

`400` with the validation message the store already produced: `{"error":"The LLM API token is too long"}`. The same holds for the other length limits below — they are client input mistakes and must answer 400, not 500.

## Where it comes from

- The classification: `services/api/src/http/error-classification.ts:20-32` lists the legacy messages that stay 400 (`is required`, `must`, `cannot`, `does not match`, `invalid`, …) and has no pattern for a length rejection, so `services/api/src/http/index.ts:3944` falls through to the 500 branch at `:3946`.

| site | message |
| --- | --- |
| `services/api/src/store/secrets.ts:198` | `The LLM API token is too long` |
| `services/api/src/store/settings.ts:420` | `The proxy URL is too long` |
| `services/api/src/store/settings.ts:348` | `neo4jHttp is too long` |
| `services/api/src/store/settings.ts:351` | `neo4jUser is too long` |
| `services/api/src/store.ts:3012` | `The Neo4j password is too long` |
| `services/api/src/store.ts:3858` | `Model ID is too long` |
| `services/api/src/store.ts:5533` | `The stored ${kind} is too long` (remote-host credential) |

`grep -rn "too long" services/api/src --include=*.ts | grep -v .test.` finds nothing else that throws: the remaining hits are prompt text (`session-naming.ts:26`, `:198`), comments, and `configuration/schema-normalizer.ts:86/104` which goes through `invalid()` and is already classified.

not ok 1 - probe: an over-long provider API token is a client error, not a 500

The Specialist settings surface turns ordinary client mistakes into a bare internal error. Saving a Specialist whose name is already taken, editing or deleting a Specialist that no longer exists, and editing a built-in Specialist all answer `500`:

```
POST /api/specialists {"name":"duplicate-name subject","description":"d","instructions":"i","connectorIds":[],"enabledSkillIds":[]}
  first call   → 201 {"name":"duplicate-name subject","id":"9c1f45d8-…"}
  second call  → 500 {"error":"Internal server error"}

PUT    /api/specialists/nope                    → 500 {"error":"Internal server error"}
DELETE /api/specialists/nope                    → 500 {"error":"Internal server error"}
PUT    /api/specialists/assessment-screener {"name":"assessment-screener renamed"}
                                                → 500 {"error":"Internal server error"}   (built-in, read-only)
```

The same settings area already answers these shapes correctly on the neighbouring MCP-servers surface:

```
POST /api/mcp/servers {"name":"dup mcp","transport":"stdio","command":"echo","args":[]}
  first call   → 201
  second call  → 400 {"error":"A server with this name already exists"}
DELETE /api/mcp/servers/custom-000000000000     → 404 {"error":"MCP server not found"}
```

Other resource routes answer `404` for an unknown id as well (`GET/PUT/DELETE /api/models/nope`, `/api/providers/nope`, `/api/proxy/servers/nope`, `/api/projects/nope`, `/api/permission-grants/nope`), so the Specialist routes are the outlier, not the norm.

The user sees the generic text: `apps/web/src/Orchestration.tsx:262` (create/update) and `:275` (delete) hand the API message to `onError`, and `apps/web/src/api/auth.ts:26-36` (`ApiRequestError`) carries the server's `error` body verbatim — so the Specialist pane prints "Internal server error" where the store already knows the reason.

## What is expected

- a taken name → `400 {"error":"Specialist name already exists"}` (the message the store already produces);
- an unknown id on `PUT`/`DELETE` → `404 {"error":"Specialist not found"}`;
- an edit of a built-in Specialist → `400 {"error":"Built-in specialists are read-only; only their enabled flag can be toggled"}`.

## Where it comes from

- The routes: `services/api/src/http/index.ts:1827-1843` — `POST /api/specialists`, `PUT|DELETE /api/specialists/:id` call the store with no error mapping at all.
- The throws they forward: `services/api/src/store.ts:4347` and `:4378` (`Specialist name already exists`), `:4358` and `:4387` (`Specialist not found`), `:4364` (`Built-in specialists are read-only; only their enabled flag can be toggled`).

issue:937.body:
## Problem

The in-flight length-rejection fix (`#932`) adds `/\bis too long\b/i` to `isKnownClientInputError` (`services/api/src/http/error-classification.ts:30`). Any message containing that phrase is then answered `400` **and the message text is sent back to the client**.

Two messages in the tree match that pattern and embed a filesystem path, while the client does not need that path to understand the rejection:

- `packages/executor/src/runner-bundle.ts:76` and `:80` — `` `Runner bundle path is too long for tar: ${file.path}` ``
- `packages/executor/src/remote-compute.ts:777` — `` `The remote data directory path is too long for a Unix socket: ${prepared.dataDir}` ``

Before `#932` both answered `500 {"error":"Internal server error"}` and the text stayed hidden. After it they answer `400` with the path in the body.

## Severity

Low, not a gate: the caller is already authenticated, the path has to be pathological (long enough to trip the length check), and it cannot be produced on demand. Reported by Security while reviewing `#932` at `8b4c124caf`.

## Suggested fix

Anchor the pattern to the end of the message:

```diff
-/\bis too long\b/i
+/\bis too long$/i
```

Every message the fix intends to reclassify ends with the phrase, so the anchor keeps them all and drops the executor ones. The eight legitimate ones are:

- `The LLM API token is too long`
- `The proxy URL is too long`
- `neo4jHttp is too long`
- `neo4jUser is too long`
- `The Neo4j password is too long`
- `Model ID is too long`
- `The stored runnerToken is too long`
- `pip indexUrl is too long` (`packages/schema/src/environment.ts:393`; added after Security's review of the first draft of this issue, which listed only seven)

## Acceptance

1. A unit test pins that the two executor messages above are **not** client input (a negative assertion): they must not become `400`-with-text.
2. All eight length messages listed above still answer `400` with their text. Pin them by name rather than by count, so a future narrowing of the pattern cannot silently drop one.
3. No change to the `500` path for anything else.

## Not for the current sprint window

`#932` must not be re-tipped for this: pushing a new tip dismisses the approval already recorded on it. This issue is the follow-up and is intentionally parked until after the window.

issue:938.body:
## Problem

`POST /api/settings/web` answers a generic `500 {"error":"Internal server error"}` for six shapes that are plainly the client's mistake. `normalizeWebSettings` (`services/api/src/store/settings.ts`) throws a bare `Error` for each of them, so the chain in `services/api/src/http/index.ts:3930-3936` falls through to the catch-all instead of the 400 it gives other validation failures.

| Input | Throw site | Message |
|---|---|---|
| `{"deepseekEnabled": "yes"}` | `store/settings.ts:374` | `deepseekEnabled must be a boolean` |
| `{"paidSearchProviders": ["bogus"]}` | `:384` | `paidSearchProviders must list supported paid search providers` |
| `{"freeSearchEngines": {"brave": "yes"}}` | `:396` | `freeSearchEngines.<engine> must be a boolean` |
| `{"searchCacheTtlSeconds": 1e9}` | `:403` | `<field> must be an integer between 0 and …` |
| `{"freeSearchEngines": {"nope": true}}` | `:392` | `Unknown free search engine: nope` |
| non-object body (`[]`, `"x"`, `null`) | `:370` | `Web settings must be an object` |

Impact: a client that retries on 5xx retries a request that can never succeed, while the message it needs is already in the response body. This is the same class of defect `#923` fixed for the unknown-key case one line above.

## Origin

Review comment on `#929` (`sciencediscovery-bot`, 2026-11-05T13:55:59Z, `store/settings.ts:374`) — recorded here as a follow-up so `#929` stays scoped to `#923`.

## Suggested fix

Give every throw in `normalizeWebSettings` the same `code: "INVALID_WEB_SETTINGS"` the unknown-key path already carries (message text unchanged), then let the existing route mapping answer 400. A small helper keeps it one line per throw.

## Acceptance

1. For each of the six shapes above: a test that asserts `400`, not `500`, with the message text preserved.
2. Negative assertions: `Catalog database is not initialized` and a genuine internal fault still answer `500`.
3. No change to any message wording; no change outside `normalizeWebSettings` and the route mapping.

issue:939.body:
## Problem

In the Chinese activity panel, a reminder's state still prints as a raw English token, and the same holds for the transfer file-progress rows.

- `AgentActivity.timers[].state` is `"pending" | "fired" | "cancelled"` (`apps/web/src/api/runs.ts:40`)
- `STATE_KEYS` (`apps/web/src/AgentActivityPanel.tsx:34-41`) only covers the execution vocabulary (`queued|running|completed|failed|cancelled|unknown`), and `stateLabel` falls back to the raw token when a key is missing (`:54-57`)
- so a reminder that has not fired renders `pending` inside an otherwise Chinese panel, and after it fires, `fired`; `cancelled` is named because it happens to share the execution vocabulary.

The same gap applies to the transfer file rows, whose per-file progress states are outside the eight keys `#925` enumerated.

## Where it came from

Raised twice on `#929`/`#927` review rounds (`sciencediscovery-bot` at 2026-11-05T13:49:27Z, confirmed still reproducing at `0da863ea` at 15:38:57Z, and `agent-ci-infra-bot` F2 at 15:58:53Z). `#925` deliberately bounded itself to eight keys; this issue is the slice that was left out, not an oversight in that PR.

## Suggested fix

A separate `TIMER_STATE_KEYS` map (so `pending` keeps its execution meaning intact) plus the transfer file-progress keys, both going through `stateLabel`. Values live in the existing `activity.*` section of `apps/web/src/i18n/messages.ts`; the badge `className` keeps the raw token for styling and comparisons.

## Acceptance

1. zh-CN and en both name `pending`, `fired` and the transfer file-progress states; no raw token is visible in either locale.
2. `fired` has its own unit assertion — it is the state a reader sees long after the dialog closed.
3. The badge `className` still carries the raw token (no test may assert localized text through the class).
4. An unknown value outside both maps still renders its raw token (no blanking).

issue:948.body: ## English ### Checklist - [x] I have searched for related issues but did not get the expected help. - [x] This bug has not been fixed in the latest version. ### 🐞 Detailed Description of the Problem The evolution run does not stop when the given goal has already been met. Once a candidate's score reaches `1.0` (goal achieved), the search keeps expanding new nodes until the expansion budget is exhausted. Observed, from the evolution tree in the web UI: - Header: `扩展次数 23/24`, `深度 5`, `Token 608361` - Nodes `#1`, `#15`, `#18` all scored `1.000`, and `#15` is marked as the current best - After `#15` reached `1.000`, the run still produced and expanded `#16`–`#23` (several of them `没跑起来`) - The best-score curve keeps adding points after the line reaches `1.0` - The run terminates at the expansion cap (`23/24`), not because the target was solved ### Expected When any node reaches the goal (score `1.0`, i.e. at or above the solved threshold), the whole evolution tree should stop: - no further expansions are scheduled, neither from the winning branch nor from any other branch - the run ends with a solved / target-reached stop reason instead of the expansion cap - the tree is left as it is at that point ### Steps to Reproduce 1. Start an evolution run whose goal can be fully satisfied (target score `1.0`). 2. Let any candidate reach `1.0`. 3. Watch the evolution tree panel. Actual: new nodes keep being expanded after a `1.0` candidate exists, and the run only ends at the expansion budget. ### Additional Context - The scorecard already carries a `solvedThreshold` (`SOLVED_THRESHOLD_BY_SCORING` in `@sciencediscovery/schema`) and `search_finished` carries a `stopReason`, so the search is expected to end on the solved condition rather than only on the cap. - In this run three nodes reached `1.000`, yet the stop reason was the expansion cap. - I can provide the run event log (`seeded` / `expanded` / `search_finished`) if needed. ### Detailed Environment Information - Web UI, evolution tree view, Chromium on Windows 11 - Repository `main` @ `face1d40` (2026-11-06) - Run settings: expansion budget `24`, depth `5`, token usage `608361` ### Additional Information Screenshot of the evolution tree and the candidate list is attached below. ### Version Information `main` @ `face1d40` (2026-11-06); reproduced on the current web build. --- ## 中文 ### 检查项 - [x] 已搜索相关 issue，未找到有效帮助。 - [x] 该问题在最新版本中仍未修复。 ### 问题详细描述 进化功能在完成给定目标后不会主动停止。当某个候选节点的分数达到 `1.0`（即目标已达成）后，搜索仍会继续扩展新节点，直到扩展次数预算耗尽。 实际表现（来自 Web 端进化树）： - 顶部统计：`扩展次数 23/24`、`深度 5`、`Token 608361` - 节点 `#1`、`#15`、`#18` 均为 `1.000`，`#15` 被标记为当前最优 - `#15` 达到 `1.000` 后，仍继续生成并扩展 `#16`–`#23`（其中多个为“没跑起来”） - 最优分数曲线在达到 `1.0` 之后仍继续产生新点 - 运行以扩展次数上限（`23/24`）结束，而不是因为目标已达成 ### 预期结果 当任一节点达到目标（分数 `1.0`，达到或超过 solved 阈值）时，整棵进化树应全部停止： - 无论最优分支还是其他分支，都不再产生新的扩展 - 运行应以“已解决 / 目标达成”结束，而不是以扩展次数上限结束 - 树保持当时的状态不再变化 ### 复现步骤 1. 启动一个目标可完全满足（目标分数 `1.0`）的进化任务。 2. 等待任一候选节点达到 `1.0`。 3. 观察进化树面板。 实际结果：已存在 `1.0` 节点后仍继续扩展新节点，运行只在扩展预算耗尽时结束。 ### 补充信息 - 评分卡已带 `solvedThreshold`（`@sciencediscovery/schema` 中的 `SOLVED_THRESHOLD_BY_SCORING`），`search_finished` 也带 `stopReason`，说明搜索本应在 solved 条件上结束。 - 本次运行中有三个节点达到 `1.000`，但停止原因仍是扩展上限。 - 如需要，我可以提供运行事件日志（`seeded` / `expanded` / `search_finished`）。 ### 环境信息 - Web 界面，进化树视图，Windows 11 + Chromium - 仓库 `main` @ `face1d40`（2026-11-06） - 运行配置：扩展预算 `24`，深度 `5`，Token `608361` ### 其他补充 进化树与候选流水截图见下方 ### 版本信息 `main` @ `face1d40`（2026-11-06）；在最新 Web 构建上复现。

issue:953.body:
## Description

When running an evolve-design task (RR-03), the agent's model response is truncated at the output token limit (`finish_reason: length`), producing a 4.35MB response that contains no deliverables. The agent generates a very long response (likely the PUCT search Python code) in a single turn, hits the token ceiling, and the run completes with 0 workspace files and 0 artifacts.

## Environment

- Commit: `3061bc3e` (main branch, 2026-11-06)
- Platform: WSL2 (Ubuntu), JiuwenSwarm workswarm0.2.6
- Model: glm-5.3-flash via yibuapi.com

## Reproduction

1. Start the stack normally
2. Submit the `/evolve-design` prompt requesting compress/decompress functions with PUCT search (16 expansions, 4 workers)
3. Wait for completion (~7.5 minutes)

## Actual behavior

The run completes with status `completed` but produces **0 workspace files and 0 artifacts**. The model SSE summary shows:

```
startedAt: 2026-11-06T05:23:34Z
elapsedMs: 286900 (4.8 minutes)
bytes: 4353601 (4.35 MB)
finishReason: "length"  ← truncated at output token limit
hasText: false
hasToolCalls: false
```

The `finish_reason: length` indicates the model ran out of output tokens before finishing its response. The 4.35MB response was too large to be useful — it was truncated mid-generation, so no tool calls were executed and no files were written.

Only 3 model calls were made (turns 0-2) before the run ended.

## Expected behavior

The agent should either:
1. Break the PUCT search code into smaller chunks across multiple turns, or
2. Detect the `finish_reason: length` truncation and retry with a shorter response, or
3. Use the output-recovery mechanism to continue from where the response was truncated.

## Evidence

- Project: `4a69796f-75b6-42de-9ced-cdb4c2430601`, Session: `4aa16d10-7a68-4e93-823d-27fbf9b5a8cb`
- Run: `e507c422` (completed 2026-11-06T05:28:21Z, 7.5 min duration)
- 3 model calls, 3 turns (0-2)
- Last call: 286.9s, 4.35MB, `finish_reason: length`
- 0 workspace files, 0 artifacts
- API log: `[model-sse-summary] {"requestId":"model-...","finishReason":"length","truncated":true,"bytes":4353601,"elapsedMs":286900}`

## Impact

Any task that requires generating large code or documents in a single model response will silently fail when the output hits the token limit. The run reports `completed` but produces no deliverables, which is misleading.

issue:954.body:
## Description

When the workspace contains a large directory (e.g., 470MB of pip-installed packages in `deps/`), the `workspace_snapshot` operation that runs on every agent turn becomes extremely slow — taking 15-60 seconds per snapshot. This severely degrades agent performance, as the snapshot runs on every turn.

## Environment

- Commit: `3061bc3e`
- Platform: WSL2 Ubuntu, bubblewrap sandbox
- Model: glm-5.3-flash via yibuapi.com

## Reproduction

1. Start a run that requires installing Python packages (e.g., RR-02 clinical trial analysis)
2. The agent installs packages to `/workspace/deps/` (470MB, ~3000+ files)
3. Observe workspace_snapshot times in the API log (`[recording-progress]` entries with `stage: workspace_snapshot`)

## Actual behavior

The `snapshotWorkspace` function in `packages/cas/src/versioning.ts:447` recursively traverses **every file** in the workspace, calling `lstat`, `open`, `putWorkspaceFile` (hash + store), and `lstat` again for each file. There is **no exclusion mechanism** for large generated directories like `deps/`, `node_modules/`, `.venv/`, etc.

Performance data from RR-02 r3 (244 snapshot operations):
- **Max: 59,239ms (59 seconds)**
- **Average: 1,790ms**
- **10% of snapshots exceed 10 seconds**
- **24 out of 244 snapshots took 10-60 seconds**

Top 10 slowest snapshots:
```
59239ms at 04:04:54 (after deps install)
21227ms at 04:29:23
20392ms at 04:05:17
17868ms at 04:16:48
17721ms at 04:05:35
17458ms at 04:17:06
16814ms at 04:06:30
16807ms at 04:05:52
16587ms at 04:09:05
16405ms at 04:07:19
```

## Expected behavior

The workspace snapshot should either:
1. **Exclude known large/generated directories** (e.g., `deps/`, `node_modules/`, `.venv/`, `__pycache__/`) via a configurable ignore list (similar to `.gitignore`), or
2. **Use incremental snapshotting** — only re-hash files that have changed since the last snapshot (based on mtime/ctime/inode), rather than re-hashing the entire tree on every turn, or
3. **Cache file content hashes** — if a file's size + mtime hasn't changed, reuse the previously computed hash instead of re-reading and re-hashing the file.

## Evidence

- API log: `/tmp/api-r3.log` — 244 `workspace_snapshot` completions, 24 exceeding 10 seconds
- Workspace: `~/sd779/.sciencediscovery-data/projects/0a5d0d9f.../sessions/065f92ca.../workspace/deps/` (470MB, 49 subdirectories of pip packages)
- Source: `packages/cas/src/versioning.ts:447` — `snapshotWorkspace` function with no exclusion logic
- The slow snapshots all occur after the agent installed packages to `/workspace/deps/` at ~04:00 UTC
- Before the deps install, snapshots were 2-10ms; after, they jumped to 15-60 seconds

## Impact

- Every agent turn is delayed by 15-60 seconds when the workspace contains large generated files
- For a 32-turn run, this adds 8-32 minutes of pure overhead
- The agent appears "stuck" to the user during each snapshot
- This discourages agents from installing necessary dependencies, as doing so penalizes all subsequent turns

issue:956.body:
## Context

#900 reports two failures. #901 fixes the thinking-control half: the loopback gateway now accepts the `enable_thinking`/`reasoning` keys Swarm puts on its tool-less probe, and the model client tolerates a provider that rejects thinking controls. The image half is untouched.

## What still happens

`jiuwenswarm-model-gateway.ts` rejects every non-text message with `images are not supported by this gateway` (HTTP 400). Swarm's image-modality warmup probe sends exactly such a request, so on a model without image input the start-up log still shows

```
llm_call_error … images are not supported by this gateway
```

and the warmup records `image_input=unknown (not cached)` instead of "image input not supported".

## Expected

A model that does not accept images should be recorded as `image_input=unsupported`. A capability the model does not have is not a transport error, and it should not be logged as a repeated 400 on every start.

## Where

- `services/api/src/agent-run/jiuwenswarm-model-gateway.ts:285` produces the rejection.
- The consumer that decides `image_input` is the JiuwenSwarm warmup, which can only classify what the gateway returns, so the fix needs a signal it can tell apart from a real failure — e.g. a dedicated error `type`/code (or a 200 with an explicit "unsupported" marker) that the probe maps to `image_input=unsupported`.

## Why it is not part of #901

What the probe should receive is a contract decision between the gateway and Swarm, not a model-client hardening change, so it is tracked separately.

issue:961.body:
### 🚀 Background Description

In the desktop app the sidebar section that holds sessions outside any project is labelled **"最近会话" / "Recent sessions"**.

That label does not describe what the section is. It is not a truncated "recent" window: it is the inbox, i.e. every session that has not been filed under a project, sorted by recency (`apps/desktop/src/app/use-workspace.ts`, `recent` at line 1726; `apps/desktop/src/views/Sidebar.tsx:350`). A name that reads as a time range makes users expect a short history rather than "everything not in a project", and when it sits next to the rail item 「会话」 and the sidebar heading 「科研会话」, the three labels do not make their relationship clear.

The same string is also reused as the display name of the inbox pseudo-project: when an open session belongs to the inbox, `activeProjectName` returns this label (`use-workspace.ts:1743`). So the wording appears in two different places and both should read consistently.

**Requested change:** rename the label to **"会话" / "Sessions"**.

### Design Ideas

- **Option A (what this issue asks for):** change only the wording — `sidebar.recent` in `zh.ts` and `en.ts`, plus the strings that quote it: `sidebar.noRecent` ("还没有最近会话" → "还没有会话") and the landing hint that says a session will appear in 「最近会话」.
- **Option B:** also reword the other two surrounding labels (rail 「会话」 and sidebar heading 「科研会话」) so the three levels are visibly distinct. Larger scope, needs a copy decision, not requested here.
- **Option C:** call the inbox 「未归类」 / "Unfiled" instead. More precise about the semantics, but longer and it reads as an error state rather than a normal place to work. Not recommended unless the product wants the inbox to be explicit.
- Rejected: sorting/labelling the section as a true "recent" list (e.g. last N sessions across all projects). That would change behaviour, not wording, and is out of scope for this request.

### Involved Public APIs

None. This is a display-string change in the desktop app. The server-side inbox project label is unchanged; `use-workspace.ts` deliberately never shows the stored server name (`inbox is never shown under its stored name: it is a server label`).

### Description of Relevance to Other Modules

- `apps/desktop/src/app/use-workspace.ts` — `activeProjectName` reuses the same key as the section label, so both surfaces change together.
- `apps/desktop/src/views/Sidebar.tsx` — section label and empty state.
- `apps/desktop/src/views/Landing.tsx` / `text` dictionaries — the hint that says a session without a project appears in that section.
- English dictionary `en.ts` must change in step, since `Text` is `typeof ZH` and the compiler rejects a dictionary out of shape.
- Session ordering (`session-order.ts`) and boot resume are unaffected — they do not read the label.

### Test Design and Test Plan

1. Switch the interface to 简体中文 and to English, and in each confirm the four surfaces above: sidebar section label, sidebar empty state, project-name position while an inbox session is open, and the landing hint.
2. Empty inbox: the section shows the empty-state string and no session rows.
3. Open a session that belongs to a real project, then one from the inbox, and confirm the project-name position switches between the project name and the new label.
4. Grep the two dictionaries for the old wording to confirm no surface was left behind.
5. Static gate: `pnpm ci:l1`. Desktop journey tests that read these strings (first-run guide, sidebar) should still pass.

### Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] The sidebar section label reads 「会话」 in Chinese and "Sessions" in English.
- [ ] The empty state reads 「还没有会话」 / "No sessions" and appears when the inbox holds nothing.
- [ ] While a session from the inbox is open, the project-name position shows the new label, not 「最近会话」.
- [ ] The landing hint that references this section uses the new wording in both languages.
- [ ] No user-visible string still says 「最近会话」 or "Recent sessions" in the desktop app.
- [ ] Switching language at runtime updates all of the above without a reload.
- [ ] Command that must pass: `pnpm ci:l1`

### Additional Information

Found while building a feature map of `apps/desktop` for usability patrol. Current strings:

```
zh.ts:53   recent: "最近会话"
zh.ts:54   noRecent: "还没有最近会话"
en.ts:58   recent: "Recent sessions"
en.ts:59   noRecent: "No recent sessions"
```

Not a defect — the current behaviour is internally consistent; this is a copy change requested by the maintainer.

issue:962.body:
Follow-up work split out of #717 (`fix(tools): bound model-facing execution and MCP results`) so that PR does not have to carry it. None of these blocks that PR. @moShangLouTou — GitHub refuses to assign this issue to you because your account has no write access to this repository; it is yours regardless.

## 1. The audit path has a depth cap but no total-size budget

`redactToolDetails` (`packages/tools/src/registry.ts`) deliberately drops the interactive size limits — that is the point of it, the durable record keeps complete safe metadata — and keeps only `MAX_AUDIT_DETAIL_DEPTH = 128`. Depth is bounded; total size is not. A result whose `details` are *wide* rather than deep — an MCP `records` array with many small records, for example — is written whole through `recordResult` into the durable trajectory and into the version recorder.

That is the same shape the interactive view already avoids with `MAX_DETAIL_TOTAL_CHARS`. Suggest a total-byte budget for the audit copy too, with an explicit `[audit-details truncated]`-style marker, so a reader can tell the difference between "the tool returned this" and "the recorder cut it".

## 2. `mcpModelResultView` copies the whole result twice

`mcpModelResultView` (`packages/workspace/src/mcp-result-view.ts`) runs `safeMcpValue` over the entire provider result to build a safe copy, and then `mcpRetainedContent` runs `JSON.stringify` over that copy whenever the projection is lossy. For a large result that is a full deep copy plus a full serialization on every MCP call.

Worth measuring against a realistically large provider result before deciding; if it shows up, a size gate on the retention serialization (retain only while the result is under some bound, with the existing "could not be stored" notice when it is not) would keep the recovery contract and remove the worst case.

## 3. Two journey assertions changed for reasons unrelated to this PR

- `test/journey-artifact-viewer-large-screen.spec.ts`: the readable-measure assertion moved from a fixed `760px` to `76ch` measured from the paragraph's computed font.
- `test/journey-model-connect-wizard.spec.ts`: the "高级配置" button assertion moved from `boundingBox().width > 50` to `scrollWidth <= clientWidth`.

Neither is needed by the tool-result contracts this PR introduces. If they were required to keep the suite stable, say so in a one-line note on #717; otherwise they belong in their own change.

issue:978.body:
## Checklist

- [x] I have searched for related issues but did not get the expected help.
- [x] This bug has not been fixed in the latest version.
- [x] Please note that if your bug description lacks corresponding environment information and a minimal reproducible demo, it will be difficult for us to reproduce and resolve the issue, which will reduce the possibility of receiving feedback, or even lead to the issue being closed.

## 🐞 Detailed Description of the Problem

### What happens

While a session is running shell tool calls, a shell execution submitted by the API to the **local Runner** is rejected with HTTP 401. The Runner answers `Execution not found for this Agent`, the API only records a warning (`shell_execution_unconfirmed … accepted=false stage=submission`), and the tool call never completes. The run then stays in `status: "running"` with no further events and never reaches a terminal state — no idle timeout, no failure, no cancel. Queued messages behind it are blocked indefinitely.

### Evidence (session `fe1ef6bf-e61a-49c2-a62f-75904a37a375`, run `ed84697e-426f-4679-9ac2-627d2c15c1fe`)

Run timeline (`GET /api/sessions/{id}/runs` and `…/runs/{id}/events`):

```text
run        ed84697e-426f-4679-9ac2-627d2c15c1fe
started    2026-11-07T13:53:56.620Z
last event 2026-11-07T13:58:01.895Z   assistant.response.settled (turn 13)
status     "running"                  observed at 2026-11-07T14:23:55Z  (25m 54s with zero events)
```

The last model call of that turn did request tools, so the turn was not finished:

```text
[model-sse-summary] {"requestId":"model-a455c319-…","model":"glm-5.2","httpStatus":200,
  "completedAt":"2026-11-07T13:58:01.819Z","finishReason":"tool_calls","hasToolCalls":true,
  "sseRecords":329,"sseParseErrors":0,"truncated":false}
```

There is **no `tool.started` event after that `assistant.response.settled`**, and no terminal event.

`data-dir/logs/api.log`:

```text
2026-11-07T13:47:08.702Z WARN [api] event=shell_execution_unconfirmed
  executionId=shell:e32f3d538ec7c0595af069d5a2b21ec8d7728d3101deb19dea4b40258a2e242a
  runnerId=local sessionId=fe1ef6bf-e61a-49c2-a62f-75904a37a375 agentId=main
  accepted=false stage=submission errorMessage="Runner request failed (401)" httpStatus=401
  runnerConnection=local
```

`data-dir/logs/runner.log` — the API keeps polling that execution for ~10 minutes and the Runner keeps answering that it does not know it:

```text
2026-11-07T13:46:55.482Z ERROR [runner] event=request_failed errorMessage="Execution not found for this Agent"
  method=GET path="/shell-executions/shell%3Ae32f3d538ec7c0595af069d5a2b21ec8d7728d3101deb19dea4b40258a2e242a"
…
2026-11-07T13:56:34.232Z ERROR [runner] event=request_failed errorMessage="Execution not found for this Agent"
  method=GET path="/shell-executions/shell%3Ae32f3d538ec7c0595af069d5a2b21ec8d7728d3101deb19dea4b40258a2e242a"
```

The Runner process itself was healthy and beating the whole time in the same log (`event=runner_heartbeat`, `uptimeMs` monotonically 3.25M → 4.08M across 13:45–13:59), so this is not a Runner crash or restart artifact.

While the run was stuck, the JiuwenSwarm agent side was still holding the turn open and only emitting keepalives:

```text
2026-11-07 22:02:04.779 INFO jiuwenswarm.server.agent_ws_server: [AgentWebSocketServer] keepalive chunk 发送: request_id=chat-80877aad80b3
2026-11-07 22:02:34.791 INFO jiuwenswarm.server.agent_ws_server: [AgentWebSocketServer] keepalive chunk 发送: request_id=chat-80877aad80b3
…
```

### Same signature in a second, independent session

`session 9666c93a-26dc-4c26-9760-d185bb4d9a54` (a literature-review run) hit the same class of failure: `api.log` records `shell_execution_unconfirmed … "Runner request failed (401)"` for `shell:ec32f855…`, and the run ended as `failed` with the opaque message `interaction round execution failed` (`errorCode=semantic-error`), which is the adapter's `run.failed` text passed through at `services/api/dist/agent-run/jiuwenswarm-agent.js:604`. No cause is surfaced to the session.

### Steps to reproduce

1. Local-source mode on Linux/WSL2: run `scripts/start-stack.sh --mode local` (JiuwenSwarm backend, local Runner).
2. Register a tool-calling model and create a session with `approvalMode = "always_allow"`.
3. Send a task whose plan runs several shell commands, e.g. the evolve-design case from `docs/zh/domains/evolve-a-solution.md`:

```text
/evolve-design 写一对处理文本的 compress/decompress：compress(text) -> bytes、decompress(bytes) -> str。
往返必须完全无损。只用标准库 —— 不许用 zlib、lzma、bz2。分数是压缩后小了多少。
```

4. Observe `data-dir/logs/api.log` for `shell_execution_unconfirmed … httpStatus=401` and `runner.log` for repeated `Execution not found for this Agent` for the same `shell:` id.
5. The run stops emitting events and stays `running` forever (`GET /api/sessions/{id}/runs`), while `GET …/runs/{id}/events` shows no event after `assistant.response.settled`. Sending another message leaves it `queued` behind the stuck run.

### Expected

- A shell execution that the Runner rejects must fail the tool call visibly (error returned to the agent/UI), not be downgraded to a warning.
- If a run makes no progress, the platform's idle protection must terminate it with a terminal state (`failed`) instead of leaving it `running` indefinitely and blocking the queue.

### Observed

- `401` from the Runner is logged as `shell_execution_unconfirmed` and the turn continues as if the tool were still pending.
- The run never reaches `completed`/`failed`/`cancelled`; no timeout fires; queued messages stay `queued`.

## Detailed Environment Information Description

```text
Host        Windows 11 26200, WSL2, distro Ubuntu 24.04 (D:\WSL\Ubuntu), WSL 3.0.3.0, kernel 6.18.54.1
Mode        local source checkout, scripts/start-stack.sh --mode local --no-build
Component   adapter :4310, API :4410, Runner :4311 (bubblewrap), memory-graph :17674, JiuwenSwarm gateway :20001
Node        v22.23.4      pnpm 11.1.2      uv 0.13.7      Python 3.12 (system) + starter-python scientific env
Model       glm-5.2 over an OpenAI-compatible relay (openai-chat-completions variant); 12/13 model calls in this
            session returned HTTP 200, the last one finished with finishReason=tool_calls
Sandbox     sandbox=bubblewrap, sandboxUsable=true; scientificEnvs available=true (starter-python ready)
Runner      runnerConnection=local, runnerVersion=bebd64e9
```

## Additional Information

Related reports I checked before filing: #819 (tool `started` without `completed`, but that one died at the 240 s idle timeout), #899 (`ask_user` wait trips the 240 s idle watchdog), #952 (MCP gateway python path). This report is different: here no watchdog fires at all, and the trigger is a 401 on execution submission.

Two questions for the maintainers, which would pin the root cause faster:

1. What makes the local Runner reject an execution submission for `agentId=main:<session>` with 401 / `Execution not found for this Agent` while the same Runner is healthy and beating? (agent binding rotation? auth token scope? execution registry TTL?)
2. Which layer is supposed to apply the idle timeout to a run that is waiting for a tool result? In this session nothing fired in 25+ minutes.

Logs, run ids and the full event dump can be provided on request.

## Version Information

- Repository: `openJiuwen-ai/sciencediscovery`
- Tested commit: `bebd64e907e3a1f4e1fe7684535df423409276cf` (main, 2026-11-07T09:28:17Z)
- Runner reported version: `bebd64e9`
- JiuwenSwarm: `workswarm0.2.6` (pinned tag, `scripts/jiuwenswarm.sh setup`)

issue:979.body:
## Summary

After an artifact download is approved, reopening the Session still shows a permission card for that download with all three buttons disabled. The download did run — the catalog records the answer and the artifact plan is `approved` — but the run's event log holds only the `permission.required` snapshot, so replaying the run rebuilds a pending request inside a run that has already terminated. The UI then renders it greyed out because `run.terminal = true`, and it can never be answered or dismissed.

This affects every governed artifact download (bioRxiv / PubMed MCP results written to the workspace). Denying the download leaves the same residue, and an approval-mode switch that clears pending requests leaves the cards behind as well.

## Reproduction

1. Start the local stack and connect a project whose Session requires approval for artifact downloads.
2. Ask the agent to fetch a paper through an MCP connector (bioRxiv or PubMed) into the workspace.
3. Answer the permission card once (allow or deny).
4. Let the run finish, then reopen the Session from the history list.

Reproduced on Windows 10 desktop + local API service, data directory `%LOCALAPPDATA%\ScienceDiscovery`. Session `e4876453-277c-4882-ad3b-45ead0085b34`, second-turn run `27e45b93-bfb6-4efd-a580-dc48151ff175`, request `3c3fde16-e0ef-4466-874a-8b798c78e288`:

- `run-events/<session>/<run>/main.jsonl` line 227 is a `permission.required` with `"state":"pending"` and `"action":"artifact_download"`. The request id appears exactly once in the file — there is no matching `permission.resolved`, while the other 14 permission flows in the same run each have both halves.
- `catalog.sqlite` holds the same id with `"state":"allowed"`.
- `artifact-plans/<session>.json` holds the same `permissionRequestId` with `"state":"approved"`.
- The run itself is `completed`; later turns, tool calls and the final answer are all present.

## Observed behaviour

The Session history ends with a disabled card:

```
需要权限
Download biorxiv-10.1101_2025.04.16.649149-v2.pdf
to workspace path papers/edgar2025_pediatric_liver_atlas.pdf

[ Allow once ]  [ Allow matching ]  [ Deny ]     ← all disabled
```

## Expected behaviour

A request the catalog has already decided should not reappear as pending when the run is replayed. Either the resolution should be part of the run stream so replay folds the request to its answer, or the client should reconcile a replayed pending snapshot against the catalog's terminal state.

## Root cause

`permission.required` was the only half of the artifact-download flow that reached the run stream. The decision endpoint answered the request in the catalog, but published no `permission.resolved`, so the log's last snapshot for that request stayed `pending`. Session replay is the event log, so the answer never reached the UI. The approval-mode switch (`PATCH` approval mode), which cancels pending requests, had the same gap.

## Fix

Fixed by #975 (merged 2026-11-07, merge commit `8041ca13`):

- The decision endpoint and the approval-mode switch now publish `permission.resolved` onto the owning run (direct run id, subagent mapped to its parent turn, otherwise the run still in flight), written once so a decision is not duplicated on the stream.
- The desktop reconciles a replayed pending request against `GET /api/permission-requests?sessionId=` when a replay ends on a pending request, so logs already written before this fix also display their real answer. The merge only touches entries the replay already holds, and a catalog-pending request keeps its card.

## Environment

- ScienceDiscovery desktop 0.3.0 on Windows 10, local API service, JiuwenSwarm backend.
- Reproducible from a run log alone: replaying `run 27e45b93…` reproduces the card without the gateway; the new test `apps/desktop/tests/permission-card-residue.test.ts` replays exactly that log.

## Relates to

- #445, #587 — earlier MCP download approval work; this is the follow-up where the answer never reached the run stream.
- #436 — also about permission cards, but about `always_allow` flooding new cards, a different symptom.

### 🐞 Detailed Description of the Problem

A user reports that importing an exported conversation fails when its original conversation belongs to a project, but the import destination is a different project or has no project. The exported conversation therefore depends on its original project, preventing portable session restoration.

There is also an error-reporting problem: the message does not clearly explain the failure or how to recover, and the Chinese UI displays an English error.

#### Minimal reproduction

1. Create project A and a conversation belonging to A; add conversation content.
2. Export that conversation as a research/session package.
3. Import the package with no project selected (the default import destination).
4. Observe the import failure and its unclear English error in the Chinese UI.
5. Repeat with another existing project B selected, or in an installation where original project A does not exist.

The user reports failures when the destination does not match the original project. The exact error text, stack trace, and affected export mode were not supplied; these should be captured during reproduction rather than inferred.

#### Expected behavior

- An exported conversation must be independent of the source project's existence, identifier, and membership.
- Importing without a project creates an unassigned conversation.
- Selecting an existing destination project assigns the imported conversation to that project, regardless of its original project.
- Source project information may be retained as provenance, but must not be a prerequisite for importing or continuing the conversation.
- The imported conversation preserves its relevant history and files and supports continued conversation and branching from an intermediate message.
- Genuine import errors provide a clear reason and recovery action in the currently selected UI language.

### Detailed Environment Information Description

- Product: ScienceDiscovery Windows desktop installer, x64.
- UI language: Simplified Chinese.
- Tested workflow: project-owned conversation export followed by import with a different project or no project.
- OS: Windows; exact OS build and export mode were not included in the user report.
- No server logs, stack trace, or reproduction package have been attached yet.

### Additional Information

Related feature: #803. Related desktop implementation: #970; research package backend implementation: #498.

Suggested investigation: inspect how source project identifiers and project-scoped references are serialized, validated, and mapped during import. Resolve destination project ownership independently from source provenance. Investigate the actual backend response before attributing a root cause.

#### Regression coverage / acceptance criteria

- Cover both essential and full exports.
- Import a project-owned source into no project, a different existing project, and an installation without the original project.
- Confirm the destination project assignment is correct, imported history/files remain usable, and continuation and prefix-only branching work without source-project lookup failures.
- Confirm the source conversation and source project remain unchanged.
- Validate Chinese and English error messages for genuinely invalid destinations (for example, a destination deleted before import); do not expose untranslated backend errors or raw internal identifiers as the only explanation.

- Desktop test installer: `0.3.0-pr970.a933f7fe`.
- Source commit: `a933f7fe35d5bb5a084302402715253228471134`.
- Latest-main verification: pending.

issue:982.body:
### Checklist

- [x] I have searched for related issues but did not get the expected help.
- [ ] This bug has not been fixed in the latest version.
- [x] I understand that environment information and a minimal reproduction are needed.

Investigated against the PR #970 test build; latest-main verification is pending.

### 🐞 Detailed Description of the Problem

The desktop repeatedly displays `Session not found`. Investigation identified a concrete persistent-error mechanism in research continuation polling: a durable operation can remain on disk after its source session is absent, the status route returns 404, and the frontend retries this terminal error forever every three seconds.

#### Confirmed evidence

- Local API logs contain repeated 404s at 2026-11-08 01:42:30.686Z, 01:42:33.712Z, 01:42:36.722Z, and 01:42:39.751Z, matching the frontend's three-second retry delay.
- Persisted research-continuation records include failed operations with `Research copy integrity mismatch: executionRuns.environmentRevisionId`.
- Read-only authenticated requests to the running local API confirmed, for two persisted failed operations, that both their source-session endpoint and continuation-status endpoint return HTTP 404 with `Session not found`. No conversation content or credentials are included here.
- These observations confirm the missing-source/status-route failure and indefinite retry mechanism. The historical 404 log records omit the URL, so those particular requests cannot individually be attributed with certainty. The reason the source sessions disappeared, and whether every reported occurrence shares this cause, remain unconfirmed. A failed copy must not be assumed to have deleted its source.

#### Root cause in code

1. `services/api/src/http/index.ts`, continuation route around lines 1117–1126: `store.getSession(sourceId)` is required before reading the durable operation. A missing source produces `404 Session not found`, even when the operation JSON exists and contains its terminal failure.
2. `apps/desktop/src/views/ResearchPackage.tsx`, copy-poll effect around lines 91–95: every rejected status request sets the raw error and schedules another poll after 3000 ms. There is no terminal-404 handling, retry bound, or clearing of the stale copy.
3. The effect depends on the client and copy operation, not the currently displayed session. Copy state is not cleared by a session switch. Closing the dialog also does not stop this task poll. Consequently a stale operation can keep surfacing the same error while the user works elsewhere.
4. Raw backend text is displayed via `setError(String(reason.message ?? reason))`, leaving Chinese users with an unexplained English message.

#### Minimal deterministic reproduction

1. Start creating a research continuation from an imported snapshot and keep its status poll active.
2. Make the source unavailable before the next status response (for an automated UI regression, return `404 {"error":"Session not found"}` from the status route).
3. Observe repeated status requests every three seconds and the raw error remaining on the page.
4. Switch the active conversation or close the initiating dialog; confirm the stale poll continues while the component remains mounted.

For an API regression, retain a durable failed operation while its source session is absent; request its status and verify the current route returns `Session not found` before consulting the operation record.

#### Expected behavior / proposed correction

- Treat a confirmed missing source/operation as a terminal polling outcome: stop polling, clear stale task state, and provide a localized explanation with a recovery action.
- Distinguish terminal missing-resource errors from retryable transport/service errors; bound retries for transient failures.
- Define task ownership across session switches explicitly. A deliberately backgrounded task may continue, but must not repeatedly overwrite the current conversation's error UI.
- Consider making durable terminal operation results readable after source deletion, with the appropriate ownership/access checks; do not simply remove the source check without assessing access control.
- Separately investigate the observed environment-revision integrity failure and the source-session lifecycle. Fixing either alone does not fix unbounded 404 polling.

### Detailed Environment Information Description

- ScienceDiscovery Windows desktop, x64; Simplified Chinese UI.
- Evidence: local API logs, persisted continuation metadata, read-only live HTTP checks, and source inspection.
- User reports frequent occurrences during current conversation-package testing.
- No changes were made to user conversations or project data during investigation.

### Additional Information

Related implementation: #970; backend research packages: #498; feature: #803. Related reports #980 and #981 should remain separate until a common cause is demonstrated.

#### Regression tests / acceptance criteria

- A continuation status 404 stops further polls and produces one readable, localized result.
- Existing terminal failed operation + missing source is handled according to the defined API contract.
- Session switch/dialog closure cannot leave an unowned infinite error poll.
- Transient request failures use bounded retries and recover normally when the service returns.
- Ready/failed operations, source deletion during copying, and application restart are covered.
- Chinese and English messages explain what is missing and how to recover; raw `Session not found` is not the only explanation.

### Version Information

- Test installer: `0.3.0-pr970.a933f7fe`.
- Source commit inspected: `a933f7fe35d5bb5a084302402715253228471134`.
- Latest-main reproduction: pending.

issue:983.body:
### Checklist

- [x] I have searched for related issues but did not get the expected help.
- [ ] This bug has not been fixed in the latest version.
- [x] I understand that environment information and a minimal reproduction are needed.

### 🐞 Detailed Description of the Problem

After exporting a conversation, deleting the original, and importing the package, the user cannot create a writable research conversation to continue chatting. The Chinese UI reports:

```text
创建研究会话失败（restore）：Research copy integrity mismatch: executionRuns.environmentRevisionId。原始导入快照保持不变。
```

The English internal diagnostic is not a readable explanation or recovery action in the Chinese UI.

#### Confirmed root cause

The integrity verifier assumes execution IDs are unique within execution history, but the store intentionally preserves multiple observations of an execution with the same ID.

- `services/api/src/store.ts:7070` (`appendExecutionRun`) permits an `unconfirmed` observation to advance to a settled outcome and appends the new record while retaining the old one. This is intentional append-only provenance history.
- `services/api/src/research-package-history.ts:41` exports that history; `restoreHistory` restores each observation, preserving the repeated IDs.
- `services/api/src/research-snapshot-integrity.ts:65` uses `actual.find(item => item.id === ids.id(String(row.id)))`. Every observation with that ID is therefore compared against the FIRST restored observation, regardless of status or position.
- Local package metadata confirms two executions, each represented by an `unconfirmed` record with `environmentRevisionId: "system-shell-bwrap-v1"` followed by a `failed` record with `environmentRevisionId: null` under the SAME ID.
- When verifying the failed observation, the expected null environment is compared against the first observation's remapped non-null environment. This produces the exact reported mismatch even when the history was restored correctly. Other changed fields, including status, can also be falsely rejected.
- `research-snapshots.ts:870` runs this verifier before publishing the writable copy; `research-continuations.ts` marks the operation failed. Consequently continuation remains unavailable.

**Deleting the original conversation is not required for this root cause.** A synthetic, in-memory reproduction triggers the same failure without accessing any original conversation, project, package archive, or environment installation. Source-deletion portability must still be covered by regression tests.

#### Minimal reproduction and verification performed

Call the production compiled `verifyResearchCopy` with one source session containing:

```json
[
  {"id":"exec","status":"unconfirmed","environmentRevisionId":"system-shell-bwrap-v1"},
  {"id":"exec","status":"failed","environmentRevisionId":null}
]
```

Build the target using production `ResearchPackageIds` and `remapRunEvent`, explicitly mapping the execution ID and session ID. Pass the source-to-target session map to the verifier. Source and target histories have identical observations under the correct ID remapping.

Observed locally:

```text
REPRODUCED: Research copy integrity mismatch: executionRuns.environmentRevisionId
CONTROL_PASS: single observation copies correctly
```

The control keeps only the failed observation on both sides and passes the same production verifier. This isolates duplicate-observation matching rather than source deletion or missing original environments.

#### Expected behavior and correction direction

- Match corresponding execution observations, preserving their multiplicity and history, rather than selecting the first record with an execution ID. Define stable observation/order correspondence and verify the full record set.
- Keep strict integrity checks: do not suppress environment mismatches, skip verification, or discard provenance history merely to make continuation succeed.
- Successfully publish a writable copy when restored history is genuinely equivalent, including after deleting the source or importing into another installation.
- Provide a structured error code plus localized, actionable user-facing text for genuine integrity failures. Retain field-level diagnostics for troubleshooting without using raw English internal text as the user explanation.

### Detailed Environment Information Description

- ScienceDiscovery Windows desktop, x64; Simplified Chinese UI.
- User workflow: export → delete source conversation → import → create research conversation / continue chatting.
- Investigation: read-only package metadata and production-code inspection; synthetic in-memory reproduction and passing control. No user conversations were changed during investigation.
- Exact export mode was not supplied; regression coverage must include essential and full packages where the repeated execution observations are retained.

### Additional Information

Related: feature #803, implementation #498 / #970. #982 tracks infinite 404 polling separately; it noted this integrity failure but did not diagnose it. #980 concerns project portability; #981 concerns a separate unclear legacy error.

#### Regression tests / acceptance criteria

- Same execution ID with unconfirmed → failed, unconfirmed → succeeded, and multiple distinct executions restores and verifies correctly.
- Preserve observation count, order semantics, remapped references, status, environment references (including null), and immutable evidence.
- Genuine changes to environment reference, status, output, or missing/duplicated observations still fail integrity checks.
- End-to-end export → delete source → import → create writable conversation → continue chat succeeds; repeat in a clean destination without source IDs or source environment catalog entries.
- Cover essential/full packages, retry after an earlier failed copy, and API restart.
