closed_recent.body:
### Checklist

- [x] I have searched for related issues but did not get the expected help.
- [x] This bug has not been fixed in the latest version.
- [x] The description below includes the environment details and the request log needed to reproduce the failure on a real installation.

### 🐞 Detailed Description of the Problem

**What the user sees.** On Windows, launching ScienceDiscovery 0.3.0 opens a maximized window with no content — a full-screen white page. Clicking the desktop icon again does not recover it: the new process exits immediately because it does not acquire the single-instance lock, and every later launch does the same. Only killing the shell process that still owns the lock lets the app start again — and it then goes white again within a few minutes once a session is open.

**What is actually failing.** The local API process (`services/api`, the Node process behind the adapter) dies of V8 heap exhaustion while research-package previews are being warmed in the background. The shell's stack supervisor (`scripts/start-stack.mjs`) sees the API child exit and tears down the adapter and the sidecars, so the UI origin on `127.0.0.1:4310` is gone while the Electron window stays alive and keeps the single-instance lock. A relaunch therefore exits as a "second instance" before any window exists, and the user has no way back into the app.

The shell log from the shipped 0.3.0 build shows this sequence twice:

```text
# crash on an already-running shell
[stack:err] FATAL ERROR: MarkCompactCollector: young object promotion failed Allocation failed - JavaScript heap out of memory
# heap at the abort: 3832.9 (3867.4) MB

# cold start, no export dialog opened by the user, crash after 284 s
[20056:00004F200011C000] 284002 ms: Scavenge 3775.5 (3806.8) -> 3730.9 (3784.6) MB ...
FATAL ERROR: MarkCompactCollector: young object promotion failed Allocation failed - JavaScript heap out of memory
```

After each crash, every new launch exits before creating a window:

```text
second instance: single-instance lock not acquired; exiting so the first instance stays the only one
loadUi: ui origin not answering within 30s; loading anyway (did-fail-load retry is the backstop)
```

The window state is restored as maximized, so "loading anyway" is what the user experiences as a full-screen white window.

**What produced the crash.** In the same cold-start run, the stack log shows ordinary session browsing followed by repeated full package builds. All timestamps below are from one run; IDs are redacted:

- `GET /api/sessions/<id>` for several different sessions (each of these calls `exportPreviews.watch(...)` on the server);
- **18** `POST /internal/research-package/export` calls (the memory-graph snapshot request issued once per `buildResearchPackageInput`) between 03:27:21Z and 03:30:38Z;
- `research-package/preview?level=necessary&includeFullTrajectory=0&includeFullMemoryGraph=0` at 03:30:23Z, and `level=complete&includeFullTrajectory=0&includeFullMemoryGraph=0` at 03:30:33Z;
- `FATAL ERROR ... JavaScript heap out of memory` at 03:31:35Z, 284 s after the stack started.

**Why the background warming is so heavy (confirmed in the installed build).**

1. `GET /api/sessions/:id` calls `exportPreviews.watch(projectId, sessionId)`. `watch()` calls `warm()`, and `warm()` calls `defaults()`, which computes **five** preview profiles per session: `necessary`; `complete`; `complete + full trajectory`; `complete + full memory graph`; `complete + both`. A plain session read is therefore enough to start five full export builds.
2. Every profile runs `buildResearchPackageInput` from scratch. For every session in the dependency closure it materialises all messages, all runs, **every event of every run stream**, workspace files and provenance, all artifact versions, reviews and audit tasks, export history, claims and evidence, plus a memory-graph snapshot. The `necessary` filter is applied **after** this load, so the "small" profile pays the full materialisation cost.
3. `sessionTrajectory` reads the same run streams a second time to build the trajectory index. `complete + full trajectory` then hydrates every trajectory detail into a single array.
4. The preview path only avoids reading CAS payload bytes. Every metadata object above is still resident at the same time.
5. Builds are serialised on one queue, so the five profiles run back to back and the previous build's garbage has not been collected when the next one starts. `tick()` repeats the warm for watched sessions every 3 s.
6. No launch path sets `--max-old-space-size` or `NODE_OPTIONS`, so the process aborts at the Node default old-space limit (about 4 GB).

On this installation (about 2.7 GB of project data and 3 GB of versioning/CAS data), two preview profiles raised the API process from about 164 MB to about 949 MB of private bytes, and a third request for `complete + includeFullTrajectory=1` killed it. That is consistent with the 4–5 minute crash above.

**What I expected.** Opening the app and browsing sessions should not start a full export build. Preview work should be bounded, should run when the user opens the export dialog, and a dead API should not leave the desktop shell stuck on a white window that cannot be relaunched.

**Suggested direction.**

- Do not warm previews from `GET /api/sessions/:id`; warm on export-dialog open only, and at most one profile at a time.
- Apply the `necessary` filter while streaming, or before loading run streams, and make run-stream reads cursor-based (the same direction as #1011).
- Skip the warm when the revision is unchanged (the cache key exists, but the first warm of each revision still runs five builds).
- Give the shell a failure path: if the stack dies while the window is open, surface an actionable error and allow a restart instead of holding the single-instance lock over a dead origin.
- Make the heap budget explicit and observable on every launch path.

### Detailed Environment Information Description

- OS: Windows 10 Pro 10.0.19045, x64.
- ScienceDiscovery desktop 0.3.0 (win-x64 installer), local mode via `start-stack.mjs --mode local --no-node-build`. No `NODE_OPTIONS` or `--max-old-space-size` in the environment or in the launch scripts.
- Data directory: about 2.7 GB of projects, 3 GB of versioning/CAS, 38 MB of run-event streams. The project involved contains several sessions, including a long-running session with tool and subagent streams.
- The failure was reproduced twice: once on a shell that had already been running, and once from a cold start, without opening the export dialog in either case.

### Additional Information

- Related but not duplicates: #1011 reports the same class of heap growth in a long real session, but its user-visible symptom is teardown `ECONNREFUSED`; the trigger reported here is preview warming on a plain session read, and the symptom is a white window that cannot be relaunched. #1079 / #1083 report a failed preview for `complete + includeFullTrajectory`; on this installation that exact request kills the API instead of returning 404. #1024 covers the export dialog redesign; this issue is about the runtime cost behind the preview.
- The analysis was done against the shipped 0.3.0 build, so file/line locations should be confirmed against `main`.
- Session and project identifiers and local paths are redacted on purpose.

### Version Information

- ScienceDiscovery 0.3.0.0 (win-x64), build dated 2026-11-10.
- Electron/Node as shipped with that installer; the aborts occurred at 3.8–4.1 GB of V8 heap, the default old-space limit.

## Problem

`POST /api/settings/web` answers a generic `500 {"error":"Internal server error"}` for six shapes that are plainly the client's mistake. `normalizeWebSettings` (`services/api/src/store/settings.ts`) throws a bare `Error` for each of them, so the chain in `services/api/src/http/index.ts:3930-3936` falls through to the catch-all instead of the 400 it gives other validation failures.

| Input | Throw site | Message |
|---|---|---|
| `{"deepseekEnabled": "yes"}` | `store/settings.ts:374` | `deepseekEnabled must be a boolean` |
| `{"paidSearchProviders": ["bogus"]}` | `:384` | `paidSearchProviders must list supported paid search providers` |
| `{"freeSearchEngines": {"brave": "yes"}}` | `:396` | `freeSearchEngines.<engine> must be a boolean` |
| `{"searchCacheTtlSeconds": 1e9}` | `:403` | `<field> must be an integer between 0 and …` |
| `{"freeSearchEngines": {"nope": true}}` | `:392` | `Unknown free search engine: nope` |
| non-object body (`[]`, `"x"`, `null`) | `:370` | `Web settings must be an object` |

Impact: a client that retries on 5xx retries a request that can never succeed, while the message it needs is already in the response body. This is the same class of defect `#923` fixed for the unknown-key case one line above.

## Origin

Review comment on `#929` (`sciencediscovery-bot`, 2026-11-05T13:55:59Z, `store/settings.ts:374`) — recorded here as a follow-up so `#929` stays scoped to `#923`.

## Suggested fix

Give every throw in `normalizeWebSettings` the same `code: "INVALID_WEB_SETTINGS"` the unknown-key path already carries (message text unchanged), then let the existing route mapping answer 400. A small helper keeps it one line per throw.

## Acceptance

1. For each of the six shapes above: a test that asserts `400`, not `500`, with the message text preserved.
2. Negative assertions: `Catalog database is not initialized` and a genuine internal fault still answer `500`.
3. No change to any message wording; no change outside `normalizeWebSettings` and the route mapping.
closed_recent.title: [Bug]: six client-side web-settings rejections still answer 500 instead of 400

Follow-up work for #834 (`feat(sizeopt): slim the Windows installer 797.6 -> ~578.0 MiB, merge 6 envs into 2`). That PR's code is reviewed; this issue carries the parts deliberately left out of it, so they are not only recorded in a review thread.

## 1. Real-machine smoke (the minimum the maintainer asked for)

The full matrix (three install-root lengths timed, bilingual screenshots, 30–60 s recording) was reduced to one smoke pass:

- [ ] One clean Windows machine: install → first launch, with a first-launch timing next to the f26 baseline.

`treeHasPycache` (`win_desktop/src/bootstrap.ts:230-251`) skips the first-run `compileall` as soon as one `__pycache__` directory holds one `.pyc` (`:243`). - [ ] Write a manifest or count of the precompiled set at assemble time and check it at bootstrap, so an incomplete set (quarantined file, partial copy, interrupted unpack) fails the build or names itself at first launch instead of surfacing as an `ImportError` at first tool use.

closed_recent.author: HugoXK
closed_recent.body:
Implementation: ScienceDiscovery (ours) — PR follows within 24h. Do not pick up without a `pickup-ok` comment on this issue.

Written-by: ScienceDiscovery Product
Claimed-by: ScienceDiscovery Product
Claim-Id: 17fa595af9c94fc1b2bb977b4a4c9101
Branch: dev2/fix/specialist-client-errors
Base: 2908e9e8bb4f
At: 2026-11-05T14:14:26Z

## What happens

The Specialist settings surface turns ordinary client mistakes into a bare internal error. Saving a Specialist whose name is already taken, editing or deleting a Specialist that no longer exists, and editing a built-in Specialist all answer `500`:

```
POST /api/specialists {"name":"duplicate-name subject","description":"d","instructions":"i","connectorIds":[],"enabledSkillIds":[]}
  first call   → 201 {"name":"duplicate-name subject","id":"9c1f45d8-…"}
  second call  → 500 {"error":"Internal server error"}

PUT    /api/specialists/nope                    → 500 {"error":"Internal server error"}
DELETE /api/specialists/nope                    → 500 {"error":"Internal server error"}
PUT    /api/specialists/assessment-screener {"name":"assessment-screener renamed"}
                                                → 500 {"error":"Internal server error"}   (built-in, read-only)
```

The same settings area already answers these shapes correctly on the neighbouring MCP-servers surface:

```
POST /api/mcp/servers {"name":"dup mcp","transport":"stdio","command":"echo","args":[]}
  first call   → 201
  second call  → 400 {"error":"A server with this name already exists"}
DELETE /api/mcp/servers/custom-000000000000     → 404 {"error":"MCP server not found"}
```

Other resource routes answer `404` for an unknown id as well (`GET/PUT/DELETE /api/models/nope`, `/api/providers/nope`, `/api/proxy/servers/nope`, `/api/projects/nope`, `/api/permission-grants/nope`), so the Specialist routes are the outlier, not the norm.

The user sees the generic text: `apps/web/src/Orchestration.tsx:262` (create/update) and `:275` (delete) hand the API message to `onError`, and `apps/web/src/api/auth.ts:26-36` (`ApiRequestError`) carries the server's `error` body verbatim — so the Specialist pane prints "Internal server error" where the store already knows the reason.

## What is expected

- a taken name → `400 {"error":"Specialist name already exists"}` (the message the store already produces);
- an unknown id on `PUT`/`DELETE` → `404 {"error":"Specialist not found"}`;
- an edit of a built-in Specialist → `400 {"error":"Built-in specialists are read-only; only their enabled flag can be toggled"}`.

## Where it comes from

- The routes: `services/api/src/http/index.ts:1827-1843` — `POST /api/specialists`, `PUT|DELETE /api/specialists/:id` call the store with no error mapping at all.
- The throws they forward: `services/api/src/store.ts:4347` and `:4378` (`Specialist name already exists`), `:4358` and `:4387` (`Specialist not found`), `:4364` (`Built-in specialists are read-only; only their enabled flag can be toggled`).
- Why that becomes a 500: `services/api/src/http/error-classification.ts:23-32` recognises only `is required`, `must`, `contains an unknown value`, `cannot`, `does not match`, `invalid`, `unsafe … (archive|package|path)`, `plain basename`. None of the four messages above matches, so `services/api/src/http/index.ts:3938-3946` falls through to `500 "Internal server error"`.
- The shape the sibling surface uses: `services/api/src/http/custom-mcp.ts:87-90` — one `catch` that answers `404` for its not-found message and `400` with the store's message for everything else.

## Failing test (reproduce before the fix)

Any harness that starts the real API server works; the probe below reuses the isolated fixture style of `services/api/src/configuration/http.integration.test.ts` (temp data dir, stub Runner, `createApiServer`, `offlineMcpTransport`), creates one Specialist, then checks the four rejected shapes. Temporary probe file, not committed:

```ts
// services/api/src/configuration/zz-specialist-conflict-probe.test.ts
const specialist = { name: "duplicate-name subject", description: "d", instructions: "i", connectorIds: [], enabledSkillIds: [] };
await call("POST", "/api/specialists", specialist);
await check("duplicate name", "POST", "/api/specialists", specialist, 400);
await check("unknown PUT", "PUT", "/api/specialists/nope", { x: 1 }, 404);
await check("unknown DELETE", "DELETE", "/api/specialists/nope", undefined, 404);
await check("built-in edit", "PUT", "/api/specialists/assessment-screener", { name: "assessment-screener renamed" }, 400);
assert.deepEqual(failures, []);
```

Command and observed output:

```
$ cd services/api && node --import tsx --test src/configuration/zz-specialist-conflict-probe.test.ts
not ok 1
  error: |-
    Expected values to be strictly deep-equal:
    + actual - expected

    + [
    +   'duplicate name: expected 400, got 500 {"error":"Internal server error"}',
    +   'unknown PUT: expected 404, got 500 {"error":"Internal server error"}',
    +   'unknown DELETE: expected 404, got 500 {"error":"Internal server error"}',
    +   'built-in edit: expected 400, got 500 {"error":"Internal server error"}'
    + ]
    - []

# tests 1
# pass 0
# fail 1
```

## Environment

- `main` @ `2908e9e8bb4f400eb8ad5fde0d7bd50225214349` (2026-11-05T13:01:38Z)
- node `v22`; from `services/api`: `node --import tsx --test src/<file>`
- the fixture's built-in Specialists come from the default catalog (`assessment-screener`, `code-engineer`, `creative-material-design`); no network, no model call.

## Smallest mergeable slice

One source block, one test file:

1. `services/api/src/http/index.ts:1827-1843` — wrap the three Specialist handlers in the same `try { … } catch` shape `custom-mcp.ts:87-90` already uses: `sendError(response, message === "Specialist not found" ? 404 : 400, message)` with a fallback message when the thrown value is not an `Error`. Keep the store's wording; do not reword any throw.
2. A route test (`services/api/src/specialists-http.test.ts`, or the existing HTTP test file the fixture lives in) pinning the four checks above plus the two that must not regress: toggling `enabled` on a built-in Specialists still answers `200`, and a genuinely internal failure still answers `500`.

Do not touch `services/api/src/store.ts` (its messages are right), do not add a pattern to `services/api/src/http/error-classification.ts` (that file is held by the in-flight length-rejection fix), and do not touch `apps/web` (the client already shows whatever the server says).

## Acceptance

- Duplicate name → `400` with `Specialist name already exists`; the first create still answers `201`.
- Unknown id on `PUT` → `404 Specialist not found`; on `DELETE` → `404 Specialist not found`.
- Editing a built-in Specialist's `name`/`description`/`instructions`/`connectorIds`/`enabledSkillIds`/`runtime` → `400` with its read-only message; `PUT {"enabled":false}` on a built-in still answers `200` and flips the flag.
- Deleting a built-in still answers `400 Built-in specialists cannot be deleted` (unchanged — it matches the classifier's `cannot` rule today; the route catch must preserve it).
- A real internal failure in the same block still surfaces as `500`: the catch keys on the not-found message and passes everything else through as `400` **only** for store validation, so the test must include at least one 500 case (e.g. a stubbed store method throwing an unexpected error) to prove the route did not turn every fault into a client error.

## Why this is not a duplicate

- Checked every open pull request's file list (`GET /search/issues?q=repo:openJiuwen-ai/sciencediscovery+is:pr+is:open`, 70 open, then `GET /pulls/<n>/files` for each): no open PR touches the Specialist handlers in `services/api/src/http/index.ts`; `#931` also edits that file but in the model-deletion routes, far from `:1827-1843`.
- Issue search for `specialist 500`, `already exists specialist`, `specialist name unique`, `duplicate specialist` returns no issue about rejected Specialist input answering 500.
- The in-flight length-rejection fix (`#930`) covers a different validator via the shared classifier; this one is route-level on a surface whose sibling already behaves this way, so the two fixes do not overlap.
closed_recent.title: [Bug]: Rejected Specialist input answers 500 while the MCP settings surface answers 400 and 404

## What happens

The delimited-preview payload carries a `warnings: string[]` field that no consumer reads, and which duplicates text the client already composes and localizes.

## Where

- `services/api/src/artifact-dashboard.ts` (at `0477d328`): the `warnings` array is built at the end of `parseDelimitedTable` ("The file has {total} columns; the preview shows the first {shown}." and "{n} cells past the preview width are not shown.") and returned in the payload type (`:161`-ish in that revision).
- `apps/web/src/artifact-dashboard.ts` mirrors the field in the web payload type.
- The viewer does not use it: `ArtifactModal` passes `clippedColumns` / `clippedCells` down and `DatasetTable` composes its own sentences from `artifact.tableClippedColumns` / `artifact.tableClippedCells` (`apps/web/src/ScientificArtifacts.tsx`).

## Why it matters

Two places decide what the user is told about a clipped preview: the server strings are English-only, so a Chinese UI would drift from them the moment anyone read them, and a future consumer could show untranslated text. Today the field is dead weight in every preview payload.

## Suggested fix

Either drop `warnings` from the payload and keep `clippedColumns` / `clippedCells` as the only source of truth (the client already localizes from them), or make the client render the server strings through the i18n layer. Pick one owner for the copy.

closed_recent.author: yuanzhou75
closed_recent.body:
### 🚀 Background Description

Daily use of the desktop client (0.3.0, built from main `5c765cd0`) surfaces five places in the session UI where the interface shows something the user did not ask for, cannot act on, or cannot read. In two of them the UI *takes away* what the user is interacting with. The direction is the same in all five: keep the page terse, one short sentence where a sentence is needed, and never redraw the thing the user is clicking.

They come from four reports; the export dialog contributes two of them (list redraw and omission text).

All of them are in the desktop application (`apps/desktop/src/views/ResearchPackage.tsx`); the web client carries the same research-package flows in `apps/web/src/research-package/ResearchPackageActions.tsx` and has diverged, so parity has to be checked separately. **Both locales (zh-CN and en) must change together** — each item below names the strings that exist today.

**1. Branch dialog quotes the source reply.** Opening 创建新分支聊天 shows, under the hint, a 240-character excerpt of the reply being branched from (`:326`, `…content.slice(0, 240)`). The dialog is about creating a new conversation, and the excerpt adds nothing: the hint already says what is carried over. Requested: drop the excerpt, keep the hint line.

**2. Export: selecting a workspace file empties the dialog.** In 导出会话 → 必要导出 the workspace file list lives inside `{preview ? … : null}` (`:318`), and every change to the selection resets the preview (`setPreview(undefined)` at `:220`, effect at `:217-227`) while the size is recomputed. The first checkbox click therefore unmounts the whole list — the user loses their place, cannot tick a second file until it comes back, and the dialog momentarily shows only 正在计算范围与大小… (`:317`). Computing the size is wanted; blanking the page is not.

**3. Export: 范围与省略说明 is unreadable.** The same dialog renders `preview.omissions` verbatim as a bullet list (`:319`) — internal packaging language, long, and nothing a user can act on. Requested: one or two plain sentences at most (e.g. how many versions/files are left out), or nothing.

**4. Import: the same omission list appears right after choosing a package.** `:325` renders `inspection.manifest.omissions` as a `<ul>` immediately below the file name and object count. Requested: either a single file summary line (name · objects · size) or nothing at all.

**5. After import: a second, permanent navigation entry point.** Once the research copy exists, `:301` keeps rendering `研究副本已准备好` (`t.ready`) plus an 打开会话 button (`t.open`) below the conversation. 继续聊天 already creates the copy and navigates as soon as it is ready (`:257`), so this line is a duplicate way in that never goes away. Requested: remove the ready state and its button entirely; keep only the passive 正在复制… line while the copy runs (and the failure message).

### Design Ideas

1. **Branch dialog** — render only `t.branchHint`. Delete the `<blockquote>` and the `messageId` content lookup; keep passing `messageId` for the request itself.

2. **Export file list** — keep the list mounted for the whole dialog. Split the preview into "the data the user is choosing from" (`files`, from the last successful response) and "the size being recomputed" (a pending flag). On selection change: keep `files` and the open `<details>`, mark the estimate line as recalculating, and swap in the new bytes when they arrive. Never call `setPreview(undefined)` for a selection change; a level change may still reset, since the list itself changes there.

3. **Export omissions** — replace the rendered list with a single localized summary built from counts (e.g. `{versions} 个历史版本、{files} 个未选文件未包含`), or drop the block. If a raw list is kept at all it belongs behind an explicit 详情 disclosure, not in the default view.

4. **Import inspection** — delete the omissions `<ul>`. Keep `{file.name} · {objectCount} 个内容对象` and, if useful, the payload size on the same line.

5. **Copy status** — stop rendering the `ready` branch: no 研究副本已准备好, no 打开会话. Keep `copying` (passive progress) and `failed` (error). Navigation stays exactly as it is today: 继续聊天 → the copy is created → the client jumps to it when ready, and 打开会话 as a separate affordance disappears with the line.

Copy to change in both languages: desktop `text/zh.ts` + `text/en.ts` (`ready`, `open`, `branchHint`, `omissions`, `calculating`, `files`); web `i18n/messages.ts` (`researchPackage.viewLimitations`, `researchPackage.omissions`, `researchPackage.statLimitations`, `researchPackage.previewCalculating`) for the equivalent surfaces.

### Involved Public APIs

None. All five changes are client-side rendering; the preview, inspect, import and continuation endpoints keep their current payloads. No server-side field is added or removed.

### Description of Relevance to Other Modules

| Module | Responsibility |
| --- | --- |
| `apps/desktop/src/views/ResearchPackage.tsx` | Branch dialog, export dialog (file list + omissions), import inspection, copy status line |
| `apps/desktop/src/text/zh.ts`, `text/en.ts` | Every string above, both locales |
| `apps/desktop/src/styles/research-package.css` | Layout for the trimmed blocks |
| `apps/web/src/research-package/ResearchPackageActions.tsx` | Same flows; already refactored, verify each of the five behaviours there |
| `apps/web/src/i18n/messages.ts` | Web strings for the same surfaces |

**Conflict to resolve before starting:** #1024 proposes *adding* per-dimension counts and an explicit "will not be restored" block to the export and import dialogs. The direction recorded here is the opposite — the user asked for fewer lines and less unexplained detail. This issue supersedes the information-density part of #1024 (its items 2, 3 and 7); #1024's export-centre and size-limit parts are unaffected. Do not implement both.

### Test Design and Test Plan

- **Component tests (desktop):** toggling a workspace file leaves the list mounted and keeps the previously known estimate visible with a pending marker; the dialog never returns to the calculating-only state on a selection change; a branch dialog renders no excerpt; an import review renders no omission list; a ready copy renders neither the ready text nor the open button.
- **E2E on the desktop build** with the real local stack, using a session that has several workspace files:
  1. 导出会话 → 必要导出 → tick file A, then tick file B without waiting: both stay ticked, the list stays open, the size settles on the value that includes both.
  2. 导出会话 → check the omissions block: at most two short lines, readable in zh-CN and en.
  3. 导入会话 → choose a package → only the summary line is shown.
  4. Import a package → 继续聊天 → land in the copy; no 研究副本已准备好 / 打开会话 line remains anywhere in the session view.
  5. Branch from an intermediate reply: the dialog shows the hint and no quoted excerpt.
- **Commands:** `pnpm --filter @sciencediscovery/desktop typecheck`, `pnpm --filter @sciencediscovery/desktop test`, `pnpm --filter @sciencediscovery/desktop build`, `pnpm ci:l1`.
- Screenshots of all five surfaces (zh-CN and en) go in the PR body for the owner's visual approval, per the UI rule.

### Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] 创建新分支聊天 shows the hint only; no excerpt of the source reply, in both languages.
- [ ] Selecting or deselecting a workspace file never unmounts or collapses the file list, and a second file can be selected without waiting for the first recalculation.
- [ ] The size keeps recalculating in place; the dialog never replaces itself with the calculating state on a selection change.
- [ ] 范围与省略说明 is at most two plain-language lines (or removed); no internal packaging text in the default view.
- [ ] Import shows a one-line package summary (name · objects · size) and no omission list.
- [ ] After import, no 研究副本已准备好 / 打开会话 line persists; 继续聊天 navigates to the copy by itself, and failures still report.
- [ ] zh-CN and en strings both updated, no untranslated leftovers on either surface.
- [ ] `pnpm --filter @sciencediscovery/desktop typecheck|test|build` and `pnpm ci:l1` pass.
- [ ] Owner has seen the screenshots in the PR body before approval.

### Additional Information

Reported from the Windows desktop client, build `0.3.0` from main `5c765cd0` (2026-11-09T22:07Z), Simplified Chinese UI.

Related: #1024 (export UI redesign — the density items conflict, see above), #986 / PR #999 (the save flow the export dialog got in that round), #995 (import opened two sessions; item 5 here is the leftover navigation affordance from that flow), #803 (feature scope).
closed_recent.title: [Feature]: Trim five information-heavy surfaces in the desktop session UI (branch excerpt, export file list and omissions, import omissions, copy notice)

closed_recent.author: ink999107
closed_recent.body:
## 🚀 Background Description

The desktop app (`apps/desktop`, Electron + React) is the primary client, but program evolution (evolve) can only be designed, started, and watched from the web UI or the CLI via `/evolve-design`. Evolve is the one capability that keeps running after the turn that started it and keeps producing candidates: a user needs one surface to design the search, confirm its checkpoints, watch it live, inspect candidates and scores, and return to a finished search later. The desktop app has no such entry point or panel, so users must switch to the web client.

This issue tracks the full desktop delivery: the design entry point, checkpoints, the live panel, and result inspection, with the official tutorial's sample as the acceptance path.

Related issues: checkpoint token budget #780, natural-language entry point #310, `/evolve` documentation #55 / #567, desktop client delivery #400.

Related pull request: #715 — budget for the thinking a model cannot be told to stop (closes #780). It is the source of the per-call ceiling the checkpoint cards show.

## Design Ideas

- **A confirmation switch, chosen up front.** A toggle at the very start of the flow decides whether the checkpoints require a human confirmation. When it is off, the agent runs the remaining checkpoints and launches the search in one pass without stopping to wait; when it is on, each checkpoint pauses for confirmation as described below. The switch is set before anything is designed, so the user decides the pace once, not at every checkpoint.
- **Conversation-first.** No configuration form is added. `/evolve-design` opens the algorithm picker and a create dialog that collects only the two things a person knows — what should get better, and which search fits the problem — then hands that sentence to the conversation as the command it would have typed. The agent still designs the plan and scorecard and runs the checkpoints in the session.
- **Checkpoints stay in the conversation.** The four checkpoints (requirements, evaluation, scale, launch) appear as cards in the message stream; the user confirms or edits them there instead of navigating to another page.
- **A persistent session shelf.** A thin row under the session header lists the session's searches (running and finished); closing the panel never makes a running search unreachable, and a session that never used evolve renders nothing.
- **A result cockpit.** The panel answers the questions a person watching a search actually asks, in order: did it get better (best score), how did it get there (chart), what did it try (candidate table), why was that one rejected (inspector). On a narrow window the inspector becomes a drawer over the table.
- **Runtime install up front.** A first-time install of the evolve runtime happens inside the create dialog, not after the user has written a whole goal.
- **Events first, polling as fallback.** Subscribe to the evolve SSE stream; fall back to polling the run list when the stream is unavailable, and make an idle session cost nothing.

Alternatives considered and rejected: embedding the web page inside the desktop shell (splits interaction and state handling, and ships the whole web bundle), and a standalone search window (a search belongs to a session; a separate window makes both "return to the conversation" and "start another search" awkward).

## Involved Public APIs

No new public API. The desktop app reuses the existing evolve REST/SSE routes (runtime status, init, run list and detail, candidates, event stream), wrapped in `apps/desktop/src/api/evolve.ts`. The shared `EvolveRun` and evolve event types come from `packages/schema`, the same ones the web client uses. Any route change must keep the web client and CLI behavior unchanged and be described here.

## Description of Relevance to Other Modules

- `packages/schema`: evolve run and event types; the desktop app does not duplicate them.
- Desktop run pipeline: `run-stream` model and reducer must carry checkpoint and evolve state without disturbing text placement in ordinary conversations.
- Internationalization: every new string lands in both `text/zh.ts` and `text/en.ts`.
- The web evolve dashboard reads the same data; any behavioral difference between the two surfaces must be deliberate and documented.
- End-to-end tests: the desktop e2e fixtures need a mocked evolve runtime.

## Test Design and Test Plan

- **Unit tests:** command parsing (`/evolve-design`, the algorithm flag, a seeded goal); run status and label mapping; candidate reduction and best score; shelf folding (a running search is never folded away).
- **Component tests:** the create dialog's runtime install and error path; checkpoint cards; panel selection (clicking a row fills the inspector); the narrow-window drawer.
- **End-to-end (`apps/desktop/e2e/evolve.spec.ts`, mocked runtime):** start a search from a session → checkpoints → run → live updates → select a candidate and inspect it → stop; plus a session with no search rendering exactly as before.
- **Two complex math smoke cases:** (a) symbolic regression — recover a closed-form expression for a nonlinear function from sampled points, scored by fit error; (b) numerical optimization — improve a numerical routine's accuracy or runtime (for example an ODE integrator or a linear solver), scored by error against a reference. In each case the pass bar is that evolve triggers normally and runs through several nodes (at least three expansions with recorded candidates); the full search does not have to finish.
- **Regression:** the web evolve dashboard and the CLI behave unchanged; ordinary sessions keep their text placement, tool cards, and artifact panel.

Commands that must pass: `pnpm check` (typecheck and unit tests); `npm run typecheck` and `npm test` in `apps/desktop`; the desktop e2e suite.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] The sample in the Evolve tutorial runs successfully: complete one PUCT search from the desktop app following `docs/en/domains/evolve-a-solution.md` (Chinese: `docs/zh/domains/evolve-a-solution.md`) — design checkpoints, launch, watch live, finish, and open the result.
- [ ] The UI design passes review: the create dialog, checkpoint cards, session shelf, and result panel are reviewed against the agreed design and all review comments are closed.
- [ ] A session with no search looks exactly as it did before the change.
- [ ] Commands that must pass: `pnpm check`; `npm run typecheck` and `npm test` in `apps/desktop`; the desktop e2e suite.

## Additional Information

Tutorial sample: `docs/en/domains/evolve-a-solution.md` (Chinese: `docs/zh/domains/evolve-a-solution.md`). The implementation lives in the desktop worktree, and the panel follows the existing session shell and settings visual language.

---

## 🚀 背景描述

桌面端（`apps/desktop`，Electron + React）是主要客户端，但程序演进（evolve）目前只能在 Web 界面或命令行里通过 `/evolve-design` 完成设计、启动和观察。evolve 是唯一一个在对话结束后仍在后台运行、并且会持续产生候选产物的能力：用户需要在一个界面里完成方案设计、确认检查点、实时观察搜索、查看候选与得分，并随时回到已结束的搜索。桌面端缺少这套入口和面板，用户必须切到 Web 才能使用。

本 issue 跟踪桌面端支持 evolve 的完整交付，覆盖设计入口、检查点、实时面板与结果查看，并以官方教程中的样例作为验收路径。

相关 issue：evolve 检查点的预算展示 #780、自然语言入口 #310、`/evolve` 文档 #55 / #567、桌面客户端交付 #400。

相关 PR：#715——为无法被要求停止思考的模型预留预算（关闭 #780）。检查点卡片展示的单次调用上限即来自该改动。

## 设计思路

- **人工确认开关（开始时选定）**：流程最开始提供一个开关，决定检查点是否需要人工确认。关闭时，Agent 一次跑完余下的检查点并直接启动搜索，中途不停下等待；开启时，每个检查点仍按下面的方式暂停等待确认。开关在设计开始前就确定，用户只需决定一次节奏，而不是在每个检查点重复决定。
- **对话优先**：不新增配置表单。`/evolve-design` 打开算法选择器与创建对话框，只收集两件人真正知道的事——想让什么变好、哪种搜索适合这个问题——然后把这句话作为命令送进对话；方案、评分卡与检查点仍由 Agent 在会话中完成。
- **检查点留在对话里**：需求、评测、规模、启动四个检查点以卡片形式出现在消息流中，用户在对话里确认或修改，不跳到另一个页面。
- **常驻会话书架**：会话头部下方一条细书架列出该会话的搜索（运行中与已结束）；关闭面板不会让运行中的搜索不可达，没有搜索的会话不显示任何东西。
- **结果驾驶舱**：面板按观察搜索的人真正会问的顺序回答——有没有变好（最优分数）、怎么变的（曲线）、试过什么（候选表）、为什么没选那个（检查器）。窄窗口时检查器变为覆盖在表格上的抽屉。
- **运行时安装前置**：首次安装 evolve 运行时在创建对话框内完成，而不是写完全部目标后才发现没装。
- **事件优先、轮询兜底**：优先订阅 evolve SSE 事件；流不可用时退回运行列表轮询，空闲会话不产生请求。

考虑过但未采用的方案：在桌面端内嵌 Web 页面（交互与状态处理被割裂，且会带上整份 Web 资源）；单开一个独立搜索窗口（搜索属于会话，独立窗口会让"回到会话"和"再开一个搜索"都变得别扭）。

## 涉及的公共 API

不新增公共 API。桌面端复用现有的 evolve REST/SSE 接口（运行时状态、初始化、运行列表与详情、候选、事件流），客户端封装在 `apps/desktop/src/api/evolve.ts`。共享类型 `EvolveRun` 与 evolve 事件来自 `packages/schema`，与 Web 端使用同一份定义。任何接口调整都必须保持 Web 端与命令行行为不变，并在本 issue 中说明。

## 与其他模块的关联

- `packages/schema`：evolve 运行与事件类型；桌面端不复制定义。
- 桌面端运行流水线：`run-stream` 的模型与 reducer 需要承载检查点与演进状态，同时不能打乱普通对话的文本归位。
- 国际化：新增文案同时进入 `text/zh.ts` 与 `text/en.ts`。
- Web 端演进面板读取同一份数据；两套界面之间的行为差异必须是有意为之并记录下来。
- 端到端测试：桌面 e2e 的 fixture 需要模拟的 evolve 运行时。

## 测试设计与测试计划

- **单元测试**：命令解析（`/evolve-design`、算法参数、带初始目标的命令）；运行状态与文案映射；候选归并与最优分数；书架折叠规则（运行中的搜索永不折叠）。
- **组件测试**：创建对话框的运行时安装与错误路径；检查点卡片；面板选择语义（点击一行填充检查器）；窄窗口抽屉。
- **端到端（`apps/desktop/e2e/evolve.spec.ts`，模拟运行时）**：从会话发起搜索 → 检查点 → 运行 → 实时更新 → 选择候选并查看检查器 → 停止；另外验证没有搜索的会话与改动前完全一致。
- **两个复杂数学冒烟用例**：（a）符号回归——从采样点恢复某非线性函数的闭式表达式，按拟合误差评分；（b）数值优化——改进某个数值例程的精度或耗时（例如 ODE 积分器或线性求解器），按与参考解的误差评分。两个用例的通过标准都是 evolve 正常触发、并能跑过若干节点（至少三次扩展且有候选记录），不要求完整跑完整个搜索。
- **回归**：Web 端演进面板与命令行行为不变；普通会话的文本归位、工具卡片与产物面板不受影响。

必须通过的命令：`pnpm check`（类型检查与单元测试）；`apps/desktop` 下的 `npm run typecheck` 与 `npm test`；桌面 e2e 套件。

## 验收标准

- [ ] 成功运行 evolve 介绍文档中的样例：在桌面端按 `docs/zh/domains/evolve-a-solution.md`（英文版 `docs/en/domains/evolve-a-solution.md`）完整走完一次 PUCT 搜索——设计检查点、启动、实时观察、结束并打开结果。
- [ ] UI 设计通过评审：创建对话框、检查点卡片、会话书架、结果面板均通过对照设计稿的评审，评审意见全部关闭。
- [ ] 没有搜索的会话在界面上与改动前完全一致。
- [ ] 必须通过的命令：`pnpm check`；`apps/desktop` 下的 `npm run typecheck` 与 `npm test`；桌面 e2e 套件。

## 补充信息

教程样例：`docs/zh/domains/evolve-a-solution.md`（英文 `docs/en/domains/evolve-a-solution.md`）。实现在桌面端工作树中进行，面板沿用现有的会话外壳与设置页视觉规范。

### Checklist

- [X] I have searched for related issues but did not get the expected help.
- [X] This bug has not been fixed in the latest version.
- [X] Please note that if your bug description lacks corresponding environment information and a minimal reproducible demo, it will be difficult for us to reproduce and resolve the issue, which will reduce the possibility of receiving feedback, or even lead to the issue being closed.

### 🐞 Detailed Description of the Problem

**What the user sees.** Two real-E2E evolve journeys click the send button and then wait forever for a Run that is never created. In both cases the product had already opened a **"Confirm evolution settings"** dialog, and nothing in the journey answers it.

**Evidence** (Nightly run [42907916462](https://github.com/openJiuwen-ai/sciencediscovery/actions/runs/42907916462), sha `4bb737c2`).

*Shard `research-8`, PUCT-COMPRESS (artifact `real-e2e-evidence-research-8`, id 13808780763).*

Page snapshot captured at failure (`error-context.md`) contains the dialog and an empty run area:

```yaml
- heading "What should we investigate?" [level=2]
- dialog "Confirm evolution settings":
    - text: Program evolution
    - heading "Confirm evolution settings" [level=2]
    - paragraph: 写一对处理文本的 compress/decompress：compress(text) -> bytes、 decompress(bytes) -> str。往返必须完全无损。只用标准库 —— 不许用 zlib、lzma
```

Its `stack.log` has **no `POST /api/sessions/<id>/messages` at all** — the only POSTs in the whole shard are setup and teardown:

```text
POST /api/models 201 Created
POST /api/projects 201 Created
POST /api/sessions/2a4f6a97-.../runs/current/cancel 200 OK
POST /cleanup/project 200 OK
```

Test error:

```text
Error: expect(received).toBeTruthy()  Received: undefined
  - Timeout 30000ms exceeded while waiting on the predicate
    at send (test/evolve-compression-real.spec.ts:100:31)
```

*Shard `research-6`, desktop /evolve-design (artifact `real-e2e-evidence-research-6`, id 13808301012).*

Journey report step 3 (`~程序演进实验~` with PUCT) fails after 123.9 s:

```text
Error: the command should create a persisted Run
  - Timeout 120000ms exceeded while waiting on the predicate
    at waitForNewRun (test/helpers/desktop-evolve.ts:377:73)
    at test/desktop-evolve-srbench-real.spec.ts:317:22
```

Its `stack.log` also contains no `POST /api/sessions/<id>/messages` (only `POST /api/inbox`, the workspace upload, `/api/sessions/.../runs/current/cancel` and `/cleanup/project`).

The journey reports for both shards say *"无 console 错误/警告，无失败请求"* — consistent with a dialog waiting for input rather than a failed request.

**Code.** The dialog is `apps/web/src/evolve/DirectionDialog.tsx` and, on desktop, `apps/desktop/src/views/evolve/EvolveCreateDialog.tsx`. The journeys that never answer it are `test/helpers/journeys.ts` (`sendUserMessage`), `test/helpers/desktop-evolve.ts:377` (`waitForNewRun`) and the two specs (`test/evolve-compression-real.spec.ts:100`, `test/desktop-evolve-srbench-real.spec.ts:317`).

**Why this needs a decision, not just a patch.** Two readings are both consistent with the evidence, and they need different fixes:

1. The confirmation dialog is intended product behaviour for starting an evolve search. Then both journeys are stale and must confirm the dialog (click the confirm button, then wait for the Run). Test-side fix only.
2. The dialog should not gate the first Run of a freshly created evolve Session. Then the product is wrong and the journeys are right.

The evidence above does not distinguish them; picking one is a product decision.

### Detailed Environment Information Description

- Repository: `openJiuwen-ai/sciencediscovery`, `main` at `4bb737c2fccc8b55471dfd08f4f58754c5981cb3`.
- Nightly (`profile: daily`) real E2E, run started 2026-11-10T21:44:15Z (2026-11-11 05:44 CST); shards `research-6` (desktop entry on 4178) and `research-8`.
- Stack: adapter 4410 → Node API 4510, runner 4411, memory-graph 17774, JiuwenSwarm backend, `E2E_LLM_MODEL=deepseek-flash`.
- Both cases are `@real @tier:l4 @sandbox:bubblewrap` and passed on the previous Nightly (2026-11-08, `c95f080`) — the commits between `c95f080` and `4bb737c` include the conversational-configuration work, which is where the dialog was introduced.

### Additional Information

The two shards are the only evolve cases in the real profile, so this dialog currently makes the whole evolve layer red. `research-1`, `-2`, `-3`, `-5` failed for unrelated reasons on the same run (model stream resets / a run-side error); they are not part of this report.

### Version Information

- `main` @ `4bb737c2fccc8b55471dfd08f4f58754c5981cb3`
- Nightly run 42907916462; artifacts `real-e2e-evidence-research-8` (13808780763), `real-e2e-evidence-research-6` (13808301012)

## 背景 / 输入

在 ScienceDiscovery 沙箱 / science-env 中复现 meK-means（Monod `mminference`）：

- 环境：`/opt/science-env/bin/python`
- 依赖：`monod==0.2.9.0`、`loompy`、`anndata`、较新的 `numpy`（≥2）

Case：`s43588-024-00689-2`；驱动脚本 `run.py`。

## 问题是什么

Monod 0.2.9.0 与 **numpy 2** 组合需要额外 shim 才能跑通作者路径，例如：

- `np.meshgrid` 返回值按 list 使用的兼容
- float bounds / `gridsize=[1,1]` 等调用约定修补

否则 Agent 卡在依赖/兼容调试，而不是论文复现本身。预装科学栈「开箱可跑作者代码」的承诺打折。

## 我们怎么规避的

在会话内自建/修补 `mekmeans-cpu` 路径与 shim（详见会话 `REPRODUCTION_REPORT.md` §3），再跑真实 loom。

## 期望应该是什么样

1. science-env（或官方 skill）对常见复现栈给出**钉死且测过的** monod/numpy/loompy 组合，或提供已知 shim 文档。
2. Agent 首次导入失败时，表面友好的「已知兼容问题 + 推荐 pin」提示，而不是长 traceback 试错。
3. 可选：NatureBench / 论文复现模板预装最小可跑镜像，与 brief 中的计算提示对齐。

closed_recent.author: HugoXK
closed_recent.body:
## Problem

The in-flight length-rejection fix (`#932`) adds `/\bis too long\b/i` to `isKnownClientInputError` (`services/api/src/http/error-classification.ts:30`). Any message containing that phrase is then answered `400` **and the message text is sent back to the client**.

Two messages in the tree match that pattern and embed a filesystem path, while the client does not need that path to understand the rejection:

- `packages/executor/src/runner-bundle.ts:76` and `:80` — `` `Runner bundle path is too long for tar: ${file.path}` ``
- `packages/executor/src/remote-compute.ts:777` — `` `The remote data directory path is too long for a Unix socket: ${prepared.dataDir}` ``

Before `#932` both answered `500 {"error":"Internal server error"}` and the text stayed hidden. After it they answer `400` with the path in the body.

## Severity

Low, not a gate: the caller is already authenticated, the path has to be pathological (long enough to trip the length check), and it cannot be produced on demand. Reported by Security while reviewing `#932` at `8b4c124caf`.

## Suggested fix

Anchor the pattern to the end of the message:

```diff
-/\bis too long\b/i
+/\bis too long$/i
```

Every message the fix intends to reclassify ends with the phrase, so the anchor keeps them all and drops the executor ones. The eight legitimate ones are:

- `The LLM API token is too long`
- `The proxy URL is too long`
- `neo4jHttp is too long`
- `neo4jUser is too long`
- `The Neo4j password is too long`
- `Model ID is too long`
- `The stored runnerToken is too long`
- `pip indexUrl is too long` (`packages/schema/src/environment.ts:393`; added after Security's review of the first draft of this issue, which listed only seven)

## Acceptance

1. A unit test pins that the two executor messages above are **not** client input (a negative assertion): they must not become `400`-with-text.
2. All eight length messages listed above still answer `400` with their text. Pin them by name rather than by count, so a future narrowing of the pattern cannot silently drop one.
3. No change to the `500` path for anything else.

## Not for the current sprint window

`#932` must not be re-tipped for this: pushing a new tip dismisses the approval already recorded on it. This issue is the follow-up and is intentionally parked until after the window.

closed_recent.author: HugoXK
closed_recent.body:
Implementation: ScienceDiscovery (ours) — PR follows within 24h. Do not pick up without a `pickup-ok` comment on this issue.

Written-by: ScienceDiscovery Product
Claimed-by: ScienceDiscovery Product
Claim-Id: 5fcbd6c7878d49f0af0d49f904d6851f
Branch: dev/930-bug-a-length-rejection-answers-500-inter
Base: 2908e9e8bb4f
At: 2026-11-05T13:49:58Z

## What happens

A provider form accepts a pasted API token of any length, and the API answers an over-long one with a bare internal error instead of naming the field:

```
POST /api/providers/preview-models
{"name":"Probe provider","baseUrl":"https://example.test/v1","apiProtocol":"openai-chat-completions","apiToken":"<20 000 chars>"}

HTTP 500 {"error":"Internal server error"}
```

The very same validator rejects the empty-token case correctly, so one form gets two different failure shapes for two client mistakes:

```
POST … {"apiToken":""}      → 400  "The LLM API token cannot be empty"
POST … {"apiToken":"k"×20000} → 500  "Internal server error"
```

The `500` also reaches the user as the generic error surface, so the form cannot say which field to shorten.

## What is expected

`400` with the validation message the store already produced: `{"error":"The LLM API token is too long"}`. The same holds for the other length limits below — they are client input mistakes and must answer 400, not 500.

## Where it comes from

- The throw: `services/api/src/store/secrets.ts:194-199` — `normalizeApiToken` throws plain `new Error("The LLM API token is too long")` when the trimmed token exceeds 16 384 characters (`"…cannot be empty"` on the line above matches a known pattern, which is why only the length case leaks).
- The route: `services/api/src/http/index.ts:2174-2181` (`POST /api/providers/preview-models` → `validateLiveProvider` → `normalizeApiToken`) and `POST /api/providers` → `store.createProvider`, which normalizes the same token.
- The classification: `services/api/src/http/error-classification.ts:20-32` lists the legacy messages that stay 400 (`is required`, `must`, `cannot`, `does not match`, `invalid`, …) and has no pattern for a length rejection, so `services/api/src/http/index.ts:3944` falls through to the 500 branch at `:3946`.

Seven sites share this exact shape today, all of them client-supplied strings:

| site | message |
| --- | --- |
| `services/api/src/store/secrets.ts:198` | `The LLM API token is too long` |
| `services/api/src/store/settings.ts:420` | `The proxy URL is too long` |
| `services/api/src/store/settings.ts:348` | `neo4jHttp is too long` |
| `services/api/src/store/settings.ts:351` | `neo4jUser is too long` |
| `services/api/src/store.ts:3012` | `The Neo4j password is too long` |
| `services/api/src/store.ts:3858` | `Model ID is too long` |
| `services/api/src/store.ts:5533` | `The stored ${kind} is too long` (remote-host credential) |

`grep -rn "too long" services/api/src --include=*.ts | grep -v .test.` finds nothing else that throws: the remaining hits are prompt text (`session-naming.ts:26`, `:198`), comments, and `configuration/schema-normalizer.ts:86/104` which goes through `invalid()` and is already classified.

## Failing test (reproduce before the fix)

Any harness that starts the real API server works; the probe below reuses the isolated fixture style of `services/api/src/configuration/http.integration.test.ts` (temp data dir, provider stub, `createApiServer`), then makes one request:

```ts
// temporary probe, not committed
const f = await fixture(context);
const result = await f.call("/api/providers/preview-models", {
  name: "Probe provider", baseUrl: "https://example.test/v1", apiProtocol: "openai-chat-completions",
  apiToken: "k".repeat(20_000),
}, "POST");
assert.equal(result.status, 400, `status ${result.status}: ${result.text}`);
```

Command and observed output:

```
$ cd services/api && node --import tsx --test src/configuration/zz-token-too-long-probe.test.ts
# STATUS 500 TEXT {"error":"Internal server error"}
not ok 1 - probe: an over-long provider API token is a client error, not a 500
  error: |- status 500: {"error":"Internal server error"}
# tests 1
# pass 0
# fail 1
```

## Environment

- `main` @ `7057aaf65f2c81d0b0af64a449d9259c62128673`
- node `v22`; from `services/api`: `node --import tsx --test src/<file>`
- the request is a normal authenticated call with a JSON body well under the 10 MB request cap, so the body reader is not involved.

## Smallest mergeable slice

One source line, one test file:

1. `services/api/src/http/error-classification.ts` — add `/\bis too long\b/i` to the pattern list. That is the whole fix, and it converts all seven sites above from 500 to 400 with their original message preserved, without touching the modules that throw.
2. `services/api/src/http/error-classification.test.ts` — extend the existing table so the classifier is pinned on this shape: `The LLM API token is too long`, `The proxy URL is too long`, `Model ID is too long`, `The stored runnerToken is too long` are client input; a message that merely mentions length without the validation shape (e.g. `Database invariant failed`) stays 500.

Do not add a new error code, do not change `normalizeApiToken` or any limit value, and do not touch the throw sites — this is a classification fix, not a validation change. `POST /api/providers` and `preview-models` both reach the same normalizer, so the route assertion can use either.

## Acceptance

- The probe passes: an over-long `apiToken` answers `400` with `{"error":"The LLM API token is too long"}`.
- An empty `apiToken` still answers `400` with its existing message, and the classifier's existing eight patterns still classify as before (`apps` tests that rely on them keep passing).
- A genuinely internal failure still answers `500`: `isKnownClientInputError(new Error("Database invariant failed"))` stays false and the existing `http/error-classification.test.ts` assertion on it is unchanged.
- The other six length messages are covered by the classifier unit test, so a future endpoint that throws one gets the same 400 without another special case.

## Why this is not a duplicate

- No open pull request touches `services/api/src/http/error-classification.ts` (checked every open PR's file list); `#697` touches `services/api/src/store/secrets.ts` for a Windows platform change and does not alter this path.
- `#884` (binary artifact diff) and `#877` (artifact provenance/diff) are the same *symptom class* on different endpoints and are being fixed endpoint-locally; this one is the shared classifier, and fixing it does not change their behaviour.
- Issue search for a length-limit 500 (`too long`, `Internal server error` + validation, `client error 400 instead of 500`) returns no issue covering a length rejection.

closed_recent.author: HugoXK
closed_recent.body:
## Summary

`scripts/binary-release/fetch-runtime.mjs` reads the whole response with `response.arrayBuffer()` and has no progress guard. Two shapes therefore end in the caller's generic timeout with nothing a reader can act on:

1. **200, then nothing.** The pinned CPython download answers `200` and sends zero bytes: in #909 a bare `node fetch` got `status 200` in 1.1 s and then 0 bytes for 60 s before aborting.
2. **A trickle.** The same 34,184,519-byte asset streams at 9–31 KB/s (three independent samples: 9,445 / 25,735 / 18,312 B/s; `curl -L` delivered 818,498 bytes in 45 s). `ST`'s per-file setup hook is then killed by the journey's own 300 s `execFile` cap, and the job log only shows `NODE_HOOK_OR_COLLECTION_FAILED` and `##[error]Process completed with exit code 1` (run `41999191976`, job `127150383484`).

## What it should do

The downloader should produce **one readable line** instead of being killed:

```
external asset download too slow: 223.7 KB in 5.1 s (44.3 KB/s, below the 128.0 KB/s floor): https://github.com/astral-sh/python-build-standalone/releases/download/20260805/cpython-3.12.13+20260805-x86_64-unknown-linux-gnu-install_only_stripped.tar.gz
```

That line above is a real reading from a cold-cache run on 2026-11-09 (`BINARY_DOWNLOAD_MIN_BYTES_PER_SECOND=131072`, exit 1 after 7.3 s), from the prototype described below.

## Proposed shape (prototype removed from #1025 on purpose)

- Stream the response instead of buffering it blindly, so progress is visible.
- `BINARY_DOWNLOAD_STALL_MS` (default `30000`): fail when no bytes arrive for that long.
- `BINARY_DOWNLOAD_MIN_BYTES_PER_SECOND` (default `0`, opt-in per job): once 512 KiB or 5 s of body has arrived, fail when the average rate is below the floor. A floor of 128 KB/s is what the `ST` job would set; the binary build keeps the default because its own budget is 90 minutes and a slow but working link should keep waiting.
- A 100 ms interval watchdog plus an `AbortController`, with every `await` (`fetch` and `reader.read()`) racing the guard, so a stalled read is unblocked even when a fetch implementation ignores the abort signal.
- Both guards collapse into the single `external asset download too slow: …` line.

## Evidence collected while prototyping

- Two new cases in `scripts/binary-release/fetch-runtime.test.mjs` (a stalled stream, and a rate below the floor) failed against the current downloader — `still waiting after 3 s`, i.e. an unbounded read — and passed once the guard existed: `# tests 9 / # pass 9 / # fail 0`.
- The cold-cache run above printed the intended line and exited within seconds instead of waiting for the 300 s cap.
- A third case pinned that a verified local archive is reused with zero requests, including when a remote cache URL is configured (that property already holds; the case is a regression guard).

## Why this is a separate issue and not #909's option 3

#909's option 3 was allowed to merge in `#1025` only as "the downloader's own single line of error text". This guard is a behaviour change in the downloader — two new environment knobs, a streaming reader, a watchdog and an abort race — so it does not qualify for that carve-out. It needs its own decision and review; the prototype was removed from `#1025`, which now carries option 1 (the runtime cache) only.

## Not implemented

Nothing in this issue is implemented, and no pull request is open for it.
closed_recent.title: [Bug] a stalled or sub-rate runtime download should fail with one readable line, not the caller's timeout

closed_recent.body:
## Checklist

- [x] I have searched for related issues but did not get the expected help.
- [x] This bug has not been fixed in the latest version.
- [x] Please note that if your bug description lacks corresponding environment information and a minimal reproducible demo, it will be difficult for us to reproduce and resolve the issue, which will reduce the possibility of receiving feedback, or even lead to the issue being closed.

## 🐞 Detailed Description of the Problem

A research package does **not** capture the session's **evolve runs**. The package carries only the evolve result files (`evolve/<runId>/candidate.py`, because they are ordinary artifacts), so after import the session's evolve content is gone: `GET /api/evolve/runs?sessionId=…` returns an empty list, and the Evolve panel has nothing to show — no search tree, no candidate scores, no token/budget record, no baseline, no candidate history.

Importing an evolve session back therefore does **not** reproduce the evolve content, which is exactly what a user expects from “导出会话 → 导入会话” when the session used `/evolve-design`.

### Evidence

Source session `fe1ef6bf-e61a-49c2-a62f-75904a37a375` (project `299bc26a-6e56-46d7-a977-5d4e3c264aaa`), build `c95f080a`:

```text
source evolve runs:
  83cbb6de  status=succeeded candidates=20 tokens=171084
  a539ffc0  status=succeeded candidates=20 tokens=95575
source artifacts:
  evolve/83cbb6de/candidate.py  v2
  evolve/a539ffc0/candidate.py  v2
```

Exported with 必要导出 (`level=necessary`, 109,724-byte package) and imported into a fresh project:

```text
records.json top-level keys:
  ["exportLevel","exportProfile","project","sessions","artifacts",
   "environmentRevisions","versionObjects","memoryGraph"]
records keys containing "evolv": []          ← no evolve dimension at all

imported session 4e9d0664-ae6c-499a-b154-5343791153f9:
  GET /api/evolve/runs?sessionId=4e9d0664…  → []        (0 runs)
  artifacts                                 → evolve/83cbb6de/candidate.py v2,
                                              evolve/a539ffc0/candidate.py v2   (restored)
```

So the candidate files survive as artifacts while the run records — the thing that makes them meaningful — do not.

Root cause in code: `services/api/src/research-snapshots.ts` builds `records` as `{ exportLevel, exportProfile, project, sessions, artifacts, environmentRevisions, versionObjects, memoryGraph|memoryGraphSummary }`. The session record (`services/api/src/research-package-history.ts`) exports `executionRuns`, `messages`, `runs`, `workspace`, `validations`, `trajectory`, … but nothing from `store.dataDir/evolution/*` (runs / ledger / results / programs). `countExport(...)` likewise has no evolve counter, which is why the preview's included/omitted numbers never mention evolve content either.

### Steps to reproduce

1. Run an evolve-design case so the session has one or two evolve runs (each with candidates and a candidate.py artifact).
2. 更多会话操作 → 导出会话 → 必要导出 (or 完整导出), save the package.
3. Import the package into a new project.
4. Open the imported session: the messages and the `evolve/<runId>/candidate.py` artifacts are there, but the Evolve panel and `GET /api/evolve/runs?sessionId=…` show nothing.

### Expected

After importing a session that used evolve, the imported (read-only) snapshot shows the same evolve runs as the source: run id, algorithm, status, candidate count, scores/best candidate, token/cost budget and baseline; and continuing research from it keeps that evolve content available. If a run cannot be reproduced byte-for-byte, the import should at least list it as an explicit omission instead of silently dropping it.

### Observed

- `records` has no evolve section; the import receipt lists no evolve omission either, so the loss is silent.
- Imported session reports zero evolve runs; only `evolve/<runId>/candidate.py` artifacts remain.

## Detailed Environment Information Description

```text
Host        Windows 11 26200 + WSL2 Ubuntu 24.04, local source checkout
Mode        ./scripts/start-stack.sh --mode local (adapter :4310, API :4410, runner :4311, evolve sidecar, memory-graph :17674)
Node v22.23.4, pnpm 11.1.2, uv 0.13.7, Python 3.12
Model       glm-5.2 over an OpenAI-compatible relay
Case        docs/zh/domains/evolve-a-solution.md (compress/decompress, stdlib only)
```

## Additional Information

Science memory **is** carried: the same necessary package contains `memoryGraph` with 20 nodes / 19 relationships, and after import the snapshot reports the same 20/19 (verified through the export preview of the imported session). So the gap is specific to evolve.

Related: #995 (import opens two sessions), #803 (feature), and the export-blocking issue filed separately for sessions whose executions are stuck in recovery. A separate observation from the same test: 完整导出 with both “包含完整轨迹详情” and “包含完整科学记忆图谱” fails for this session with `Research package exceeds the archive size limit` (`MAX_TOTAL_BYTES = 512 MB` in `packages/research-package/src/index.ts`), while plain 完整导出 succeeds (20.2 MB compressed, 933 MB estimated uncompressed).

## Version Information

- Repository: `openJiuwen-ai/sciencediscovery`
- Tested commit: `c95f080a6c3b1bb5e020808b5114e1894148422d` (main, 2026-11-08T18:06:21Z)

closed_recent.author: yuanzhou75
closed_recent.body:
### Checklist

- [X] I have searched for related issues but did not get the expected help.
- [X] This bug has not been fixed in the latest version.
- [X] Please note that if your bug description lacks corresponding environment information and a minimal reproducible demo, it will be difficult for us to reproduce and resolve the issue, which will reduce the possibility of receiving feedback, or even lead to the issue being closed.

### 🐞 Detailed Description of the Problem

**What the user sees.** Nightly real E2E shard `research-12` runs a 46-minute case to completion — `integration: passed`, `total_score: 68.75`, `generation_duration_ms: 2495109` — and then fails in teardown with:

```text
Error: apiRequestContext.fetch: connect ECONNREFUSED 127.0.0.1:4410
```

Nothing was listening on 4410 any more, because the API process behind the adapter had just aborted on V8 heap exhaustion.

**Evidence of the abort.** From the shard's `stack.log` (artifact `real-e2e-evidence-research-12`, Nightly run [42519625781](https://github.com/openJiuwen-ai/sciencediscovery/actions/runs/42519625781), sha `c95f080`):

```text
<--- Last few GCs --->

[5236:0xb123000]  2641988 ms: Scavenge (interleaved) 4020.2 (4116.5) -> 4002.8 (4111.7) MB, pooled: 6 MB, 11.37 / 0.01 ms  (average mu = 0.194, current mu = 0.113) allocation failure;
[5236:0xb123000]  2642420 ms: Mark-Compact 4029.7 (4126.5) -> 3989.8 (4101.4) MB, pooled: 6 MB, 412.69 / 0.01 ms  (average mu = 0.159, current mu = 0.122) task; scavenge might not succeed

FATAL ERROR: Ineffective mark-compacts near heap limit Allocation failed - JavaScript heap out of memory
...
Aborted (core dumped)
[ELIFECYCLE] Command failed with exit code 134.
```

- The heap dies at **4126.5 MB**, i.e. the Node default old-space limit: no launch path passes `--max-old-space-size` or `NODE_OPTIONS` (`services/api/package.json:9`, `scripts/start-stack.mjs`, `scripts/start-stack.sh`), and nothing in `services/api/src` samples `process.memoryUsage()` or RSS, so the abort arrives with no warning.
- Process uptime at the abort is **2,641,988 ms (~44 min)**, the length of the real case itself.
- After the abort every proxied call turns into `ConnectError` → 502 (`/health`, `/api/models`, `/api/sessions/...`), the adapter shuts down, and teardown cannot reach 4410.

**What this issue previously blamed, and why that was wrong.** An earlier revision named the project plugin event stream (`GET /api/projects/:id/plugins/events`, the adapter's longest-lived request in that run: `phase=body`, `elapsed_ms=2685438`) as the suspected allocation source. That correlation is not a cause and the attribution is withdrawn (review comment [6731433551](https://github.com/openJiuwen-ai/sciencediscovery/issues/1011#issuecomment-6731433551)):

- that response writes one `event: changed` frame per `PluginControl.changed()` notification plus a `: heartbeat` every 15 s (`services/api/src/plugins/http.ts:23-38`);
- `PluginControl.changed()` is invoked only from settings, project and session mutations — `store.ts:2452,2458,2463,3383,3565,3578,3590,3626,3651,6251` — not per model token or per tool step;
- `control.snapshot(scope)` (`plugins/control.ts:65-69`) is a JSON digest plus a `structuredClone` of the installed plugin list: transient and collectable, and its size does not grow with session length.

So the stream's own writes are kilobytes over 44 minutes. Coalescing frames or caching the snapshot would leave the abort unchanged.

**Where the heap can actually go** (verified at `c95f080`): the API still materialises whole run streams on read paths that are exercised during a long session.

1. `listRunStreamEvents` (`services/api/src/store.ts:6950-6968`) pushes the whole main-run array and every line of the requested stream into `records[]` and only then filters by `after` and sorts — so a replay or reconnect *with* a cursor still allocates the entire stream, twice (array + parsed lines).
2. `exportRunStreams` (`store.ts:6979-6986`) `Promise.all`s that over **every** stream of the run, so the allocations overlap.
3. The plan plugin's `state` query (`services/api/src/plugins/control.ts:114-122`) calls `listRunStreamEvents` **without** `after`, only to keep the `plan.updated` events.
4. `sessionTrajectory` (`services/api/src/trajectory.ts:17-47`) pushes every event of every run and of every subagent/tool stream into a single `events[]` before returning.
5. The file already treats this class as dangerous: `store.ts:7052-7056` says *"A run's stream can reach hundreds of MB. Reading it whole to find the tail allocated the file twice (one string plus the split array) and could exhaust the heap before the process served a single request"* — yet `readStreamLines` (`store.ts:7069-7073`) still accumulates the whole file for the read paths above.

**Missing measurement.** There is no heap profile, RSS/`process.memoryUsage()` timeline, per-stream byte size, or record of which routes were in flight at the abort; the GC lines exist only in the artifact, not in the job log. Without that, the items above stay the better-supported suspects rather than a proven cause, and any fix is unverifiable.

**Expected.**

1. Give the stream read paths a real cursor: filter by `after` **while** streaming lines, never building the whole array; bound or serialise `exportRunStreams`.
2. Let the plan plugin query read only the sequence range it needs, or keep a compact `plan.updated` index instead of the full stream.
3. Bound `sessionTrajectory`: paginate, or stream it to the response.
4. Make the heap budget explicit and observable on every launch path: `--max-old-space-size`, periodic `process.memoryUsage()` logging, and a warning/fatal path before V8 kills the process. A larger cap alone only delays the abort.
5. Land the measurement first (heap snapshot near the limit via `--heapsnapshot-near-heap-limit=1`, an RSS timeline, and the session's stream file sizes), so the fix can be shown to work.

**Impact.** This is not a case-level failure: the case delivered and scored. The gate goes red because teardown talks to a dead process, and `merge-gate` / `Report the outcome` then fail the whole Nightly. The same abort also kills a real user's 46-minute session.

### Detailed Environment Information Description

- Repository: `openJiuwen-ai/sciencediscovery`, `main` at `c95f080a6c3b1bb5e020808b5114e1894148422d`; the read paths above are unchanged at `578a9505` (one desktop commit later).
- GitHub Actions `ubuntu-latest` runner, 15.6 GiB RAM, 4 CPUs; Nightly (`profile: daily`) real E2E, shard `research-12`, started 2026-11-08T20:20:32Z (2026-11-09 04:20 CST).
- Stack: adapter (Python/uvicorn) on `127.0.0.1:4410` in front of the Node API on `4510`, runner on `4411`, memory-graph on `17774`, JiuwenSwarm backend, `E2E_LLM_MODEL=deepseek-flash`.
- Case: `TC-E2E-01 research team with custom Specialist and MCP signoff`, 46.1 min.

### Additional Information

**Revision note.** The body was revised after review comment [6731433551](https://github.com/openJiuwen-ai/sciencediscovery/issues/1011#issuecomment-6731433551): the plugin SSE handler is withdrawn as the target, whole-stream materialisation is promoted to the leading suspect, the missing measurement is stated instead of assumed, and the scope is narrowed to the heap abort.

**Scope.** This issue is the heap abort only. The 89 pending `GET /api/projects/:id/research-package/preview` requests seen in shard `research-8` are not shown to share this cause and are not part of the fix; the teardown behaviour when the API is already dead stays with #1012.

Related: #1012 (the same Nightly, shard `research-8`: an execution stuck in `unknown` making cancel and project delete never return).

### Version Information

- `main` @ `c95f080a6c3b1bb5e020808b5114e1894148422d`
- Nightly run 42519625781 (2026-11-08T20:20:32Z), shard `research-12`, artifact `real-e2e-evidence-research-12` (artifact id 13638505632)

Once a candidate's score reaches `1.0` (goal achieved), the search keeps expanding new nodes until the expansion budget is exhausted. Observed, from the evolution tree in the web UI: - Header: `扩展次数 23/24`, `深度 5`, `Token 608361` - Nodes `#1`, `#15`, `#18` all scored `1.000`, and `#15` is marked as the current best - After `#15` reached `1.000`, the run still produced and expanded `#16`–`#23` (several of them `没跑起来`) - The best-score curve keeps adding points after the line reaches `1.0` - The run terminates at the expansion cap (`23/24`), not because the target was solved ### Expected When any node reaches the goal (score `1.0`, i.e. at or above the solved threshold), the whole evolution tree should stop: - no further expansions are scheduled, neither from the winning branch nor from any other branch - the run ends with a solved / target-reached stop reason instead of the expansion cap - the tree is left as it is at that point ### Steps to Reproduce 1. Start an evolution run whose goal can be fully satisfied (target score `1.0`). 2. Let any candidate reach `1.0`. 3. Watch the evolution tree panel. Actual: new nodes keep being expanded after a `1.0` candidate exists, and the run only ends at the expansion budget. ### Additional Context - The scorecard already carries a `solvedThreshold` (`SOLVED_THRESHOLD_BY_SCORING` in `@sciencediscovery/schema`) and `search_finished` carries a `stopReason`, so the search is expected to end on the solved condition rather than only on the cap. - In this run three nodes reached `1.000`, yet the stop reason was the expansion cap. - I can provide the run event log (`seeded` / `expanded` / `search_finished`) if needed. ### Detailed Environment Information - Web UI, evolution tree view, Chromium on Windows 11 - Repository `main` @ `face1d40` (2026-11-06) - Run settings: expansion budget `24`, depth `5`, token usage `608361` ### Additional Information Screenshot of the evolution tree and the candidate list is attached below. ### Version Information `main` @ `face1d40` (2026-11-06); reproduced on the current web build. --- ## 中文 ### 检查项 - [x] 已搜索相关 issue，未找到有效帮助。 - [x] 该问题在最新版本中仍未修复。 ### 问题详细描述 进化功能在完成给定目标后不会主动停止。当某个候选节点的分数达到 `1.0`（即目标已达成）后，搜索仍会继续扩展新节点，直到扩展次数预算耗尽。 实际表现（来自 Web 端进化树）： - 顶部统计：`扩展次数 23/24`、`深度 5`、`Token 608361` - 节点 `#1`、`#15`、`#18` 均为 `1.000`，`#15` 被标记为当前最优 - `#15` 达到 `1.000` 后，仍继续生成并扩展 `#16`–`#23`（其中多个为“没跑起来”） - 最优分数曲线在达到 `1.0` 之后仍继续产生新点 - 运行以扩展次数上限（`23/24`）结束，而不是因为目标已达成 ### 预期结果 当任一节点达到目标（分数 `1.0`，达到或超过 solved 阈值）时，整棵进化树应全部停止： - 无论最优分支还是其他分支，都不再产生新的扩展 - 运行应以“已解决 / 目标达成”结束，而不是以扩展次数上限结束 - 树保持当时的状态不再变化 ### 复现步骤 1. 启动一个目标可完全满足（目标分数 `1.0`）的进化任务。 2. 等待任一候选节点达到 `1.0`。 3. 观察进化树面板。 实际结果：已存在 `1.0` 节点后仍继续扩展新节点，运行只在扩展预算耗尽时结束。 ### 补充信息 - 评分卡已带 `solvedThreshold`（`@sciencediscovery/schema` 中的 `SOLVED_THRESHOLD_BY_SCORING`），`search_finished` 也带 `stopReason`，说明搜索本应在 solved 条件上结束。 - 本次运行中有三个节点达到 `1.000`，但停止原因仍是扩展上限。 - 如需要，我可以提供运行事件日志（`seeded` / `expanded` / `search_finished`）。 ### 环境信息 - Web 界面，进化树视图，Windows 11 + Chromium - 仓库 `main` @ `face1d40`（2026-11-06） - 运行配置：扩展预算 `24`，深度 `5`，Token `608361` ### 其他补充 进化树与候选流水截图见下方 ### 版本信息 `main` @ `face1d40`（2026-11-06）；在最新 Web 构建上复现。
