closed_recent.body:
### Checklist

- [x] I have searched for related issues but did not get the expected help.
- [x] This bug has not been fixed in the latest version.
- [x] The description below includes the environment details and the request log needed to reproduce the failure on a real installation.

### 🐞 Detailed Description of the Problem

**What the user sees.** On Windows, launching ScienceDiscovery 0.3.0 opens a maximized window with no content — a full-screen white page. Clicking the desktop icon again does not recover it: the new process exits immediately because it does not acquire the single-instance lock, and every later launch does the same. Only killing the shell process that still owns the lock lets the app start again — and it then goes white again within a few minutes once a session is open.

**What is actually failing.** The local API process (`services/api`, the Node process behind the adapter) dies of V8 heap exhaustion while research-package previews are being warmed in the background. The shell's stack supervisor (`scripts/start-stack.mjs`) sees the API child exit and tears down the adapter and the sidecars, so the UI origin on `127.0.0.1:4310` is gone while the Electron window stays alive and keeps the single-instance lock. A relaunch therefore exits as a "second instance" before any window exists, and the user has no way back into the app.

The shell log from the shipped 0.3.0 build shows this sequence twice:

```text
# crash on an already-running shell
[stack:err] FATAL ERROR: MarkCompactCollector: young object promotion failed Allocation failed - JavaScript heap out of memory
# heap at the abort: 3832.9 (3867.4) MB

# cold start, no export dialog opened by the user, crash after 284 s
[20056:00004F200011C000] 284002 ms: Scavenge 3775.5 (3806.8) -> 3730.9 (3784.6) MB ...
FATAL ERROR: MarkCompactCollector: young object promotion failed Allocation failed - JavaScript heap out of memory
```

After each crash, every new launch exits before creating a window:

```text
second instance: single-instance lock not acquired; exiting so the first instance stays the only one
loadUi: ui origin not answering within 30s; loading anyway (did-fail-load retry is the backstop)
```

The window state is restored as maximized, so "loading anyway" is what the user experiences as a full-screen white window.

**What produced the crash.** In the same cold-start run, the stack log shows ordinary session browsing followed by repeated full package builds. All timestamps below are from one run; IDs are redacted:

- `GET /api/sessions/<id>` for several different sessions (each of these calls `exportPreviews.watch(...)` on the server);
- **18** `POST /internal/research-package/export` calls (the memory-graph snapshot request issued once per `buildResearchPackageInput`) between 03:27:21Z and 03:30:38Z;
- `research-package/preview?level=necessary&includeFullTrajectory=0&includeFullMemoryGraph=0` at 03:30:23Z, and `level=complete&includeFullTrajectory=0&includeFullMemoryGraph=0` at 03:30:33Z;
- `FATAL ERROR ... JavaScript heap out of memory` at 03:31:35Z, 284 s after the stack started.

**Why the background warming is so heavy (confirmed in the installed build).**

1. `GET /api/sessions/:id` calls `exportPreviews.watch(projectId, sessionId)`. `watch()` calls `warm()`, and `warm()` calls `defaults()`, which computes **five** preview profiles per session: `necessary`; `complete`; `complete + full trajectory`; `complete + full memory graph`; `complete + both`. A plain session read is therefore enough to start five full export builds.
2. Every profile runs `buildResearchPackageInput` from scratch. For every session in the dependency closure it materialises all messages, all runs, **every event of every run stream**, workspace files and provenance, all artifact versions, reviews and audit tasks, export history, claims and evidence, plus a memory-graph snapshot. The `necessary` filter is applied **after** this load, so the "small" profile pays the full materialisation cost.
3. `sessionTrajectory` reads the same run streams a second time to build the trajectory index. `complete + full trajectory` then hydrates every trajectory detail into a single array.
4. The preview path only avoids reading CAS payload bytes. Every metadata object above is still resident at the same time.
5. Builds are serialised on one queue, so the five profiles run back to back and the previous build's garbage has not been collected when the next one starts. `tick()` repeats the warm for watched sessions every 3 s.
6. No launch path sets `--max-old-space-size` or `NODE_OPTIONS`, so the process aborts at the Node default old-space limit (about 4 GB).

On this installation (about 2.7 GB of project data and 3 GB of versioning/CAS data), two preview profiles raised the API process from about 164 MB to about 949 MB of private bytes, and a third request for `complete + includeFullTrajectory=1` killed it. That is consistent with the 4–5 minute crash above.

**What I expected.** Opening the app and browsing sessions should not start a full export build. Preview work should be bounded, should run when the user opens the export dialog, and a dead API should not leave the desktop shell stuck on a white window that cannot be relaunched.

**Suggested direction.**

- Do not warm previews from `GET /api/sessions/:id`; warm on export-dialog open only, and at most one profile at a time.
- Apply the `necessary` filter while streaming, or before loading run streams, and make run-stream reads cursor-based (the same direction as #1011).
- Skip the warm when the revision is unchanged (the cache key exists, but the first warm of each revision still runs five builds).
- Give the shell a failure path: if the stack dies while the window is open, surface an actionable error and allow a restart instead of holding the single-instance lock over a dead origin.
- Make the heap budget explicit and observable on every launch path.

### Detailed Environment Information Description

- OS: Windows 10 Pro 10.0.19045, x64.
- ScienceDiscovery desktop 0.3.0 (win-x64 installer), local mode via `start-stack.mjs --mode local --no-node-build`. No `NODE_OPTIONS` or `--max-old-space-size` in the environment or in the launch scripts.
- Data directory: about 2.7 GB of projects, 3 GB of versioning/CAS, 38 MB of run-event streams. The project involved contains several sessions, including a long-running session with tool and subagent streams.
- The failure was reproduced twice: once on a shell that had already been running, and once from a cold start, without opening the export dialog in either case.

### Additional Information

- Related but not duplicates: #1011 reports the same class of heap growth in a long real session, but its user-visible symptom is teardown `ECONNREFUSED`; the trigger reported here is preview warming on a plain session read, and the symptom is a white window that cannot be relaunched. #1079 / #1083 report a failed preview for `complete + includeFullTrajectory`; on this installation that exact request kills the API instead of returning 404. #1024 covers the export dialog redesign; this issue is about the runtime cost behind the preview.
- The analysis was done against the shipped 0.3.0 build, so file/line locations should be confirmed against `main`.
- Session and project identifiers and local paths are redacted on purpose.

### Version Information

- ScienceDiscovery 0.3.0.0 (win-x64), build dated 2026-11-10.
- Electron/Node as shipped with that installer; the aborts occurred at 3.8–4.1 GB of V8 heap, the default old-space limit.

closed_recent.author: HugoXK
closed_recent.body:
## Summary

`packages/data-source/src/source-health.test.ts` gives its fault injection a wall-clock budget of about `200 ms` (`200` iterations at `1 ms`). On a busy runner that budget is exhausted before the injected fault lands, the case fails with `Timed out waiting for local fault injection`, and because `UT` is one of the jobs `merge-gate` aggregates, an unrelated pull request turns red on the only required status check in this repository.

Two pull requests were hit by the same identity in two different time windows today, and the same file passes in a normal run.

## Failing identity

```text
packages/data-source/src/source-health.test.ts::parallel 429 callers share cooldown, drain their queue and do not retry inside one slot@linux/amd64
message: "Timed out waiting for local fault injection"
```

## Evidence

**Hit 1 — `#872`**, `UT` job `126735548839`, run [`41875320473`](https://github.com/openJiuwen-ai/sciencediscovery/actions/runs/41875320473), read from the job's uploaded `ut-results` artifact (`group-227/worker-1-events.jsonl`; the job log itself only carries `Run`/`Done` lines). Group summary `planned 16 / executed 16 / passed 15 / failed 1`; whole layer `planned 6279 / executed 6279 / passed 6278 / failed 1`.

**Hit 2 — `#878`**, `UT` job `126741018427`, same identity, another window.

**Control — the same file passing**, `UT` job `126822084143` (`2026-11-04T19:54:21Z`): `Run 229/555: packages/data-source/src/source-health.test.ts (16)` → `Done (6210ms)`, layer `{"status":"PASS","planned":6281,"passed":6281,"failed":0}`.

Neither pull request touches `packages/data-source`: `#872` changes four files under `apps/web`, `#878` changes `apps/web` only. So the failing identity is unreachable from either diff.

## Cause

`packages/data-source/src/source-health.test.ts:98-101` polls for the first of 12 concurrent callers to observe the injected fault:

```ts
// ~200 iterations × 1 ms ≈ 200 ms total
```

When the event loop is loaded (parallel `UT` workers, coverage instrumentation), `200 ms` is not enough for the fault to be observed, and the wait falls through to `assert.fail("Timed out waiting for local fault injection")`. The product behaviour is correct; the budget is what fails.

## Effect

Any pull request can be blocked by this, and a re-run only helps if the runner happens to be less loaded. Contributors cannot re-run: `POST /actions/jobs/{id}/rerun` and `POST /actions/runs/{id}/rerun-failed-jobs` answer `403 Must have admin rights to Repository` to a non-member token. So the only currently available recovery is asking a maintainer.

## Options

1. **Replace the fixed budget with a deadline** (for example `waitFor` with a `10 s` timeout and a short poll interval), so a loaded runner still passes and a genuinely missing fault still fails quickly enough.
2. **Wait on the event rather than polling** — if the injection can expose a promise or an emitter, awaiting it removes the timing assumption entirely.
3. If the current budget is deliberate, document the expected runner load and treat the red as a known flake; then it should not be able to block `merge-gate` for unrelated changes.

We can prepare option 1 as a pull request if that is the preferred shape; tell us which option you want and we will follow that instead of choosing for you.

## Checklist

- [x] I searched existing issues (open and closed) before filing this one.
- [x] This is a defect report, not a feature request.
- [x] I can reproduce it from the code path described below.

## Detailed Description of the Problem

`SessionStore.writeArray` writes a temp file, replaces the target, and removes the temp file in a `finally` block:

```ts
// services/api/src/store.ts:2156-2166
try {
  await writeFile(temporaryPath, `${JSON.stringify(values, null, 2)}\n`, "utf8");
  await renameReplace(temporaryPath, path);   // retries a transient EPERM/EACCES/EBUSY
} finally {
  await rm(temporaryPath, { force: true });
}
```

`renameReplace` classifies an exhausted retry as `FileReplaceError`, which keeps the errno in `code` and the original failure in `cause` so a caller can tell a locked file from a full disk. That classification is lost when the `rm` in the `finally` block itself throws: on Windows an antivirus scanner or an indexer can hold the same fresh temp file that made the replace fail, so `rm` raises a bare `EPERM`, the `finally` throws it, and it replaces the `FileReplaceError` on the way out. The caller then sees an unclassified `EPERM` — exactly the shape this area was just hardened against.

Current vs expected:

- current: replace exhausted → `rm` raises `EPERM` → caller receives a raw `EPERM` (no `FileReplaceError`, no `cause`, no attempt count).
- expected: the classified `FileReplaceError` reaches the caller; the cleanup failure must not substitute for the write failure.

The second half is coverage: the retry-success path asserts no `*.tmp` is left behind (`services/api/src/store-replace.test.ts:60-75`), but the exhausted-failure path has no assertion, so 'the finally still runs' is currently a code-reading claim rather than a checked behaviour.

### Minimal reproduction (red first)

In `services/api/src/store-replace.test.ts`, wrap the same fixture with `context.mock.method(fs, "rename", …)` throwing `EPERM` for every attempt **and** `context.mock.method(fs, "rm", …)` throwing `EPERM`:

```ts
await assert.rejects(() => store.writeArray(sessionId, values), (error) => {
  assert.equal(error.name, "FileReplaceError");          // currently fails: a bare EPERM arrives
  assert.equal(error.code, "EPERM");
  return true;
});
```

Observed now: the assertion fails with `error.name === "Error"` and the message `EPERM: operation not permitted, rm …`. Expected after the fix: `FileReplaceError`. Add a second assertion on the exhausted path that `readdir(sessionRunsDir)` contains no `*.tmp` entry.

### Fix

`services/api/src/store.ts` — the cleanup must not mask the write failure, e.g. `await rm(temporaryPath, { force: true }).catch(() => undefined);`. The retry policy, `FileReplaceError` and the non-transient errno behaviour stay as they are. This is deliberately **not** folded into #816: #816's tip is in review and the change is a separate failure mode.

## Detailed Environment Information Description

- Repository state: `main` at `89cd2d30c93e11c6e98e264cc08b171f6a3705f0`
- File:line: `services/api/src/store.ts:2156-2166`, existing coverage `services/api/src/store-replace.test.ts:60-75`
- Node: `v22.23.2`; package manager: `pnpm 11.1.2`
- Command for the area: `cd services/api && node --import tsx --test src/store-replace.test.ts`
- Reported by: ScienceDiscovery Security (review of #816 at `82d31f6111ff87be3e2709d7230dd8babc10d507`), filed by ScienceDiscovery Lead

## Version Information

- `main` @ `89cd2d30c93e11c6e98e264cc08b171f6a3705f0`
- Reported 2026-11-04

## Before you start (three constraints on the tests, from a read of the fixtures)

1. **The two acceptances cannot live in one test.** If `rm` is mocked to always throw `EPERM`, the temp file necessarily stays on disk, so a `readdir` assertion that no `*.tmp` remains in the same test can never hold. Split it: **A** = `rm` throws `EPERM`, assert only that the classified error reaches the caller; **B** = `rename` is exhausted while `rm` is the real implementation, assert `FileReplaceError` *and* no `*.tmp` leftover.
2. **The mock needs `syncBuiltinESMExports()`, and the `rm` filter must match the file name, not a substring.** `store.ts:25` imports `rm` as a named ESM binding, and the existing `failReplaces` helper (`store-replace.test.ts:44-55`) is what lets a mock reach the store; without it the mock silently does nothing and the red assertion passes for the wrong reason. Also do not filter on `.tmp`: the fixture root is `<cwd>/.tmp/state-replace-<uuid>` (`store-replace.test.ts:23`) and the teardown calls `rm(root, { recursive: true, force: true })` (`:24`), so a substring filter mocks the teardown too and the test blows up in cleanup. Match `basename` against the `.state-<pid>-<uuid>.tmp` shape written by `store.ts:2156`.
3. **The assertions above do not stop a fake fix.** Asserting only `name`/`code`/no-leftover can be satisfied by wrapping any bare `EPERM` in a hand-built `FileReplaceError` higher up. Add the two cheapest discriminators: `assert.equal(error.attempts, 20)` (and confirm the attempt count with the mock's own counter) and `assert.equal(error.cause.code, "EPERM")`.

A note against over-fixing: the swallowed-cleanup leftover is **inert**. Only two `readdir` calls exist in `store.ts` — `.trash` (`:2103`) and `agent-workspaces` (`:2001`) — and nothing enumerates `session-runs/` or the array directory; `readArray` reads an exact path (`:2147-2153`). So no startup sweep and no retry on `rm` are needed; the fix stays one line plus the tests.

### Checklist

- [x] I have searched for related issues but did not get the expected help.
- [x] This bug has not been fixed in the latest version.
- [x] Please note that if your bug description lacks corresponding environment information and a minimal reproducible demo, it will be difficult for us to reproduce and resolve the issue, which will reduce the possibility of receiving feedback, or even lead to the issue being closed.

### 🐞 Detailed Description of the Problem

**Current:** the desktop attachment tray prints a file's size with the *next* unit's number still attached to the *previous* unit name. A file of `1_048_575` bytes (1 MiB − 1) reads **`1024KB`** on its card, and `1_073_741_823` bytes (1 GiB − 1) reads **`1024MB`**. The upload limit is printed by the same shape of ladder and shows **`1024 MiB`** for `1_073_741_823`.

The unit is picked from the *unrounded* value (`1023.999 KB`, so the loop stops at KB) while the printed number comes from `Math.round(value)` at that scale, which rounds up to `1024` — a number no KB value can hold.

**Expected:** a size one byte under 1 MiB reads `1MB`, one byte under 1 GiB reads `1GB`; the limit one byte under 1 GiB reads `1 GiB`. Never `1024KB` / `1024MB` / `1024 MiB`.

**Minimal reproduction** (pure functions, no DOM):

```ts
import { formatFileSize } from "./apps/desktop/src/app/attachments.js";
import { formatByteLimit } from "./apps/desktop/src/app/upload.js";

console.log(formatFileSize(1_048_575));      // 1024KB
console.log(formatFileSize(1_073_741_823));  // 1024MB
console.log(formatByteLimit(1_073_741_823)); // 1024 MiB
```

Observed on `main` `89cd2d30` (`node --import tsx`):

```text
value          formatFileSize   formatByteLimit
1_048_574      1024KB           1024 KiB
1_048_575      1024KB           1024 KiB
1_048_576      1MB              1 MiB
1_073_741_823  1024MB           1024 MiB
```

**Where.**

- `apps/desktop/src/app/attachments.ts:161-173` — `formatFileSize` (attachment card, `:167` loop condition `value >= 1024`, `:172` prints the rounded value).
- `apps/desktop/src/app/upload.ts:36-47` — `formatByteLimit` (upload limit line, `:42` loop, `:46` `Number(value.toFixed(1))`).

**Note on scope.** `#867` fixed the same class in `apps/web` (`formatBytes` in the provenance modal and the CSV inspector). The desktop app has its own ladders and shares no code with `apps/web`, so this is a separate defect in a separate app, not a duplicate: the web fix never reaches `apps/desktop`.

### Detailed Environment Information Description

- Repository: `openJiuwen-ai/sciencediscovery`, `main` at `89cd2d30c93e11c6e98e264cc08b171f6a3705f0`.
- `apps/desktop` (`@sciencediscovery/desktop`), pure functions checked with `node --import tsx` on Node `v22.23.2`, pnpm `11.1.2`, Linux x86_64.
- No DOM, no running stack: both formatters are pure and are called by the attachment tray and the upload limit line.

### Additional Information

Found while dogfooding `apps/web` size formatting (`#867`) and checking the desktop shell for the same reading: `apps/desktop` builds its own unit ladders (`attachments.ts`, `upload.ts`, and a separate whole-GiB one in `resource-format.ts`).

### Version Information

- `main` `89cd2d30c93e11c6e98e264cc08b171f6a3705f0` (2026-11-04).
- `apps/desktop` package version as of that commit.

closed_recent.author: yuanzhou75
closed_recent.body:
## Checklist

- [x] I have searched for related issues but did not get the expected help.
- [x] This bug has not been fixed in the latest version.
- [x] Please note that if your bug description lacks corresponding environment information and a minimal reproducible demo, it will be difficult for us to reproduce and resolve the issue, which will reduce the possibility of receiving feedback, or even lead to the issue being closed.

## 🐞 Detailed Description of the Problem

While a shell execution sits in the provenance-commit retry loop, **every attempt rewrites `data/execution-runs/<sessionId>.json` even though the file's bytes never change**. The rewrite replaces the file (new inode) and moves `mtime`/`ctime`, so anything that watches those timestamps sees constant change in a session whose content is static.

This is the root cause behind the export-revision churn in #1018. PR #1020 makes the export revision immune to it (a content digest instead of `size`/`mtime`/`ctime`, plus a stable shell projection) and explicitly calls itself a defence, not a cure. This issue tracks the wasted write itself.

### Evidence

Session `dcfe6ace-c7d1-45c7-a781-9928f5c29c0e`, build `c95f080a`, local stack. The file is rewritten every ~10 s, alternating between two inodes (each write is a temp file plus replace), and every sample has the same 4,826 bytes and the same digest:

```text
2026-11-09 13:32:40.870   inode 45097   4826 bytes
2026-11-09 13:32:50.922   inode 45093   4826 bytes
2026-11-09 13:33:00.890   inode 45097   4826 bytes
2026-11-09 13:33:10.894   inode 45093   4826 bytes
2026-11-09 13:33:20.914   inode 45097   4826 bytes
2026-11-09 13:33:30.930   inode 45093   4826 bytes

two samples 12 s apart:  4826 bytes  md5 59a848023ad12930497826a781aed049  (identical)
```

The content is three records and the last one is already settled — `id: shell:30b80e…`, `status: succeeded`, `finishedAt: 2026-11-08T08:47:32.158Z` — while the shell execution itself is `accepted: true`, `provenance: unconfirmed`, `finalization: failed`, `observation.lastError.code = PROVENANCE_COMMIT_FAILED`. So the ledger write succeeds and the attempt fails afterwards, and the next attempt rewrites the same bytes.

The same churn appeared in the #1018 report as `12:56:09.510 / 12:56:17.530 / 12:56:25.562`, all 4,826 bytes.

### Root cause

1. The recovery loop's `finalize` handler is `commitExistingShellExecutionResult` (`services/api/src/bootstrap/platform.ts:664`, `services/api/src/agent-run/workspace-bindings.ts:319`).
2. `commitExistingShellExecutionResult` (`packages/provenance/src/recorder.ts:997-1050`) computes a `resultDigest`, loads the settled row, and **only throws when an existing digest differs** (`:1020-1022`). When the digest matches it keeps going and appends the run again (`:1037`). There is no "already committed, return" path — `adoptShellOutcome` in the same file does have one (`:1139-1146`).
3. `store.appendExecutionRun` **does** detect the duplicate and returns from the mutator without pushing (`services/api/src/store.ts:7143-7146`), so the array is unchanged.
4. But `mutateArray` calls `writeArray` unconditionally (`services/api/src/store.ts:2233-2237`), and `writeArray` always writes a temp file and replaces the target (`:2213-2225`). Hence new inode, new `mtime`/`ctime`, byte-identical content.

Verified from code and the samples above; the ~10 s cadence is inferred from the record shape (the settled row exists while the attempt still fails), nobody has captured a stack trace — `/proc/<pid>/io` is unreadable and ptrace is unavailable in this environment.

## Proposed fixes (two independent options, different risk)

**A. Short-circuit in the recorder — low risk.** After computing `resultDigest`, if `existing?.resultDigest === resultDigest`, return the result instead of re-appending. This is the same idempotency check `adoptShellOutcome` already uses, and it only skips work that is provably a no-op. Nothing else reads a bumped `mtime` for this file legitimately.

**B. Skip no-op writes in `mutateArray` — wide blast radius, needs its own evaluation.** Snapshot the array before the operation and skip `writeArray` when nothing changed. This removes the whole class of empty writes (`messages`, `sessionRuns`, `artifactPlans`, `artifactReviews`, `claims`, … all go through `mutateArray`), but it changes write semantics for every array the store owns: cross-process visibility, the `replaceFile` retry story, and any reader that uses `mtime` invalidation (the research-package revision did exactly that) would need to be re-checked. It also needs a test that a genuine change still writes.

A alone fixes this report; B is the broader cleanup and should not ride along with a bug fix.

## Expected

- Re-committing a shell execution whose settled row and digest already exist leaves `execution-runs/<sessionId>.json` untouched — same inode, same `mtime`.
- A retry loop can never produce disk writes for state that has not changed.

## Observed

- One write every ~10 s forever: ~8,600 redundant rewrites per day for this single session, each with a `fsync`-worthy replace, and a continuously moving `ctime`.
- Anything hashing `size`/`mtime`/`ctime` of session data never converges while the execution is stuck (this is how #1018 was produced).

## Detailed Environment Information Description

```text
Host        Windows 11 26200 + WSL2 Ubuntu 24.04, local source checkout
Mode        ./scripts/start-stack.sh --mode local (adapter :4310, API :4410, runner :4311, memory-graph :17674)
Node v22.23.4, pnpm 11.1.2, uv 0.13.7, Python 3.12
Data dir    ~/sciencediscovery/.sciencediscovery-data
Session     dcfe6ace-c7d1-45c7-a781-9928f5c29c0e (project 04a09bcd-a2f5-4ef9-a17a-3f9ef43a75ff)
```

## Additional Information

Related: #1018 (the export-side consequence this write produces), #1012 (the execution that never settles), #978 (the finalization 401 behind it), and PR #1020 (defence: content-digest revision, does not change the writer).

## Version Information

- Repository: `openJiuwen-ai/sciencediscovery`
- Tested commit: `c95f080a6c3b1bb5e020808b5114e1894148422d` (main, 2026-11-08T18:06:21Z)
closed_recent.title: [Bug]: A failed shell finalization rewrites execution-runs/<session>.json with byte-identical content on every retry

closed_recent.author: yuanzhou75
closed_recent.body:
## Checklist

- [x] I have searched for related issues but did not get the expected help.
- [x] This bug has not been fixed in the latest version.
- [x] Please note that if your bug description lacks corresponding environment information and a minimal reproducible demo, it will be difficult for us to reproduce and resolve the issue, which will reduce the possibility of receiving feedback, or even lead to the issue being closed.

## 🐞 Detailed Description of the Problem

A session can become **permanently un-exportable** after one of its shell executions gets stuck in the provenance-commit recovery loop. The recovery loop rewrites the session's execution record every few seconds, and the export revision hashes that file's mtime/ctime, so the revision never stabilizes: the preview never leaves `EXPORT_PREVIEW_PENDING`, and every export attempt fails with `导出期间会话内容发生变化，请基于最新内容重新导出。`

This makes both 必要导出 and 完整导出 unusable for that session — the user has no way out except editing the data directory.

### Evidence

Session `dcfe6ace-c7d1-45c7-a781-9928f5c29c0e` (project `04a09bcd-a2f5-4ef9-a17a-3f9ef43a75ff`), build `c95f080a`:

```text
GET /api/projects/{pid}/research-package/preview?sessionId=dcfe6ace…&level=necessary
  → 409 {"code":"EXPORT_PREVIEW_PENDING"} repeatedly (observed 6/6, and 3/4 in an earlier run)

POST /api/projects/{pid}/research-package/exports  (with the revision that finally returned)
  → 202 … then
  → failed "导出期间会话内容发生变化，请基于最新内容重新导出。"
```

Two consecutive previews returned **different** revisions for the same unchanged session (`803b8ecf…`, `05794da2…`, `1381d7ef…`, `e7551a38…`), while a control session that has no stuck execution kept the **same** revision across four previews over 45 s (`411c6ccb…` ×4).

The churn source — `data/execution-runs/<sessionId>.json` is rewritten continuously:

```text
2026-11-09 12:56:09.510   (size unchanged, 4826 bytes)
2026-11-09 12:56:17.530
2026-11-09 12:56:25.562
```

and the execution responsible is the one from the finalization-401 case in #978:

```text
id:            shell:30b80e039b1649cbb900d4ff512b5c2b09ea89bd95c55151d1f9c8a2f3c46236
accepted:      true
provenance:    unconfirmed
finalization:  failed
finishedAt:    null
observation:   {"status":"blocked","failureCount":1,
                "nextRetryAt":"2026-11-09T04:56:34.553Z",
                "lastError":{"code":"PROVENANCE_COMMIT_FAILED",…}}
```

`services/api/src/shell-executions.ts` reschedules it (`configureRecovery` → `reconcilePending` every 1 s, retry backoff ~8 s), each retry rewrites the execution record.

Relevant revision inputs in `services/api/src/research-snapshots.ts` (`previewRevision`): it hashes `files` (every file under `store.sessionDataPaths(session.id)` with `size`/`mtimeMs`/`ctimeMs`) **and** `shells: store.shellExecutions.snapshot(session.id)` — so a forever-retrying execution invalidates the revision on every tick.

### Steps to reproduce

1. Produce a session whose shell execution ends in `PROVENANCE_COMMIT_FAILED` (e.g. the finalization-401 path from #978 — in this data set it came from a run that ran `run_shell` and then hit the 401 on finalization).
2. Open 更多会话操作 → 导出会话 and watch the size preview: it keeps saying 正在计算范围与大小… and never settles.
3. Start an export anyway; it fails with 导出期间会话内容发生变化.
4. Compare with a session whose executions all committed — its preview settles in seconds and exports fine.

### Expected

- Export must be able to snapshot a session whose execution is stuck in recovery: either exclude volatile recovery bookkeeping (`observation.nextRetryAt`, lease timestamps) from the revision, or take the revision from committed/stable fields only, and let packaging succeed with the last known execution state (marked as such).
- A session with a stuck execution should not be permanently un-exportable; the recovery loop should reach a terminal state (or back off without rewriting the record every tick).

### Observed

- `EXPORT_PREVIEW_PENDING` forever, then a revision that changes under the export, so packaging always aborts with "会话内容发生变化".
- No user-facing explanation that the block is caused by an execution stuck in recovery.

## Detailed Environment Information Description

```text
Host        Windows 11 26200 + WSL2 Ubuntu 24.04, local source checkout
Mode        ./scripts/start-stack.sh --mode local (adapter :4310, API :4410, runner :4311, memory-graph :17674)
Node v22.23.4, pnpm 11.1.2, uv 0.13.7, Python 3.12
Model       glm-5.2 over an OpenAI-compatible relay
Data dir    ~/sciencediscovery/.sciencediscovery-data (evolve runs + science memory present in this session)
```

## Additional Information

Related: #978 (the finalization 401 that leaves the execution `accepted=true / provenance unconfirmed` — this report is the export-side consequence), #995 (import opens two sessions), #803 (the feature).

The same session also demonstrates that evolve runs are not carried by the package; that is filed separately.

## Version Information

- Repository: `openJiuwen-ai/sciencediscovery`
- Tested commit: `c95f080a6c3b1bb5e020808b5114e1894148422d` (main, 2026-11-08T18:06:21Z)

closed_recent.body:
### Checklist

- [x] I have searched for related issues (terms: `inapplicable`, `os:linux`, `platform skip`, `node --test windows`, `test discovery`, `silently skipped`, `host mismatch`) and did not find this behavior reported.
- [x] Verified still present on `main` at the commit listed under *Version Information*.
- [x] Environment information and a self-contained minimal reproduction are included below.

## 🐞 Detailed Description of the Problem

When a test file declares an OS tag that the current host does not match, the package-level compatibility shim makes every registration call a no-op, so the file registers **zero** test cases — and `node --test` still prints `pass`, reports `skipped 0`, and exits `0`. Nothing in the output says the file was excluded because of its `os:` tag, so "ran nothing" and "ran and passed" are indistinguishable to the developer running the suite locally.

This affects the **direct** execution path only (`node --test <file>`, i.e. a package's own `"test": "node --import tsx --test \"src/**/*.test.ts\""` script). The shared plan path used by CI is not affected — see *Root-cause code references*.

### Root-cause code references

`test/support/tagged/compat.mjs`:

- **lines 19–22** — `declares()` treats a declared group as an allowlist: if a file declares any `os:` tag, only the declared hosts pass.
- **lines 45–52** — `createTest()` consults the host at line 48 (`hostPlatform(process.platform)` / `hostArch(process.arch)`) and returns `inapplicable()` at line 49 when the host is not in the declared set.
- **lines 30–36** — `inapplicable()` returns `{ ...native, test: declaration, it: declaration, describe: declaration, ...hooks }`, where `declaration` is `() => {}` and `declaration.skip`/`.todo`/`.only` are the *same* no-op. Every `test(...)` call is discarded, and an explicit `.skip(...)` request is discarded with it.

The comment at **lines 24–29** documents registering nothing as deliberate ("Registering nothing is what those files did before they were tagged"). The problem reported here is not that design decision — it is the observable outcome: the built-in runner counts the *file* as one test, so an excluded file is indistinguishable from a file whose cases all passed.

Contrast with the layers that do report, which is why this reads as a residual gap rather than intended behavior:

| location | behavior |
|---|---|
| `test/support/tagged/plan.mjs:88` | throws `EMPTY_SELECTION: no test instances selected` when a plan selects nothing |
| `test/support/tagged/plan.mjs:76` | plan selection is by tags only and never reads the host |
| `test/support/tagged/environment.mjs:47–49` | `preflight()` records a `HOST_MISMATCH` problem per entry when the plan target is not the host |
| `test/support/tagged/node.mjs:40` | the registry path refuses direct use outright: *"direct node --test would not enforce the frozen plan"* |
| `test/support/tagged/compat.mjs:49` | silent zero registration |

`compat.mjs:46` shows the two paths are disjoint: when the shared run has installed the registry symbol (`node-collect.mjs:22` → `node.mjs:24`), `createTest` delegates to the registry path and the host gate is never reached.

### Minimal reproduction

Save this as `os-tag-probe.mjs` in the repository root and run it. It needs no `node_modules`, no `tsx`, and no service — it imports the repository's own shim.

```js
// os-tag-probe.mjs
import * as native from 'node:test';
const { createTest } = await import('./test/support/tagged/compat.mjs');

const VARIANTS = {
  A: ['category:ut', 'os:linux'],                    // what the default branch declares today
  B: ['category:ut', 'os:linux', 'os:windows'],
  C: ['category:ut'],                                // no os: group declared at all
};

const tags = VARIANTS[process.env.PROBE_GROUP];
const t = createTest(import.meta.url, { tags });

console.log(
  `OBS tags=${tags.join(',')} host=${process.platform}/${process.arch} node=${process.version} ` +
  `returned_test_is_native=${t.test === native.test} test_is_describe=${t.test === t.describe} ` +
  `test_skip_is_test=${t.test.skip === t.test}`
);

t.test('probe-case-one', () => console.log('CASE_RAN probe-case-one'));
t.test('probe-case-two', () => console.log('CASE_RAN probe-case-two'));
```

```bash
for G in A B C; do PROBE_GROUP=$G node --test os-tag-probe.mjs; echo "exit=$?"; done
```

One file, one runner, one host — only the `tags` array differs between the three groups.

### Actual behavior

Group A, verbatim on a Windows host:

```text
# OBS tags=category:ut,os:linux host=win32/x64 node=v22.23.4 returned_test_is_native=false test_is_describe=true test_skip_is_test=true
# Subtest: os-tag-probe.mjs
ok 1 - os-tag-probe.mjs
1..1
# tests 1
# pass 1
# fail 0
# skipped 0
exit=0
```

Neither `CASE_RAN` line appears: **0 of the 2 declared cases ran**, `# skipped 0`, exit code 0, and no line mentions the platform or the tag. With the default spec reporter — what a developer actually looks at:

```text
✔ os-tag-probe.mjs (88.6081ms)
ℹ tests 1
ℹ pass 1
ℹ skipped 0
```

Groups B and C, verbatim tails from the same command:

```text
# OBS tags=category:ut,os:linux,os:windows host=win32/x64 node=v22.23.4 returned_test_is_native=true test_is_describe=false test_skip_is_test=false
# CASE_RAN probe-case-one
# CASE_RAN probe-case-two
# tests 2
# pass 2
# skipped 0
```

```text
# OBS tags=category:ut host=win32/x64 node=v22.23.4 returned_test_is_native=true test_is_describe=false test_skip_is_test=false
# CASE_RAN probe-case-one
# CASE_RAN probe-case-two
# tests 2
# pass 2
# skipped 0
```

| Group | Declared tags | `createTest()` returns | named cases executed | `# tests` | `# skipped` | exit |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| A | `os:linux` only | `inapplicable()` no-op | **0** | 1 (the file itself) | 0 | 0 |
| B | `os:linux` + `os:windows` | native `node:test` | 2 | 2 | 0 | 0 |
| C | no `os:` declared | native `node:test` | 2 | 2 | 0 | 0 |

Stability: the A/B/C set was run 3 times with identical results (A always `# tests 1 / # pass 1 / # skipped 0` with 0 `CASE_RAN`; B and C always `# tests 2` with 2). Group A also reproduced unchanged under Node v20.12.2 on the same host (`# tests 1`, `# pass 1`, `# skipped 0`, no `CASE_RAN`), so this is not tied to one Node minor.

### Expected behavior

Groups B and C are correct. Group A should not be able to read as a pass. Either:

- the file is reported as skipped with a reason naming host and tag, e.g. `# skipped 1` plus `platform-inapplicable: host windows/amd64 is not declared by os:linux`; or
- the summary distinguishes "0 cases, excluded by tag" from "cases ran and passed".

An assertion that silently never executes is worse than one that fails, because it also silently satisfies any "all tests pass" gate built on the exit code.

## Detailed Environment Information Description

| item | value |
|---|---|
| OS | Windows 11, `10.0.22631.6199`, x64 |
| Shell used for the repro | Git Bash / MSYS2 `MINGW64_NT-10.0-22631 3.6.5` |
| Node.js (primary) | `v22.23.4`, the version the project pins |
| Node.js (cross-check) | `v20.12.2`, same group-A outcome |
| `process.platform` / `process.arch` | `win32` / `x64` → `hostPlatform` = `windows`, `hostArch` = `amd64` (`test/support/tagged/environment.mjs:17–18`) |
| Runner | Node's built-in test runner via `node --test` (TAP and `spec` reporters both shown) |
| Dependencies installed | none required for the probe |
| Services / devices / credentials | none involved |
| Repository revision | `main` at `7caff0e156a00800df6d5cb01bf95f81ea1f7a9a` |

## Additional Information

**How many files this covers on the default branch.** Measured at the commit above:

```bash
git grep -l "tagged/compat.mjs" origin/main | wc -l                    # 619  (files using the shim)
git grep -l '"os:linux"'    origin/main > linux.txt
git grep -l '"os:windows"'  origin/main > windows.txt
git grep -l "tagged/compat.mjs" origin/main > imports.txt
comm -23 <(sort imports.txt | grep -Fxf linux.txt) \
         <(sort imports.txt | grep -Fxf windows.txt) | wc -l            # 538  (shim + linux-only declared)
```

So 538 of the 619 files that use the shim register zero cases when run directly on a Windows host. They concentrate in `services/api` (146), `apps/web` (120), `apps/desktop` (85), `services/runner` (30), `services/launcher` (18), and 139 more spread over the remaining 35 package/directory groups — including `packages/specialist/src/builtins.test.ts`.

**What this report does not claim.**

1. **It is not a CI problem.** `test/support/tagged/profiles.mjs:25,28` set `os: 'linux'` for every rule, targets derive from that field (line 63), and `.github/workflows/` contains no `windows` reference at all. CI never reaches `compat.mjs`'s host gate (`compat.mjs:46`), and plans select by tags alone (`plan.mjs:76`). No CI result changes because of this.
2. **It is not claimed to happen on Linux.** On `linux/amd64` the declared set contains the host, so `declares()` passes and native `node:test` is returned. That is read from `environment.mjs:17–18` + `compat.mjs:48`; it was not measured here, since only one Windows host was available.
3. **It is not a claim that Windows is a supported test host.** The profiles say it is not. The question is what a developer should see when they run the suite on an unsupported host anyway.
4. **It is not a product or agent-runtime defect.** Only `test/support/tagged/` registration behavior is involved; no runtime code path is implicated.
5. The 538 figure is a static tag scan. It does not mean those files' assertions would fail on Windows — only that none of them execute there.

**Suggested improvement.** The smallest option stays inside `inapplicable()`: instead of returning only no-ops, register exactly one skipped case, e.g.

```js
native.test('platform-inapplicable',
  { skip: `host ${hostPlatform(process.platform)}/${hostArch(process.arch)} not declared by ${declaredTags}` },
  () => {});
```

The tally then shows `# skipped 1` with the reason, while still running no real assertions — this keeps the documented intent of lines 24–29 and removes the false green. If registering a case is considered too invasive for this path, emitting a single diagnostic line naming the file and the unmet tag would already make the two outcomes distinguishable.

Whether Windows/macOS should become supported test hosts at all is a separate decision, and per `profiles.mjs` the compliant lever for that is adding targets, not per-file `os:` tags.

Related closed issue **#126** ("Consolidate test entry points and enforce complete test discovery") states the principle this residual gap runs against: *"a successful command must not conceal missing, unsupported, or unexecuted tests."*

Filed as a report only — no code change is proposed or attached, and no branch or PR is involved.

## Version Information

- Repository: `openJiuwen-ai/sciencediscovery`, default branch `main`, commit `7caff0e156a00800df6d5cb01bf95f81ea1f7a9a` (2026-11-09).
- File under analysis: `test/support/tagged/compat.mjs`, blob `b8b9e2c74bea5e2f647e37a42527de8ccf1ba832`.
- Supporting files read at the same revision: `test/support/tagged/plan.mjs`, `test/support/tagged/environment.mjs`, `test/support/tagged/profiles.mjs`, `test/support/tagged/node.mjs`, `test/support/tagged/node-collect.mjs`.
- Node.js used for the reproduction: `v22.23.4` (project-pinned); cross-checked with `v20.12.2`.
- No package version participates in the outcome; the probe imports no dependencies.

> **Bilingual tracking issue.** The English sections are authoritative; the Chinese sections mirror them and are kept in sync. The separate Chinese tracking issue #806 has been merged into this issue and closed as a duplicate, so both languages now live here. Chinese is included on the requester's explicit ask.
>
> **本 issue 为双语跟踪**：英文部分为权威版本，中文部分与之同步。原先独立的中文跟踪 issue #806 已并入本 issue 并按 duplicate 关闭，两种语言今后只维护这一份。保留中文版是应提出者的要求。

---

# English

## 🚀 Background Description

**Start point — what a user actually waits today.** On installed builds, the first message of a session takes **~60–135s** (field measurements from our Windows-desktop tracker: ~85s typical, ~135s on a fresh-install cold boot), while the same-session second message takes **~6s**. Every boot profile — cold first boot, warm restart, or a new session in a running app — pays the same kind of first-message tax.

**What the tax is made of** (log-line-timed decomposition, dev stack + field forensics):

| Chunk | Size | Owner | Mechanism |
|---|---|---|---|
| MCP catalog cold-start | **~48s** (zero once warm) | **SD side** | the bundled stdio MCP servers spawn and enumerate tools on the catalog's first refresh; a fresh install delays that refresh to the first chat run. Verified locally: catalog warmed at boot → first message pays zero here. |
| SD-side run preparation | **~14s** | SD API | serial RPC chain per run (`skills.list` ×3, `permissions.tools.update`, per-run MCP re-registration) plus API acceptance (~4s) |
| Session assembly | **~5.3s** warm / ~17s pre-0015 | JiuwenSwarm | per-session `create_instance`; the 0015–0017 patches already moved the ~5.2s import tax off this path |
| Tool-schema handling | **~7–8s every turn** | upstream default | ~72 tool definitions ≈ 28k input tokens ride every model call (`progressive_tool_enabled=false`; #582 measured the same) |
| Model network/TTFT + machine tax | remainder | — | real model latency, cold-file reads, antivirus scanning on installed machines |

**Where the "26.09s" figure belongs** (an earlier draft of this issue wrongly led with it): it is an **anatomy anchor, not the user-facing start point** — a dev-stack first message measured with a *warm catalog* and a *mock model*, versus 8.67s for the second message. Its only purpose is attributing each chunk to its owning side: it proves the 48s chunk is the SD catalog (JW `reconcile` only opens one local loopback shared-tools server, milliseconds), and it sizes the SD-side run-preparation chain. Quoting it as the baseline would understate the real-world problem by the catalog chunk and the model time.

**End point (expected, to be replaced by packaged A/B measurements).** With the full plan below landed: first message **6–10s** on a warm-restart profile (vs ~60–135s today), second message ~5s (vs ~6s), cold-install first message no longer carrying the ~48s catalog chunk. Total optimization space: **~50–120s off the first message, plus ~3.5s off every subsequent turn**.

Related upstream context: #582 documented the input-side half (72 tools ≈ 28k tokens on a short "你好"); jiuwenswarm has adjacent requests openJiuwen-ai/jiuwenswarm#6683 (on-demand MCP registration), #7101 (request-level MCP registration failure bypass), #9938 (blocking snapshot out of the chat data plane).

## Design Ideas

Ordered by measured value. Options already invalidated by measurement are recorded so the discussion does not restart them.

1. **S1 — Warm the MCP catalog right after agent-ready** (implemented on the workstream branch; PR to follow).
   The shell's `watchAgentReady` already probes `/agent/info`. The moment `jiuwenswarm.reachable` turns true it now issues `GET /api/mcp/sources` in the background — the exact request the MCP settings page uses to refresh the catalog. The stdio spawns and tool enumeration then overlap the user's "ready screen" time instead of the first message. Best-effort: failures are logged to `shell.log` only; if the warmup loses the race the run path re-runs the same steps, so behaviour never forks.
   Direct evidence: catalog refreshed at boot → first message at +3min paid **zero** MCP chunk.

2. **S3 — Trim the per-run preparation chain in the control API** (planned, highest remaining value in the warm-catalog scenario).
   `executeAgentRun`'s head runs a serial RPC chain against JiuwenSwarm before `chat.send`: `skills.list` ×3 (~4s in the anatomy anchor), permission updates, and per-run MCP re-registration (~1–2s). Candidates: cache the skills list with invalidation on skill-set changes, collapse the three lists into one, and let the API prove "tool table unchanged" so the adapter skips its re-registration round trips. Session-creation-time pre-warm follows once the chain is idempotent.

3. **J2 — Progressive tool exposure** (needs upstream discussion; JiuwenSwarm native).
   `DEFAULT_PROGRESSIVE_TOOL_ENABLED=False` sends all ~72 tool schemas on every call (~28k tokens; ~7s of per-turn cost under a mock endpoint — not model time). Enabling the existing `ProgressiveToolRail` with a small direct-exposure whitelist would cut input tokens ~3× on **every** turn, first and subsequent. Upstream note: the constant's comment/docstring already says "enabled by default" while the code returns `False` — the drift is a low-controversy entry point. Recall-rate validation on real tasks is required before flipping any default.

4. **J3 — Session-assembly warm pool** (second batch).
   Extend the existing `AgentWarmPool` so the per-session adapter is pre-built on session create; measured remaining value ~5.3s → ~1–2s on hit, with a mandatory seamless fallback to today's full path.

**Invalidated by measurement (recorded to save re-litigating):**
- *J1 — concurrent MCP connect with timeouts in JW*: the JW-side reconcile only opens one local loopback server (ms-level); the 48s was the SD catalog. Kept only as a small upstream-hygiene proposal.
- *S2 — adapter-side pre-registration at lifespan*: the tool table is assembled by the control API per run and handed over `/agent/runs`; the adapter has no table to pre-register at startup, and an empty pre-registration would force a generation bump on the first real run.

## Involved Public APIs

- Existing: `GET /api/mcp/sources` (MCP settings page's refresh endpoint; now also called by the shell after agent-ready).
- No new HTTP APIs, IPC channels or configuration surfaces in S1. S3 may add an internal invalidation signal for the skills cache; any new surface will be listed in its PR.

## Description of Relevance to Other Modules

- `win_desktop`: shell `watchAgentReady` warmup hook + `first-chat-warmup.ts` (new, unit-tested).
- `services/api`: S3 target — `executeAgentRun` head, `jiuwenswarm-skills.ts` reconcile chain.
- `services/adapter`: `ensure_shared_tools` already diffs tool tables; S3 may hand it an "unchanged" fast path proof.
- JiuwenSwarm patches (`jiuwen_swarm/patches/`): no new patches for S1/S3; J3 would land as patch 0020+ (numbering shared with a parallel packaging workstream).
- `apps/desktop`: no UI change; the ready screen timing is unchanged.
- #582 (input-token analysis): complementary — J2 addresses that input directly.

## Test Design and Test Plan

- **S1 (landed in branch)**: unit tests for URL/header construction and timeout (`win_desktop/test/first-chat-warmup.test.ts`); full shell suite 116/116 green and `win_desktop` build + typecheck clean, re-run on 2026-11-05.
- **Integration A/B** (per change): dev stack, mock OpenAI endpoint on loopback, `agent_server.log` line-timestamped segmentation; baseline vs change measured in the **same host-load window** (parallel packaging builds invalidate absolute numbers); first message of a fresh session vs second message of the same session, median of 3.
- **Cold-scenario check**: with the MCP catalog forcibly cold (fresh data dir), confirm the shell warmup completes before a human-plausible first message and the first run no longer contains the stdio-spawn chunk.
- **Regression**: shell build + full shell suite; `pnpm test` for the api package after S3; JiuwenSwarm smoke (gateway / agentserver / main chat / memory) where patches are touched.
- **Packaged validation**: GUI-interactive install (no `/S`), three boot profiles (cold first boot / warm restart / attach) with first-message timing recorded and the second message non-regressed.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] Shell warmup: after `jiuwenswarm.reachable` becomes true, `shell.log` shows `[warmup] first-chat /api/mcp/sources -> 200` (or a failure line) without any change to the ready-screen timing or user-visible behaviour.
- [ ] Warmup failure never surfaces to the user, and a lost race falls back to today's run path with identical behaviour.
- [ ] Cold-install first message no longer contains the stdio-spawn/tool-enumeration chunk (field: ~48s of the 60–135s).
- [ ] Warm-restart first message: field baseline ~60–135s → **≤20s after S1+S3** [expected, to be replaced by packaged A/B] → **6–10s after the full plan** [expected].
- [ ] Second message ~6s is not regressed beyond noise, trending to ~5s with J2.
- [ ] Every-turn input: J2, where accepted upstream, cuts tool-schema tokens by ≥50% with zero regression on a fixed set of real-task scenarios (recall rate held).
- Commands that must pass: `pnpm ci:l1` (static gate), `pnpm --dir win_desktop build`, `pnpm --dir win_desktop typecheck`, `pnpm --dir win_desktop test` (116/116), `pnpm test` for the api/desktop scopes touched by S3, plus the packaged three-profile run above.
- Performance threshold: the ready screen and every user-visible behaviour are unchanged; the warmup is off the critical path by construction (fire-and-forget, 60s timeout, logged only).

## Additional Information

- Measurement note: anatomy-anchor numbers were taken while a parallel packaging build was running on the host; they may read 10–25% high. Field numbers (60–135s) are user-measured and unaffected. The structural findings (chunk boundaries, catalog-warm ⇒ zero MCP chunk, JW loopback being ms-level) are load-independent. A/B pairs are always measured within one load window.
- Revision note (2026-11-03): this body was re-aligned after review — the original draft led with the 26.09s anatomy anchor as the baseline, which understated the user-facing start point. The start point is now the field measurement (~60–135s); the 26.09s figure is kept only as the internal attribution anchor it was measured to be.
- Revision note (2026-11-05): the two-language tracking was merged from #806 into this single issue (English first, Chinese mirrored below), and the body was re-aligned with the repository feature template added in #776 — `[Feature]:` title prefix, the seven template sections, and checkbox acceptance criteria naming the commands that must pass.
- S1 is implemented for the desktop shell only; Linux/macOS source-stack paths benefit indirectly through the same control-plane endpoint.
- Evidence pack (internal): session-creation timestamped `agent_server.log` segmentation, the mock endpoint fixture, and the run-preparation RPC chain listing are archived in the workstream's knowledge base.

---

# 中文

## 🚀 背景描述

**起点：用户现在到底要等多久。** 在已安装的版本上，一个会话的第一条消息要花 **60~135 秒**（我们 Windows 桌面端的实测数据：典型值约 85 秒，全新安装后第一次冷启动约 135 秒），而同一个会话的第二条消息只要 **6 秒左右**。无论哪种启动方式——首次冷启动、热重启，还是在运行中的程序里另开新会话——都要为第一条消息付出一笔额外的"首条税"。

**这笔税由哪些部分构成**（按日志逐行时间戳分解，开发栈 + 现场取证）：

| 耗时环节 | 耗时 | 归属 | 原因 |
|---|---|---|---|
| MCP catalog 冷启动 | **约 48 秒**（预热后归零） | **SD 侧** | 内置的 stdio MCP 进程要到 catalog 第一次刷新时才启动并枚举工具；全新安装会把这次刷新推迟到第一条消息发出时。本地验证：启动时就预热 → 第一条消息的这一段耗时为 0 |
| SD 侧 run 准备链 | **约 14 秒** | SD API | 每轮 run 开始前要顺序走完一串 RPC（`skills.list` 调 3 次 + 权限更新 + MCP 重注册），再加上 API 受理本身约 4 秒 |
| 会话装配 | 热态 **约 5.3 秒**（0015 补丁前约 17 秒） | JiuwenSwarm | 每个会话都要 `create_instance`；0015–0017 补丁已把约 5.2 秒的 import 开销从该路径上移除了 |
| 工具 schema 处理 | **每轮约 7~8 秒** | 上游默认 | 每次调用模型都全量携带约 72 个工具定义 ≈ 2.8 万 token（`progressive_tool_enabled=false`；#582 同口径实测） |
| 模型网络 / TTFT + 机器开销 | 其余 | — | 模型本身的网络耗时与 TTFT、首次读文件、杀毒软件扫描等 |

**"26.09 秒"这个数字该怎么看**（本 issue 初版曾错误地拿它当起点）。它是**内部分析用的锚点，而不是用户实际感受到的耗时**——那是在开发环境、catalog 已预热、使用 mock 模型的条件下测出的首条耗时（对照第二条 8.67 秒）。它只有一个用途：给上面各段耗时"分归属"——证明 48 秒花在了 SD 的 catalog 上（JW 的 `reconcile` 只连一个本地回环服务器，毫秒级就能完成），并量出 SD 侧准备链的大小。如果拿它当基线，会严重低估真实问题——因为它既不含 catalog 预热前的 48 秒，也不含真实模型的耗时。

**目标：全部方案落地后的预期效果**（具体数字待装机 A/B 实测后更新）。热重启后第一条消息 **6~10 秒**（现状 60~135 秒），第二条约 5 秒（现状约 6 秒），全新安装后的第一条消息不再背负那 48 秒的目录预热。**总体优化空间：第一条消息省 50~120 秒，之后每条消息还能再省约 3.5 秒。**

相关背景：#582 记录了问题的另一半在输入侧——只说一句"你好"也要带上 72 个工具、约 2.8 万 token；JiuwenSwarm 侧的相关诉求见 openJiuwen-ai/jiuwenswarm#6683（MCP 按需注册）、#7101（请求级 MCP 注册失败时旁路）、#9938（把阻塞快照移出对话数据面）。

## 设计思路

以下按实测价值从高到低排列。已经被测量数据否掉的方案也一并列出，免得以后再被拿出来讨论。

1. **S1：agent-ready 之后立刻预热 MCP catalog**（已在工作分支实现，PR 稍后提交）。
   shell 的 `watchAgentReady` 本来就在探测 `/agent/info`；一旦 `jiuwenswarm.reachable` 变为 true，就在后台发起 `GET /api/mcp/sources`——和 MCP 设置页点"刷新"发出的是同一个请求。这样，stdio 进程的启动和工具枚举就挪到了用户看就绪屏的间隙里进行，不再占用第一条消息的时间。这是 best-effort（尽力而为）的设计：失败了只写一行 `shell.log`；万一预热没赶在第一条消息前完成，run 路径会把同样的步骤重跑一遍，用户侧行为不会有任何分叉。
   直接证据：catalog 启动时预热后，3 分钟再发第一条消息，这一段耗时为 **0**。

2. **S3：精简控制面 API 的每轮准备链**（计划中，catalog 已预热场景下剩余价值最大）。
   `executeAgentRun` 在真正 `chat.send` 之前，要先对 JiuwenSwarm 顺序走完一串 RPC：`skills.list` 调 3 次（合计约 4 秒）、权限更新、每轮一次的 MCP 重注册（约 1~2 秒）。优化方向：给 skills 列表加缓存（技能集变化时失效）、把三次 list 合并成一次、由 API 直接告知"工具表没有变化"让 adapter 跳过注册往返。等这条链变得幂等之后，还可以把预热进一步提前到会话创建时。

3. **J2：渐进式工具暴露**（需上游讨论；JiuwenSwarm 原生）。
   `DEFAULT_PROGRESSIVE_TOOL_ENABLED=False` 意味着每次调用都要全量带上约 72 个工具 schema（约 2.8 万 token；在 mock 端点下每轮为此花约 7 秒——这部分时间跟模型本身无关）。启用现成的 `ProgressiveToolRail`、只配一小份"直接暴露"白名单，就能把每轮的输入 token 降到原来的约 1/3。一个很好的切入点是：这个常量的注释/docstring 写着 "enabled by default"，代码里却是 `False`——修正这个偏差争议最小。但在翻转默认值之前，必须先在真实任务上验证工具的召回率。

4. **J3：会话装配 warm pool**（第二批）。
   扩展现有的 `AgentWarmPool`，在创建会话时就把 adapter 预先建好；实测剩余价值约 5.3 秒，命中时只要 1~2 秒。必须能无缝回退到现有的完整路径。

**已被实测否掉的方案（存档，避免再议）：**
- *J1：JW 侧 MCP 并发连接 + 超时*——JW 侧的 reconcile 只开一个本地回环服务器（毫秒级），48 秒实际花在了 SD 的 catalog 上。此条仅留作上游代码卫生类的小改进建议。
- *S2：adapter 启动时预注册*——工具表是控制面 API 每轮 run 现组装的、经 `/agent/runs` 才交给 adapter；adapter 启动时手里根本没有表可以预注册，硬要预热一张空表，反而会迫使第一条消息触发一次注册代际变更（generation bump）。

## 涉及的公开 API

- 现有：`GET /api/mcp/sources`（MCP 设置页的刷新端点；shell 在 agent-ready 之后也会调用它）。
- S1 不引入任何新的 HTTP API / IPC / 配置项。S3 可能为 skills 缓存增加一个内部失效信号，届时会在其 PR 里写明。

## 与其他模块的关系

- `win_desktop`：shell 的 `watchAgentReady` 预热钩子 + `first-chat-warmup.ts`（新增文件，带单测）。
- `services/api`：S3 的主战场——`executeAgentRun` 头部、`jiuwenswarm-skills.ts` 的 reconcile 链。
- `services/adapter`：`ensure_shared_tools` 本来就会 diff 工具表；S3 可以让它直接走"表未变化"的快速通道。
- JiuwenSwarm 补丁（`jiuwen_swarm/patches/`）：S1/S3 不需要新补丁；J3 会落成 0020+（编号与并行打包工作流协调）。
- `apps/desktop`：UI 无任何变化；就绪屏时序不变。
- #582（输入 token 分析）：与本 issue 互补——J2 直接针对那里说的输入问题。

## 测试设计

- **S1（已在分支上）**：URL/头部构造与超时的单测（`win_desktop/test/first-chat-warmup.test.ts`）；shell 全量测试 116/116 通过，`win_desktop` 构建 + typecheck 干净，2026-11-05 复跑确认。
- **集成 A/B**（每处改动各测一轮）：开发栈 + 本地 mock OpenAI + 按 `agent_server.log` 逐行分段计时；基线和改动必须在**同一主机负载窗口**内测（并行跑着打包构建会让绝对数值失效）；新会话第一条 vs 同会话第二条，跑 3 轮取中位数。
- **冷场景验证**：强制 catalog 为冷（全新数据目录）时，确认 shell 的预热能在用户发出第一条消息之前完成，且第一个 run 里不再出现 stdio 拉起这一段。
- **回归**：shell 构建 + 全量 shell 测试；S3 落地后对 api 包跑 `pnpm test`；涉及补丁时跑 JW 冒烟（gateway / agentserver / 主对话 / 记忆）。
- **装机验证**：GUI 交互安装（不用 `/S` 静默参数），三种启动方式（全新首启 / 热重启 / attach）下记录首响时间，第二条消息无性能回归。

## 验收标准

- [ ] shell 预热：`jiuwenswarm.reachable` 变为 true 后，`shell.log` 里出现 `[warmup] first-chat /api/mcp/sources -> 200`（或一条失败记录）；就绪屏时序和用户可见行为无任何变化。
- [ ] 预热失败永不暴露给用户；竞速失败时自动回退到现有的 run 路径，行为完全一致。
- [ ] 全新安装后的第一条消息不再包含 stdio 拉起 / 工具枚举这一段（现场实测约 48 秒）。
- [ ] 热重启第一条：现场基线 60~135 秒 → **S1+S3 落地后 ≤20 秒**【预期值，待装机 A/B 实测更新】 → **全部方案落地后 6~10 秒**【预期】。
- [ ] 第二条消息约 6 秒，回归幅度不超过噪声水平，随 J2 落地降至约 5 秒。
- [ ] 每轮输入：J2（上游接受后）把工具 schema 的 token 减少 50% 以上，在一组固定真实任务上零回归（召回率不掉）。
- 必须通过的命令：`pnpm ci:l1`（静态门禁）、`pnpm --dir win_desktop build`、`pnpm --dir win_desktop typecheck`、`pnpm --dir win_desktop test`（116/116）、S3 触及包的 `pnpm test`（api / desktop），以及上面说的装机三档验证。
- 性能红线：就绪屏和一切用户可见行为保持不变；预热在设计上就不在关键路径上（fire-and-forget、60 秒超时、只写日志）。

## 附加信息

- 测量说明：拆解锚点的数字是在本机同时跑着并行打包构建时测的，绝对值可能偏高 10~25%；现场数字（60~135 秒）是用户实测，不受影响。结构性结论（各段边界、catalog 预热后 MCP 段归零、JW 回环毫秒级）与负载无关。A/B 永远在同一负载窗口内测。
- 修订记录（2026-11-03）：正文经评审后重新对齐——初版错误地把 26.09 秒的拆解锚点当起点，低估了用户侧的问题；起点已改为现场实测（60~135 秒），26.09 秒只保留它本来的角色：内部分析锚点。
- 修订记录（2026-11-05）：双语跟踪由 #806 合并进本 issue（英文在前、中文镜像在后）；正文同时对齐了 #776 引入的仓库级 feature 模板——`[Feature]:` 标题前缀、七个模板小节、验收标准改为复选框并点名必须通过的命令。
- S1 只实现了桌面 shell 侧；Linux/macOS 源码栈路径通过同一个控制面端点间接受益。
- 证据包（内部）：带会话创建时间戳的 `agent_server.log` 分段、mock 端点 fixture、run 准备链 RPC 清单，归档在本专项知识库。

closed_recent.author: zhaozhaozz
closed_recent.body:
## Background

The CI board for a real end-to-end run is the GitHub Actions run summary. The Nightly workflow (`Nightly`, `.github/workflows/nightly.yml`) calls CI with `profile: daily` and its report job writes only the gate result, the SHA, and the binary artifact names. That is not enough to see how each L5 case actually ran.

L5 is the `release` profile. L4 is the `daily` profile used by Nightly. `test/support/tagged/profiles.mjs` states that every existing eligible real case starts at L3 or L4, so L5 currently selects the same real cases as L4. A table that appears only on a release run would almost never be visible. This issue publishes the same per-case table on both the nightly real E2E run and a release real E2E run.

The shared slice summary (`.ci/tagged-summary.mjs`) stays as it is. Its columns are slice, plan digest, planned, executed, passed, failed, and skipped. This issue adds a separate per-case table. It does not replace that slice summary.

The real E2E score stager (`.ci/prepare-real-e2e-results.mjs`) already keeps `schema_version`, `case`, `case_id`, `integration_status` / `integration`, `started_at`, `finished_at`, `generation_duration_ms`, and the numeric evaluation fields (`score`, `total_score`, `baseline_gate_score`, `best_gate_score`, `overall_score`, citation fields, `status`, `gating`). It does not publish peak memory, generated tokens, judge tokens, total tokens, or tool-call counts. Case metrics do fetch session usage (`generation_usage` or `usage`) and then the stager drops it, because raw results can contain model text and credentials. The only per-case table written to the step summary today is the separate, non-gating PUCT review table.

This is not a substitute for #817. #817 remains the coverage, flake-stability, and release-duration issue. This issue does not change which cases run, the gate rules, required check names, or repository rulesets.

## What to build

Publish one markdown table of real E2E case execution details.

Column contract, in this order:

| # | case | status | score | peak memory GB | generated tokens | judge tokens | total tokens | tool calls | duration min |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |

- `#` is the execution order, starting at 1.
- `case` is the case id, such as `da-1-3`.
- `status` is the case outcome (`passed`, `failed`, `skipped`, or the recorded `integration_status`). The reference layout shows completed rows only. Failed and unfinished selected cases must stay in the table, so this status column is required.
- `score` is the case's official evaluation score. Prefer `evaluation.overall_score`, then `evaluation.total_score`, then `evaluation.score`. Do not use the non-gating PUCT review score.
- `duration min` is `generation_duration_ms / 60000`, shown to one decimal place. Do not substitute the shard wall clock.
- `generated tokens` is the generator's recorded completion tokens. `judge tokens` is the judge's recorded tokens. `total tokens` is the recorded total. When the usage record has only one total, put that number in `total tokens` and leave the split as `n/a`. Do not invent a split.
- `tool calls` is the recorded tool-invocation count for that case.
- `peak memory GB` is the measured peak RSS of that case, in gigabytes, to two decimals. Record it from the case process when the run can sample it.

Display tokens in compact form (`34.2K`, `14.5M`) when the value is at least 1000, and as an integer below that. A missing measurement is the text `n/a`. Never write `0` or a guessed number in place of a missing measurement.

Row order is `started_at` ascending. A selected case with no `started_at` is still listed, after the timed rows, ordered by case id. The table includes every case selected for that real E2E run, not only successes.

Copy only these numeric and identity cells into the table and the artifact. Do not copy prompts, answers, traces, assertion text, error strings, or secrets, even if they sit beside the measurements in the raw result.

Write the table to:

1. The GitHub Actions job summary of the combined real E2E account step, for `profile: daily` and `profile: release`.
2. A run artifact named `case-execution-details.md` on that same run.
3. The Nightly report summary, so opening the Nightly run shows the table or a direct link to that artifact next to the existing gate line. A release run shows the same table in its real E2E summary and artifact.

The slice summary and the PUCT review table stay unchanged.

## Acceptance

- A nightly run (`profile: daily`) and a release run (`profile: release`) each produce `case-execution-details.md` and show the table in the run summary.
- The header is exactly the columns above, in that order.
- Rows follow `started_at`. Every selected case appears once. A failed case is visible and is not dropped.
- A case that recorded a score and a duration shows those values. A case with no peak-memory sample shows `n/a` in that cell.
- A planted secret or model answer in a fixture result does not appear in the markdown.
- Gate results, the required check name `merge-gate`, and rulesets are unchanged. A missing optional cell does not fail the gate.
- A contract test covers the header, the order, `n/a` for a missing metric, inclusion of a failed case, and the exclusion of secret or model text.

## Out of scope

- Changing L4/L5 case selection, coverage collection, flake retries, or the release duration goal in #817.
- A new web page. The Usage page is not this board.
- Editing gate logic or rulesets.

closed_recent.body:
## What happens

A delimited dataset preview (`services/api/src/artifact-dashboard.ts`, `parseDelimitedTable`) takes its width from the **widest line of the whole file**, so one outlier line decides how many columns every returned row shows. A two-column file that contains a single line with 200,001 fields renders as 1,001 columns, 999 of them carrying an empty header and an empty cell in every row.

## Where

- `services/api/src/artifact-dashboard.ts` (at `0477d328`): `const widest = lines.reduce(...)`, `const totalColumns = Math.max(header.length, widest)`, `const width = Math.min(totalColumns, MAX_PREVIEW_COLUMNS)` (`MAX_PREVIEW_COLUMNS = 1001`), and the blank header names built at `columns: header.length >= width ? header.slice(0, width) : [...header, ...Array.from({length: width - header.length}, () => "")]`.

## Measured at `0477d328` (default `maxRows`)

- two-column header plus one line of 200,001 fields: `columns 1001`, `clippedColumns {total: 200001, shown: 1001}`, rows padded to 1001 cells each, so 999 columns and ~99,900 cells in the payload are blank.
- the same file without the outlier line: `columns 2`.

## Why it matters

The preview is widened by a line that is not part of the returned rows, and the extra columns carry no header - the grid shows a two-column table as a 1,001-column one. `clippedColumns` does report `{total, shown}`, so the cut is signalled, but the blank columns themselves are still rendered.

## Suggested fix

Cap the *unnamed surplus* columns the way the CSV importer already does (`apps/web/src/csv-artifact/csv/inferCsv.ts`, `surplusColumnLimit`: `min(16, max(2, header.length))`) while never capping header columns, and keep reporting the dropped cells in `clippedCells` / `clippedColumns`.
closed_recent.title: [Bug] One outlier line sets a delimited preview's width, so a two-column file renders 1,001 mostly-blank columns

closed_recent.author: HugoXK
closed_recent.body:
**Update:** `D1` is fixed inside `#890` itself at `fdb835fb6664acb85e77c2f64c1b3ebfb7fdb7ff` (red first in `ddd14462`; the stem is now cut at the first colon as well as the first dot, so `nul:stream` resolves to `nul` and `con:$DATA` to `con`, with `conin$`/`conout$` and trailing dot/space stripping unchanged). This issue therefore tracks `D2` only — the POSIX-side segment split where `CON\notes.txt` stays one segment and is accepted.

## Summary

`#890` adds a Windows-reserved-device-name guard to the session file write path — `isWindowsReservedDeviceName` in `packages/workspace/src/workspace.ts` plus a per-segment check in `services/api/src/http/index.ts`. It refuses `CON/notes.txt`, `nul.dir/x.csv` and `notes/CON.txt`.

**Residual coverage gap.** After `#890` (with `D1` fixed there), the input below is still accepted:

| Input | Predicate result at `#890`'s head | What happens |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `CON\notes.txt` (POSIX host) | `false` | creates a file literally named `CON\notes.txt`; the same request is refused on a Windows host |

Both were raised as `medium, suggestion` review threads on `#890` (`F1` at `workspace.ts:479`, `F2` at `http/index.ts:3815`) and are tracked here instead of being fixed there. Expected behaviour for all of them: **`400`, naming the offending segment**, exactly as `CON/notes.txt` is answered today.

## D1 — `nul:stream` / `con:$DATA`: the stem keeps the colon, so the predicate misses the device

- **Where:** `packages/workspace/src/workspace.ts:478-481` (predicate added by `#890`).
- **Cause:** the stem is everything before the first dot, so `nul:stream` keeps its colon, `WINDOWS_RESERVED_DEVICE_NAME` does not match it, and the predicate returns `false`. Windows resolves `nul:stream` as the `NUL` device plus the named stream `stream`, so the write does not create a file there.
- **Measured at `#890`'s head:** `"CON" → true`, `"nul.txt" → true`, `"nul.dir" → true`, but `"nul:stream" → false` and `"con:$DATA" → false`.
- **Failing input:** `POST /api/sessions/:id/files` with `{"path":"nul:stream"}` or `{"path":"con:$DATA"}`.
- **Observed:** on POSIX the route answers `201` and creates a file Windows cannot open; on Windows the write targets the device.
- **Expected:** `400`, naming the offending segment.
- **Suggested fix:** split the stem on `:` as well as `.` — for example `name.split(/[.:]/)[0]?.replace(/[. ]+$/, "")` — and add `nul:stream` / `con:$DATA` cases next to the existing ones. `conin$` / `conout$` do not contain a colon and must keep matching.

## D2 — `CON\notes.txt`: the segment walk splits on the host separator only

- **Where:** `services/api/src/http/index.ts:3815`.
- **Cause:** `relative(workspaceRoot, target).split(sep)` splits on `/` on Linux, so `CON\notes.txt` stays one segment, the stem reads `CON\notes`, and the predicate allows it — while the predicate and the route comment both claim the rule is platform-independent.
- **Failing input:** `POST /api/sessions/:id/files` with `{"path":"CON\\notes.txt"}` against a Linux server.
- **Observed:** `201` and a workspace file literally named `CON\notes.txt`; the same request is refused on a Windows host, so the answer depends on which platform serves it.
- **Expected:** refused on every host, with a test case alongside the existing `CON/notes.txt` one.
- **Suggested fix:** split on both separators (`relative(...).split(/[\\/]+/)`) and/or refuse `\` inside a segment.

## D3 — the duplicate private predicate in the upload path

- **Where:** `services/api/src/workspace-upload.ts` (the upload path keeps its own private copy of the reserved-device-name check, wider in two respects: it recognises the named-stream form `NUL:anything` and superscript ports `[1-9¹²³]`).
- **Cause:** the same rule now lives in two places, so a later change to one does not reach the other — exactly how `D1` slipped past the shared predicate.
- **Expected:** after `#890` lands, the upload path imports `isWindowsReservedDeviceName` from `@sciencediscovery/workspace` instead of keeping a private copy (`workspace-upload.ts:19` already imports that package, so this is a one-line change plus deleting the local copy), and its tests keep covering the stream form and superscript ports through the shared predicate.
- **Why it belongs here and not in a new issue:** same family as `D2` — device-name detection precision and de-duplication — and it is one line of code once `#890` is on `main`.

## Acceptance

- All four inputs (`nul:stream`, `con:$DATA`, `CON\notes.txt`, and `notes\CON.txt`) answer `400` with the offending segment named.
- The `WSP-005` cases added by `#890` stay green.
- The guard's claim of being platform-independent holds on Linux and Windows.
- Any documentation or reply describing the guard must say **partial coverage** until this lands: `nul:stream`, `con:$DATA` and POSIX-side `CON\notes.txt` remain accepted.
