closed_recent.body:
## What happens

`#866` / `#868` add a Windows reserved-device-name guard to the **upload** path. The sibling user-write path, `POST /api/sessions/:id/files`, still has no such guard, so the same device names remain writable there.

- Route: `services/api/src/http/index.ts:3804` (`filesMatch` handler), `body.path` resolved at `:3807`.
- `resolveWorkspaceFile` (`packages/workspace/src/workspace.ts:2225`) delegates to `assertWorkspacePath` (`:456`), which only rejects absolute paths and escapes — it knows nothing about device names.
- The result goes straight to `writeFile(target, body.content ?? "", "utf8")` at `:3811`. `sanitizeUploadFilename` (`services/api/src/workspace-upload.ts:67`), where the reserved-name guard lives, is never called on this path.

On a Windows workspace that means `{"path": "con", "content": "x"}` targets the console device (the write silently goes to the console instead of a file) and `{"path": "nul.txt", ...}` fails with a raw `EPERM` that the handler does not classify — the client sees `500 Internal server error`. That is the exact failure shape `#866` reports, on a second user-write path.

## Expected

The reserved-name rule should be a workspace invariant, not an upload-only check: `POST /api/sessions/:id/files` with `CON`, `nul.txt`, `COM1.log`, or `CON .csv` should answer **400** naming the file, and nothing should be written.

## Red first

`#868`'s guard is deliberately platform-independent, so this is testable on Linux without a Windows host: current `main` accepts the name and creates a file.

Suggested test (route level, next to `WSP-004` in `services/api/src/server.test.ts`): create project + session, then

```ts
const res = await fetch(`${origin}/api/sessions/${id}/files`, {
  method: "POST", headers: { ...authorization, "content-type": "application/json" },
  body: JSON.stringify({ path: "CON", content: "x" }),
});
assert.equal(res.status, 400);          // currently 201
assert.match((await res.json()).error, /reserved device name/);
```

and assert the workspace listing is unchanged. Legal look-alikes (`conifer.csv`, `console.log`, `auxiliary.csv`) and `com10.csv` must keep returning 201.

## Fix direction (maintainer's call)

Two shapes work; the first is smaller:

1. Call `sanitizeUploadFilename` (or the exported predicate) on the basename of `body.path` in the `filesMatch` handler before resolving the target.
2. Move the predicate into `packages/workspace` next to `assertWorkspacePath` and call it from both write paths, so the rule cannot drift again.

Either way the guard itself is already written and tested in `#868` (`workspace-upload.ts`, mirrored in `services/api/src/workspace-upload.test.ts`); this issue is about the second entry point.

## Scope

- In: the `POST /api/sessions/:id/files` write path.
- Out: upload paths (fixed by `#868`), read paths, and the desktop client.

## Origin

Raised as finding F2 in `agent-ci-infra-bot`'s review of `#868` (`https://github.com/openJiuwen-ai/sciencediscovery/pull/868#issuecomment-6637755714`), which classed it as a follow-up rather than a blocker for that PR. Filed so the second entry point is not left behind.
closed_recent.title: [Bug]: A Windows reserved device name still writes through the session file-write endpoint

closed_recent.author: HugoXK
closed_recent.body:
### Checklist

- [x] I have searched for related issues but did not get the expected help.
- [x] This bug has not been fixed in the latest version.
- [x] Please note that if your bug description lacks corresponding environment information and a minimal reproducible demo, it will be difficult for us to reproduce and resolve the issue, which will reduce the possibility of receiving feedback, or even lead to the issue being closed.

### 🐞 Detailed Description of the Problem

`services/api/src/workspace-upload.ts` `sanitizeUploadFilename()` guards an empty name, a NUL byte, absolute paths, drive letters and traversal — but not Windows reserved device names. On a Windows runner the OS resolves `CON`, `PRN`, `AUX`, `NUL`, `COM1`–`COM9`, `LPT1`–`LPT9`, `CONIN$` and `CONOUT$` in **every** directory and with **any** extension, so `con.csv` and `nul.txt` pass the guard, reach `writeFile()`/`rename()` in the workspace and fail there with a raw `EPERM`/`ENOENT` that the upload path reports as an unclassified error. `CON` is worse than a failure: opening it targets the console device.

Minimal reproduction (no Windows needed — the guard is the defect):

```ts
import { sanitizeUploadFilename } from "./services/api/src/workspace-upload.ts";

sanitizeUploadFilename("CON.csv");   // expected: rejected; actual: accepted as "CON.csv"
sanitizeUploadFilename("nul.txt");   // expected: rejected; actual: accepted as "nul.txt"
sanitizeUploadFilename("COM1.log");  // expected: rejected; actual: accepted as "COM1.log"
sanitizeUploadFilename("conin$.txt");// expected: rejected; actual: accepted as "conin$.txt"
```

Observed on `main` `8708320f` (`node --import tsx --test services/api/src/workspace-upload.test.ts` after adding the assertions):

```
not ok 2 - sanitizeUploadFilename rejects Windows reserved device names
  error: 'Missing expected exception: CON must be rejected as a Windows reserved device name'
  code: 'ERR_ASSERTION'
# tests 16
# pass 15
# fail 1
```

The other half of the same defect is over-rejection, which any fix must avoid: `conifer.csv`, `console.log`, `auxiliary.csv` and `com10.csv` (two-digit port, not reserved) are legal names and must keep working.

References: <https://learn.microsoft.com/windows/win32/fileio/naming-a-file#naming-conventions> — "Do not use the following reserved names for the name of a file: CON, PRN, AUX, NUL, COM1…COM9, LPT1…LPT9. Also avoid these names followed immediately by an extension; for example, NUL.txt and NUL.tar.gz are both equivalent to NUL." Windows also ignores a trailing dot or space on a segment, so `nul.` and `CON ` name the device too.

Expected: `sanitizeUploadFilename()` rejects those names with `INVALID_UPLOAD_PATH` and names the file in the message, before any write is attempted; legal stems that merely begin with a reserved word stay accepted.

### Detailed Environment Information Description

- OS: Linux (Ubuntu, CI runner) — the guard is platform-independent; the failure it prevents is Windows-only.
- Node.js v22.23.2, pnpm workspace at commit `8708320f` (`main`).
- No Python or GPU dependency; reproduction is a single `node --import tsx --test` run.
- Windows behaviour per the Microsoft naming-conventions document quoted above.

### Additional Information

Found by dogfooding the `services/api` upload path (`SessionStore`'s atomic-write neighbour). The fix keeps the existing guard style (same `INVALID_UPLOAD_PATH` code, same `Object.assign(new Error(...))` shape) and is covered by one test with both directions: the reserved names above must throw `/reserved/`, and `conifer.csv` / `console.log` / `com10.csv` / `auxiliary.csv` must still sanitize unchanged.

### Version Information

`main` @ `8708320f` (2026-11-04). `services/api` `workspace-upload.ts` at line 67 (`sanitizeUploadFilename`).
closed_recent.title: [Bug]: Workspace uploads accept Windows reserved device names and fail at write time

closed_recent.author: qingkwl
closed_recent.body:
## Background

Measuring Windows desktop startup timelines (`python -X importtime`) on workswarm0.2.6 showed `jiuwenswarm.common.config` pulling in a full `portalocker` -> `portalocker.redis` -> `redis asyncio` stack at import time — **~1.00s cold, 95% of which is the redis asyncio stack** (portalocker itself is ~7ms).

```
import time: self [us] | cumulative | imported package
...
      25 |       6795 | portalocker
...
     972 |    999000 |   redis.asyncio.client        <- the actual tax
```

`config.py` is an all-entry import (every jw process — `app_agentserver`, `app_gateway`, `app` — imports it at module load), so this ~1s was paid by **every process, every launch**, even though:

- `update_config()` is a rare write path (uses `portalocker.Lock` only when persisting config changes)
- the same module-level `import portalocker` pattern is repeated in `gateway/cron/store.py` and `common/media_capability_config.py`

`portalocker.redis` is a wrapper that unconditionally imports the full redis client even when you only ever use plain file locks — so any module importing portalocker for file locking pays the redis tax.

## What we did (desktop line, patch 0017)

Three-file fix, <30 lines of product code:

1. **`common/config.py`** — `import portalocker` moved into `update_config()`; the lock dependency only pays on first write.
2. **`gateway/cron/store.py`** — moved into `_call_under_file_lock()`; only the locked store operations pay.
3. **`common/media_capability_config.py`** — the interesting one: `migrate_media_capability_switches()` runs at module load of every jw process. After the first run the `.env` already carries all explicit switches and `os.environ` has them exported, so the locked read-modify-write is a no-op. Added a fast path: if all `MEDIA_CAPABILITY_ENV_FIELDS` keys are already present in the environment, `return {}` — the process never touches the lock branch at all. The first cold run (or a `.env` missing switches) still takes the locked path.

## Measured Effect

Same-machine A/B on the Windows desktop installer line (f25 -> f26):

| metric | before | after |
|---|---|---|
| portalocker/redis in importtime chain (agentserver/gateway) | ~1.0s | 0 hits |
| hot-start gateway `run_entered` | ~4.8s | ~4.7s (R0, cold pyc) |
| first-start net (total minus wizard) | 50.3s | 40.1s |

The hot-start number is partially masked on machines where 360/Defender rescans fresh `.pyc` files (our R0 was all-cold bytecode); the first-start number (28.1s, full first-launch timeline) is the cleaner signal — ~5s of that comes from this patch plus the AgentServer construction re-chain of 0016 (AgentServer listen 13.95s -> 1.53s in the f26 field logs).

## Suggestion for upstream

Either of these would benefit any embedding product that imports `jiuwenswarm.common.config` at entry:

1. **Cheap**: move `import portalocker` into the lock-using functions (as we did — happy to upstream this as a PR).
2. **Upstream of us**: `portalocker.redis` importing the full redis asyncio stack eagerly is the root cause; if you depend on plain file locking only, consider whether `portalocker` is worth ~1s of every process's import time, or use `os.open` + `msvcrt.locking`/`fcntl.flock` directly for the file-lock use cases.

Happy to provide the three-file patch (diff against workswarm0.2.6, shipped as `0017-lazy-portalocker-imports.patch` in our desktop patch chain) as a starting point.

## Version

- workswarm0.2.6 (commit `70aa671`)
- Windows 11, Python 3.12

closed_recent.author: yuanzhou75
closed_recent.body:
### Checklist

- [X] I have searched for related issues but did not get the expected help.
- [X] This bug has not been fixed in the latest version.
- [X] Please note that if your bug description lacks corresponding environment information and a minimal reproducible demo, it will be difficult for us to reproduce and resolve the issue, which will reduce the possibility of receiving feedback, or even lead to the issue being closed.

### 🐞 Detailed Description of the Problem

**What the user sees.** In the Nightly real E2E shard `research-8`, the PUCT-COMPRESS case runs to completion and is scored (`integration_status: passed`, `score: 0.693134`, LLM evaluation `90`) — and then the journey fails in teardown:

```text
Error: DELETE /api/projects/6dfc35df-891e-42c2-b5a5-b89c36d75805 -> 502: {"error":"legacy_unavailable","message":"ReadError","requestId":"762bacad18934c84b5b9dc8ad5c6a09a"}
  at apiJson (test/helpers/journeys.ts:149)
  at cleanupJourney (test/helpers/journeys.ts:1006)
```

A shell execution had been left `unknown` one minute into the run, and from then on the session could neither run a new command nor be torn down: cancelling that execution never returns, and the project delete waits behind it until the adapter's read deadline expires.

**Evidence** (shard `stack.log`, artifact `real-e2e-evidence-research-8`, Nightly run [42519625781](https://github.com/openJiuwen-ai/sciencediscovery/actions/runs/42519625781), sha `c95f080`).

1. The execution that could not be committed:

```text
[jiuwenswarm-bridge] tool run_shell failed: {"executionId":"shell:b8d0dc54332628eb510f7ee6ce92db2d6de9021f2ff429b14e78439eb952b16f","state":"unknown","error":"Existing execution result could not be committed; retry uses the same result","recovery":{"schemaVersion":1,"capability":"unknown","reason":"NOT_REPORTED"},"finalization":"failed",...}
```

2. Every later shell call in that workspace is refused (the agent retried this for the rest of the case):

```text
{"ok":false,"error":{"attempts":1,"code":"TOOL_EXECUTION_FAILED","message":"Execution shell:b8d0dc54... has an unconfirmed outcome. Inspect execution_status before starting more work in this workspace; no replacement was submitted.","retryable":false}}
```

3. At teardown, cancelling exactly that execution never answers — the request line carries no status code at all, i.e. it never completed:

```text
POST /api/sessions/2707a3fe-bb5c-4104-89bf-4a8af4c69ba2/agent-activity/executions/shell%3Ab8d0dc54332628eb510f7ee6ce92db2d6de9021f2ff429b14e78439eb952b16f/cancel HTTP/1.1
```

4. The project delete then trips the adapter's proxy read deadline:

```text
legacy_proxy_failure request_id=762bacad18934c84b5b9dc8ad5c6a09a method=DELETE path=/api/projects/6dfc35df-891e-42c2-b5a5-b89c36d75805 phase=headers elapsed_ms=10350 causes=[{'type': 'ReadError', ...}]
INFO:  127.0.0.1:45568 - "DELETE /api/projects/6dfc35df-891e-42c2-b5a5-b89c36d75805 HTTP/1.1" 502 Bad Gateway
```

5. The API was already parking requests for many minutes in the same window — 89 `GET /api/projects/6dfc35df-891e-42c2-b5a5-b89c36d75805/research-package/preview` requests were still pending at shutdown, the oldest `elapsed_ms=936120` (~15.6 min).

**Code.**

`services/api/src/shell-executions.ts`

- `unavailable()` at 428-464 turns any commit/observation failure into `execution.state = "unknown"`, `provenance = "unconfirmed"`, `finalization = "failed"`, and stores a canned detail built at 451-453 — for this failure the text is `Existing execution result could not be committed; retry uses the same result`, so the underlying error is not visible. The real error is only emitted as a `shell_execution_unconfirmed` warning at 795-796, which did not reach the shard log.
- The commit path at 760-822 (`existingResult` 416-426, `commitFailure` 400-414, fallback 813) is where an execution becomes `unknown` with no transition back to a terminal state.
- The workspace guard that then refuses every new `run_shell` is the "unconfirmed outcome" branch reached from the same record.

Harness side that turns this into a red case: `test/helpers/journeys.ts:995-1010` (`cleanupJourney` → `cancelActiveSessionRuns` → project DELETE) and `test/helpers/session-shutdown.ts:123-131`, which returns `cleanup_failed` whenever runs/executions never go quiet inside its 45 s deadline.

**Expected.**

- An execution whose result cannot be committed must be settlable. Cancelling it must return a definite answer, or cancellation must not be a precondition for the session to go quiet.
- Project deletion must not wait indefinitely on one such execution; a project delete that cannot finish should fail fast with a diagnostic naming the blocker.
- The underlying commit error should be retained on the record (a code plus a short reason), not replaced by the canned sentence, so the next occurrence is diagnosable from `stack.log` alone.
- Today the only recovery is restarting the whole stack, which converts an already-passing real-E2E case into a Nightly failure.

### Detailed Environment Information Description

- Repository: `openJiuwen-ai/sciencediscovery`, `main` at `c95f080a6c3b1bb5e020808b5114e1894148422d`.
- GitHub Actions `ubuntu-latest`, 15.6 GiB RAM; Nightly (`profile: daily`) real E2E, shard `research-8`, started 2026-11-08T20:20:32Z (2026-11-09 04:20 CST).
- Stack: adapter (Python/uvicorn) on `127.0.0.1:4410` in front of the Node API on `4510`, runner on `4411`, memory-graph on `17774`, JiuwenSwarm backend (`CI_E2E_BACKEND=jiuwenswarm`), `E2E_LLM_MODEL=deepseek-flash`.
- Case: `PUCT-COMPRESS documented text compression search` (`test/evolve-compression-real.spec.ts`), 27.1 min; run metrics: `integration_status: passed`, `score 0.693134`, `baseline_gate_score 0.285339`.

### Additional Information

This is not a one-off: on the same Nightly, `research-5` also failed with the harness giving up on a 5 s read (`apiRequestContext.fetch: Timeout 5000ms exceeded`), and `research-12` was killed by an API heap OOM (issue #1011). A plausible shared cause is that long real sessions accumulate work the API never bounds; this issue is the part that makes teardown unrecoverable once one execution is stuck.

### Version Information

- `main` @ `c95f080a6c3b1bb5e020808b5114e1894148422d`
- Nightly run 42519625781 (2026-11-08T20:20:32Z), shard `research-8`, artifact `real-e2e-evidence-research-8` (artifact id 13636806778)

closed_recent.author: JinhZhao
closed_recent.body:
## 1. Summary

When the main agent dispatches multiple subagents that share the **same specialist** configuration in parallel, each subagent independently calls `prepareSkillSandbox()` to initialize a content-addressed skill snapshot directory. Because the directory name is a deterministic SHA-256 hash of the skill set (`skillPackageSetHash()`), all parallel subagents targeting the same specialist compute the **same target path** and race to `rename()` their individual staging directories to that shared target.

On Windows NTFS, `rename()` over an existing directory returns `EPERM`. The error handler in `skill-sandbox.ts` (line 212) only catches `EEXIST` and `ENOTEMPTY` (POSIX error codes), so the Windows `EPERM` error is re-thrown as an unhandled exception, killing the subagent before it executes a single turn.

**Observed impact**: 3 out of 4 parallel subagents failed at Turn 0 with EPERM, before performing any work.

---

## 2. Environment

| Field | Value |
|-------|-------|
| OS | Windows 11 (Build 22631), NTFS |
| Node.js | v24.18.0 |
| SD commit (upstream) | `b31f74eb368a0e07848c2aa72acf9451348471bb` (HEAD of `main`) |
| JD commit (downstream) | `b78fa615dc4395955546ae047089d3e54e149e05` (HEAD of `main`) |
| JD import baseline | SD v0.3.0-rc1 |
| Executor type | Native Windows direct-execution (not Docker, not WSL) |
| Model | DICP DeepSeek-Flash (model ID `6a2d8980-f1e1-47e0-8d12-9272971d89bd`) |
| Concurrent specialists | 4 × `builtin-literature-searcher` (same specialist ID) |
| Skill in use | `catalyst-research-team` (revision 1) + 19 other skills |
| Approval mode | `always_allow` |

**Note**: The `skill-sandbox.ts` file is byte-identical (CRLF-normalized SHA-256: `9ff817692572f8bdc28925c7121f69ac91390f545e77b4b44d7cb38460907aac`) across SD upstream (`b6967407a` through `b31f74eb`) and JD downstream (`262c2c2b2` through `b78fa615d`). The defect was introduced in SD commit `7daf63637` and has never been modified by JD.

---

## 3. Steps to Reproduce

### 3.1 From real E2E test (E2E-045)

These steps reflect what actually happened during the failing test run:

1. Start the ScienceDiscovery API server on Windows (native executor, not Docker).
2. Create a session with the `catalyst-research-team` skill enabled.
3. Send a prompt that causes the main agent to dispatch **multiple subagents with the same `specialistId`** in parallel. In our test, the prompt asked for a Pd catalysis literature review, and the model independently chose to dispatch 4 × `builtin-literature-searcher` (lanes L1–L4) simultaneously.
4. All 4 subagents are created at the same timestamp (`2026-11-09T10:17:27.587Z`).
5. Each subagent calls `prepareSkillSandbox()` during initialization.
6. Because all 4 use the same specialist configuration, they compute the same snapshot hash (`765160e2...`).
7. The first subagent to reach `rename(staging, root)` succeeds and creates the target directory.
8. The remaining 3 subagents hit `EPERM` when their `rename()` targets the now-existing directory.
9. All 3 fail at Turn 0 with `EPERM: operation not permitted, rename ...`.

### 3.2 Suggested minimal reproduction

Based on code analysis (not independently tested):

1. Call `prepareSkillSandbox()` concurrently (e.g., `Promise.all`) 2+ times with the same `root` path and same `skills` array.
2. On Windows, observe that all but one call throw `EPERM`.
3. On Linux/macOS, verify whether the existing `EEXIST`/`ENOTEMPTY` handling correctly manages concurrent initialization under the same conditions.

### 3.3 What is observed vs. inferred

- **Observed**: Steps 1–9 above are from real SSE event traces (see §8 Evidence).
- **Inferred**: The minimal reproduction (§3.2) is derived from code analysis. The actual trigger requires the main agent to dispatch same-specialist subagents in parallel, which depends on the model's autonomous scheduling decision.

---

## 4. Expected Behavior

- Multiple subagents selecting the same skill set should safely share one content-addressed snapshot directory.
- The concurrent `rename()` race should be handled gracefully on **all** platforms, including Windows.
- A subagent that loses the rename race should detect that the winning subagent already created a valid snapshot (via `existingSnapshotMatches()`) and proceed normally.
- The existing code comment acknowledges this design intent: *"Either is fine as long as the winner staged the same bytes."*

---

## 5. Actual Behavior

From the E2E-045 test run (Session `610ecb7b-58d2-471e-8026-7e7549af3cda`):

| Subagent ID | Lane | Status | Turn Count | Error |
|-------------|------|--------|------------|-------|
| `8336eff9-e83b-4837-9fbd-7b397b49bb00` | L2 | Survived | 15 | — |
| `fa3598ee-bdd0-4fe0-ab13-e3347a59d762` | L3 | **Failed** | 0 | EPERM |
| `b8df2786-01d7-4b10-8a1e-eac954d8ebe2` | L4 | **Failed** | 0 | EPERM |
| `be633c8c-cde1-44de-9eb1-146ba17a422e` | L1 | **Failed** | 0 | EPERM |

**Evidence count by scope**:

| Counting scope | Count | Notes |
|----------------|-------|-------|
| Unique failed subagents | 3 | `fa3598ee`, `b8df2786`, `be633c8c` — distinct incidents |
| Unique EPERM error instances | 3 | One per failed subagent, each targeting the same hash |
| Raw SSE text matches | 31 | Each failure echoed across multiple SSE event types |
| Processed SSE text matches | 81 | Further propagated into `error`, `subagent_error`, `summary.error` fields |

The 31 raw and 81 processed counts do **not** represent 31 or 81 independent failures. They arise because each of the 3 failure events is echoed across multiple SSE event types (`subagent.updated`, `tool.output`, `tool.completed`) and repeated in structured error fields. The 3 unique subagent failures in the table above are the distinct incidents.

**Additional observations**:
- All 3 failures targeted the same snapshot hash: `765160e2edbdb8d52dbb031b6b709a52cbd176da2d5a4cf7dc30c680b6516a0f`.
- Each subagent created its own unique staging directory (`.UUID.skill-snapshot`), but all tried to rename to the same target.
- All 3 failures occurred within 5–6 seconds of subagent creation (10:17:27 → 10:17:32–33).
- The target directory `765160e2...` exists on disk, confirming the winning rename succeeded.

---

## 6. Technical Findings

### 6.1 Defect location

**File**: `services/api/src/skill-sandbox.ts`  
**Lines**: 206–215 (current version, SD `b6967407a` onward)

```typescript
try {
  await rename(staging, root);                              // line 206
} catch (error) {                                           // line 207
  // Concurrent runs sharing one content-addressed root race here; POSIX
  // reports a non-empty destination as ENOTEMPTY or EEXIST depending on
  // the platform. Either is fine as long as the winner staged the same bytes.
  const code = (error as NodeJS.ErrnoException).code;       // line 211
  if ((code !== "EEXIST" && code !== "ENOTEMPTY")           // line 212 ← BUG
      || !await existingSnapshotMatches(root, expectedManifest)) {
    throw error;                                            // line 214 ← EPERM hits this
  }
}
```

### 6.2 Platform-specific `rename()` behavior

| Platform | `rename(temp, existing_dir)` returns | Handled? |
|----------|--------------------------------------|----------|
| Linux (ext4) | `ENOTEMPTY` | Yes (line 212) |
| macOS (APFS) | `EEXIST` | Yes (line 212) |
| **Windows (NTFS)** | **`EPERM`** | **No** |

The code comment explicitly references POSIX behavior ("POSIX reports a non-empty destination as ENOTEMPTY or EEXIST") but does not account for Windows NTFS returning `EPERM`.

### 6.3 Call chain

```
runs/index.ts:871   → main agent calls prepareSkillSandbox(skillPackagesRoot, ...)
runs/index.ts:1926  → subagent calls prepareSkillSandbox(subagentSkillPackagesRoot, ...)
                    → prepareSkillSandbox() at skill-sandbox.ts:142
                    → rename(staging, root) at skill-sandbox.ts:206
                    → Windows returns EPERM
                    → catch at line 207 checks EEXIST/ENOTEMPTY only
                    → EPERM re-thrown at line 214
                    → subagent fails at Turn 0
```

### 6.4 Content-addressed hash mechanism

The `skillPackageSetHash()` function (line 124–130) computes a SHA-256 hash from the sorted set of skill IDs, revisions, versions, and content hashes. This is **by design** — the code comment at lines 119–123 states:

> *"Identity of one selected Skill set, used as the content-addressed snapshot directory name. Runs that select the same frozen revisions reuse one staged tree, which also keeps a persistent kernel's mounts stable across runs."*

This means any parallel dispatch of the same specialist **will** produce hash collisions and trigger the rename race. This is not an edge case — it is the expected behavior of the content-addressed design.

### 6.5 Introducing commit

| Field | Value |
|-------|-------|
| Commit | `7daf636372867dcfc780fe6b5f6d6695033bfa6b` |
| Author | wang_cheng_zhao |
| Date | 2026-08-31 12:01:53 +0000 |
| Message | `feat(skills): 技能包按变量寻址并按集合内容去重` |
| Repository | `openJiuwen-ai/sciencediscovery` |

This commit added the content-addressed hash mechanism and the `ENOTEMPTY` check (for Linux), but did not include `EPERM` (for Windows). The commit message references Linux `ENOTEMPTY` and the code comment references POSIX — Windows was not considered.

### 6.6 Control comparison: sequential dispatch

In a separate test (TEST-042, same environment), the main agent dispatched 4 **different** specialists **sequentially** (literature-searcher → evidence-extractor → hypothesis-designer → experiment-designer). Each specialist has a different skill configuration → different hash → different target path → **zero rename collisions** → 4/4 succeeded with no EPERM. This is consistent with the defect being specific to concurrent same-hash initialization, though it does not isolate concurrency as the sole variable (the test also differs in specialist type and dispatch order).

---

## 7. Proposed Investigation / Fix Direction

These are suggestions for the SD development team to consider, not prescriptive requirements.

### 7.1 Areas to investigate

1. **Windows `rename()` concurrency behavior**: Verify whether `fs.rename()` on NTFS consistently returns `EPERM` when the target directory exists, or whether the error code varies by Windows version or Node.js version.

2. **Cross-platform error code coverage**: Audit all `rename()` error handling in the codebase for platform-specific error codes. The current code covers `EEXIST` (macOS) and `ENOTEMPTY` (Linux) but not `EPERM` (Windows).

3. **Safe reuse of existing snapshots**: When the rename race is lost, the code already calls `existingSnapshotMatches()` to verify the winner's snapshot. Ensure this verification is robust — the target directory existing on disk does not guarantee it was fully written by a concurrent process.

4. **Snapshot integrity under concurrency**: Consider whether the `wx` (exclusive create) flag on `writeFile()` provides sufficient protection against reading a partially-written snapshot from a concurrent loser's staging directory.

5. **Staging directory cleanup**: Verify that the `finally { await rm(staging, ...) }` block correctly cleans up the loser's staging directory even when the rename fails with `EPERM`.

### 7.2 Suggested handling logic

The general approach would be:

1. Catch the rename exception.
2. Check if the error code is one of the expected concurrency indicators (`EEXIST`, `ENOTEMPTY`, `EPERM`, or any other platform-specific code).
3. If it is a concurrency indicator, verify the target snapshot's integrity (content matches expected manifest).
4. If integrity is confirmed, treat the rename as successfully handled (another process won the race with identical content).
5. If integrity is not confirmed, either retry or raise a more descriptive error.

---

- **E2E-045**: 3/4 parallel `builtin-literature-searcher` subagents failed at Turn 0 on Windows.

### 9.2 Potential impact (inferred from code analysis)

This defect affects **any** scenario where:
1. The runtime is on Windows (NTFS).
2. Multiple subagents with the same specialist configuration are dispatched concurrently.
3. The subagents share the same session (same content-addressed snapshot path).

This is not limited to the catalyst research team workflow. Any skill that uses the `prepareSkillSandbox()` function with parallel same-specialist dispatch is potentially affected.

- Linux (ext4, etc.): `rename()` returns `ENOTEMPTY`, which is handled.
- macOS (APFS): `rename()` returns `EEXIST`, which is handled.

A separate incident on our side reported "File is locked by another process" errors during file **write** operations. closed_recent.title: [Bug]: Concurrent skill snapshot initialization fails with EPERM on Windows

closed_recent.author: qingkwl
closed_recent.body:
### 🚀 Background Description

The Windows desktop installer weighed **797.6 MiB** at the f26 baseline (`836,309,864 B`, SHA256 `9f82926d…`). A payload audit (per-package import scans plus reverse-dependency tracing) confirmed roughly **1.2 GB of uncompressed dead weight**: dependency packages never imported by runtime code, giant binaries pulled in by extras (claude.exe 237 MB, the codex toolchain ~437 MB, the playwright driver 88 MB, uv.exe 49 MB), lint-group dev tools (mypy/ruff/pylint ~40 MB), transitive dependencies of chromadb/jinja2/a2ui (kubernetes 37 MB, onnxruntime 42 MB, babel 32 MB, google_adk ~20 MB), and heavy duplication across the five Python service envs (pydantic/fastapi/uvicorn each stored five times).

Four waves of optimization have been implemented, taking the installer from f26 to **578.0 MiB (`606,126,666 B`), −219.6 MiB / −27.5%** — W1 dead-weight removal, W2 env merge, W3 version alignment, W4 build gates + locales trim. Each wave shipped its own installer and was verified independently. The uncompressed payload went **2827 → 1694 MB (−40%)**.

**Where the work stands.** The four waves live in **PR #834** (open, head `61c59a46`, base `main`), pushed to the author's fork branch `sizeopt/f26-6to2`. The PR is **not merged**, the repository has no `release4` tag or GitHub release (latest release is `v0.3.0`). So `578.0 MiB` is a **measured local build**, not a published artifact. This issue is the single tracking item for that work; the earlier Chinese-only twin has been merged into it and closed.

Three blockers on that PR head, only one of which CI reports:

1. **UT red — test harness.** `test/support/tagged/shared.mjs` still provisions one venv per service, which a uv workspace no longer creates. `PREPARATION_FAILED`.
2. **ST red — a real regression introduced by this PR, not the harness.** Job 126320174165 ran the whole plan (`executed: 51, passed: 50, failed: 1`) and failed only `check:swarm-sdk-contract@linux/amd64`. That check runs `bash scripts/jiuwenswarm.sh setup` and then `pytest jiuwen_swarm/tests` **on the same venv this PR builds**. W1 added `--no-default-groups` to that setup, and JW's `[tool.uv] default-groups = ['dev']` with `dev = test + lint` — so pytest is excluded from the venv the contract check then runs pytest with. Reproduced locally, not inferred: `.venv\Scripts\python.exe -m pytest --version` → **`No module named pytest`**. Fixing the harness alone would leave ST red.
3. **The Docker product image does not build from this tree, and CI cannot see it.** `Dockerfile:137/146/155/163/170` still `--mount=type=bind` each `services/<svc>/uv.lock`, which W2 deleted → BuildKit fails with "failed to compute cache key". Dropping only the mounts does not help either: that dependency layer carries just the member `pyproject.toml`s, so `uv sync --locked` then reports `Unable to find lockfile at 'uv.lock'` (reproduced with uv 0.13). The `Docker image` job is **skipped** in the PR profile and `merge-gate` only requires UT/ST/L2, so nothing flags this. Same class of breakage in `scripts/binary-release/build-payload.sh`. Details and the fix in *Relevance to Other Modules* → collateral damage.

This issue is closed **manually** — PR #834 carries no closing keyword (it links #807/#808 as context only), so merging it will not close anything here.

**Hard constraints (owner decision, unchanged throughout):** offline double-click install, zero network at first run, no first-run slowdown. The W15 all-baked pyc precompile design is untouched — assemble now *fails the build* if precompile fails, which is what protects that design.

**Scope evolved after install testing (2026-11-04).** Installing release4 on a real machine met the size goal but surfaced two problems that are not size problems: the hot start measured **31.97 s**, and the longest payload path measured `maxRel = 224`, giving a **path-budget margin of 0** at that install root. Fixing those is tracked as **Phase 5 (D10–D12)** below — code written, release5 being packaged, install verification pending. Phase 5 is *not* part of PR #834 yet.

### Design Ideas

Wave-based: every wave produces its own installer, is verified on its own, and can be reverted alone (three independent commits, plus reversible JW patches).

Two units are used throughout and must not be mixed — every size figure below states which one it is:
- **uncompressed payload** (what assemble lays on disk), and
- **installer** (7z-compressed; f26 overall retention 29.6%).

The first projection round got this wrong and over-promised by 43–113 MB per wave, because it applied the *overall* retention to slices that compress far better than average. The corrected rule: project a wave with the **mixed retention of the content actually being removed**. W1 measured 18.6% on its removed slice (dominated by `.py` sources such as `claude_agent_sdk`).

**W1 — slim the JW payload + strip the codex vendor (done, installer −184.2 MiB → 613.4 MiB / `643,132,732 B`; payload 2827 → 1786 MB, −1041 MB)**

1. `scripts/jiuwenswarm.sh`: `uv sync` gains `--no-default-groups`, so lint/test groups never enter the runtime venv (**measured ~40 MB**: mypy 12 + mypyc 5 + the `fb62009__mypyc` .pyd 19 + pylint/astroid/codespell etc.). The same change fixes a hard-coded POSIX `jw_bin` that broke setup under Git Bash — it now picks `Scripts/` by existence.
2. **claude/codex extras close (the bulk of this wave).** A fresh `uv sync` never installs extras; the old tree was an `--all-extras` leftover. Measured old-vs-new venv diff: `claude_agent_sdk` (238 MB) is no longer installed; playwright (104 MB) is then formally moved out of JW main deps by patch 0018. Together these took the JW venv **1578 → 895 MB** (746 MB after the patch).
3. New `win_desktop/scripts/lib/payload-slim.mjs`: an assemble-time whitelist sweep for transitive deps uv cannot exclude (kubernetes / onnxruntime / babel / google_adk / the mypy family / claude_agent_sdk / playwright / uv, plus venv `Scripts` launchers and the nested `google/adk`). Every rule carries an audit citation in-code, and the rule set is unit-tested (5/5). Backstop philosophy: fresh trees never install them; stale trees get swept.
4. assemble drops the `@openai/codex` vendored native toolchain (**~437 MB uncompressed**). Verified the SDK never touches those binaries at import time (it resolves them at `Codex` construction), so api startup is unaffected — only a codex specialist *run* fails at use time. That failure mode is the reason the degradation contract below exists.
5. JW patch chain gains `0018-desktop-slim-deps`: playwright/uv removed from main deps in JW's pyproject (uv.lock regenerated into the patch; chain **14 → 15** — `main` carries 14 patch files, 0001–0010 plus the 0015/0016/0016b/0017 startup patches), and `huawei_selectors.py`'s top-level import degrades to `Any` via try/except (**−156 MB**; every runtime call site was verified to be a function-level lazy import or pip fallback).

**W2 — merge five service envs into one uv workspace (done, installer −30.1 MiB → 583.3 MiB / `611,529,375 B`; payload → 1684.5 MB, envs-template 525.3 → 423.7 MB)**

1. A **virtual** workspace root at `pyproject.toml` (`[tool.uv.workspace]`, five members, no `[project]` so the root is never itself installed). The five per-service `uv.lock` files are deleted; one root `uv.lock` resolves 68 packages, every conflict taking the highest version inside the constraint intersection (fastapi 0.162 / websockets 17.4 / pydantic 2.14 / numpy 2.5.4 / pandas 3.1).
2. `start-stack.mjs`: five per-service syncs → one workspace sync (still including the evolve `candidates` extra); all four service pythons resolve to `envs/sd-services`.
3. `bootstrap.ts` `venvNames` → `["sd-services"]`; `assemble-backend.mjs` `VENV_NAMES` likewise.
4. Trade-off, stated explicitly: this revisits the earlier "never merge venvs" principle. After highest-version unification the only hard conflict was websockets (JW caps `<16`), handled by the W3 patch. The accepted cost is that **any single service's dependency upgrade now needs full-stack regression**, since there is one env.

**W3 — version alignment + a falsified idea (done; no installer-size wave of its own)**

JW patch `0019-align-workspace-versions` raises the websockets cap `<16` → `<18` and aligns numpy/pandas with the workspace (2.5.4 / 3.1.0), manifest 15 → 16. Two findings worth recording:
- websockets **17 is pinned out** by google-genai's `<17`, so the lock stays on 15.0.1 — zero behaviour change. Every call site was audited and carries a legacy→new-API fallback, which is what made raising the cap safe at all.
- **Hardlink dedup across venvs was designed, measured, and closed as ineffective.** Identical content across the JW venv and the shared venv measured 59.9 MB, but 7z solid-window mechanics plus venv isolation mean hardlinks buy nothing in the installer. Closing it avoided spending engineering effort on a lever that cannot pay. The merge benefit was already banked in W2.

**W4 — build gates + locales trim (done, installer −5.3 MiB → 578.0 MiB)**

assemble gained four hard gates, all modelled on the JW official packaging scripts and all following the same philosophy — *self-proving, always printed, hard-failing*:
- **precompile failure fails the build** (was a warning). This roots out the "payload pyc silently skipped" class of defect.
- **A1 payload import self-check** — run the *payload's own* interpreters and import the shipped modules (JW: `jiuwenswarm.common.config`, `gateway.app_gateway`, `server.app_agentserver`; services: `sciencediscovery_gateway/_memory_graph/_evolve/_adapter`). This is the gate that would have caught the silent precompile skip. It caught a real timing bug on its first run.
- **A2 RequiredFiles manifest** — 9 entries an installer must contain (SEA, patch manifest, the editable `.pth`), hard failure if any is missing.
- **A4 payload size always printed** at the end of assemble.

Electron locales were trimmed by a new afterPack hook (`win_desktop/scripts/after-pack-trim-locales.cjs`): **55 shipped → 52 removed → 3 kept** (en-US / zh-CN / zh-TW). The release4 build log records `[afterPack] trimmed 52 Electron locale pak(s)`; ~45 MB raw became ~5 MiB in the installer — the smallest of the four waves, and a good reminder that raw-MB and installer-MiB are different currencies.

**Phase 5 — quality governance triggered by install testing (code written; release5 packaging; install verification pending)**

Not in PR #834. Five items, all from measured install-tree evidence rather than projection:
- **Path budget (A5 gate + layout shortening).** Install root `D:\ProgramData\SD\ScienceDiscovery` measured `maxRel = 224` over 95,002 files → `maxAbs = 259` against a 259 usable budget, **margin 0**. Fixed by (a) a new assemble gate that walks the payload tree and prints `maxRel` with dual thresholds (runtime 189 / build-time 170) and fails over the limit, and (b) shortening the payload prefix `backend\.sciencediscovery-data\jiuwenswarm\src` → **`backend\jw`** (saves 36 chars, `maxRel` 224 → 188). A bug in the gate itself was found and fixed during calibration: it computed paths relative to the build dir, undercounting by 6 chars on short build trees — exactly enough to mask a violation.
- **Startup performance.** The hot-start breakdown attributed **12.42 s of 31.97 s (39%)** to a single synchronous import (`install_subagent_observability_hook()`, pulling 3,946 modules). JW patch `0020-lazy-observability-import` moves it to `asyncio.to_thread`, adds a third idempotent guard in `get_agent()` (matching the two already added by 0015/0016), and cancels the task in shutdown's `finally`. Patch chain 16 → **17**, `verify` exit 0. **Expected** hot start 31.97 s → ~19.5 s — *expected, not measured*.
- **`verifyPatches` fixed cost (0.87 s).** Fingerprint cache (patch name+size+mtime vs. the src manifest), with `--force-verify` / `JIUWENSWARM_FORCE_VERIFY=1` escape hatches. Implementing it exposed a genuine pre-existing bug: `recordVerified` called `writeFileSync` **without importing it**, the `ReferenceError` was swallowed by a surrounding `try/catch`, the marker never landed, and the cache never hit — so every start repaid the 0.87 s. That cost *is* the bug.

### Test Design and Test Plan

Measurement procedure, stated so the numbers are reproducible and comparable:

- **Size.** Installer bytes are read off the produced `.exe` (`release4`: `606,126,666 B`), not off a projection. Payload figures are uncompressed on-disk totals printed by assemble's A4 gate. Every figure is labelled with its unit.
- **Startup.** End-to-end is defined as **shell T0 → the shell's first successful gateway TCP probe**. Profiles: cold = first launch including provisioning, warm = second launch, hot = third launch onward. Three consecutive launches, one machine, logged via the `[SD-PERF]` / `[perf]` marks in `shell.log` (UTC) and `startup-diagnostics.log`. Note the clock discipline: `jiuwenswarm.log` is local UTC+8 while shell logs are UTC, and `[AgentServer]` vs `[App]` are two processes with independent `process_elapsed` clocks — segments may only be differenced within one prefix, cross-process steps must use absolute timestamps.
- **Path budget.** Walk the installed tree, take `maxRel = max(len(path) − len(root) − 1)`, then `maxAbs = len(root) + 1 + maxRel` against a 259 usable budget.

### 设计思路

分波次实施：每波独立出包、独立验证、可单独回退（三个独立 commit，加上可 reverse 的 JW 补丁）。

全文使用两套口径，不得混用 —— 下方每个体积数字都标明是哪一套：
- **未压缩载荷**（assemble 落盘的实际内容）
- **安装包**（7z 压缩口径；f26 整体留存 29.6%）

首轮预期正是栽在这里：对压缩率远好于均值的切片套用了*整体*留存率，每波高估 43–113 MB。修正后的规则：波次预期必须按**被砍内容自身的混合压缩率**折算。W1 被砍切片实测留存 18.6%（以 `claude_agent_sdk` 之类 `.py` 源码为主）。

**W1 —— JW 载荷瘦身 + codex vendor 剔除（已完成，安装包 −184.2 MiB → 613.4 MiB / `643,132,732 B`；载荷 2827 → 1786 MB，−1041 MB）**

1. `scripts/jiuwenswarm.sh`：`uv sync` 加 `--no-default-groups`，lint/test 组不再进运行时 venv（**实测 ~40 MB**：mypy 12 + mypyc 5 + `fb62009__mypyc` .pyd 19 + pylint/astroid/codespell 等）。同一处顺带修掉硬编码 POSIX `jw_bin` 导致 Git Bash 下 setup 不通的问题 —— 现按存在性自适应 `Scripts/`。
2. **claude/codex extras 收口（本波大头）。** 新鲜 `uv sync` 本就不装 extras，旧树是 `--all-extras` 历史遗留。新旧 venv diff 实测：`claude_agent_sdk`（238 MB）不再安装；playwright（104 MB）随后由补丁 0018 正式移出 JW 主依赖。两步叠加使 JW venv **1578 → 895 MB**（打完补丁 746 MB）。
3. 新增 `win_desktop/scripts/lib/payload-slim.mjs`：assemble 阶段按白名单清扫 uv 无法排除的传递依赖（kubernetes / onnxruntime / babel / google_adk / mypy 系 / claude_agent_sdk / playwright / uv，以及 venv `Scripts` 启动器与嵌套 `google/adk`）。每条规则在代码内带审计出处注释，规则库有单测（5/5）。backstop 哲学：新树不装、旧树扫掉。
4. assemble 剔除 `@openai/codex` vendor 原生工具链（**~437 MB 未压缩**）。已实测 SDK import 时不触二进制（`Codex` 构造时才 resolve），故 api 启动不受影响 —— 只有 codex specialist *运行时*才会失败。这个失败形态正是下面「降级契约」存在的原因。
5. JW 补丁链新增 `0018-desktop-slim-deps`：JW pyproject 主依赖移除 playwright/uv（uv.lock 重生成入补丁，链 **14 → 15** —— `main` 上有 14 个补丁文件，即 0001–0010 加 0015/0016/0016b/0017 四个启动补丁），`huawei_selectors.py` 顶层 import 改 try/except 降级为 `Any`（**−156 MB**；全部运行时调用点已验证为函数级懒 import 或 pip 兜底）。

**W2 —— 五服务 env 合并为 uv workspace（已完成，安装包 −30.1 MiB → 583.3 MiB / `611,529,375 B`；载荷 → 1684.5 MB，envs-template 525.3 → 423.7 MB）**

1. 仓库根新建**虚拟** workspace `pyproject.toml`（`[tool.uv.workspace]`，五个 member，无 `[project]` 故根本身不被安装）。5 个 per-service `uv.lock` 删除，统一为根 `uv.lock`，解析 68 包，冲突全部「约束交集内就高」（fastapi 0.162 / websockets 17.4 / pydantic 2.14 / numpy 2.5.4 / pandas 3.1）。
2. `start-stack.mjs`：5 次 per-service sync → 单次 workspace sync（仍含 evolve `candidates` extra），四个服务 python 全部指向 `envs/sd-services`。
3. `bootstrap.ts` `venvNames` → `["sd-services"]`；`assemble-backend.mjs` `VENV_NAMES` 同步。
4. 取舍说明（明确写出）：这是对既有「不合并 venv」原则的再评估。就高统一后唯一硬冲突是 websockets（JW cap `<16`），由 W3 补丁处理。已接受的代价是**任一服务升依赖都需全量回归**，因为只剩一个 env。

**W3 —— 版本对齐 + 一个被证伪的想法（已完成；本身不构成体积波次）**

JW 补丁 `0019-align-workspace-versions` 把 websockets cap `<16` → `<18`，numpy/pandas 与 workspace 对齐（2.5.4 / 3.1.0），manifest 15 → 16。两点值得记录：
- websockets **17 被 google-genai 的 `<17` 钉死**，故 lock 维持 15.0.1 —— 零行为变化。所有调用点均已审计且自带 legacy→新 API 回退，这正是放宽 cap 安全的前提。
- **跨 venv 硬链接去重：设计了、实测了、证伪后关闭。** JW venv 与共享 venv 之间同内容实测 59.9 MB，但 7z 固态压缩窗口机制 + venv 隔离使硬链接在安装包上收益≈0。及时关闭避免了在一个不可能回本的杠杆上浪费工程量；合并本身的收益 W2 已经拿到。

**W4 —— 构建门禁 + locales 裁剪（已完成，安装包 −5.3 MiB → 578.0 MiB）**

assemble 新增四道硬门禁，全部对标 JW 官方打包脚本，遵循同一哲学 —— *自证、常显、硬失败*：
- **预编译失败即构建失败**（原为 warning）。根治「载荷 pyc 静默跳过」这一类缺陷。
- **A1 载荷 import 自证** —— 用*载荷自己的*解释器 import 出厂模块（JW：`jiuwenswarm.common.config`、`gateway.app_gateway`、`server.app_agentserver`；服务：`sciencediscovery_gateway/_memory_graph/_evolve/_adapter`）。这正是能抓住静默预编译跳过的那道门，上线第一跑就抓出一个真实时机 bug。
- **A2 RequiredFiles 清单** —— 9 项安装必备文件（SEA、补丁 manifest、editable `.pth`），缺任一即硬失败。
- **A4 载荷总量常显** —— assemble 收尾打印。

Electron locales 由新增 afterPack 钩子（`win_desktop/scripts/after-pack-trim-locales.cjs`）裁剪：**出厂 55 → 删 52 → 留 3**（en-US / zh-CN / zh-TW）。release4 构建日志记录 `[afterPack] trimmed 52 Electron locale pak(s)`；~45 MB 原始体积在安装包里只落成 ~5 MiB —— 四波中最小的一波，也是个很好的提醒：原始 MB 与安装包 MiB 是两种货币。

**Phase 5 —— 装机实测引出的质量治理（代码已落地；release5 出包中；装机验收待做）**

不在 PR #834 内。五项，全部基于装机树实测证据而非推算：
- **路径预算（A5 门禁 + 缩布局）。** 安装根 `D:\ProgramData\SD\ScienceDiscovery` 实测 95,002 文件下 `maxRel = 224` → `maxAbs = 259`，可用预算 259，**余量 0**。修法：(a) 新增 assemble 门禁，遍历载荷树常显 `maxRel`，双阈值（运行时 189 / 构建期 170），超限 `fail()`；(b) 载荷前缀 `backend\.sciencediscovery-data\jiuwenswarm\src` → **`backend\jw`**（省 36 字符，`maxRel` 224 → 188）。校准过程中还抓出门禁自身的 bug：它按构建目录算相对路径，在短构建树下每个文件少算 6 字符 —— 恰好足以掩盖一次破线。
- **启动性能。** 热启动分解把 **31.97 s 中的 12.42 s（39%）** 归到一次同步 import（`install_subagent_observability_hook()`，拉进 3,946 个模块）。JW 补丁 `0020-lazy-observability-import` 改 `asyncio.to_thread`，在 `get_agent()` 加第三条幂等兜底（照抄 0015/0016 已有两条），并在 shutdown 的 `finally` 里 cancel。补丁链 16 → **17**，`verify` exit 0。**预期**热启 31.97 s → ~19.5 s —— *预期，未实测*。
- **`verifyPatches` 固定开销（0.87 s）。** 指纹缓存（补丁 name+size+mtime 对 src manifest），保留 `--force-verify` / `JIUWENSWARM_FORCE_VERIFY=1` 逃生口。实现过程中抓出一个真实的既有 bug：`recordVerified` 调用了 `writeFileSync` 却**从未 import**，`ReferenceError` 被外层 `try/catch` 吞掉，marker 从未落盘，缓存从未命中 —— 于是每次启动都重付 0.87 s。**那笔开销本身就是这个 bug。**
- **向导路径校验。** `mkdirSync("E")` 按 drive-relative 解析，创建了 `<安装目录>\E`；`probeDataDir` 只挡空串、不挡非绝对路径。已在任何 fs 副作用**之前**加 `isAbsolute` + `parse().root` 守卫，并在 `ensureWritableDir` 做纵深防御（非完全限定路径直接 `return false`，绝不 mkdir）。壳单测 118 → **121**（3 个新用例）。
- **度量纪律。** 任何启动数字现在必须标注测量树（dev / packaged）与端到端定义。dev 树的 17.8 s 曾被当作装机结论对外表述，真实 packaged 数字是 31.97 s —— 偏差 75%。f26 出包记录自身写明装机实测「待装机」，且 f26 从未真机实测过，所以**不存在可对比的 f26 热启基线**；release4 的三档实测是这条线上的第一组 packaged 基线。

**被裁能力的降级契约**（应评审要求补充 —— 这部分此前只有一句话）：

| 被裁能力 | 用户看到什么 | 机制 |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `claude_agent_sdk`（claude CLI 运行时） | 界面显示**「未安装」** | JW `external_cli_runtime` 以 `find_spec` 探测；缺失是一种状态，不是异常 |
| codex vendor 工具链 | **委派执行时才失败**，配置时不报错 —— 这是薄弱点 | `Codex` 构造时才 resolve 二进制；api 启动不受影响 |
| playwright（2 个浏览器类 skill 的抓取函数） | skill 函数调用时抛错，模块 import 安全 | `huawei_selectors.py` 顶层 import 经 try/except 降级为 `Any`；调用点为懒 import / pip 兜底 |
| uv（JW 自升级 / 扩展安装加速） | 回退到 **pip**，更慢但可用 | uv 移出 JW 主依赖 |

以上均不在首启与主对话链路上。需要拍板的是 codex 那一行：`docs/en/advanced-setup/configure-specialists.md` 仍把 `runtime.kind: "codex"`（以及 `"claude-code"` / `"acp"`）写成可用配置，于是照着文档配置的用户，会在委派时才发现失败，且仅限 Windows —— 一处未标注的平台差异。预期的修法是：在**配置期**给出明确的*不可用*状态（specialist 运行时卡片 + 委派错误），而不是用运行期异常，同时在该文档中英文两版加平台说明。

### 涉及的公开 API

无。全部改动都在打包/构建链（assemble、setup 脚本、JW 补丁链）或桌面壳内部（bootstrap env 变量与载荷路径）。无 HTTP API、IPC 通道、preload 桥或配置面变更。

真正变化的是 Windows 上四项能力的*可用性*（见上表）—— 每项都有 pip/探测兜底，且都不在首启与主对话链路上。

### 测试设计与测试计划

度量规程（写明以便数字可复现、可对比）：

- **体积。** 安装包字节数直接读产出的 `.exe`（release4：`606,126,666 B`），不取预期值。载荷数字是 assemble 的 A4 门禁打印的未压缩落盘总量。每个数字都标注口径。
- **启动。** 端到端定义为 **壳 T0 → shell 首次成功探到 gateway TCP**。三档：冷 = 含 provisioning 的首次启动，温 = 第二次，热 = 第三次及以后。同机三连启，经 `shell.log`（UTC）与 `startup-diagnostics.log` 的 `[SD-PERF]` / `[perf]` 打点记录。时钟纪律需注意：`jiuwenswarm.log` 是本地 UTC+8 而壳日志是 UTC，且 `[AgentServer]` 与 `[App]` 是两个进程、各自独立的 `process_elapsed` 时钟 —— 分段只可在同前缀内作差，跨进程步骤必须用绝对时刻。
- **路径预算。** 遍历安装树取 `maxRel = max(len(path) − len(root) − 1)`，再按 `maxAbs = len(root) + 1 + maxRel` 对 259 可用预算核验。

结果：

- **单测 / 壳：** PR head 上 `win_desktop` 壳测试 **118/118**（payload-slim 规则库 5/5；bootstrap fixture 已按共享 venv 布局重建）。Phase 5 增至 121（3 个向导守卫用例）；其中 1 项在构建机上**环境性失败**（`probeDataDir: real writable dir` 用 C 盘 `tmpdir()`，当时 C 盘仅 4.88 GB 可用，低于产品自身 5 GB 门槛 —— 同一函数在有空间的卷上通过）。
- **服务测试：** gateway 30/30、paper 2/2、memory-graph 109 过（78 error 全为「needs a live Neo4j」，既有环境依赖）、evolve 335 过 / 33 失败。evolve 的失败集**与 f26 基线树逐一对照完全一致**（Windows 无沙箱既有问题）→ 零回归。这些是在共享 venv 上本地跑出的。
- **全链冒烟：** start-stack 在共享 venv 上起全栈；adapter `/agent/info` 返回 `reachable: true`。
- **载荷抽查（每波）：** 7 个审计死重包逐一复查不在；JW pyc 全量落盘（移除依赖后 29,908 → 29,087 个 —— W15 首启加速不受损，且现由硬失败门禁保障）；补丁 manifest 在位且含 0018/0019；活包全保留（numpy/pandas/transformers/chromadb/faiss/lark_oapi/openjiuwen）。
- **出包实测（全部实测，无预期值）：** v0.2 = 613.4 MiB、v0.3 = 583.3 MiB、release4 = 578.0 MiB。release4 成品核验：签名 ✅、blockmap ✅、locales 恰为 en-US/zh-CN/zh-TW ✅。
- **真机装机（release4，2026-11-04）：** 安装根 `D:\ProgramData\SD\ScienceDiscovery`、数据目录 `E:\tmp`、载荷 95,002 文件。三连启：**冷 95.53 s / 温 38.40 s / 热 31.97 s**（冷启含首启 provisioning，`bootstrapPackaged-done elapsed=45729ms`）。路径预算：`maxRel = 224` → `maxAbs = 259/259`，**余量 0**。
- **PR #834 head（`61c59a46`）CI：** L1 静态检查 ✅、Coverage ✅、五个 mocked L2 E2E 矩阵 ✅、CodeCheck ✅、策略选择 ✅；**UT ❌**（测试脚手架 `PREPARATION_FAILED`）、**ST ❌**（`check:swarm-sdk-contract` —— 是 `--no-default-groups` 引入的 pytest 回归，**不是**脚手架问题；51 executed / 50 passed / 1 failed）、**merge-gate ❌**；Docker image 与 Binary release 两个 job 为 skipped（这正是 Dockerfile 断裂在 CI 上不可见的原因）。

尚未做、且明确列出而非含糊带过的：**GUI 三档装机验证 + 主对话 / 记忆 / skill 冒烟**。性能已真机实测，功能冒烟从未做过。这一项自 v0.2 起就欠着，适用于每一波。

### 验收标准

体积目标 —— 已达成、已实测、待合并：

- [x] f26 797.6 MiB → ≤ 600 MiB。实测 **578.0 MiB**（`606,126,666 B`），−219.6 MiB / **−27.5%**，位于 PR #834 head `61c59a46`。合并后生效；仓库尚无 `release4` tag。
- [x] 审计出的死重包在载荷中逐一复查不存在（7/7）；活包全保留。
- [x] pyc 预编译全量落盘（29,908 → 29,087 个；W15 首启加速不受损），且已改为强制 —— 预编译失败即构建失败。
- [x] 全链冒烟通过：adapter ↔ JW reachable，五服务从同一共享 venv 起栈。
- [x] PR head 壳测试 118/118；服务测试与 f26 基线持平（零回归）。
- [x] 各波数字自洽且可逐项相加：797.6 −184.2（W1）−30.1（W2）−5.3（W4）= 578.0。W3 贡献的是对齐与一个被证伪的杠杆，不是体积。（本 issue 早期版本把 W1 写作 −214 MiB，与其自身的 613.4 MiB 结果对不上；−184.2 MiB 才是实测安装包差值，−1041 MB 是未压缩差值。）

硬约束 —— 一项达成，一项未经验证：

- [x] 离线双击即用；首启零网络下载。被裁内容没有任何运行时下载路径。
- [ ] **首启不变慢 —— 未验证，且在现有数据上无法判定。** 该约束针对的是全新安装后的首次启动，即**冷**档，实测 **95.53 s**（含首启 provisioning，`bootstrapPackaged-done elapsed=45729ms`）；温档 38.40 s。勾这一项有两个问题：(a) **f26 从未真机实测过**（`出包记录-f26.md:59` 记为「f26 装机三连启实测：待装机」），不存在可作差的 packaged 冷启基线；(b) 本项目至今给出的所有阈值 —— 包括 Phase 5 的 ≤22 s —— 都是**热**启目标，于是 95.53 s 这个首启数字被记录下来了却从未被判定过。本 issue 早期版本曾以热启 31.97 s 为依据勾上此项，那是拿另一档位的证据；**该勾选在此撤回**。需要 owner 裁决：要么明确设定首启阈值，要么记录「接受 95.53 s 现状」。另外，dev 树 17.8 s vs packaged 31.97 s 是测量树差异，不是回归，不可当作回归读。

待办项 —— 正是这些使本 issue 保持 open：**本 issue 是手动跟踪项，PR #834 没有 closing keyword，合并它不会关掉这里任何一项。** 目前每项都尚未指派 owner 与期限。下面四组 **[决策]** 是维护者/owner 的裁决、不是工程活，应先定 —— 定完才谈得上给 **[工程]** 项排期。

**[决策]** —— 需要 owner 与结论，不先写代码：

- [ ] **Docker / 二进制发行链是否在本 PR 范围内？** 现状是本 PR 把两条都打断了（见「连带损伤」）。要么在本 PR 内修好，要么明说不在范围内**并**给出它们如何保持可构建。
- [ ] **codex 降级走哪个方向。** 要么记录「Windows 包内 `runtime.kind: codex` 不可用」这一决定 —— 那就必须在配置/委派期给出明确的*不可用*状态，并在 `docs/en/advanced-setup/configure-specialists.md` 及其中文对应文档加平台说明；要么恢复该工具链。对着文档配置却在使用时才抛异常，不是可接受的终态。
- [ ] **首启阈值。** 明确设定冷启预算，或记录「接受实测的 95.53 s」（见上文被撤回的那条验收）。同时需裁定：受约束的档位到底是首启还是热启 —— 至今给出的每个阈值都是热启口径。
- [ ] **剩余体积杠杆**，每项都要记录结论与已接受的风险：evolve `candidates` extra 是否退出安装包（安装包 −~25 MiB / 未压缩 ~100 MB，代价是 /evolve 不可用）、飞书 `lark_oapi`（95 MB）、`imageio_ffmpeg`（84 MB）/ `matplotlib`（23 MB）的引用审计。另一项：路径余量是否需要从缩布局后的 **1** 提到 ≥19 —— 要达到该值必须改安装根，而改根与 `perMachine: false` 语义冲突，属产品决策而非工程决策。

**[工程]** —— 上面决策定了之后即可排期：

- [ ] **PR #834 的 UT 转绿。** 修 `test/support/tagged/shared.mjs`，让 sync 与 coverage 安装都解析 workspace 根 venv（或显式 `UV_PROJECT_ENVIRONMENT`），并保留 per-service extras；随后重跑 UT，把真实数字回填到这里，取代本地数字。这一项**不会**修好 ST —— 见下条。
- [ ] **PR #834 的 ST 转绿（另一个成因）。** `check:swarm-sdk-contract` 会在 `scripts/jiuwenswarm.sh setup` 刚建好的 venv 上跑 `pytest`，而本 PR 给这次 setup 加了 `--no-default-groups`，把 pytest 排除掉了（JW 侧：`default-groups = ['dev']`、`dev = test + lint`）。本地已复现：`No module named pytest`。修法是给 contract 单独制备环境 —— setup 后再 `uv sync --group test`（或用 `test` extra），或建专用 contract venv —— 使出包载荷保持精简。**不要**用回退 `--no-default-groups` 来修：那会悄悄抹掉 W1 实测的 ~40 MB。请读 `.ci-results/st/run.log`（或重跑 `bash .ci/run-research-python.sh contract`）记录真实报错，取代此处的推断。
- [ ] **Docker 与二进制发行链恢复可构建。** Dockerfile 的 bind mount 与 `--locked/--frozen` 改指根 `pyproject.toml`/`uv.lock`；`scripts/binary-release/build-payload.sh` 的 `uv export --frozen` 同理（根 lock 已把五个 member 作为具名包收录，故 `uv export --frozen --package <member>` 可保住 hash-pinned）；`scripts/docker-build-context.test.mjs` 通过；两份 `binary-packaging.md`（中/英）修正。**这一项 CI 看不见** —— PR profile 下 `Docker image` job 是 skipped —— 所以要显式构建验证，不能靠流水线转绿。
- [ ] **真机 GUI 安装三档验证（全新首启 / 热启动 / attach）+ 主对话 / 记忆 / skill 冒烟。** 自 v0.2 起欠着；性能已测，功能冒烟未测。
- [ ] **审计证据可访问化。** 五份审计文档（import 扫描、反向依赖链、就高统一可行性论证、「装包即终态」裁剪设计、原始 `du` 输出）目前只在作者工作树 `E:\CodeFile\SDWin\f26-size-analysis\` —— `main` 上没有，PR #834 的 32 个文件里也没有。`pyproject.toml` 里引用的 workspace 冲突矩阵（写作 `sizeopt\agent-knowledge\design\D1`）、以及 `payload-slim.mjs` 中 15 条 `JW_VENV_SWEEP_RULES`（其文件头引用的正是这个仓外路径）同样如此。在他人能评审清扫白名单之前，这些必须随代码一起提交，或把生成脚本 + 结果摘要附到 PR 上。一条错误的清扫规则只会在客户机器上表现为一次离线 `ImportError`，所以这一项不能靠文字描述兜底 —— 它也是 −27.5% 这一结论目前唯一的技术评审阻塞点。

明确不在范围内：做到 ~200 MB。那需要 Python 环境联网安装，是与离线硬约束冲突的产品形态变更，且从未获授权。Phase 5（D10–D12：启动性能、路径预算、向导校验、度量纪律）有它自己的验收数字 —— 热启 ≤22 s、路径破线 0、A5 常显、缓存命中时 `verifyPatches` ≤50 ms、向导零垃圾目录 —— 全部为**预期、未实测**，待 release5 装机验证。

### 附加信息

**代码与评审入口。** PR **#834**（`qingkwl:sizeopt/f26-6to2` → `openJiuwen-ai:main`，open，`mergeable` / `mergeStateStatus: BLOCKED`），head `61c59a46`。该 PR 共 **8 个 commit**：其中三个是体积优化波次，五个是更早的启动延迟线顺带带进来的：

| Commit | 内容 | 安装包 |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `80b079a6` | perf：壳/栈/JW 三处毫秒级启动时间线打点 | —（顺带） |
| `96d906f2` | perf：JW 启动延迟补丁 0015–0017 + 补丁链构建修复 | —（顺带） |
| `6c0179f1` | fix：wheel 形态下 `tests/` 补丁目标的兼容性 | —（顺带） |
| `d4afaac9` | fix：PR #720 评审后续（0016 线程锁、swarm-patches 测试） | —（顺带） |
| `b7eb4cac` | fix：把 wheel 构建的补丁 manifest 带进 wheel 形态安装 | —（顺带） |
| `d2fd4f51` | **W1** —— JW 载荷瘦身 + codex vendor 剔除 | 613.4 MiB |
| `1dc952a0` | **W2** —— 五服务 venv → 一个 uv workspace | 583.3 MiB |
| `61c59a46` | **W3** 版本对齐 + **W4** assemble 门禁与 locales | 578.0 MiB |

分支只存在于作者 fork；`sizeopt/f26-6to2` 在 `openJiuwen-ai/sciencediscovery` 上返回 404。**回退范围，写明：** 只 revert 三个 `feat(sizeopt)` commit 会移除 W1–W4，但**那五个启动补丁 commit 仍在** —— 这不等于回退整个 PR。要恢复 `main`，须 revert 全部八个（或直接丢弃分支）。补丁级回退：0018/0019 支持 `apply --reverse`，施工前的补丁链已备份。本 issue 早期版本的这张表只列了三个波次 commit，漏掉了五个启动 commit，因此回退指引是错的。给引用这条线上 hash 的人的提醒：本项目自己的记录里早期写过 `0cec7abb`，后查明是**游离 commit**（`git branch --contains` 为空）—— 与 `61c59a46` 标题相同、相差 26 插入 / 16 删除，且其 revert 命令不可执行。此后立下的规矩：hash 只有在 `git branch --contains <hash>` 返回非空后才可写入记录；revert 命令只有在试跑到干净的 `git revert --abort` 之后才可记录。

**issue 合并。** 本 issue 此前以中英孪生形式存在 —— #807（中文）与 #808（英文），内容相同。两份副本意味着评审结论、验收勾选与验证结果都要维护两遍并且必然漂移。按维护者指示，两者合并为本 issue（英文在前供外部读者，中文在下供内部跟踪），**#807 作为重复项关闭并指向此处**。#807 上的全部讨论仍可在原处阅读，合并不丢失任何信息。**以英文半篇为准**：两者若有出入，以英文文本为准，中文半篇随之修正对齐。任何编辑必须在同一次提交里同时落到两半 —— 只改一侧即属缺陷。

**预期 vs 实测，留档。** 方案预期 ~465 MB（−42%），实际结果 578.0 MiB（−27.5%）。差距已完整归因：(1) 首轮预期对压缩率好于均值的切片套用了整体 29.6% 留存率（各波合计 +43~113 MB）—— 已改为按切片混合留存率折算；(2) 硬链接去重先设计进预期、后被**实测证伪**（约 30 MB）；(3) locales 裁剪 ~45 MB 原始体积在安装包里只落 ~5 MiB。未压缩账本（2827 → 1694 MB，−40%）全程准确 —— 错的只是压缩折算。
closed_recent.title: [Feature]: Installer size optimization (f26 797.6 MiB -> 580.0 MiB, -27.5%, PR #834)

closed_recent.author: HugoXK
closed_recent.body:
## Environment

- `openJiuwen-ai/sciencediscovery` `main` at `0e7075c475fe657a7e772d7efdaa55cab1bcd9ba` (2026-11-01T17:05:39Z)
- `packages/cas/src/index.ts`: `readPaths()` `:173-177`, `read()` `:102-122`, `stream()` `:129-146`

## What is wrong

The two methods search the same three layouts, but they disagree about what a corrupt first copy means.

- `read()` (`:102-122`) skips a copy whose digest does not match and keeps looking, so a corrupt `versioning/agent-state` copy does not hide an intact `versioning/data` one (`#707` / `#706`).
- `stream()` (`:129-146`) keeps the older rule: the first copy that exists decides. A corrupt first copy fails the whole call even when the mirror is intact.

Measured on the source, with one 210,000-byte object written by `CasStore.put()` (agent-state) plus `new VersionStore(root).put("data", bytes)` (intact mirror), then only `versioning/agent-state/blobs/sha256/<hash>` overwritten with `corrupt`:

```
read(hash)           -> returned the 210000 original bytes
stream(hash)         -> THREW Error("CAS integrity failure") after 7 bytes
```

## Current vs expected

Current: `read()` and `stream()` of the same hash disagree — one returns content, the other refuses it.
Expected (this issue asks which one, and makes both follow it): either both fall back to the intact mirror, or neither does. The choice belongs with the maintainers; the code should not depend on which accessor a caller happens to use.

## Why it is reachable

`materializeArtifact()` (`services/api/src/artifacts/materialize.ts:20`) is the only `stream()` caller in the tree, and it fails the request when the primary copy is corrupt even though `read()` would have served the same object. `services/api/src/artifacts/materialize.test.ts:64-66` pins the current `stream()` behaviour by corrupting only `versioning/agent-state/blobs/sha256/<hash>` and asserting the request fails.

## Suggested test

In `packages/cas/src/index.test.ts`, one case that stores a blob, writes `corrupt` over the agent-state copy, keeps an intact copy in the other pool, and asserts that `read()` and `stream()` reach the same conclusion — whatever that conclusion is.

## Scope

- Not a duplicate of `#708` (that one asks for `stream()` to verify before it yields; this one is the accessor disagreement that `#708`'s fix exposed) or of `#706`/`#707` (those are `read()`-only).
- No PR from us yet: recorded, benched, and not picked up without a `pickup-ok` comment on this issue.
closed_recent.title: [Bug] CasStore.read() serves an intact mirror that stream() refuses, so one object is readable but not streamable

closed_recent.author: HugoXK
closed_recent.body:
## Checklist

- [x] I have searched existing issues and this is not a duplicate (terms and results at the end of this report).
- [x] I am on the current `main` (`89cd2d30c93e11c6e98e264cc08b171f6a3705f0`).
- [x] This is a defect in existing behaviour, not a feature request.
- [x] I can reproduce it offline, with no Neo4j and no model call.

## Detailed Description

The memory-graph sidecar caps every read query at `_NODE_LIMIT = 500` and reports
`truncated: true` when the result was cut. The cut flag is computed **after** the
Cypher `LIMIT`, so a result set that is exactly 500 nodes long cannot be told
apart from one that was cut — and the code reports it as cut:

`services/memory-graph/src/sciencediscovery_memory_graph/query.py:431`
```python
"truncated": len(hits) >= _NODE_LIMIT,
```

The module's own contract, a few lines above, says the opposite:

`services/memory-graph/src/sciencediscovery_memory_graph/query.py:319`
```
# shared hard cap (500); results beyond it carry ``truncated: True``.
```

"beyond the cap" is not "at the cap". The same off-by-one is repeated at every
read that returns the shared result shape:

- `query.py:272` — `get_subgraph` nodes
- `query.py:431` — `query_match` hits
- `query.py:465` — `by_node_type` hits
- `query.py:518` — `by_edge_type` edges
- `query.py:898` — member-scope nodes

Each of these runs its Cypher with `LIMIT $limit` bound to `_NODE_LIMIT`
(`query.py:424`, `:458`, `:496`, ...), so the Python side can never observe a
501st row and `len(...) >= 500` is true for a complete 500-node answer.

### What the reader sees

The flag is forwarded verbatim by the API (`services/api/src/http/index.ts:3506`
for `POST /api/memory/query/match`, mapped in
`packages/memory/src/memory-graph.ts:1082`) and rendered by the memory-graph
panel:

`apps/web/src/MemoryGraphExplorer.tsx:1336`
```tsx
setSearchNote(result.hits.length
  ? t(result.truncated ? "memory.search.matchesTruncated" : "memory.search.matches",
    { shown: onScreen, total: result.hits.length })
  : t("memory.search.noMatches"));
```
`apps/web/src/i18n/messages.ts:1376` — `"memory.search.matchesTruncated":
"{shown} of {total}+ (truncated) match(es) in view"`

So a query with exactly 500 matches in the graph reports

```
12 of 500+ (truncated) match(es) in view
```

The trailing `+` asserts that at least one additional match exists. There is
none: 500 is every match the graph holds. The subgraph badge path is the same
shape — `MemoryGraphExplorer.tsx:1718` draws the "(truncated)" badge from
`graph.truncated`, which `get_subgraph` sets by the same `>=` comparison, so a
Session whose graph is exactly 500 nodes is badged as a partial graph.

This is the class #655 ("Structure preview reports truncated: true while
returning the complete source") was fixed for in #659: the flag must mean
"content was left out", not "the last page came back full".

### Minimal reproduction (no Neo4j)

`services/memory-graph/tests/test_smoke.py` already has the pattern this needs:
a fake driver that satisfies `is_reachable()` and returns canned rows, so
`query_match` runs its real Python path. Add a fake result that yields exactly
`_NODE_LIMIT` rows, then:

```python
result = query.query_match("TP53")          # fake driver: 500 Paper nodes
assert result["truncated"] is False         # nothing was left out
```

Current output, on `89cd2d30`:

```
# rows=500 hits=500 truncated=True
AssertionError: exactly 500 matches (the graph holds nothing more) reported as truncated
```

and the control case at 501 is already correct apart from the count of returned
rows, which the fix has to keep at the cap:

```python
result = query.query_match("TP53")          # fake driver: 501 Paper nodes
assert result["truncated"] is True
assert len(result["hits"]) == 500
```

Run it with:

```
cd services/memory-graph
uv run --project . --extra test pytest tests/ -k truncated
```

### Expected

- exactly `_NODE_LIMIT` matches → `truncated: false`, and the web note drops the
  `+` and says "N of N match(es) in view".
- more than `_NODE_LIMIT` matches → `truncated: true`, `len(hits) == 500`, note
  keeps the `+`.
- a subgraph with exactly 500 nodes → no "(truncated)" badge.

### Fix direction (one slice, no new query)

Ask for one row more than the cap and let the extra row decide the flag:
bind the Cypher limit to `_NODE_LIMIT + 1`, take `cut = len(rows) > _NODE_LIMIT`,
return `rows[:_NODE_LIMIT]`, and set `truncated: cut`. The same two-line change
covers all five sites above; `total` keeps its current meaning (the number of
rows the response carries), so no client contract changes. A dev may prefer to
count the raw rows before `_to_hit` drops unknown labels — that is the more
correct variant, since a dropped label is not a truncation either.

## Environment

- Repository: `openJiuwen-ai/sciencediscovery`, branch `main`, commit `89cd2d30c93e11c6e98e264cc08b171f6a3705f0`
- Component: `services/memory-graph` (Python sidecar), read path only
- Node v22.23.2, pnpm 11.1.2, Python 3.10.12, `uv` project `services/memory-graph`
- No Neo4j needed for the reproduction (fake driver); a live graph is needed only to see the panel text itself

## Version Information

- ScienceDiscovery 0.3.0 development tree (`main` @ `89cd2d30`)
- Affected: memory-graph search note and subgraph "(truncated)" badge in `apps/web`, for any graph whose result set reaches the 500-node cap

## Duplicate check (open + closed)

Searched issues with `truncated`, `memory graph`, `500 matches`, `NODE_LIMIT`:

- #655 (closed) / #659 (closed), #649/#652 (closed), #650 (closed), #660/#663 (closed), #368 (closed) — artifact/structure/text **preview** truncation. Same class, different surface; #655's fix is the precedent this report follows, not a duplicate of it.
- #841, #842 (open) — artifact preview `maxRows` clamp and clipped-preview notice. Different endpoint, different flag.
- #210/#212 (closed), #836 (closed), #725/#723 (closed) — memory-graph folding, health request bound, Escape handling. Passed the same read path but none changes `truncated`.
- #770, #801, #345 — memory-graph configuration/desktop features. Not this flag.
- `NODE_LIMIT` returns no issue at all.

## Current behaviour

`GET /api/sessions/:session/artifact-versions/:version/diff` answers **500 `Internal server error`** when either side of the pair is not a textual artifact, and logs a false `unclassified_request_error status=500`.

## Expected behaviour

A client error (400/422) that says the comparison is not available for those versions, consistent with the other client-input rejections on the same route.

## Where it comes from

`services/api/src/artifacts/index.ts:355-357` (live `main` `89cd2d30`):

```ts
const isText = (mediaType: string) => mediaType.startsWith("text/")
  || /\b(?:json|javascript|xml|yaml)\b/i.test(mediaType);
if (!isText(from.mediaType) || !isText(to.mediaType)) throw new Error("Diff is available only for textual or comparable artifact versions");
```

The plain `Error` matches none of the classification paths:

- `services/api/src/http/error-classification.ts:23-32` — the client-input patterns are `is required`, `must`, `contains? an unknown value`, `cannot`, `does not match`, `invalid`, `unsafe … (archive|package|path)`, `plain basename`; "available only for" matches none;
- the 404 message mapper in `services/api/src/http/index.ts` only knows `Project|Session|Proxy server|Provider|Model not found` and `Execution|Transfer|Timer|Subagent not found:`;
- so the top-level catch falls through to 500.

Found while reviewing #881 (`Fixes #877`), which fixed the *missing version* cases on this route family; that PR's reviewer classified this one as a non-blocking follow-up because it is not a regression — the binary pair answered 500 before #881 too. Verified against the code at `89cd2d30`, not by re-running the server.

## Suggested fix (either is one small change)

1. Hoist the media-type check into the route in `services/api/src/http/index.ts` next to the version-existence checks and answer 400 with a stable message, or
2. Throw `ApiStatusError` from `artifactVersionDiff` for this case, or add the message to `isKnownClientInputError` if a message-based classification is preferred.

Option 2 is the smaller diff but keeps classification tied to prose; option 1 matches how `#881` handles the missing-version case.

## Reproduce

Any two artifact versions of non-textual media types (e.g. two `.zip` uploads) in one session, then call the `diff` route with the later version id. No mock needed; the throw happens before CAS reads.

## Dedupe

Searched open+closed: `"Diff is available only for textual"` → 1 hit, this report (the phrase appears only in the source). `provenance 500` (13) and `unclassified_request_error` (3, #779/#784) are different sources; #877 covers the missing-version case only.

### Checklist

- [x] I have searched for related issues but did not get the expected help.
- [x] This bug has not been fixed in the latest version.
- [x] Please note that if your bug description lacks corresponding environment information and a minimal reproducible demo, it will be difficult for us to reproduce and resolve the issue, which will reduce the possibility of receiving feedback, or even lead to the issue being closed.

### 🐞 Detailed Description of the Problem

From ten million tokens up, the same count is printed two different ways depending on the screen, and nothing states which one is intended.

- Model settings badges (`apps/web/src/ProviderModelFields.tsx`, `compactTokenCount`) keep whole millions from 10M up: `10_500_000 → "11M"`.
- The usage page (`apps/web/src/usageFormat.ts`, `formatCompactTokenValue`) has no ≥10M branch: `10_500_000 → "10.5M"`.

Measured with `node --import tsx` on `main` `89cd2d30` plus the two open fixes (#864 for `formatCompactTokenValue`, #869 for `compactTokenCount`):

```text
value       badge (settings)   usage page
9_999_999   10M                10.0M
10_000_000  10M                10.0M
10_499_999  10M                10.5M
10_500_000  11M                10.5M
12_345_678  12M                12.3M
```

**Why it matters.** Both are honest for their own precision, but a user comparing a model's declared 10.5M window in Settings with a 10.5M figure on the usage page sees `11M` in one place; and the badge's own rule — whole millions from 10M because a `0.1M` fraction is below the badge's resolution — is not stated as a decision at the branch, only in the doc comment, and the test at `apps/web/tests/ProviderModelList.test.tsx:59` pins `10_500_000 → "11M"` without pinning the other side of the boundary (`10_499_999 → "10M"`).

**Expected.** One decision, stated and covered: either both surfaces print one decimal from 1M up (`10.5M` on both), or both switch to whole millions at 10M (`11M` on both), with the boundary pinned on both sides and the threshold's rationale next to the branch.

**Minimal reproduction** (no DOM):

```ts
import { compactTokenCount } from "./apps/web/src/ProviderModelFields.js";
import { formatCompactTokenValue } from "./apps/web/src/usageFormat.js";

console.log(compactTokenCount(10_500_000));      // "11M"
console.log(formatCompactTokenValue(10_500_000)); // "10.5M"  (with #864 applied)
```

**Where.** `apps/web/src/ProviderModelFields.tsx:190-197`; `apps/web/src/usageFormat.ts:19-25`; `apps/web/tests/ProviderModelList.test.tsx:59`; `apps/web/tests/UsagePage.test.tsx`.

### Detailed Environment Information Description

- Repository: `openJiuwen-ai/sciencediscovery`, `main` at `89cd2d30c93e11c6e98e264cc08b171f6a3705f0`.
- `apps/web` (React + Vite), checked with `node --import tsx` on Node `v22.23.2`, pnpm `11.1.2`, Linux x86_64.
- Depends on the open fixes in #864 (usage formatter unit crossing) and #869 (model-settings badge fractions); both are pure functions, no browser needed.

### Additional Information

Raised in review of #869 (`apps/web/src/ProviderModelFields.tsx:193`). #869 intentionally keeps the ≥10M whole-million rule (that was the reviewed decision), so this is recorded here rather than folded into that tip.

### Version Information

- `main` `89cd2d30c93e11c6e98e264cc08b171f6a3705f0` (2026-11-04).

### Checklist

- [x] I searched existing issues for this symptom and found none (terms below).
- [x] I reproduced this on the latest `main` (`89cd2d30c93e11c6e98e264cc08b171f6a3705f0`).
- [x] This report includes the environment and a minimal reproduction.

### Detailed Description

**What the user sees.** In Settings › Models, each provider row shows the context window and the max output tokens as a compact badge (for example `1M / 131k`). Those badges round to a whole unit with `Math.round`, so a window of 1,500,000 is displayed as **`2M`** and a 1,400,000 window as **`1M`**. The badge is the only place the row shows these numbers (it has no tooltip), so the user reads a capacity the model profile does not have: a 1.5M-token window is advertised as 2M, and a request sized against that badge can exceed the real limit.

**Minimal reproduction** (pure function, no DOM):

```ts
import { compactTokenCount } from "./apps/web/src/ProviderModelFields.js";
console.log(compactTokenCount(1_400_000)); // 1M
console.log(compactTokenCount(1_500_000)); // 2M
console.log(compactTokenCount(999_999));   // 1000k
```

Observed on `89cd2d30`:

```text
# 1050000 -> 1M
# 1400000 -> 1M
# 1500000 -> 2M
# 1999999 -> 2M
# 2000000 -> 2M
# 999999 -> 1000k
```

**Expected.** A declared 1.5M window reads `1.5M` (and 1.4M reads `1.4M`); compacting must not round across half a million tokens. `999,999` should read `1M` (or `999,999`), never `1000k`.

**Where.** `apps/web/src/ProviderModelFields.tsx:188-193` on `89cd2d30`:

- `:190` — ``if (value >= 1_000_000) return `${Math.round(value / 1_000_000)}M`;`` — whole-million rounding is the source of `1_500_000 → 2M`.
- `:191` — ``if (value >= 1_000) return `${Math.round(value / 1_000)}k`;`` — the same boundary produces `1000k` for `999_999` (and for any `999_500..999_999`).
- `:209` — `ModelRowFacts` renders `{compactTokenCount(contextWindow)} / {compactTokenCount(maxOutputTokens)}` as a plain `<span className="fact">` with no title, so the compact string is the only reading a user gets.
- The same helper is re-exported through `apps/web/src/ProviderModelSettings.tsx:65` and used by `ModelConnectWizard.tsx:660`, so the badge appears in both the settings list and the connect wizard.

**Red-first fix proposal.** First add a test that fails on `89cd2d30`:

```ts
assert.equal(compactTokenCount(1_500_000), "1.5M");
assert.equal(compactTokenCount(1_400_000), "1.4M");
assert.equal(compactTokenCount(999_999), "1M");
```

then format with one significant decimal below 10 units (`(value / 1_000_000).toFixed(1)` trimmed of a trailing `.0`, e.g. `1.5M`, `1M`, `2M`) and promote a rounded `1000k` to `1M` instead of printing `1000k`. Values below the unit keep their current form.

**Duplicate check (open and closed).** GitHub search: `"compactTokenCount"` → 0; `"context window"` → unrelated issues (#686 test-button rendering, #845 model deletion, #824 connectivity); `"1000k"` → 0; `"1.5M"` → 0. No open PR touches `apps/web/src/ProviderModelFields.tsx` (`#811` touches `usageFormat.ts`/`UsagePage.tsx` for reasoning tokens only). Issue #860 (filed today) is the same rounding pattern in the *usage* formatter `formatCompactTokenValue`, a different file and a different fix; this one is the settings badge.

### Environment

- Commit: `89cd2d30c93e11c6e98e264cc08b171f6a3705f0` (live `main`, read 2026-11-04).
- Node `v22.23.2`, pnpm `11.1.2`, Linux x86_64.
- Command: `cd apps/web && node --import tsx --test tests/zz-compact-token-probe.test.ts` (temporary probe file, not committed).

### Version Information

- Repository: `openJiuwen-ai/sciencediscovery`
- `main` at `89cd2d30c93e11c6e98e264cc08b171f6a3705f0`
- Affected package: `apps/web` (`@sciencediscovery/web`)

## What happens

`GET` artifact version preview (`services/api/src/artifact-dashboard.ts`, `buildArtifactVersionPreview` → `parseDelimitedTable` / `recordArrayTable`) now bounds its payload with two server-side constants:

- `const maxRows = Math.min(MAX_PREVIEW_ROWS, parsePositiveInt(maxRowsParam, DEFAULT_MAX_ROWS));` — `MAX_PREVIEW_ROWS = DEFAULT_MAX_ROWS = 100` (`artifact-dashboard.ts:719` at `0477d328`)
- `const width = Math.min(totalColumns, MAX_PREVIEW_COLUMNS);` — `MAX_PREVIEW_COLUMNS = 1_001` (`artifact-dashboard.ts:398`)

A caller that asks for more gets less, with no error: the response just carries `truncated` and `clippedColumns`/`clippedCells`.

## Measured at `0477d328`

- 1,500-column CSV → `columns 1001`, `clippedColumns {shown 1001, total 1500}`, `clippedCells 499` (named columns past 1,001 are dropped).
- 401-row CSV at `?maxRows=400` → `rows 100`, `totalRows 400`, `truncated true`.
- 500-record JSON at `?maxRows=400` → the same 100 rows (the clamp applies to the record-array path too).

## Why it matters

The bundled web client never sends `maxRows` (`apps/web/src/api/artifacts.ts:201` forwards an optional value only, and `apps/desktop` reads local CSV), so there is no in-repo regression — but for any other API caller this is a silent contract change: asking for 400 rows returns 100, and a legitimately wide table loses named columns. `#829` asked for a preview that keeps every row as wide as the columns it advertises; the bound is what makes the payload finite, so the trade is deliberate — it is the *silence* that needs a decision.

Two questions to settle, and then to write down where a caller can find them:

1. Should `maxRows` above the server constant be rejected (400 with a stated limit) instead of clamped, or should `truncated` stay the only signal?
2. Should the preview document the row limit and the column limit (with `clippedColumns`/`clippedCells` as the reporting half) in the API docs, and should a caller be able to learn both limits without probing?

Related: `#829` (the shear this bound fixes), `#839` (the width rule taken from the widest line), `#840` (the payload `warnings` field has no consumer).

## Suggested fix

Decide the two questions above, then either reject over-limit `maxRows` with a stated maximum or document the clamp; document `MAX_PREVIEW_ROWS` and `MAX_PREVIEW_COLUMNS` (and that a wider/taller request is clipped, not failed) in the API reference, so an outside caller can size its request without probing.
closed_recent.title: [Bug] The artifact preview endpoint silently clamps `?maxRows=` to 100 and caps the column set at 1,001, so an outside API caller gets less than it asked for
