## Background and environment

During a source installation on a Debian 13 cloud desktop on 2026-10-11, using main commit `5ddaa38bd68a84e4e20b14116d91880fe87bdd08`, two problems required manual investigation:

1. The desktop terminal did not inherit the outbound proxy environment. The initial managed micromamba download failed with `ECONNREFUSED`; an installation environment with the required network configuration could complete the download.
2. When the adapter inherited a SOCKS proxy configuration, it failed to start because `socksio` was missing, affecting access to the application.

The first observation is an environment-triggered failure, not proof of a downloader implementation defect. The second has a concrete dependency declaration gap.

## Conditions and observed behavior

### A. Different proxy environments across installation and runtime entry points

- External access required a proxy, but the terminal initiating scientific-environment preparation did not inherit the corresponding configuration.
- The micromamba connection was refused and scientific-environment preparation could not complete.
- Installation succeeded through an official download/install path with the necessary network configuration, retaining the pinned version and SHA-256 verification.
- The scientific environment subsequently became ready, with Python 3.12, NumPy, pandas, SciPy, and Matplotlib available.

### B. SOCKS configuration prevents adapter startup

- Create a clean adapter environment from the declared project dependencies and start it with a valid SOCKS proxy configuration.
- During HTTP client initialization, the missing socksio dependency prevents adapter startup.
- In this installation, adding socksio from official PyPI to the adapter's isolated environment restored startup; API health and page HTML checks then passed.

Source references:
- [Adapter declares plain httpx](https://github.com/openJiuwen-ai/sciencediscovery/blob/5ddaa38bd68a84e4e20b14116d91880fe87bdd08/services/adapter/pyproject.toml#L19-L25).
- [HTTP clients are constructed during startup](https://github.com/openJiuwen-ai/sciencediscovery/blob/5ddaa38bd68a84e4e20b14116d91880fe87bdd08/services/adapter/src/sciencediscovery_adapter/app.py#L47-L63).

## User impact

- Users may have already installed the source and other dependencies, yet still be blocked at first startup or scientific-environment preparation, preventing access to the workbench or relevant computations.
- Users must investigate differences between terminal and child-process proxy environments, and may need to install undeclared dependencies manually.
- A component-level failure can look like a failed installation of the entire application, leading to unnecessary reinstalls. This is not evidence that micromamba itself is unsuitable or unavailable.

## Expected behavior and proposed improvements

1. Unify installation/startup preflight checks: inspect the actual child process's proxy configuration, connectivity to required download sources, and dependencies for the selected proxy protocol. Report redacted status, never credentials.
2. Declare and lock SOCKS support, for example through `httpx[socks]`. Define the proxy boundary between loopback service calls and external requests, including correct `NO_PROXY` handling.
3. Identify the failing component, stage, underlying cause, and actionable next step. After configuration is corrected, allow retrying the failed step while reusing verified tools and caches.
4. Report Web entry point, adapter, and scientific-environment readiness separately instead of treating partial readiness as an all-or-nothing result.

The repository already has [download retry and cache mechanisms](https://github.com/openJiuwen-ai/sciencediscovery/blob/5ddaa38bd68a84e4e20b14116d91880fe87bdd08/scripts/fetch-managed-micromamba.mjs#L179-L295), as well as [classified errors and mirror/preinstalled-tool recovery guidance](https://github.com/openJiuwen-ai/sciencediscovery/blob/5ddaa38bd68a84e4e20b14116d91880fe87bdd08/services/runner/src/environment-store.ts#L1138-L1173). The goal is to connect these capabilities into a coherent first-run experience, not to replace the downloader.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] A clean adapter environment starts with HTTP/SOCKS proxy configurations without manually installing undeclared dependencies.
- [ ] Missing or incorrect proxy configuration produces redacted, actionable diagnostics while retaining the underlying error.
- [ ] Correcting configuration allows retrying the failed step and reusing verified artifacts, without clearing all data or reinstalling.
- [ ] Version pinning and hash verification remain enforced; recovery does not disable TLS verification.
- [ ] Tests cover no proxy, HTTP/SOCKS proxies, unreachable download sources, and successful retry after correction; installation documentation is updated.

Related: #29 (actionable dependency preflight), #213 and #229 (onboarding feedback). This issue focuses on the observed proxy-related failures and first-install recovery experience.
items.title: [Bug] Improve proxy-aware installation: declare SOCKS support and unify preflight and recovery

items.author: yuanzhou75
items.body:
### 🚀 Background Description

Exporting a session works today, but the dialog is still shaped like a developer tool rather than a user task. Everything a user needs in order to decide *what* they are handing off, *how big* it will be, and *what happened* to the last export is either missing, misleading, or only reachable by reopening a modal. This is the session-export UI design work, desktop first.

The save flow itself was fixed in #986 / PR #999 (native save dialog, automatic save, per-export tracking) and the capability is specified in #803, so this issue is not about those. It is about the presentation of scope, size, progress and outcome.

Observations from the current desktop UI (`apps/desktop/src/views/ResearchPackage.tsx`, main 2026-11-09) and from a real export of a session with evolve runs and scientific memory (build `c95f080a`):

| What the user sees | What is actually true | Why it misleads |
| --- | --- | --- |
| 预计大小（未压缩）**910.6 MiB** on the 完整导出 card | the saved `.sdresearch` was **19.2 MiB** (20,161,641 bytes) | one number, 46× the real file; it is `estimateKind: "uncompressed"` and the label is the only hint |
| no size limit anywhere in the dialog | the archive cap is **512 MiB**, checked against the *compressed* archive (`packages/research-package/src/index.ts:15`, `:231`) | the one size shown cannot be compared with the limit that decides success |
| 完整导出 + 包含完整轨迹详情 + 包含完整科学记忆图谱 → packaging runs, then fails | `Research package exceeds the archive size limit`, in **English**, inside a zh-CN UI | minutes of packaging for an outcome that was predictable, plus an untranslated, unactionable message |
| 正在计算范围与大小… forever, primary button disabled | `EXPORT_PREVIEW_PENDING`, retried every 1.5 s with no cap and no explanation (`ResearchPackage.tsx:217-227`) | no reason, no retry, no cancel, no way to know whether waiting helps (#1018) |
| a single line `N 个导出进行中`, expandable to filenames | phases (packaging / saving) and destination are known to the client but not shown | the user cannot tell "still packing" from "packed, now writing to disk" |
| cancelling your own export | `pushFlash("error", t.exportCanceled)` — a red error (`:152`, `:271`, `:350`) | a deliberate user action is reported as a failure |
| 已保存的会话包 list inside the export modal | the list is component state only; the shell persists just `lastExportDir` (`win_desktop/src/export-state.ts`) | after restarting the app the history is gone, and "打开文件位置" cannot be used for an earlier package |
| 导出会话 only in the session row menu (`Sidebar.tsx:210`) | — | a first-class task is buried three levels down |
| import dialog: title, object count, `omissions` | per-dimension content is unavailable (`PackageInspection` has no counts) | the user cannot see what will be restored before committing; this is also how evolve runs disappear silently (#1019) |

### Design Ideas

**1. Make the choice about content, not about jargon.** Replace the two profile cards' taglines with a per-dimension table for the selected profile — 会话 / 消息 / 产物 / 产物版本 / 工作区文件 / 执行记录 / 任务 / 科学记忆节点 / 关系 — and render the two optional switches nested under 完整导出 with their *delta* shown on the same table and on the size line. The server already computes these numbers (`countExport`, with Chinese labels in `services/api/src/research-snapshots.ts:444`); the preview payload simply does not expose them yet.

**2. Show two honest numbers and the limit.** `未压缩 ≈ 910.6 MiB` is useful for disk planning; `归档 ≈ 19.2 MiB` is what the user copies around and what the cap applies to. Show the archive limit as a meter, and once a package exists show its real archive size. Before packaging, if the selection is over the limit, say so on the card and offer the fix (drop 完整轨迹 / 完整记忆图谱, or switch to 必要导出) instead of starting a task that must fail.

**3. A durable export center instead of a transient modal.** Turn the export surface into a panel/sheet with two blocks: the scope form above, a persistent list below (filename, archive size, time, state, destination, 打开文件位置, 重新保存). The list must survive closing the panel and restarting the app, and `已取消` must be a neutral state, not a red error. Keep the modal as the confirmation step if a modal is still wanted; keeping state in component memory is what loses it.

**4. Explain blocked and pending states.** When the preview cannot settle, say why in user terms ("该会话有一个执行停在恢复流程，导出范围暂不可确定" is the #1018 case), and offer 重试 / 取消 / 查看该执行. A disabled primary button with a spinner is not a state.

**5. Give the task a first-class entry.** A 导出 button in the session header (`SessionBar`), with the row-menu item kept as a shortcut. Import stays where it is.

**6. Localize and make failures actionable.** Server errors reach the UI untranslated (`task.error` is rendered raw at `:321` and flashed at `:153`). Map known failures (archive limit, changed revision, missing task, preview pending) to zh-CN copy with a next step; keep the raw string behind a details disclosure, consistent with the failure-alert principle in #846.

**7. Import side, same information standard.** Show the same per-dimension counts from the package manifest in the inspect step, plus an explicit "不会恢复" block (this is where an evolve omission must appear, #1019), so the user decides before importing rather than discovering an empty Evolve panel afterwards.

Alternatives not selected: restyling the existing modal without changing what it shows; auto-selecting 完整导出; removing the size estimate entirely (users need it for disk planning); moving export into the settings page.

### Involved Public APIs

Additive only, no breaking change:

- `GET /api/projects/{projectId}/research-package/preview` — add `counts` (same shape as `countExport`), `archiveLimitBytes`, and if a cheap estimate is acceptable `estimatedArchiveBytes`. Keep `estimateKind` so a client never mistakes the two.
- `POST .../research-package/exports` and `GET .../exports/{id}` — expose the finished archive size (`archiveBytes`) so the list can show it without a download.
- `POST .../research-package/inspect` — expose the manifest `counts` already present in the package manifest.

`apps/web` and `apps/desktop` share `apps/desktop/src/api/research-package.ts` shapes, so both must keep working; web keeps the browser-download destination, desktop keeps the token-bound native save.

### Description of Relevance to Other Modules

| Module | Responsibility |
| --- | --- |
| `apps/desktop/src/views/ResearchPackage.tsx` | Scope form, counts table, size meter, export center, localized failures |
| `apps/desktop/src/views/SessionBar.tsx`, `Sidebar.tsx`, `App.tsx` | Entry point and panel wiring |
| `apps/desktop/src/styles/research-package.css`, `text/zh.ts`, `text/en.ts` | Layout and copy, both languages |
| `win_desktop` (`export-state.ts`, `preload.ts`, `main.ts`) | Persisted export list, destination tokens, reveal-in-folder |
| `services/api` (`research-snapshots.ts`) | Preview payload, counts, limit, archive size |
| `packages/research-package` | `MAX_TOTAL_BYTES`, manifest counts, omission strings |
| `apps/web` | Same view; parity required but not the focus |

### Test Design and Test Plan

- Component tests for the new blocks: counts table renders server counts; the size block shows both numbers and never labels the archive size as the estimate; an over-limit selection warns before `startExport` is called; cancel renders neutral; unknown server errors fall back to the raw string behind details.
- E2E on the desktop build with the real local stack, using a session that has evolve runs and scientific memory (the fixture from #1019):
  - 必要导出 and 完整导出 each round-trip to a saved `.sdresearch`, and the counts shown in the dialog match `POST .../inspect` of the produced package.
  - 完整导出 with both switches on the oversized session shows the pre-flight warning instead of a late English failure.
  - restart the app: the export list still shows the saved package and 打开文件位置 works.
  - cancel during packaging and during saving: neutral state, no error flash.
  - preview blocked (session with a stuck execution): the dialog explains the reason and offers retry/cancel.
- Import: inspect shows counts and the explicit not-restored list; compare against the live imported session.
- Commands: `pnpm --filter @sciencediscovery/desktop typecheck`, `pnpm --filter @sciencediscovery/desktop test`, `pnpm --filter @sciencediscovery/desktop build`, `pnpm ci:l1`. Screenshots of the export panel (necessary, complete with switches, over-limit warning, export list after restart) go in the PR body for the owner's visual approval, per the UI review rule.

### Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] The export scope step shows per-dimension counts for the selected profile, and the two optional switches show their effect on those counts and on size.
- [ ] The size block shows the uncompressed estimate and the archive size/limit distinctly; no single number is presented as the file the user will copy.
- [ ] A selection that cannot fit the archive limit is reported before packaging, with the fix offered on the card.
- [ ] Progress shows per-task state (packaging / saving) and destination; the export list survives closing the panel and restarting the app, and 打开文件位置 works for earlier packages.
- [ ] Cancelling a self-initiated export is neutral, not an error; known failures are localized with an actionable next step, raw text only behind details.
- [ ] A blocked preview names its cause and offers retry/cancel.
- [ ] Import inspection shows the same per-dimension counts and an explicit "will not be restored" list.
- [ ] Both zh-CN and en copy exist; `pnpm --filter @sciencediscovery/desktop typecheck|test|build` and `pnpm ci:l1` pass.
- [ ] The owner has seen the screenshots in the PR body before approval.

### Additional Information

Related: #803 (feature scope), #986 (save flow, closed by PR #999), #846 (localized, non-redundant failure presentation), #1018 (a session whose preview never settles — the blocked-state copy is a product decision there), #1019 (evolve runs absent from the package — the import "will not be restored" block must state it), #995 (import opens two sessions), #801 (desktop scientific memory), #798 (desktop evolve).

Measured numbers quoted above come from one real session on build `c95f080a`: 完整导出 preview 933,095,424 bytes uncompressed → saved archive 20,161,641 bytes; 完整导出 with both switches → `Research package exceeds the archive size limit`. The failure is not reproduced by any test in this issue description; it was observed by hand.
items.title: [Feature]: Redesign the desktop session-export UI around scope, honest size and a durable export center

items.body:
## What happens

`test/journey-custom-mcp.spec.ts` → **"Agent uses selected custom MCP servers across runs"** (test declared at `:203`, step 6 `等待修复并恢复调用`, body at `:314`) fails at `test/journey-custom-mcp.spec.ts:332`:

```
  1) [mocked] › ../test/journey-custom-mcp.spec.ts:203:1 › journey-custom-mcp.spec › Agent uses selected custom MCP servers across runs › 6. 等待修复并恢复调用

    Error: expect(received).toBeGreaterThan(expected)

    Expected: > 2
    Received:   2

      330 |       expect(terminal.status, terminal.error).toBe("completed");
      331 |       const recovered = await invocations();
    > 332 |       expect(recovered.length).toBeGreaterThan(before);
          |                                ^
```

Everything before the assertion in step 6 succeeds: the repair card `执行受阻` shows `等待 MCP 修复` with the disabled source id, `GET /api/sessions/<id>/mcp/invocations` stays at 2 while blocked, the server is re-enabled, `已修复，重新检查` is clicked, and `waitForRunTerminal` returns `completed`.

What the run then shows: the assistant's last message in that run is `MCP RECOVERED`, which the scripted model only emits **after** its `mcp_recovered_call` step (`test/journey-custom-mcp.spec.ts:243-247`):

```ts
[
  { tool: "mcp_readiness", arguments: { action: "wait", reason: "This task requires the selected echo source", sourceIds: [second.id] } },
  { tool: "mcp_recovered_call", arguments: { sourceId: second.id, toolId: second.toolId, input: { text: "mcp recovered" } } },
  { text: "MCP RECOVERED" },
],
```

So the scripted model did emit `mcp_recovered_call`, and the run continued past it, but no MCP invocation was recorded for that turn: `/api/sessions/<id>/mcp/invocations` still lists exactly the 2 invocations from the earlier runs (`custom-cbf8e…`, `custom-cea28…`), and the captured trace resource `0000f751….json` holds the same 2. The recovered call therefore never reached `McpSourceCatalog`/broker (`packages/artifact-manager/src/mcp-workspace-tools.ts` `mcpReadiness.invoke`), and the failure is silent to the user: the run completes and the message claims recovery.

## Where it is seen (evidence only)

The same journey, same assertion, fails on three unrelated heads:

| run | job | head | shard window (UTC) |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| [42619667305](https://github.com/openJiuwen-ai/sciencediscovery/actions/runs/42619667305) | [129188246374](https://github.com/openJiuwen-ai/sciencediscovery/actions/runs/42619667305/job/129188246374) | `9bf5077f7b` (#857 tip) | 13:38–13:58 failure |
| [42622133086](https://github.com/openJiuwen-ai/sciencediscovery/actions/runs/42622133086) | [129181494939](https://github.com/openJiuwen-ai/sciencediscovery/actions/runs/42622133086/job/129181494939) | `87c5da950b` (`codex/conversation-proxy-resources`) | 13:39–13:59 failure |
| [42615122979](https://github.com/openJiuwen-ai/sciencediscovery/actions/runs/42615122979) | [129160327871](https://github.com/openJiuwen-ai/sciencediscovery/actions/runs/42615122979/job/129160327871) | `127bb1fdef` (merge queue, `pr-1005`) | 12:34–12:54 failure |

It also passes on other heads in the same window, including main running the journey while the two 13:3x failures were in flight:

- main `c3678320ac`: run [42621321893](https://github.com/openJiuwen-ai/sciencediscovery/actions/runs/42621321893) job [129188930633](https://github.com/openJiuwen-ai/sciencediscovery/actions/runs/42621321893/job/129188930633), `✓ 21 … Agent uses selected custom MCP servers across runs (44.4s)` at 13:39:17Z, shard success (13:34–13:49).
- main `9feafa2730`: run [42562181452](https://github.com/openJiuwen-ai/sciencediscovery/actions/runs/42562181452) job [128981184690](https://github.com/openJiuwen-ai/sciencediscovery/actions/runs/42562181452/job/128981184690), `✓ 21` at 04:38:35Z. That shard job is red overall because of a different journey (`journey-first-run.spec.ts:59`), so the shard verdict alone does not describe this journey.

`L2 E2E (mocked, standard-config)` outcomes for completed runs created between 11:30Z and 14:00Z (jobs read one by one; cancelled runs excluded): **3 failure / 16 success**, and the three failures are the table above. Two of the green runs are `dev2/fix/upload-windows-reserved-names` `0c5f26ab03` (13:33:34Z) and `dev/884-bug-comparing-two-binary-artifact-versio` `cefe1ebd79` (13:25:34Z).

## Not caused by the #857 diff

#857 (`9bf5077f7b`) changes exactly two files, `services/api/src/runs/index.ts` and `services/api/src/runs/index.test.ts` (+210/−23); the merge ref `fdf61b56798086e573368bc82120e91e8c5cc52b` for its failing job has parents `9feafa27` + `9bf5077f` and nothing else. The two other failing heads carry none of that diff. The failing journey exercises custom-MCP registration, the repair wait and `mcp_recovered_call` — not the scheduler's delayed retry pass. #857 is linked only because its shard run is one of the three observations, not as the cause.

## What is not yet known

Whether this is a product race (the recovered call is dropped or rejected after `catalog.refresh`, so a real user also loses the recovered invocation while the message claims it ran) or a test that stops waiting too early (it asserts the invocation list immediately after the terminal state). The two need different fixes, and the 3-of-19 rate above is the only discriminator so far: a deterministic loss is a product gap, an occasional one points at the wait.

Not run: local reproduction of the journey (20 consecutive runs on a local stack). The stack could not be started in the reporting environment — the pnpm store lives on a read-only home, the pinned Chromium download did not complete, and the JiuwenSwarm virtualenv install had not finished when this was filed. No code was changed for this report.

items.author: HugoXK
items.body:
## Summary

The containment added by #857 stops an escaped scheduler write from killing the API (the #816 defect), but two recovery gaps around it remain. Both were raised as `medium, suggestion` in the 2026-11-09 review of `9bf5077f7b4104564bdee110c4f001f7b1d4a403` (F5 and F4), and neither is implemented here.

### 1. An escape raised while re-reading the run list skips the backoff entirely

`services/api/src/runs/index.ts:3738` is the file's own `finally`:

```ts
    } finally {
      scheduledSessions.delete(sessionId);
      const remaining = await store.listSessionRuns(sessionId);
```

If that read rejects (an unreadable `session-runs/` directory — the same ownership/ACL misconfiguration the cap path exists for), the promise rejects before `schedulerEscapes` is touched or `setTimeout` is reached. The `.catch` at `:3762` logs `run_scheduler_failed` and that is all: no timer, no counter, no `run_scheduler_stopped`. The comment at `:3767-3773` names this read as one of the escape sites and states the reschedule "is delayed and capped", which is not true for it.

Measured on `9bf5077f` with `listSessionRuns` mocked to reject: exactly 2 calls, no retry, no rejection reaches the process. The session silently stops scheduling while a run is still `queued`.

**Fix shape suggested in the review:** make the `finally` body tolerant so the escape still takes the backoff branch.

```ts
      let remaining: SessionRun[] = [];
      try { remaining = await store.listSessionRuns(sessionId); } catch { /* fall through with escaped already set */ }
```

### 2. After the cap, the queued run has only a server log

`services/api/src/runs/index.ts:3747`: the sixth consecutive escape (delays 500 + 1000 + 2000 + 4000 + 8000 ms ≈ 15.5 s) logs `run_scheduler_stopped` and stops. The run stays `queued` on disk, and nothing schedules it again in process — `recoverSessionRuns` only handles `running`/`blocked`, so recovery depends on the bootstrap sweep (`services/api/src/bootstrap/platform.ts:747-770`) or another HTTP-triggered `scheduleSessionRuns`.

Measured on `9bf5077f` with `updateSessionRunStatusIfCurrent` made to fail and then to succeed: **6** transition attempts and **12** `listSessionRuns` calls in 19.5 s, then **0** attempts after the fault cleared, with the run still `queued`. Realistic causes are an ownership/ACL problem that outlives 15 s, a full disk, or a long scanner hold.

**Impact:** the chat never starts and the user sees neither a failure nor a message, while #816's expected result asks for an actionable error on the affected run when persistence cannot recover.

## What it should do

- An escape raised inside the `finally` must take the same delayed-and-capped path as an escape raised inside the loop; the comment already promises it.
- After the cap, the affected run should carry an error the API returns (mark it `failed`, or `interrupted` with a reason), or the stop should become a slow fixed retry — `SCHEDULER_RETRY_MAX_MS` already allows 30 s.

## Why this is not in #857

The review classified both as `medium, suggestion`, and the second is marked `[Needs a person]`: choosing between "fail the run with an actionable error" and "retry slowly forever" changes what a user sees after an unrecoverable state write, so it is a decision, not a mechanical fix. #857 carries only its must-fix (the retry closure dropped `executionGovernance`).

## Not implemented

Nothing in this issue is implemented and no pull request is open for it.
items.title: [Bug] a queued run can end up with nothing scheduled: the escaped re-read skips the backoff, and after the cap only a server log remains

items.author: yuanzhou75
items.body:
Follow-up work split out of #717 (`fix(tools): bound model-facing execution and MCP results`) so that PR does not have to carry it. None of these blocks that PR. @moShangLouTou — GitHub refuses to assign this issue to you because your account has no write access to this repository; it is yours regardless.

## 1. The audit path has a depth cap but no total-size budget

`redactToolDetails` (`packages/tools/src/registry.ts`) deliberately drops the interactive size limits — that is the point of it, the durable record keeps complete safe metadata — and keeps only `MAX_AUDIT_DETAIL_DEPTH = 128`. Depth is bounded; total size is not. A result whose `details` are *wide* rather than deep — an MCP `records` array with many small records, for example — is written whole through `recordResult` into the durable trajectory and into the version recorder.

That is the same shape the interactive view already avoids with `MAX_DETAIL_TOTAL_CHARS`. Suggest a total-byte budget for the audit copy too, with an explicit `[audit-details truncated]`-style marker, so a reader can tell the difference between "the tool returned this" and "the recorder cut it".

## 2. `mcpModelResultView` copies the whole result twice

`mcpModelResultView` (`packages/workspace/src/mcp-result-view.ts`) runs `safeMcpValue` over the entire provider result to build a safe copy, and then `mcpRetainedContent` runs `JSON.stringify` over that copy whenever the projection is lossy. For a large result that is a full deep copy plus a full serialization on every MCP call.

Worth measuring against a realistically large provider result before deciding; if it shows up, a size gate on the retention serialization (retain only while the result is under some bound, with the existing "could not be stored" notice when it is not) would keep the recovery contract and remove the worst case.

## 3. Two journey assertions changed for reasons unrelated to this PR

- `test/journey-artifact-viewer-large-screen.spec.ts`: the readable-measure assertion moved from a fixed `760px` to `76ch` measured from the paragraph's computed font.
- `test/journey-model-connect-wizard.spec.ts`: the "高级配置" button assertion moved from `boundingBox().width > 50` to `scrollWidth <= clientWidth`.

Neither is needed by the tool-result contracts this PR introduces. If they were required to keep the suite stable, say so in a one-line note on #717; otherwise they belong in their own change.

items.author: zhaochen39
items.body:
## Summary

Model setup is the first-run gate: with no provider configured, **Settings → Model registry** opens the *Connect model* wizard automatically (`apps/web/src/ProviderModelSettings.tsx:617-618`). The screen is meant to answer one question — "which model will my runs use?" — but it currently asks it in six different places, uses one label for two different actions, and commits some answers with a Save button while committing others the moment they are clicked. This report is about that flow, not about how any single control looks.

## What the screen offers today

| # | Control | Where | What it writes |
|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | `Connect model` → `Save & connect` | registry heading (`ProviderModelSettings.tsx:897-904`) | creates the provider **and** registers every model the vendor lists, immediately |
| 2 | `Fetch model list` → tick rows → `Save & connect` | wizard footer (`ModelConnectWizard.tsx:828-841`) | same, narrowed to the ticked models |
| 3 | `Advanced configuration` → `Manual entries` / `Model identifier` | a fold inside the wizard (`ModelConnectWizard.tsx:745-794`) | same, for models the listing does not return |
| 4 | `Refresh list` → per-row `Add` | expanded provider (`ProviderModelSettings.tsx:346-348`) | one model, immediately |
| 5 | `Add model` (toggle) → manual form | bottom of the expanded provider (`ProviderModelSettings.tsx:505-515`) | one model, immediately |
| 6 | `Global default task model` select | registry heading (`ProviderModelSettings.tsx:879-896`) | `globalSettings.modelId`, immediately |
| 7 | `Edit` provider → `Save` / `Cancel` | expanded provider (`ProviderModelSettings.tsx:703-749`) | provider fields, staged until Save |

Above all of that sits a separate `Model catalog` strip with its own refresh (`ProviderModelSettings.tsx:386-400`).

## Problems

### 1. `Add model` means two different things, one above the other

Inside the same expanded provider, the per-model row action uses `t("providers.models.add")` (`ProviderModelSettings.tsx:348`) and the toggle that opens the manual form uses the *same* string (`:506`). So the row of a listed model offers "Add" (register this model) and a few pixels below the table another "Add model" opens a form. The wizard reuses the label a third time for its manual-entry toggle, but submits with a different one, `Add to list` (`ModelConnectWizard.tsx:779, 791`). A user cannot predict what any of these three controls will do from its label.

### 2. Two incompatible save models in the same panel

Provider fields are a draft: `Save` / `Cancel`, plus a `window.confirm` when another provider's `Edit` would discard the draft (`ProviderModelSettings.tsx:679-687, 693-697`). Everything else writes immediately:

- adding a model — `addModel()` calls the API at once, no confirm (`:784-823`);
- deleting a model — immediate, but guarded by `window.confirm` (`:825-863`);
- deleting a provider — immediate, guarded by `window.confirm` (`:751-754`);
- the default-model select — immediate (`:879-896`).

The same panel therefore mixes revertible and irreversible actions with no visual cue for which is which. Collapsing the row or expanding another one hides an unsaved provider draft with no prompt at that moment (`:699-701`), and the prompt only arrives later, when the settings dialog is closed — by then the user has usually forgotten the draft exists.

### 3. Registering *every* listed model is the silent default, and choosing models is hidden

With no explicit choice, `Save & connect` fetches the vendor list and registers all of it (`ModelConnectWizard.tsx:324-339`). To choose a subset the user must first press `Fetch model list` (`:828-841`) and only then do checkboxes appear. The only warning is the small plan line "Save & connect registers every model the provider lists" (`:838`), while the manual path that most users need when discovery fails is behind `Advanced configuration`, a fold that otherwise looks like protocol/proxy plumbing. Nothing states before saving that the first registered model will become the global default; that effect is only reported afterwards (`:414-421, 433-450`).

### 4. The default task model is edited in two places with different commit semantics

The registry heading has a `Global default task model` select that writes instantly (via `replaceDefaultModelOverride`, `App.tsx:5259-5269`). The same value is also edited in **Settings → Global → Task model**, which is a draft saved by the dialog's own Save (`App.tsx:5217-5219`). Two controls, one field, opposite commit behaviour — the difference is invisible until someone loses an edit.

### 5. Vocabulary: seven labels for four concepts

`Connect model`, `Save & connect`, `Add model`, `Add to list`, `Fetch model list`, `Refresh list`, `Advanced configuration` vs `Advanced connection settings` (`i18n/messages.ts:675-720, 738, 771`). "Connect", "register", "add" and "save" are used interchangeably for one operation, while "fetch"/"refresh" is the only genuinely different one.

### 6. Success does not end the flow

`resetPlan()` clears only the model plan (`ModelConnectWizard.tsx:157-164`); the API key, provider name, base URL and success banner stay (`:433-450`). Pressing `Save & connect` again therefore creates a second provider with the same display name — allowed by the store (`services/api/src/store.ts:2758-2779` has no name uniqueness check) — and there is no explicit "done" state to tell the user the wizard has finished.

## Actual vs expected

| | Actual | Expected |
|---|---|---|
| Entry points | Six ways to register a model across three levels (wizard, provider row, manual form), plus a default-model control duplicated in another tab | One way for each intent: add a provider; add models to a provider; pick the default model |
| Commit model | Provider fields staged, models and default immediate, deletes confirmed one by one | One commit model for the whole registry, with the same confirmation rule for every destructive action |
| Model choice | Register-all unless the user discovers `Fetch model list`; manual entry inside `Advanced configuration` | The listing visible by default with checkboxes, "register all" an explicit choice, manual entry next to it |
| Default model | Same field, two controls, two commit semantics, no indication of which wins | One control, or a link to the canonical one |
| After success | Form keeps the key and name; second press creates a duplicate provider | Clear, collapsed or "done" state; a duplicate name is warned about |

## Where

- `apps/web/src/ProviderModelSettings.tsx` — registry heading, wizard mount, provider rows, per-row add/delete, manual form toggle, default-model select, provider draft.
- `apps/web/src/ModelConnectWizard.tsx` — `resolveModelPlan` (register-all fallback), advanced fold, footer plan summary, success state.
- `apps/web/src/i18n/messages.ts:675-720, 722-723, 738, 771, 915` — the button and heading vocabulary.
- `apps/web/src/App.tsx:5217-5219, 5250-5280` — Mounting of the registry and of the Global settings group that edits the same default.

## Root cause

One component serves four jobs at once — registry list, provider editor, model picker, default-model setter — and each job brought its own persistence style and its own copy. The wizard was added later to make first-run setup one step, but it kept the provider editor's advanced fields *and* gained model registration, so provider creation and model registration now overlap instead of composing: the wizard can register models, the provider row can only add one at a time, and the provider editor cannot touch models at all. The `Add model` label was reused from the existing manual form for three controls that do different things.

## Suggested direction

1. **One control per intent.** `Add provider` (the wizard) and a single `Add model` per provider, opening one dialog that shows the fetched listing with checkboxes and keeps manual entry as a fallback in the same dialog. Remove the separate advanced/manual toggle, and stop using `Add` both for "register this listed model" and "open a form".
2. **Pick one commit model for the registry** and keep it: either stage every edit behind Save (provider fields, models, default) or make every action immediate with an undo. Apply the same confirmation rule to add, delete model and delete provider.
3. **Make model selection visible in the wizard.** Fetch the listing as soon as the key is entered, show it above the fold, and make "register all listed models" an explicit checkbox instead of the silent fallback. State the "first model becomes the global default" consequence before `Save & connect`.
4. **De-duplicate the default-model control.** Keep one, and link to it from the other place instead of rendering the same field twice with different commit semantics.
5. **End the flow on success.** Clear the key and name, collapse the wizard or show a `Done` state, and warn when a provider with the same name already exists.
6. **Copy pass.** Unify `Connect model` / `Save & connect` / `Add model` / `Add to list`, and keep `fetch`/`refresh` for the vendor listing only.

## Duplicate check

Searched open and closed issues for `model registry`, `Connect model`, `wizard`, `Add model`, `provider` and `usability`. #39 (closed) introduced the one-step connection wizard and is the origin of this overlap; #632 (closed) and #684 cover the *searchable model picker* rather than the registration flow; #686 covers the rendering of the provider `Test` control. None reports the overlapping entry points, the mixed save semantics or the duplicated default-model control.
items.title: [Usability] Model registration: overlapping entry points and inconsistent save semantics

## Purpose

Track the remaining research-team budget and cancellation integration validation for v0.4.0, split from #239 at the user's request. The classification fix in #239 is implemented by merged PR #426 (`7b93f92e898dca1798595fd2fa320c23887e1565`). Closing #239 does not mean the full BRCA1 journey has been revalidated.

## Existing evidence

On a post-merge snapshot (`0c6fa3fb47ccac3b69e870ac7fddc4ee00a51853`), these commands passed 61/61 tests with no paid model calls:

```sh
node --import tsx --test test/helpers/real-delivery.unit.ts scripts/real-e2e-scoring.test.mjs .ci/ci-contract.test.mjs
```

They cover active delivery classification, terminal missing-output failures, scoring, and safe result packaging. They do not execute the full team-spec timeout branch or establish its persisted metrics/cancellation outcomes. PR #426's L3 evidence is not a replacement for the L4 BRCA1 journey.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] Add and run a deterministic integration test using a local model stub and a short budget, exercising the actual team journey timeout path rather than only helper functions.
- [ ] Verify persisted `team-metrics.json` distinguishes budget exhaustion (`integration=timed_out`) from terminal delivery failure and retains budget, elapsed duration, cancellation request, shutdown outcome, and actual terminal status.
- [ ] Verify cleanup stops the main run, children, pending wakeups, and relevant executions; retain diagnostic evidence on cleanup failure.
- [ ] Cover the terminal race: cancellation coincides with completion, while budget-exhaustion attribution remains correct.
- [ ] Preserve normal delivery contracts: successful completion requires readable, nonempty final artifacts; terminal missing/empty/unreadable output remains a delivery failure.
- [ ] Run or inspect a post-fix L4/Nightly `TC-E2E-01` BRCA1 journey at its configured team budget. Record the immutable SHA, command/configuration, final artifacts, persisted metrics, cancellation outcomes where applicable, and actual passed/failed/blocked/skipped counts. A successful normal completion alone does not cover the timeout branch.

## Execution constraints

The current instruction permits only verification without paid model calls. Do not start a billable model/judge run without authorization; an already scheduled post-fix Nightly may provide the real-journey evidence. Keep unexecuted scenarios explicitly pending.

## Scope

This is validation follow-up for v0.4.0. Any newly discovered product defect should be documented with reproduction evidence and linked here. Related: #239, #426.

items.author: zy95-12
items.body:
## Problem

Successful real research runs still have a large per-case memory footprint for individual users. On current `feat/jiuwenswarm`, the highest observed worker cgroup peak is **11.12 GiB**. Although the latest GraphMemory fix prevented the previously observed runaway behavior in this experiment, this steady operational footprint deserves separate investigation and reduction for ordinary personal computers.

This is a resource-efficiency issue, not a report of another GraphMemory OOM. It is separate from #210 / its fix #212.

## Measured evidence

Experiment revision: `17d0774a` (includes #212 and TC Judge fix #209).

- Nine real scientific E2E cases, three repetitions each; four case workers concurrently.
- GraphMemory enabled throughout, local backend, isolated graph directory per case/repetition.
- Native task dispatch with Swarm execution; generator/Judge `deepseek-flash`.
- Each worker has a 24 GiB cgroup limit and no swap. The group includes the platform stack, graph service, Swarm, Runner and descendants, browser, and Judge.
- All 27 attempts delivered successfully. Retained `memory.events` show `max=0`, `oom=0`, `oom_kill=0` for every worker.

| Case / repetition | Worker cgroup peak (GiB) | Sampled Node API RSS peak (GiB) |
| --- | ---: | ---: |
| TC-E2E-01 / 1 | 11.124 | 0.977 |
| DRB-75 / 1 | 11.123 | 1.127 |
| DRB-62 / 2 | 10.796 | 0.952 |
| DRB-75 / 3 | 10.397 | 1.275 |
| DRB-59 / 2 | 10.107 | 1.080 |

The three worker peaks for TC-E2E-01 were 11.12 / 8.27 / 8.43 GiB; DRB-75 was 11.12 / 8.61 / 10.40 GiB. Even PUCT's workers peaked around 4.41 GiB in this setup.

**Measurement boundaries:**

- Cgroup peak includes charged file cache and other memory, not just anonymous RSS. It is not proof that the application requires 11 GiB of unreclaimable working memory.
- API RSS is sampled separately and its maximum need not coincide with the group peak. Do not subtract these maxima to infer another component's usage.
- GraphMemory did not appear in the retained high-RSS process samples, but these contain only the host's top 12 processes above a threshold, so its precise individual peak cannot be recovered.
- This harness includes Playwright and diagnostic sampling. Startup/provisioning, browser, diagnostics, page cache, child agents, and runtime costs must be separated before attributing the footprint to the product or GraphMemory.
- Concurrent cases and agent choices varied; this is not a controlled concurrency-scaling measurement.

## Why this matters

Users on 8–16 GiB machines also need memory for the OS, browser, and other applications. Raising per-worker limits or recommending large-memory hosts is not an adequate resource-efficiency strategy. We need to establish the actual working set and provide a practical personal-machine configuration without silently dropping research evidence or quality requirements.

## Investigation and optimization plan

1. Record `memory.stat` (`anon`, `file`, `kernel`, `slab`, etc.), `memory.current/peak/events`, and memory pressure alongside process-tree attribution for the **specific worker cgroup**. Capture phase markers for startup, provisioning, child research, synthesis, and grading.
2. Sample process RSS/PSS by role: API, Swarm/gateway, graph, Runner/executions, browser, Judge. Keep diagnostics lightweight and credential-free; measure profiler overhead explicitly.
3. Reproduce TC-E2E-01 and DRB-75 alone and with concurrent child tasks. Measure the idle stack separately and compare with/without the browser/profiling overhead. Preserve GraphMemory and the same delivery/scoring contract.
4. Identify avoidable duplication or retention only from profiles: repeated runtime processes, scientific environments/imports, per-agent contexts, trajectory buffers, graph state, caches, and teardown. Do not assume any one is the culprit from aggregate peaks.
5. Optimize the dominant confirmed contributors. If required, provide explicit resource-aware concurrency/backpressure and document the latency tradeoff rather than changing research tasks or silently disabling capabilities.

## Acceptance criteria

- Produce a component/phase memory breakdown for the highest-footprint cases, distinguishing reclaimable cache from working memory.
- Establish a measured baseline and a concrete lower memory budget suitable for a representative personal machine, with headroom for OS and interactive use; do not invent a target before attribution.
- Demonstrate improvement against that baseline on the same tasks, with GraphMemory enabled, no OOM, retained artifact delivery, and quality scoring reported independently.
- Check memory release after task completion and repeated use within a long-lived session; include lightweight regression monitoring where practical.

Retained evidence on the experiment host (not publicly accessible):
`/root/sciencediscovery-real9-graph-3x-20260927/case-summary.csv`, plus each case's `memory.csv`, `memory-events.txt`, and `memory-profiles/memory-*.jsonl`.
items.title: [Feature] Reduce real research memory footprint for personal machines: worker peaks reach 11.12 GiB

items.author: zhaozhaozz
items.body:
### Background

ScienceDiscovery does not have a recognizable product icon.

The browser tab has a title and no favicon. `apps/web/index.html` has no `rel="icon"` in `<head>`, so the product is indistinguishable from a generic page among bookmarks and tabs.

The in-app brand mark is a generic flask outline (`BrandIcon` in `apps/web/src/icons.tsx`) on an accent square. It fills the slot, but it is not a mark for this product, and it does not read at a 16px tab or bookmark size.

The README opens with a text title and a UI animation. It has no product mark.

### Expected

One product icon, the same mark in all of these places:

1. Browser favicon (at least 16×16 and 32×32, legible on both light and dark tab bars).
2. The in-app brand slot (today’s `.brand-mark`), replacing the generic flask outline.
3. The top of the English and Chinese READMEs, as a product mark. It does not replace the existing UI animation.

The mark has to stay recognizable at small sizes. Do not rely on hairline strokes alone. The drawing, colors, and whether it includes a wordmark are not decided here; this issue does not pre-select a design.

### Out of scope

- The icon is not a control that opens settings.
- The product name and copy stay as they are.
- A desktop or installer icon, if one is needed, belongs with [#34](https://github.com/openJiuwen-ai/sciencediscovery/issues/34) (a native desktop window). It does not block the favicon and the in-app mark.

### Acceptance

- [ ] After opening the local web app, the browser tab shows the product icon, not the browser’s default page icon.
- [ ] The sidebar brand slot uses the same mark, not the generic flask outline.
- [ ] The English and Chinese READMEs show the same mark at the top, and the existing UI animation remains.
- [ ] The small icon stays legible on a light UI and on a dark system tab bar.
- [ ] The icon ships in the repository (for example an SVG source plus the small favicon sizes). It does not depend on an external URL.

### Environment

Against current `main` of `openJiuwen-ai/sciencediscovery`: `apps/web/index.html` has no favicon, and `BrandIcon` is a flask outline.
items.title: [Feature] Give ScienceDiscovery a recognizable product icon
