## 🚀 Background Description

Issue #817 defined four acceptance criteria across three CI engineering capabilities: test coverage gating, CI stability, and release CI efficiency (`<5h`). Three pull requests have since landed on `main`:

- **PR #951** (`2c33bc5017`): migrated 11 previously unscheduled Playwright specs (41 case identities) onto the shared PR plan (`L2` mocked E2E) and removed the `legacy` Playwright project (`status:legacy`, `ci:e2e:legacy`, `test:legacy*`, `CI_ALLOW_LEGACY`).
- **PR #940** (`360e6b664f`): preserved `reasoning_effort: low` across Evolve and search paths, added bounded upstream transport retries (502/503/504/524 and mid-stream socket resets) for streaming model completions, and configured Nightly model and judge calls to run with `low` effort in `nightly-research` with a 75-minute research-team timeout.
- **PR #971** (`1db615cdd2`): narrowed the active BiomniBench-DA L5 execution set from 50 to 45 cases (64 total real L5 cases), pinned Biomni generator and rubric judge thinking to `enabled` with `low` effort, scaled additive resource baselines by `45/50`, and recovered `da-11-1` when a stream ends cleanly inside truncated tool-call JSON.

### Audit of #817 Acceptance Criteria on Current `main`

Measured against the latest completed `main` CI run [42968972446](https://github.com/openJiuwen-ai/sciencediscovery/actions/runs/42968972446) (`679038182e`) and recent L5 / Release runs:

#### 1. Coverage thresholds and gating
- **1.1 Coverage gate enforcement**: **Not met** — `scripts/coverage-job-summary.mjs` and `.ci/tier-policy.mjs` remain informational only (`Coverage is informational. No minimum percentage is enforced`), and the Coverage job still merges only `ut` and `st` (mocked browser E2E is not measured).
- **1.2 Whole-repo line coverage ≥80%**: **Met** — **80.82%** (`203,344 / 251,596`; Node.js `81.18%`, Python `73.93%`, up from the `73.11%` baseline at `6d3c49a`).
- **1.3 Whole-repo branch coverage ≥70%**: **Not met** — **59.86%** (`98,788 / 165,035`; Node.js `59.80%`, Python `62.06%`), **10.14 percentage points** below the `70%` target.
- **1.4 Function coverage ≥80%**: **Met (Node.js)** — **80.08%** (`13,142 / 16,411`; Python function coverage is not separately reported).
- **1.5 Statement coverage ≥80%**: **Not implemented** — `summary.json` reports `lines`, `branches`, and `functions` only.
- **1.6 New / changed code (PR diff) coverage ≥80%**: **Not implemented** — no PR diff coverage calculation, summary comment, or gate check exists in CI.
- **1.7 Per-package coverage floor ≥60%**: **Partially met** — `apps/web` (`62.89%`) and Node `services/runner` (`88.55%`) now exceed `60%`, while `packages/idea-tree` (`45.94%`), `packages/schema` (`57.89%`), and Python `services/runner` (`0%`) remain below `60%`.
- **1.8 Core-path coverage ≥90%**: **Partially met** — `services/api` (`94.84%`), `packages/sandbox-capability` (`100%`), and `packages/model` (`96.48%`) exceed `90%` line coverage, while `services/gateway` (`75.23%`) and `services/runner` (`88.55%`) are below `90%`, and no dedicated core-path gate is enforced.

#### 2. Case-level profile and module coverage
- **2.1 No case outside every profile**: **Partially met** — PR #951 eliminated all 42 `status:legacy` dead cases by moving 41 valid browser identities into the `pr` (`L2`) profile. Remaining cases outside `test/support/tagged/profiles.mjs` rules are 79 `status:external` UT/ST cases, 1 `status:quarantined` case (`test/literature-review.spec.ts`), 1 `npu:required` case, 1 `category:st + model:real` case, and 6 `os:macos` cases; `ci:catalog:check` does not yet fail on profile-unreachable tags.
- **2.2 Every module mapped to an executing gating case**: **Not implemented** — the tagged catalog does not yet carry an explicit case-to-module ownership mapping or fail when a module has no executing case.

#### 3. CI stability and flake governance
- **3.1 Automated flake identification and quarantine**: **Not implemented** — no rolling failure-rate detector, automatic quarantine transition, or tracking-issue workflow is in place.
- **3.2 Infrastructure-only retries for network/gateway faults**: **Partially met** — PR #940 and PR #971 implemented bounded transport/stream retries and clean-EOF tool-argument recovery without retrying product defects, but per-case infrastructure retry counts and gateway-outage separation are not yet surfaced in the CI summary.
- **3.3 Thinking-mode (`low` / off) A/B experiment and CI configuration**: **Partially met** — PR #940 and PR #971 pinned Nightly and Biomni L5 runs to `reasoning_effort: low` without changing product defaults, while a formal multi-run A/B pass-rate and variance comparison report remains open.

#### 4. Release CI efficiency (`<5h`)
- **4.1 L5 release CI end-to-end duration <5 hours**: **Not met** — after PR #971 landed, the `main` L5 run [42380603816](https://github.com/openJiuwen-ai/sciencediscovery/actions/runs/42380603816) (`l5 · parallel=4 · nightly-research`) ran for **15h 39m** (2026-11-07 14:13Z to 2026-11-08 05:52Z, failed); prior branch L5 runs [42340397412](https://github.com/openJiuwen-ai/sciencediscovery/actions/runs/42340397412) and [42236770100](https://github.com/openJiuwen-ai/sciencediscovery/actions/runs/42236770100) took **8h 49m** and **7h 30m**; the latest `Release` workflow run [41196686771](https://github.com/openJiuwen-ai/sciencediscovery/actions/runs/41196686771) took **25h 01m**.
- **4.2 In-pipeline duration budget tracking and over-budget alerts**: **Not implemented** — no 5-hour budget table or alert check is wired into `release.yml` or `ci.yml`.
- **4.3 Bulk data downloads managed via cache/prefetch with zero redundant downloads on cache hit**: **Not implemented** — bulk downloads across jobs are not yet uniformly cached/prefetched and timed against the budget.
- **4.4 Real-model journeys running at lowest thinking effort with latency gain recorded**: **Partially met** — `low` effort is active for Nightly and Biomni L5, but before/after per-case p50/p95 latency gain reports have not been published.

---

### Scope of Follow-up Work Tracked by This Issue

Based on the audit above, the following four deliverables require continued development:

1. **Whole-repo branch coverage ≥70% (Item 1.3)**: raise combined Node.js + Python branch coverage from the current **59.86%** (`98,788 / 165,035`) to **≥70%**, and enforce the threshold in CI.
2. **New / changed code (PR diff) coverage ≥80% (Item 1.6)**: compute diff coverage on pull requests against the merge base and enforce a **≥80%** diff coverage gate on executable changed lines/branches in CI.
3. **L5 release CI end-to-end duration <5 hours (Item 4.1)**: reduce full L5 release pipeline wall-clock duration to **<5 hours**, with per-job budget accounting and over-budget alerts in the pipeline summary.
4. **Cache/prefetch management for all bulk data downloads with zero redundant downloads on cache hit (Item 4.3)**: audit and cache/prefetch all bulk downloads in CI (JiuwenSwarm ~1.5 GB runtime and virtualenvs, pnpm/uv dependencies, benchmark datasets and fixtures, model/sidecar assets, and container/base images), record download duration separately, and eliminate repeat bulk downloads when caches hit.

## Design Ideas

1. **Whole-repo branch coverage ≥70%**:
   - Prioritize packages with the largest uncovered branch mass in `coverage/summary.json` and `coverage/python/summary.json` (such as `services/api` at `54.79%` branches, `packages/workspace` at `55.72%`, `packages/artifact-manager` at `56.63%`, `services/gateway` at `57.22%`, `services/memory-graph` at `56.95%`, and `apps/web` at `70.73%`).
   - Add targeted unit and system tests for error branches, boundary guards, and fallback paths, and wire the `≥70%` branch threshold into `scripts/coverage-report.mjs` / `.ci/tier-policy.mjs`.

2. **PR diff coverage ≥80%**:
   - Extend `scripts/coverage-report.mjs` (or add a dedicated diff-coverage step in the `Coverage` job) to intersect `git diff <base>...<head>` hunk lines with merged LCOV / JSON coverage records from Node.js (`ut` + `st`) and Python (`coverage.py`).
   - Publish a clear per-file diff coverage table in `$GITHUB_STEP_SUMMARY` and fail the `Coverage` / `merge-gate` check when changed executable lines fall below `80%`.

3. **L5 release CI end-to-end duration <5 hours**:
   - Add per-job wall-clock and phase timing (setup/download vs. execution) to the L5 summary and enforce a `<5h` (`18,000s`) end-to-end budget check.
   - Combine shard parallelism tuning, long-tail case timeout/step-budget tightening, and deduplication of overlapping lower-tier work in the release profile so the end-to-end critical path stays under 5 hours.

4. **Bulk data download caching and prefetching**:
   - Inventory every multi-hundred-megabyte download across `.github/workflows/ci.yml`, `real-e2e.yml`, and `release.yml` (JiuwenSwarm bundle and Python virtualenvs, Node/pnpm stores, benchmark datasets/fixtures, browser binaries, and Docker layers).
   - Key caches by lockfile/manifest content hashes, warm them once in an upstream setup step or shared cache entry, and log cache-hit status plus download byte/time metrics in each job summary so cache-hit runs perform zero redundant bulk downloads.

## Involved Public APIs

None. All changes are internal to CI workflows, coverage reporting/gating scripts, and test suites; no product HTTP, CLI, or SDK APIs are added or modified.

## Description of Relevance to Other Modules

- `.github/workflows/ci.yml`, `.github/workflows/real-e2e.yml`, `.github/workflows/release.yml`: coverage gating, bulk-download cache orchestration, and L5 duration budget reporting.
- `scripts/coverage-report.mjs`, `scripts/coverage-job-summary.mjs`, `.ci/tier-policy.mjs`: whole-repo branch coverage gate (`≥70%`) and PR diff coverage calculation/gate (`≥80%`).
- `packages/*`, `services/*`, `apps/*` test suites: branch coverage additions to lift whole-repo branch coverage from `59.86%` to `≥70%`.

## Test Design and Test Plan

- **Branch coverage ≥70%**: run `pnpm test:shared` with coverage enabled and `node scripts/coverage-report.mjs`; verify merged whole-repo branch coverage is `≥70.00%` and that lowering the threshold or dropping coverage causes the gate script unit tests to fail.
- **PR diff coverage ≥80%**: add unit tests for the diff-coverage calculator covering added, modified, deleted, and non-executable files, plus a synthetic PR diff below and above `80%` to verify both the step summary table and non-zero exit code on failure.
- **L5 <5h and bulk download caching**: verify on consecutive CI / L5 runs that cache-hit jobs report `cache-hit: true` with near-zero download time for JiuwenSwarm, dependencies, and datasets, that the pipeline summary outputs the job timing breakdown against the 5-hour budget, and that the end-to-end L5 run completes in `<5 hours`.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] Merged whole-repo branch coverage (`Node.js + Python` across `ut` + `st`) reaches **≥70.00%** (up from `59.86%`), and the CI coverage gate fails if whole-repo branch coverage drops below `70%`.
- [ ] Pull request CI computes diff coverage on changed executable lines against the PR base and fails the gate when PR diff coverage is below **80.00%**, with the per-file diff breakdown rendered in the job summary.
- [ ] All bulk data downloads in CI (JiuwenSwarm install and virtualenvs, pnpm/uv dependencies, benchmark datasets/fixtures, and runtime assets) are managed through content-addressed cache/prefetch steps, download duration is measured separately, and cache-hit runs perform zero redundant bulk downloads.
- [ ] The L5 release CI pipeline finishes end-to-end in **<5 hours** (`<300 minutes`) and publishes a per-job duration vs. budget summary with automatic over-budget alerting.
- Commands that must pass: `pnpm ci:l1` and `pnpm test:shared`.

## Additional Information

- Parent tracking issue: #817
- Related merged PRs: #940, #951, #971
- Reference CI runs audited:
  - `main` coverage run: [42968972446](https://github.com/openJiuwen-ai/sciencediscovery/actions/runs/42968972446) (`679038182e`)
  - L5 runs: [42380603816](https://github.com/openJiuwen-ai/sciencediscovery/actions/runs/42380603816) (`15h 39m`), [42340397412](https://github.com/openJiuwen-ai/sciencediscovery/actions/runs/42340397412) (`8h 49m`), [42236770100](https://github.com/openJiuwen-ai/sciencediscovery/actions/runs/42236770100) (`7h 30m`)
  - Release run: [41196686771](https://github.com/openJiuwen-ai/sciencediscovery/actions/runs/41196686771) (`25h 01m`)

Implementation: ScienceDiscovery (ours) — PR follows within 24h. Do not pick up without a `pickup-ok` comment on this issue. Written-by: ScienceDiscovery Product Claimed-by: ScienceDiscovery Product Claim-Id: 01bed55cb4a442f0b75c584b91b8d861 Branch: dev1/fix/945-desktop-feedback-image-truncation Base: 9871f2dd537a At: 2026-11-06T00:45:51Z ## Summary The desktop shell ships its own copy of the feedback screenshot pipeline, byte-identical to the web one, so the same silent truncation happens there: one multi-select of 10 screenshots attaches only the first 8, the two dropped files disappear, and the dialog says nothing. Web is fixed separately: #942 (fix in PR #943). PR #943's `## Scope` already names this copy and leaves it out: > `apps/desktop/src/feedback/feedback-images.ts:116` carries a copy of this function with the same silent cap drop, and its own dialog has the same gap. This change is the `apps/web` face only; the desktop copy is left untouched and needs the same fix, tracked separately. This issue is that separate desktop fix. ## Where it happens (main `9871f2dd`) - `apps/desktop/src/feedback/feedback-images.ts` is the same git blob as the web file: `69a1251` (4981 bytes, sha256 `0b66e24c…` for both). Line 122 is `if (images.length >= FEEDBACK_MAX_IMAGES) break;` and line 127 returns `{ images }` with no truncation signal. - `apps/desktop/src/feedback/FeedbackDialog.tsx:304-306` — `const result = await prepareFeedbackImages(Array.from(files), images); setImages(result.images); setImageError(result.error);`; `result.error` is `undefined` on this path. - `apps/desktop/src/feedback/FeedbackDialog.tsx:476` — only `{imageError ?

{fb.images.error[imageError]}

: null}` is rendered, so nothing appears. - The cap is 8 (`packages/operational-logging/src/feedback.ts:40`). It is only stated once the add button is already disabled at the cap (`FeedbackDialog.tsx:447-452` -> `fb.images.limit(FEEDBACK_MAX_IMAGES)`), which never fires for a single over-cap multi-select. - Desktop strings are **not** the web i18n: `apps/desktop/src/text.ts:99` proxies `TEXT` over two dictionaries, and `Text` is `typeof ZH` (`apps/desktop/src/text/zh.ts:1237`). The image block is `apps/desktop/src/text/en.ts:1134-1146` (limit `:1137`) and `apps/desktop/src/text/zh.ts:1182-1194` (limit `:1185`). Entries there are function-valued (`limit: (max) => …`), so the new one must be too. ## Steps to reproduce (desktop shell) 1. Open the desktop app's feedback dialog. 2. Click "Upload image" and select 10 PNG/JPEG files in one multi-select. 3. Observe 8 thumbnails and no message; the button then reads "Up to 8 images". 4. Submit; the relayed issue carries 8 images. Expected: a visible notice naming the cap and how many files were dropped, same wording as web: "Only the first 8 screenshots were attached; 2 skipped." Actual: no notice; 2 files vanish. ## Red first (already red on the desktop module) Run through the desktop package's own runner (`apps/desktop/package.json:7` is `tsx --test tests/*.test.ts tests/*.test.tsx`), against the byte-identical copy of `apps/desktop/src/feedback/feedback-images.ts` (git blob `69a1251`, sha256 `0b66e24c…`) plus main's `packages/operational-logging/src/feedback.ts`, stubbing `createImageBitmap`/canvas/`FileReader`: ``` $ apps/desktop/node_modules/.bin/tsx --test .local/red-desktop/desktop-feedback-images.test.ts not ok 1 - desktop: ten picks at the eight-image cap report the two skipped undefined !== 2 not ok 2 - desktop: two picks under the cap report nothing skipped undefined !== 0 not ok 3 - desktop: one removed then two picked attaches one and reports one skipped undefined !== 1 # pass 0 # fail 3 ``` `images.length` assertions pass; the failing half is exactly the missing truncation signal. Proposed test file `apps/desktop/tests/FeedbackImages.test.tsx`, mirroring the web test in #943: module assertions plus a mounted-dialog assertion (desktop's `react-test-renderer` helper `apps/desktop/tests/support/dom-renderer.ts`) that the hint text appears after an over-cap pick. ## Smallest mergeable slice (Dev-1, desktop face, <= 1 week) 1. `apps/desktop/src/feedback/feedback-images.ts` — return `skipped: number` next to `images`; count files left when the cap is hit (same shape as PR #943). 2. `apps/desktop/src/feedback/FeedbackDialog.tsx` — hold `skippedImages` in state; render one neutral hint (`className="feedback-hint"`, next to the `preparing` hint at `:475`) when `> 0`, clear it on add/remove/reset. 3. `apps/desktop/src/text/zh.ts` + `apps/desktop/src/text/en.ts` — add `truncated: (max: number, skipped: number) => string` to the `images` block in both (zh first: `Text = typeof ZH`), same wording as #943. 4. New `apps/desktop/tests/FeedbackImages.test.tsx` — the three module assertions above plus the two mounted-dialog directions. No shared-contract or Worker change; web files untouched. ## Acceptance - A1 (must): picking 10 from empty attaches 8 and shows a hint containing "8" and "2" (en) / "8" and "2" (zh). - A2 (must): picking 2 under the cap shows no such hint (negative direction, so a blanket banner does not pass). - A3: with 8 attached, remove one, pick 2 more -> 8 attached and the hint says 1 skipped. - A4: the hint exists in both desktop dictionaries and disappears after a successful submit; wording matches web (#943) so the two shells read the same. ## Dedup - `search/issues` for `desktop feedback`, `feedback-images`, `desktop screenshot`, `desktop attachment`: the only feedback-truncation item is #942 (web, PR #943 open); #879/#880 are the desktop attachment **size unit** surface, unrelated. - No open PR touches any file under `apps/desktop/src/feedback/` or `apps/desktop/src/text/` (checked the desktop PRs whose text matches: #905, #814, #904). - #943's own `## Scope` states the desktop copy is deliberately left out, so this is the tracked follow-up rather than a duplicate. ## Notes - No PR is opened with this issue now: today's new-PR budget is already spent on #941/#943, so the desktop PR queues behind whichever lands on main first. - Opened without labels (our token gets 403 on label writes); triage labels need a maintainer. - Environment: desktop face (`apps/desktop`), no API/base change; base main `9871f2dd537a6f3e3a94a7eb7b5bc67ef717d363`.

recent.body:
## What

`services/gateway/tests/test_architecture_boundaries.py:156` (`GeneratedWorkspaceBoundaryTests`, added by #915) pins only one direction of the walk: both new cases assert that something is **not** reported. Nothing asserts that a violation still **is** reported after the ignore list changed.

## Trigger

`IGNORED_DIRECTORIES` is widened again, or `_files()` is narrowed, so that a real source root (`services/api`, `packages`, `apps/web`, `test/api`) stops being walked. Every current case still passes:

- `test_a_generated_workspace_is_not_walked` and `test_a_workspace_file_removed_after_listing_is_skipped` assert absence only;
- `test_node_and_browser_sources_use_only_product_names` asserts `failures == []`, which a walk that sees nothing also satisfies.

The boundary test then silently stops policing the Gateway boundary with no red test anywhere.

## Fix

Add the mirror case in `GeneratedWorkspaceBoundaryTests`, reusing the `mock.patch.object(sys.modules[__name__], "_files", ...)` plumbing already present at `:162`:

- have the patched walk yield a path under `services/api/src` (for example `services/api/src/probe-boundary-<pid>.ts`) whose content contains a vendor token;
- assert `_node_boundary_failures()` returns that path, as `path: <relative>` or `content: <relative>`.

Three lines in the test file. No production code changes.

## Why it is worth a line

Measured at `f99cc8a24495544988045699b9e5c2429553e332` (review comment on #915): a fabricated `services/api/src/probe-zz-deerflow-boundary.ts` does produce `['path: services/api/src/probe-zz-deerflow-boundary.ts']`, and with the pre-change ignore set a probe in `services/api/.tmp` produces `['content: services/api/.tmp/probe-manual-537457.ts']`. The guard works today; only its regression direction is untested.

Found while reviewing #915 and tracked here so the review thread can be closed without losing the gap.

### Checklist

- [X] I have searched for related issues but did not get the expected help.
- [X] This bug has not been fixed in the latest version.
- [X] Please note that if your bug description lacks corresponding environment information and a minimal reproducible demo, it will be difficult for us to reproduce and resolve the issue, which will reduce the possibility of receiving feedback, or even lead to the issue being closed.

### 🐞 Detailed Description of the Problem

**What the user sees.** The mocked E2E suite is `87/88` and the one red case fails not on product behaviour but on a browser console error raised by the suite's own teardown:

```text
Error: no console/page errors expected, got:
[error] Failed to load resource: the server responded with a status of 404 (Not Found)
  @ http://127.0.0.1:4410/api/projects/3abde864-e853-4350-aa53-5ccc1a6fafa6/research-package/preview?sessionId=6bcfc3e0-...
```

Case: `test/agent-run-componentization.spec.ts:380` — `S2b subagent 首个受控工具的权限卡也出现在主对话最外层`. Job `Gate / L2 E2E (mocked, standard-journeys)` (job id 130151439627) on Nightly run [42907916462](https://github.com/openJiuwen-ai/sciencediscovery/actions/runs/42907916462), sha `4bb737c2`.

**Evidence.** The mocked stack's `stack.log` (in `mocked-e2e-results-standard-journeys`, artifact id 13807782121) shows the request arrives **after** the project was deleted by teardown:

```text
GET  /api/evolve/status HTTP/1.1 200 OK
DELETE /api/projects/3abde864-e853-4350-aa53-5ccc1a6fafa6 HTTP/1.1 200 OK
POST /cleanup/project HTTP/1.1 200 OK
DELETE /api/models/4eea8f0a-... HTTP/1.1 200 OK
GET  /api/projects/3abde864-e853-4350-aa53-5ccc1a6fafa6/research-package/preview?sessionId=6bcfc3e0-...&defaults=1 HTTP/1.1 404 Not Found
```

The same log carries **59** such `404` responses on `research-package/preview`, and in another case the deleted Session is still polled directly:

```text
GET /api/sessions/c6603f8c-e86e-46dd-a455-b87ff206c4fd/runs HTTP/1.1 404 Not Found
GET /api/sessions/c6603f8c-e86e-46dd-a455-b87ff206c4fd/agent-activity HTTP/1.1 404 Not Found
```

So the panel keeps polling a project/session that teardown has just removed. The browser logs every 404 as a console error, and the journey's "no console errors" assertion turns that into a failed case.

**Expected.** One of these, whichever the team prefers:

1. A mounted panel stops polling once its project/session is deleted (listen for the deletion the test performs, or cancel the poll on unmount).
2. The preview read treats "project gone" as a normal end of polling and does not surface it as a console error (checked request + handled 404, instead of an unhandled resource load).
3. The assertion is scoped to the case's own session being alive.

(1) is the honest fix: the product should not keep asking the API about a project it has removed.

### Detailed Environment Information Description

- Repository: `openJiuwen-ai/sciencediscovery`, `main` at `4bb737c2fccc8b55471dfd08f4f58754c5981cb3`.
- Mocked E2E (`profile: daily`, `L2 E2E (mocked, standard-journeys)`), 88 planned / 87 passed / 1 failed; run started 2026-11-10T21:44:15Z (2026-11-11 05:44 CST).
- Stack: adapter 4410 → Node API 4510, runner 4411, memory-graph 17774; no real model calls in this job.

### Additional Information

This is a harness/teardown race rather than a user-facing delivery failure, but it reds the mocked gate on its own. It is unrelated to the four real-E2E failures on the same run (see the linked issues).

### Version Information

- `main` @ `4bb737c2fccc8b55471dfd08f4f58754c5981cb3`
- Nightly run 42907916462; job 130151439627; artifact `mocked-e2e-results-standard-journeys` (13807782121)

recent.author: zy95-12
recent.body:
## Background and environment

During a source installation on a Debian 13 cloud desktop on 2026-10-11, using main commit `5ddaa38bd68a84e4e20b14116d91880fe87bdd08`, two problems required manual investigation:

1. The desktop terminal did not inherit the outbound proxy environment. The initial managed micromamba download failed with `ECONNREFUSED`; an installation environment with the required network configuration could complete the download.
2. When the adapter inherited a SOCKS proxy configuration, it failed to start because `socksio` was missing, affecting access to the application.

The first observation is an environment-triggered failure, not proof of a downloader implementation defect. The second has a concrete dependency declaration gap.

## Conditions and observed behavior

### A. Different proxy environments across installation and runtime entry points

- External access required a proxy, but the terminal initiating scientific-environment preparation did not inherit the corresponding configuration.
- The micromamba connection was refused and scientific-environment preparation could not complete.
- Installation succeeded through an official download/install path with the necessary network configuration, retaining the pinned version and SHA-256 verification.
- The scientific environment subsequently became ready, with Python 3.12, NumPy, pandas, SciPy, and Matplotlib available.

### B. SOCKS configuration prevents adapter startup

- Create a clean adapter environment from the declared project dependencies and start it with a valid SOCKS proxy configuration.
- During HTTP client initialization, the missing socksio dependency prevents adapter startup.
- In this installation, adding socksio from official PyPI to the adapter's isolated environment restored startup; API health and page HTML checks then passed.

Source references:
- [Adapter declares plain httpx](https://github.com/openJiuwen-ai/sciencediscovery/blob/5ddaa38bd68a84e4e20b14116d91880fe87bdd08/services/adapter/pyproject.toml#L19-L25).
- [HTTP clients are constructed during startup](https://github.com/openJiuwen-ai/sciencediscovery/blob/5ddaa38bd68a84e4e20b14116d91880fe87bdd08/services/adapter/src/sciencediscovery_adapter/app.py#L47-L63).

## User impact

- Users may have already installed the source and other dependencies, yet still be blocked at first startup or scientific-environment preparation, preventing access to the workbench or relevant computations.
- Users must investigate differences between terminal and child-process proxy environments, and may need to install undeclared dependencies manually.
- A component-level failure can look like a failed installation of the entire application, leading to unnecessary reinstalls. This is not evidence that micromamba itself is unsuitable or unavailable.

## Expected behavior and proposed improvements

1. Unify installation/startup preflight checks: inspect the actual child process's proxy configuration, connectivity to required download sources, and dependencies for the selected proxy protocol. Report redacted status, never credentials.
2. Declare and lock SOCKS support, for example through `httpx[socks]`. Define the proxy boundary between loopback service calls and external requests, including correct `NO_PROXY` handling.
3. Identify the failing component, stage, underlying cause, and actionable next step. After configuration is corrected, allow retrying the failed step while reusing verified tools and caches.
4. Report Web entry point, adapter, and scientific-environment readiness separately instead of treating partial readiness as an all-or-nothing result.

The repository already has [download retry and cache mechanisms](https://github.com/openJiuwen-ai/sciencediscovery/blob/5ddaa38bd68a84e4e20b14116d91880fe87bdd08/scripts/fetch-managed-micromamba.mjs#L179-L295), as well as [classified errors and mirror/preinstalled-tool recovery guidance](https://github.com/openJiuwen-ai/sciencediscovery/blob/5ddaa38bd68a84e4e20b14116d91880fe87bdd08/services/runner/src/environment-store.ts#L1138-L1173). The goal is to connect these capabilities into a coherent first-run experience, not to replace the downloader.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] A clean adapter environment starts with HTTP/SOCKS proxy configurations without manually installing undeclared dependencies.
- [ ] Missing or incorrect proxy configuration produces redacted, actionable diagnostics while retaining the underlying error.
- [ ] Correcting configuration allows retrying the failed step and reusing verified artifacts, without clearing all data or reinstalling.
- [ ] Version pinning and hash verification remain enforced; recovery does not disable TLS verification.
- [ ] Tests cover no proxy, HTTP/SOCKS proxies, unreachable download sources, and successful retry after correction; installation documentation is updated.

Related: #29 (actionable dependency preflight), #213 and #229 (onboarding feedback). This issue focuses on the observed proxy-related failures and first-install recovery experience.
recent.title: [Bug] Improve proxy-aware installation: declare SOCKS support and unify preflight and recovery

recent.author: yuanzhou75
recent.body:
### 🚀 Background Description

Exporting a session works today, but the dialog is still shaped like a developer tool rather than a user task. Everything a user needs in order to decide *what* they are handing off, *how big* it will be, and *what happened* to the last export is either missing, misleading, or only reachable by reopening a modal. This is the session-export UI design work, desktop first.

The save flow itself was fixed in #986 / PR #999 (native save dialog, automatic save, per-export tracking) and the capability is specified in #803, so this issue is not about those. It is about the presentation of scope, size, progress and outcome.

Observations from the current desktop UI (`apps/desktop/src/views/ResearchPackage.tsx`, main 2026-11-09) and from a real export of a session with evolve runs and scientific memory (build `c95f080a`):

| What the user sees | What is actually true | Why it misleads |
| --- | --- | --- |
| 预计大小（未压缩）**910.6 MiB** on the 完整导出 card | the saved `.sdresearch` was **19.2 MiB** (20,161,641 bytes) | one number, 46× the real file; it is `estimateKind: "uncompressed"` and the label is the only hint |
| no size limit anywhere in the dialog | the archive cap is **512 MiB**, checked against the *compressed* archive (`packages/research-package/src/index.ts:15`, `:231`) | the one size shown cannot be compared with the limit that decides success |
| 完整导出 + 包含完整轨迹详情 + 包含完整科学记忆图谱 → packaging runs, then fails | `Research package exceeds the archive size limit`, in **English**, inside a zh-CN UI | minutes of packaging for an outcome that was predictable, plus an untranslated, unactionable message |
| 正在计算范围与大小… forever, primary button disabled | `EXPORT_PREVIEW_PENDING`, retried every 1.5 s with no cap and no explanation (`ResearchPackage.tsx:217-227`) | no reason, no retry, no cancel, no way to know whether waiting helps (#1018) |
| a single line `N 个导出进行中`, expandable to filenames | phases (packaging / saving) and destination are known to the client but not shown | the user cannot tell "still packing" from "packed, now writing to disk" |
| cancelling your own export | `pushFlash("error", t.exportCanceled)` — a red error (`:152`, `:271`, `:350`) | a deliberate user action is reported as a failure |
| 已保存的会话包 list inside the export modal | the list is component state only; the shell persists just `lastExportDir` (`win_desktop/src/export-state.ts`) | after restarting the app the history is gone, and "打开文件位置" cannot be used for an earlier package |
| 导出会话 only in the session row menu (`Sidebar.tsx:210`) | — | a first-class task is buried three levels down |
| import dialog: title, object count, `omissions` | per-dimension content is unavailable (`PackageInspection` has no counts) | the user cannot see what will be restored before committing; this is also how evolve runs disappear silently (#1019) |

### Design Ideas

**1. Make the choice about content, not about jargon.** Replace the two profile cards' taglines with a per-dimension table for the selected profile — 会话 / 消息 / 产物 / 产物版本 / 工作区文件 / 执行记录 / 任务 / 科学记忆节点 / 关系 — and render the two optional switches nested under 完整导出 with their *delta* shown on the same table and on the size line. The server already computes these numbers (`countExport`, with Chinese labels in `services/api/src/research-snapshots.ts:444`); the preview payload simply does not expose them yet.

**2. Show two honest numbers and the limit.** `未压缩 ≈ 910.6 MiB` is useful for disk planning; `归档 ≈ 19.2 MiB` is what the user copies around and what the cap applies to. Show the archive limit as a meter, and once a package exists show its real archive size. Before packaging, if the selection is over the limit, say so on the card and offer the fix (drop 完整轨迹 / 完整记忆图谱, or switch to 必要导出) instead of starting a task that must fail.

**3. A durable export center instead of a transient modal.** Turn the export surface into a panel/sheet with two blocks: the scope form above, a persistent list below (filename, archive size, time, state, destination, 打开文件位置, 重新保存). The list must survive closing the panel and restarting the app, and `已取消` must be a neutral state, not a red error. Keep the modal as the confirmation step if a modal is still wanted; keeping state in component memory is what loses it.

**4. Explain blocked and pending states.** When the preview cannot settle, say why in user terms ("该会话有一个执行停在恢复流程，导出范围暂不可确定" is the #1018 case), and offer 重试 / 取消 / 查看该执行. A disabled primary button with a spinner is not a state.

**5. Give the task a first-class entry.** A 导出 button in the session header (`SessionBar`), with the row-menu item kept as a shortcut. Import stays where it is.

**6. Localize and make failures actionable.** Server errors reach the UI untranslated (`task.error` is rendered raw at `:321` and flashed at `:153`). Map known failures (archive limit, changed revision, missing task, preview pending) to zh-CN copy with a next step; keep the raw string behind a details disclosure, consistent with the failure-alert principle in #846.

**7. Import side, same information standard.** Show the same per-dimension counts from the package manifest in the inspect step, plus an explicit "不会恢复" block (this is where an evolve omission must appear, #1019), so the user decides before importing rather than discovering an empty Evolve panel afterwards.

Alternatives not selected: restyling the existing modal without changing what it shows; auto-selecting 完整导出; removing the size estimate entirely (users need it for disk planning); moving export into the settings page.

### Involved Public APIs

Additive only, no breaking change:

- `GET /api/projects/{projectId}/research-package/preview` — add `counts` (same shape as `countExport`), `archiveLimitBytes`, and if a cheap estimate is acceptable `estimatedArchiveBytes`. Keep `estimateKind` so a client never mistakes the two.
- `POST .../research-package/exports` and `GET .../exports/{id}` — expose the finished archive size (`archiveBytes`) so the list can show it without a download.
- `POST .../research-package/inspect` — expose the manifest `counts` already present in the package manifest.

`apps/web` and `apps/desktop` share `apps/desktop/src/api/research-package.ts` shapes, so both must keep working; web keeps the browser-download destination, desktop keeps the token-bound native save.

### Description of Relevance to Other Modules

| Module | Responsibility |
| --- | --- |
| `apps/desktop/src/views/ResearchPackage.tsx` | Scope form, counts table, size meter, export center, localized failures |
| `apps/desktop/src/views/SessionBar.tsx`, `Sidebar.tsx`, `App.tsx` | Entry point and panel wiring |
| `apps/desktop/src/styles/research-package.css`, `text/zh.ts`, `text/en.ts` | Layout and copy, both languages |
| `win_desktop` (`export-state.ts`, `preload.ts`, `main.ts`) | Persisted export list, destination tokens, reveal-in-folder |
| `services/api` (`research-snapshots.ts`) | Preview payload, counts, limit, archive size |
| `packages/research-package` | `MAX_TOTAL_BYTES`, manifest counts, omission strings |
| `apps/web` | Same view; parity required but not the focus |

### Test Design and Test Plan

- Component tests for the new blocks: counts table renders server counts; the size block shows both numbers and never labels the archive size as the estimate; an over-limit selection warns before `startExport` is called; cancel renders neutral; unknown server errors fall back to the raw string behind details.
- E2E on the desktop build with the real local stack, using a session that has evolve runs and scientific memory (the fixture from #1019):
  - 必要导出 and 完整导出 each round-trip to a saved `.sdresearch`, and the counts shown in the dialog match `POST .../inspect` of the produced package.
  - 完整导出 with both switches on the oversized session shows the pre-flight warning instead of a late English failure.
  - restart the app: the export list still shows the saved package and 打开文件位置 works.
  - cancel during packaging and during saving: neutral state, no error flash.
  - preview blocked (session with a stuck execution): the dialog explains the reason and offers retry/cancel.
- Import: inspect shows counts and the explicit not-restored list; compare against the live imported session.
- Commands: `pnpm --filter @sciencediscovery/desktop typecheck`, `pnpm --filter @sciencediscovery/desktop test`, `pnpm --filter @sciencediscovery/desktop build`, `pnpm ci:l1`. Screenshots of the export panel (necessary, complete with switches, over-limit warning, export list after restart) go in the PR body for the owner's visual approval, per the UI review rule.

### Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] The export scope step shows per-dimension counts for the selected profile, and the two optional switches show their effect on those counts and on size.
- [ ] The size block shows the uncompressed estimate and the archive size/limit distinctly; no single number is presented as the file the user will copy.
- [ ] A selection that cannot fit the archive limit is reported before packaging, with the fix offered on the card.
- [ ] Progress shows per-task state (packaging / saving) and destination; the export list survives closing the panel and restarting the app, and 打开文件位置 works for earlier packages.
- [ ] Cancelling a self-initiated export is neutral, not an error; known failures are localized with an actionable next step, raw text only behind details.
- [ ] A blocked preview names its cause and offers retry/cancel.
- [ ] Import inspection shows the same per-dimension counts and an explicit "will not be restored" list.
- [ ] Both zh-CN and en copy exist; `pnpm --filter @sciencediscovery/desktop typecheck|test|build` and `pnpm ci:l1` pass.
- [ ] The owner has seen the screenshots in the PR body before approval.

### Additional Information

Related: #803 (feature scope), #986 (save flow, closed by PR #999), #846 (localized, non-redundant failure presentation), #1018 (a session whose preview never settles — the blocked-state copy is a product decision there), #1019 (evolve runs absent from the package — the import "will not be restored" block must state it), #995 (import opens two sessions), #801 (desktop scientific memory), #798 (desktop evolve).

Measured numbers quoted above come from one real session on build `c95f080a`: 完整导出 preview 933,095,424 bytes uncompressed → saved archive 20,161,641 bytes; 完整导出 with both switches → `Research package exceeds the archive size limit`. The failure is not reproduced by any test in this issue description; it was observed by hand.
recent.title: [Feature]: Redesign the desktop session-export UI around scope, honest size and a durable export center

stale.author: hsliuustc0106
stale.body:
## Context

Since July 2026 an open-source "science workbench" category has formed, triggered by Anthropic's Claude Science launch (2026-06-30). Three direct open-source alternatives appeared the same week and are now at scale: [synthetic-sci/openscience](https://github.com/synthetic-sciences/openscience) (~3.6K★), [aipoch/open-science](https://github.com/aipoch/open-science) (~4.2K★), and [ai4s-research/open-science](https://github.com/ai4s-research/open-science) (~1.7K★). Having compared ScienceDiscovery against them (and against the autonomous-scientist systems: Sakana AI-Scientist, InternScience/InternAgent + MLEvolve), here is a strengths/gaps assessment in the hope it helps prioritization. Facts below are from public repo data collected 2026-09-15.

## Strengths (keep — and communicate)

1. **Sandbox-first security model.** Fail-closed Bubblewrap/Seatbelt execution, operator-scoped NPU chip passthrough, opt-in Broker with fixed entry points and `shell: false`. None of the three competitors communicates a default-isolation story; the highest-engagement technical question on a competitor's launch thread was literally *"are the skills executed within a secure, containerized sandbox by default, or does the user manage isolation?"* — this repo already answers that question, but almost nobody knows it does.
2. **Provenance depth.** CAS with pinned-asset drift rejection, review checks, cross-session/SubAgent citation chains. The strongest provenance story in the category.
3. **Search-camp RSI engine.** The evolve sidecar (flat-PUCT tree + OpenEvolve MAP-Elites, discriminability probe, explicit "no model training, no search-rule modification") is a clean, honest scope with a real cousin in [InternScience/MLEvolve](https://github.com/InternScience/MLEvolve) (#1 on MLE-Bench).
4. **Ascend NPU path.** 910B sandbox passthrough + allowlisted workloads (Protenix/MindScience) is unique in the category and extends machine-verifiable research to device-scale workloads.
5. **Engineering discipline beyond repo age.** Bilingual doc set, CI tiers (UT/ST/mocked E2E), self-documented limitations (e.g., Idea Tree scores are model judgments, not experimental evidence).

## Gaps (ordered by leverage)

1. **Installation/onboarding.** No binaries in Releases — #1 (open since 08-19, rated 1/5) is the only organic user feedback this repo has received, and it is someone who *could not install the product*. All three competitors ship desktop installers and a <10-minute quickstart. This pairs directly with the first-experience goal in #22.
2. **No community surface.** All merged PRs are bots; there are zero human external PRs. For comparison: aipoch merges 6+ human PRs/day; ai4s-research power users file bugs *and* land the fixes (e.g., their stall-guard for looping agents came from a user). A "good first issue" ladder + a contributor guide + weekly maintainer RFC triage would start the flywheel.
3. **Category invisibility + an unverifiable benchmark claim.** 58★ vs 1.7–4.2K for peers; one promotion event found (Sina Finance 2026-08-16) whose headline claim (BiomniBench-DA "业界SOTA") is dual-claimed by aipoch's README badge on the same benchmark. Without published methodology/splits, the claim reads as marketing and hurts credibility with scientists — either publish the eval or drop the superlative.
4. **Adoption levers validated by competitors, still missing here:** headless CLI / task API (repeated cross-repo demand — researchers want CI and agent-to-agent use, not only a GUI), model-provider onboarding (subscription reuse, connectivity-test friction), Windows parity.
5. **Cross-model skill consistency.** The single most-validated complaint in the category: *"one flag switches the model, not whether the skill actually works"* (prompts tuned on one model degrade on smaller/local models). A per-skill model-compatibility matrix or a cross-model smoke-test suite for the 300+ skills would directly differentiate.

## Suggested next steps

- [ ] Ship Linux binaries + a 10-minute quickstart (pairs with #22)
- [ ] Publish evolve/idea-tree efficiency metrics (per-node token cost, CAS reuse rate, surviving-node quality on an independent benchmark) — the pruning+reuse efficiency story is genuinely differentiating and no competitor tells it
- [ ] Benchmark-claim triage: methodology for BiomniBench-DA or remove the SOTA wording
- [ ] Community ladder: CONTRIBUTING good-first-issues + a maintainer-reserved RFC-triage day

Happy to help flesh any of these out.

items.author: yuanzhou75
items.body:
Closes #1109.

A Native run persisted **one** usage row, and its token fields were the **last main-agent turn**; the parent's other turns and every subagent turn never reached the ledger. Measured on the reported session: 5 runs, 599 per-turn figures, 5 rows, and 0.3796 % of the input the provider reported for the session.

## Owner

**PR-bot-2号** (`@yuanzhou75`). The account is shared by the team's Bots, so the author line cannot distinguish them; this line is for the ownership register.

## The shape this implements

The maintainer chose **one row per invocation, with subagents as their own rows**, and **no backfill of existing rows**. Both are recorded on the issue; this is what they mean in code.

| row | `invocationKind` | tokens | window |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| the run | `task` | the **sum** over the run's main-agent turns, with `turnsRecorded` | the run's manifest, as before |
| each delegated child | `delegation-track` (declared in `packages/schema/src/model-usage.ts` and, until now, written by nobody) | that child's own sum, with `turnsRecorded` | the child's `createdAt` → its `usage` event |

So a row's token figures now describe the same scope as its `startedAt`/`finishedAt`, which they did not before: the old row paired the whole run's window with a single turn's tokens.

## What changed

**`packages/runtime-core/src/runtime.ts`** — the loop emitted one figure per turn and kept only the last (`usage = modelTurn.usage`). It cannot add `TUsage` itself — the loop is generic and does not know the shape — so it takes an optional `accumulateUsage(previous, next)`. With it, `AgentLoopResult.usage` is the run's total and the result carries `turnsWithUsage`; without it, `usage` keeps its old meaning, so no other caller changes behaviour.

**`packages/model/src/usage.ts`** — `addUsage`, the shape-aware adder: counts add, and a field the provider never reports stays `null` rather than becoming `0`.

**`services/api/src/model-usage/index.ts`** — `addCapturedModelUsage` for the persisted shape (unknown stays unknown; a turn that reported nothing leaves the total untouched), `turnsRecorded` on the record, and `appendDelegatedModelUsage` for the child row with its own window.

**`services/api/src/runs/index.ts`** — the run collector's single overwritten slot becomes a running total plus `modelTurnsRecorded`; each `model_usage` is now also **published to the run's stream** (it used to be consumed and dropped by an early `return`, which is why no `model_usage` record existed in the capture); the three persistence sites pass `turnsRecorded`; each child's `usage` event writes its `delegation-track` row.

**`packages/schema/src/session.ts`** — `model.usage` as a run-stream event: per-turn figures are persisted so a stored row can be recomputed from the record directory alone (criterion 4).

## Consequences, stated rather than discovered later

- A run that delegates now contributes **1 + K rows** instead of 1, and the parent's row grows from one turn's worth to the run's total. `ModelUsageBucket.invocationCount` and per-run spend will step up accordingly — that is the point of the change, and it is why the numbers on any dashboard will look different after this lands.
- **No historical backfill** (the maintainer's decision): existing rows are left exactly as written. They are distinguishable because they carry no `turnsRecorded`. An audit reader can tell which shape a row came from.
- Nothing materialises zeros: a run with no completed model turn keeps `provider-not-reported` and null fields.

## Verification

- `packages/model/src/usage.test.ts` — a new case sums two turns (400/60/460 from 100+300, 20+40, 120+340) and asserts a never-reported field stays `null` and that the first turn is the total. **Mutation check:** replacing the summation with the last turn turns it red (`actual: 300, expected: 400`).
- `services/api/src/model-usage.test.ts` — sums turns into a run row, keeps `provider-not-reported` when no turn reported, and does not count an unreported turn as zero.
- Both files are tagged `os:linux`; I ran them with the tag relaxed to `os:windows` on this Windows host (14/14 and 25/25) and left the tag as committed.
- `tsc --noEmit` clean for `packages/runtime-core`, `packages/model`, `packages/schema`, `services/api` and `tsconfig.tests.json`.
- What I did not run: the full `runs/index.ts` suite and any real session. The row-per-invocation path is covered at the writer level; the end-to-end effect on a real delegated run is CI's and a live session's to show, and I am not claiming a measured reconciliation against provider invoices here.

## Not fixed here

The 128-turn ceiling that inflated this particular loss (four children cut at 128) is a separate finding with its own draft; `MAX_MODEL_TURNS` is untouched.
items.head: fix-1109-usage-per-invocation
items.title: fix(api): persist a run's summed usage and give delegated spend its own row

items.author: qingkwl
items.body:
Closes #264
Supersedes #285 (thanks @zy95-12 for the original work — the core of this PR is inherited from it, with `Co-authored-by` trailers preserved on the inherited commits)

## What this does

Takes over the remaining scope of #264 by inheriting the valuable parts of #285 (its author stopped development) and adding the unclaimed win_desktop increment.

### Inherited from #285 (cleanly applied, 46 files)

- **`packages/network`** (new, dependency-free): `resolveRoute` / `proxyProcessEnvironment` / `redactNetworkError` / `withProxyFetch` — manual redirect handling, HTTPS-downgrade refusal, cross-origin credential stripping, scoped undici Agent lifecycle
- **`services/api` proxy connectivity**: user-initiated diagnostic `POST /api/proxy/test` (HEAD probe to the micromamba release host, 10s timeout, redacted output)
- **`services/runner`**: `AsyncLocalStorage`-scoped per-operation proxy policy; subprocess environments built via `proxyProcessEnvironment` (micromamba/conda/pip children inherit the proxy instead of hanging on unreachable mirrors); setup errors redacted
- **`scripts/fetch-managed-micromamba.mjs`**: downloader defaults to `withProxyFetch` (fixes Node fetch ignoring proxy env) + `redactNetworkError`
- **data-source / model / executor**: `resolveRoute` delegation (net −21 lines in `env.ts`), proxy-aware transports
- **Web UI**: staged-draft editing for proxy settings (entries staged in the dialog, persisted on Save), URL redaction in list display, "Network and proxy" grouping, WebSearch single entry point
- **Docs** (en + zh): installation/preflight/recovery guidance for proxy environments
- **`test/journey-proxy-settings.spec.ts`**: user-perspective E2E journey

### New in this PR (win_desktop increment, the #264 gap #285 did not cover)

The Windows desktop shell previously skipped the registry's `socks=` entry when mirroring the system proxy ("v1: direct beats half-broken"). Both stack consumers now speak SOCKS5 natively — undici 8.12.2 `ProxyAgent` (verified end-to-end: SOCKS5 greeting on the wire) and `httpx[socks]` in the adapter — so the mirror is no longer half-broken:

- `socks=host:port` → `ALL_PROXY=socks5://host:port` (+ lowercase), per-scheme `http=`/`https=` entries still win for their schemes, loopback `NO_PROXY` bypass preserved in every mirrored form
- Docs updated (undici 8.9 → 8.12 note + Windows mirror behaviour)

### Conflict resolution vs main@b2a4906 (6 files, manual merge)

- `fetch-managed-micromamba.mjs`: kept main's newer `maxRetryDelayMs`/`sleep` retry parameters, threaded through the new `withProxyFetch` default
- `adapter/app.py`: `InternalClient` consolidation kept main's `legacy_limits` keepalive fix (Node idle-close race) — `InternalClient` gained a `limits` passthrough, guarded against passing an explicit `None` to httpx (its default is a live `Limits` object)
- `test/issue-143-proxy-settings.spec.ts`: adapted to the new labels/staged-draft flow while keeping main's E2E-META annotations and drawer handling
- `http/index.ts`, `environment-store.ts`, `api/package.json`: straightforward unions of both sides

## Testing (local, Windows)

| Suite | Result |
| --- | --- |
| win_desktop full suite | 223/223 |
| win_desktop proxy (flipped socks assertion + mixed-config case) | 7/7 |
| api server / store / proxy-connectivity | pass (server suite covers the new `/api/proxy/test` route) |
| runner environment-store / server | pass |
| data-source / model / executor / schema | pass |
| apps/web ProxySettingsEditor | pass |
| typecheck (api, runner, data-source, model, executor, web) | pass |
| adapter `test_network.py` via `uv run --extra test` | 9/9 (after the limits guard fix) |
| adapter full suite | 273 passed, 10 failed — all environmental on Windows (Unix `0o600` permission assertions, live gateway/LLM cases tagged `os="linux"`); unrelated to this change |

Not verifiable locally: the Linux CI matrix, the Playwright journeys (`@os:linux`), and Python-side integration — left for CI.

Desktop now opens model setup whenever the model catalog is empty, including after the last model is removed. New sessions and the first session of a new project automatically select a configured model so users can start without an additional selection step when the global task model is unset.

Model selection follows explicit user choice, project default, global task model, then the first model in the catalog's existing name order. A fallback is saved only on the new session and survives reloads and catalog reordering. Existing defaults, historical sessions, and recovery for explicitly selected deleted models retain their behavior.

## Validation

Rebased onto upstream `main` at `c3678320acb2ce31fc5390c640a1f6bf5e9f6bcd` without conflicts. Verified on head `c8ef27a10fd28835cb1c7ca817467d6a7b996367`, locally by Codex on Linux x64 with Node 22.19.0:

- Desktop bootstrap, model setup, and model refresh tests: **16 passed, 0 failed/skipped**.
- API model selection tests: **17 passed, 0 failed/skipped**, loading workspace sources through a temporary tsx path map.
- Desktop and API typechecks, the targeted API test typecheck, and `git diff --check upstream/main`: passed.

Full local suites, browser/E2E journeys, and native Windows/macOS validation were not run. Manual product verification remains for empty-catalog startup, removing the last model, completing setup, and creating sessions/projects with no global task model.

Fixes #1117: the `llm-wiki` bridge and its TypeScript connector rejected Wiki page paths using Windows `\` separators, so a `search` `page_id` could not be passed to `get_page`/`get_pages`, although the connector already folds `\`→`/` on results.

Development was requested with `bot-develop`. Goal: fold `\`→`/` once, before every existing check, at each layer's single path-validation entry point, weakening no rule.

- `services/gateway/src/sciencediscovery_gateway/llm_wiki_mcp.py`: new `_fold_separators`; `_page_path` folds before the length/char/segment checks, so both tools share one rule. `get_pages` builds that list once and uses it for the request body and the `omitted_paths` comparison, and compares the provider's `pages[].path`/`missing[]` in the same folded form, so an echo of the Windows spelling is not reported as omitted.
- `packages/mcp-sources/src/llm-wiki.ts`: new `normalizePagePath`; `isPagePath` folds before validating and `validateInput` returns the folded `path`/`paths`, so the broker's forwarded body, cache key and permission strings see one spelling.
- Still refused: `.`/`..`/empty segments, absolute and drive-letter paths, `%?#:`, control characters, empty and over-500-character inputs.

Tests: the backslash-rejection case became acceptance in both suites, plus search→`get_page`+`get_pages` round trips with verbatim Windows `page_id`s, a provider-echo case and an accept/refuse parity table. Reverting the source fix fails the new tests.

- `pnpm gateway:test` → Ran 58 tests, OK
- `pnpm --filter @sciencediscovery/mcp-sources test` → 30 pass, 0 fail; typecheck and test typecheck clean
- `pnpm ci:l1` → planned 4, passed 4
- `pnpm --filter @sciencediscovery/api test` → 2324 pass, 14 fail, all environmental (no bwrap, no `services/paper/.venv`, real provider CLIs); its mcp/broker files pass 9/9

Risk: `pnpm ci:ut`/`ci:st` stop at preflight with `BUBBLEWRAP_UNAVAILABLE` here, so those layers need CI. No unrelated changes.

items.author: yuanzhou75
items.body:
Closes #1108.

`check_runner` used to answer a question the Agent had not asked: the tool binding dropped the route (`workspace-bindings.ts:416`), so an Agent got the Python-channel verdict (`requiresShell = false`, `:196`) whatever it was about to run — and the Runner's own payload fixed `ready: true, reason: "ready"` on the `sandbox === "none"` branch (`readiness.ts:42-47`) even when the probe beside it said `shell.available: false`. This makes the verdict route-scoped structurally, per the maintainer's choice of §2 option 2.


## The contract

`RunnerExecutionCapability` gains an optional `readyFor: { python: boolean; shell: boolean }`, and `reason` gains `"shell-unavailable"`:

| field | meaning |
| --- | --- |
| `ready` | unchanged: the Python channel (a Shell gap never blocks it — PR #716's design is kept) |
| `reason` | derived from the probe on the `none` branch instead of fixed at `"ready"`; says `"shell-unavailable"` when the managed Shell is dead |
| `readyFor.python` | sandbox and dependency usable, Shell plays no part |
| `readyFor.shell` | `python` **and** the managed Shell usable; an absent `shell` field stays unknown, not false |

`check_runner`'s result now carries the same `readyFor`, and its headline `reason` is never the bare word `"ready"` while the same object reports a dead Shell. The parameter schema did **not** grow a route option: no new caller knowledge, and no new probe — `shellCapability()` already ran in the same probe, the answer was just discarded.

## What changed, file by file

- `packages/schema/src/environment.ts` — `readyFor` on `RunnerExecutionCapability`, `"shell-unavailable"` in the `reason` union, `readyFor` mirrored on `RunnerCheckResult`. Optional, because an older Runner cannot report it (same treatment as `shell?`).
- `services/runner/src/readiness.ts` — the `none` branch derives `reason`/`readyFor` from the probe; the sandboxed branch reports `readyFor` from its own sandbox verdict; the initial `report` literal carries `{python: false, shell: false}`.
- `services/api/src/agent-run/workspace-bindings.ts` — `checkRunner` computes both routes from `readyFor` when present and falls back to `ready` + `shell.available` for an older Runner; a Shell caller gets the Shell verdict and its real reason.
- `services/runner/src/server.ts` — startup now warns when the managed Shell is dead. The existing `if (!capability.ready)` could never fire on that branch, which is why the 10-hour capture in the issue produced no startup complaint.
- `services/runner/src/environment-store.ts` — the provisioning transcript is bounded (1200 chars + a pointer to the Runner log) so one failure does not put a 14 KB libmamba dump into a model result.
- `services/api/src/agent-run/workspace-bindings.ts` — the advice no longer repeats that transcript (it was in `capability.detail`, `capability.shell.unavailableReason` **and** `suggestions[0]`), and the `wait_for_runner` cancel branch no longer sends the caller to `check_runner` to recheck a blocker the check could not report.
- `packages/workspace/src/workspace.ts` — the tool description says what `ready` covers and to read the route you intend to use.

## Verification

- `services/api/src/agent-run/workspace-bindings.test.ts` — new case drives the **tool-facing binding** (`runnerReadiness.check`, which is what `check_runner` calls) with `{ready: true, reason: "shell-unavailable", readyFor: {python: true, shell: false}}` and asserts: the model-visible JSON carries `readyFor` naming both routes, `reason` is not `"ready"`, `capability.reason` is `"shell-unavailable"`, and the advice does not repeat the transcript. It also pins that the binding takes only two parameters — the reason the verdict has to be structural rather than something a caller passes in.
- `services/runner/src/readiness.test.ts` — the `none` branch now asserts `reason: "shell-unavailable"` and `readyFor: {python: true, shell: false}` while `ready` stays `true`; the repaired probe asserts `{python: true, shell: true}`; the no-probe case asserts `{python: true, shell: true}` with `shell` still absent (unknown ≠ unavailable).
- Mutation check: putting `reason` back to the literal `"ready"` turns the runner case red.
- Direct probe on this head with `shellProbe → available: false`: `{ready: true, reason: "shell-unavailable", readyFor: {python: true, shell: false}}`; with `available: true`: `{ready: true, reason: "ready", readyFor: {python: true, shell: true}}`.
- `tsc --noEmit` clean for `packages/schema`, `packages/workspace`, `services/runner`, `services/api` and `tsconfig.tests.json`.
- **`services/runner/src/readiness.test.ts` cannot run on this machine (POSIX dependency)** — its bubblewrap/seatbelt cases spawn a shell script, one asserts `platform === "linux"`, and several remove a temp directory that SQLite still holds on Windows. Its result here is therefore not a verdict on this change either way, and **CI covers it**. The route-scoped assertions I added are independently evidenced by the direct probe above and by the API-side case. The same host limitation makes 3 cleanup cases in `workspace-bindings.test.ts` fail with `EBUSY`, before and after this change alike.

## Not changed on purpose

- Python execution is never blocked by a Shell gap (criterion 9): `ready` keeps the Python meaning and `prepareExecutionTarget(..., requiresShell = false)` still reads it.
- An absent `shell` field still means "unknown", not "unavailable".
- The `RUNNER_UNAVAILABLE` repair instruction and the `wait_for_runner` card delivered by #1095 and #265 are unchanged; only the cancel branch's closing sentence changed, as criterion 7 asks.
items.head: fix-1108-route-scoped-readiness
items.title: fix(runner): make the readiness verdict route-scoped so check_runner cannot contradict run_shell

items.author: yuanzhou75
items.body:
Closes #1081

## What was wrong

Readiness was configuration-only. `statusFor()` (`packages/data-source/src/catalog.ts`) compares the tools an MCP server advertises with the manifests and never asks a provider anything, so a connector whose every call failed still read `ready`. The only way anyone learned an integration was down was an agent that called it and reported the `UPSTREAM_UNAVAILABLE` guidance back — which is how #1049 was found, and what §10 of that issue repeats. (The issue names `services/api/src/plugins/catalog.ts`; readiness actually lives in `packages/data-source/src/catalog.ts`.)

## Change

**A memory of provider outages** (`packages/data-source/src/source-outage.ts`)

The broker records the last provider-level failure per source and the catalog reports it beside the status it already computes.

**The predicate is the reviewer's — provider-level only.** `recordedOutage` judges the attempt the way admission does: a declared endpoint scope (`failureScope === "endpoint"`), or a `transport-error` / `server-error`. Nothing else is recorded. This matters because `upstreamError()` falls back to `UPSTREAM_UNAVAILABLE` for any attempt status it does not map, and the node client classifies a tool-reported `isError` as `semantic-error` — so an invalid query or a DOI the provider cannot resolve used to record a ten-minute outage and render `Last upstream outage: SEMANTIC_ERROR`. `SourceHealth` already treats those as request-specific; readiness no longer contradicts it.

**The endpoint code is preserved.** A declared endpoint scope is recorded as `ENDPOINT_UNAVAILABLE`, not as the tool-level `SEMANTIC_ERROR` it used to inherit. That is the one endpoint-level signal that exists today (the 406 refusal in `http_errors.py`), and it stays distinguishable from a request-scoped rejection. A transport/server failure records `UPSTREAM_UNAVAILABLE`.

**Advisory by construction.** `getStatus()` attaches `lastOutage` and changes nothing else: `status`, `error` and `missingTools` are exactly what configuration says. That is deliberate — `status !== "ready"` is a gate at three call sites (`http/index.ts:3133`, `:3172`, `:4704`), so a signal that flipped it would disable a working-but-flaky connector on a transient error. The record expires after ten minutes, which is unrelated to the broker's 30–120 s cooling windows: cooling governs admission, this only governs what readiness says.

**One explicit instance.** The bootstrap constructs a single `SourceOutages` and passes it to both the catalog and the broker, instead of the two sides reaching the same module-level default by accident.

**Visible where a maintainer looks** (`packages/mcp/src/connector-picker.tsx`, `apps/web/src/i18n/messages.ts`, `apps/web/src/styles/conversation.css`)

The composer's connector picker draws the line next to the readiness line it already has, in both locales, and takes the recorded provider message as its tooltip rather than shipping `detail` unused. It now has its own rule: without one it inherited `label small` (`nowrap` + `ellipsis`), so the sentence was clipped at the popover's 340 px width in the muted colour instead of the warning colour. It reuses the theme variable and the same treatment as `.connector-picker-status`.

## Screenshots

Real component (`renderToStaticMarkup`), with the real stylesheet inlined (`apps/web/src/styles/{tokens,base,primitives,conversation}.css`) and the popover rendered open in both locales. The Chinese line is the long one — `最近一次上游故障：ENDPOINT_UNAVAILABLE（2026/11/11 21:00:00）` — and it wraps onto two lines rather than truncating, in the warning colour.

![Recorded upstream outage shown in the connector picker, zh-CN and en](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/yuanzhou75/sciencediscovery/screenshots-1081/docs/screenshots/1081/connector-picker-last-outage.png)

Not an Electron window and not a live app session: this is renderer-level, which is what the change is. Stated so it is not read as more than it is.

## Tests

`packages/data-source/src/source-outage.test.ts`:

- the record survives to the last second of the window and is forgotten after it, per source;
- `getStatus` returns the outage **and** `status: "ready"` unchanged, with `availableTools` untouched;
- **new** — a tool-level rejection, a rate limit, a broker cooldown and a record-scoped 404 record **nothing**;
- **new** — a transport failure records `UPSTREAM_UNAVAILABLE`; a 406 endpoint refusal records `ENDPOINT_UNAVAILABLE` with the provider's message, and is what `getStatus` then reports.

`apps/web/tests/ConnectorPicker.test.tsx`: a `ready` connector with a recorded outage renders the line, and the status is asserted to stay `ready`.

## Verification

- `tsc --noEmit` clean for `packages/schema`, `packages/data-source`, `packages/mcp`, against the exact files this PR pushes.
- `source-outage.test.ts`: **4/4**. The suite declares `os:linux`, so the tagged collector no-ops on this Windows host; I ran the same file with the platform forced to the declared one.
- `services/api`: one error remains, `platform.ts(495) readText not in ProposalDeps`. It is a stale-checkout artifact, not this change: the same error is produced by `main`'s `platform.ts` with my three lines stripped, and none of them touch that line. CI is authoritative for that package.
- `apps/web` type-check is not usable as evidence here either (pre-existing errors from the older checkout); the picker compiles clean in `packages/mcp` and the change is one rule plus three attributes.
