recent.author: JinhZhao
recent.body:
### 1. Summary

On a **native Windows** deployment (host processes, no Docker/WSL), the Runner's managed scientific
environment never becomes usable. The micromamba provisioning run that builds `starter-python` fails
inside the **shared package cache**, and the failure is a path-length failure, not a download or a
disk failure:

* libmamba reports individual files inside extracted cache entries as `... is missing`;
* those files **are not missing** — they exist and are reachable through an extended-length (`\\?\`)
  path, and only unreachable through a normal Windows path;
* libmamba then declares the entry an invalid cache, tries to delete and re-extract it, and
  `remove_all: The directory is not empty.` fires because the delete step hits the same length limit;
* the entry is left with its `info\` directory gone, which is the condition under which conda
  considers a cache entry permanently unusable, and nothing in the Runner resets that shared cache.

Net effect: `scientificEnvs.available = false`, `shell.available = false`, and every `run_shell` call
returns `RUNNER_UNAVAILABLE`. The instance cannot heal itself by restarting, and the damaged set grew
from 1 entry to 6 across two provisioning passes over the same cache.

### 2. Environment

| item | value |
| --- | --- |
| OS | Windows 11, build 22631, x64 |
| Deployment | native Windows local stack (API, Runner, Evolve, Memory Graph as host processes) |
| Long-path policy | `HKLM\SYSTEM\CurrentControlSet\Control\FileSystem\LongPathsEnabled` = `0x0` (REG_DWORD, read with PowerShell `Get-ItemProperty`; not modified for this report) |
| Provisioner | micromamba pinned by this repo: `services/runner/src/micromamba-releases.json` -> `"version": "2.8.1-0"`, `win-64` binary, 11 311 104 bytes |
| Provisioner manifest | the binary contains the `longPathAware` manifest declaration (2 string hits), which is inert while the system policy is `0` |
| Runner self-report | `/health` -> `platform=win32`, `status=ok`, `runnerVersion=0f1ff6de` (build id of a downstream fork of `main`) |
| Node.js | v22.23.4, read from the executable the Runner process is actually running |
| Cache layout | `<DATA_DIR>` (58 characters on this machine) -> `<DATA_DIR>\scientific-envs\provisioner\pkgs` (91 characters) -> `<...>\pkgs\https\conda.anaconda.org\conda-forge\win-64` (**135 characters**) |

The command the Runner runs, as echoed back by its own failure payload (only the prefix path is
ours, the argv is the product's):

```
micromamba.exe --no-rc create --yes --strict-channel-priority --override-channels
  --prefix <DATA_DIR>\scientific-envs\revisions\starter-python\rev-<uuid>
  --channel conda-forge python=3.12 numpy=2.0 pandas=2.2 scipy=1.14
  matplotlib-base=3.9 m2-bash m2-coreutils m2-grep m2-sed
```

### 3. Observed Evidence

#### 3.1 Path-length census over the whole cache tree

Method: walk the cache with an extended-length root, then re-`stat` every file through its plain
path. Nothing was deleted, moved or rewritten.

| measure | result |
| --- | --- |
| files in the cache tree | 15 024 |
| files whose plain path length is greater than 260 | 103 |
| files whose plain path `stat()` fails | **125** |
| of the failures, files at exactly 260 characters | 22 |
| files at 259 characters or shorter that fail | **0** |
| longest plain path that still resolves | 259 |
| directories unreachable by plain `stat` | 0 |
| deepest file in the tree | 143-character relative tail (`matplotlib-base` entry), plain absolute path 278 characters |
| budget arithmetic | 135 (channel directory) + 143 (deepest tail) = 278; keeping every entry addressable needs the channel directory at or below **116** characters |

The two counts (103 and 125) differ by exactly the 22 files sitting at 260 characters, so the
effective ceiling is **259**: the documented 260 includes the terminating NUL. 125 is the damaged set;
103 is what a strict "longer than 260" filter reports, and both are quoted where they differ.

#### 3.2 The six files reported as "missing" exist

Each entry below is one file inside a cache entry, checked by extended-length path and by plain path.

| cache entry | file reported missing | plain path length | exists | reachable by plain path |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `fonttools-4.68.0-py312h05f76fc_0` | `varLib\__pycache__\interpolatableTestContourOrder.cpython-312.pyc` | 262 | yes | no |
| `libhwloc-2.15.0-default_hae90fe0_1001` | `Library\share\man\man3\hwloc_obj_attr_u_hwloc_numanode_attr_s_hwloc_memory_page_type_s.3` | 262 | yes | no |
| `matplotlib-base-3.9.4-py312h90004f6_0` | `backends\qt_editor\__pycache__\_formlayout.cpython-312.pyc` | 261 | yes | no |
| `numpy-2.0.2-py312h49bc9c5_1` | `_core\tests\__pycache__\test_casting_floatingpoint_errors.cpython-312.pyc` | 261 | yes | no |
| `pandas-2.2.3-py312h72972c8_3` | `core\array_algos\__pycache__\datetimelike_accumulations.cpython-312.pyc` | 261 | yes | no |
| `scipy-1.14.1-py312h337df96_2` | `optimize\_trustregion_constr\__pycache__\canonical_constraint.cpython-312.pyc` | 266 | yes | no |

So the correct statement is: **inaccessible through a normal Windows path, present on disk.** These
are not lost files and the archives themselves are intact (80 `.conda` archives still present,
55 under `win-64` and 25 under `noarch`; no partial-download markers anywhere).

Resulting cache state, 81 extracted entries (56 `win-64` + 25 `noarch`):

* exactly **6** entries now lack `info\` — the same six as the table above, all with the same
  directory mtime (14:41:58 of the same day);
* all 25 `noarch` entries still have `info\index.json`;
* entries that also contain over-long files but survived: `libpython` (5 files), `libwinpthread` (1),
  `m2-filesystem` (1), plus 260-character-only cases in `python` (3) and `m2-msys2-runtime` (1);
* `matplotlib-base` is the one gutted entry that also lost its `.conda` archive, which is why it is
  the entry the final `critical` line names.

#### 3.3 The messages, verbatim

First provisioning pass, one entry flagged (`<CACHE>` stands for the 135-character channel directory):

```
warning  libmamba Invalid package cache, file '<CACHE>\libhwloc-2.15.0-default_hae90fe0_1001\Library\share\man\man3\hwloc_obj_attr_u_hwloc_numanode_attr_s_hwloc_memory_page_type_s.3' is missing
error    libmamba Cannot find a valid extracted directory cache for 'libhwloc-2.15.0-default_hae90fe0_1001.conda'
critical libmamba Package cache error.
```

Second provisioning pass, same cache, now six entries flagged, each immediately followed by a failed
delete-and-re-extract:

```
warning  libmamba Invalid package cache, file '<CACHE>\<entry>\<over-long file>' is missing     (x6, alphabetical entry order)
error    libmamba Error when extracting package: remove_all: The directory is not empty.: "<CACHE>\matplotlib-base-3.9.4-py312h90004f6_0"
error    libmamba Error when extracting package: remove_all: The directory is not empty.: "<CACHE>\pandas-2.2.3-py312h72972c8_3"
error    libmamba Error when extracting package: remove_all: The directory is not empty.: "<CACHE>\numpy-2.0.2-py312h49bc9c5_1"
error    libmamba Error when extracting package: remove_all: The directory is not empty.: "<CACHE>\scipy-1.14.1-py312h337df96_2"
error    libmamba Error when extracting package: remove_all: The directory is not empty.: "<CACHE>\libhwloc-2.15.0-default_hae90fe0_1001"
error    libmamba Error when extracting package: remove_all: The directory is not empty.: "<CACHE>\fonttools-4.68.0-py312h05f76fc_0"
critical libmamba remove_all: The directory is not empty.: "<CACHE>\matplotlib-base-3.9.4-py312h90004f6_0"
```

Two things follow from this transcript. The flagged set went from 1 entry to 6 over the *same* cache,
so which entry dies depends on scan order rather than on a fixed rule - the remaining deep-path
packages can be added on a later pass. And the earlier `Failed to load shard for package 'libgdal-*'
... will download` warnings are cold-cache noise: they are self-resolving, and extraction succeeded
after them.

#### 3.4 Runner state that results from it

* `/health` (Runner) and `/api/health` (API) both report `scientificEnvs` with `available=false`,
  `enabled=true`, `startersReady=false`, `provisioner=null`, `languages=[]`, and `unavailableReason`
  carrying the full transcript above; `revisions\` ends up holding no environment at all.
* In the captured run history we hold for one session, **11** `run_shell` tool results carry
  `{"code":"RUNNER_UNAVAILABLE","dispatched":false, ... }`.
* Capability probes return `shell.available=false` while the top-level `runner.status` still reads
  `ok` - the gap is only visible in the payload, never in the headline status.
* The bootstrap is fire-and-forget: a failed `setupManagedEnvironments()` logs one `WARN`
  (`server.ts:1300-1301`) and the service continues to report itself healthy.
* The user-visible cost is not an error dialog: each shell request parks for about 10 minutes in
  `wait_for_runner` and then hands the whole micromamba transcript to the agent as its "reason".

#### 3.5 Secondary: the failure is also hard to see in the logs

Not the cause, recorded because it cost us two rounds of diagnosis. `shortErrorMessage()`
(`packages/operational-logging/src/redaction.ts:40-42`) front-slices at 500 characters. The two
`runner.log` bootstrap-failure lines unescape to exactly 500 characters: 448 of them are the echoed
command line, leaving 52 characters of actual child-process stderr, so in `runner.log` the first
failing package name is simply absent. The untruncated copies exist only in `api.log`
(2 936 and 8 698 characters).

### 4. Controlled Experiment

#### 4.1 Reproduction recipe

1. Windows host, `LongPathsEnabled = 0`, native (non-Docker, non-WSL) stack.
2. Put the instance data directory at a realistic depth. The channel directory is the data directory
   plus 77 characters (`\scientific-envs\provisioner\pkgs\https\conda.anaconda.org\conda-forge\win-64`)
   and the deepest tail this package set creates is 143 characters, so a data directory of **40
   characters or more** is already enough to push an entry to 260 and out of reach (40 + 77 + 143 =
   260). Ours is 58.
3. Start the Runner so that it bootstraps `starter-python` with the default package set.
4. Observe: the messages in 3.3, `scientificEnvs.available=false`, and, in the cache tree, entries
   that have no `info\index.json` while still containing files whose plain path is 260 characters or
   longer.

#### 4.2 The comparison arm

Same micromamba binary, same `win-64` package set, same long target prefix (109 characters). The
only variable changed: the **package cache root** was pointed at a 10-character directory through the
mechanism `SCIENCE_AGENT_PACKAGE_CACHE_DIR` feeds (`CONDA_PKGS_DIRS` plus `--offline`). The long-path
registry policy stayed at `0` in both arms.

| measure | long cache root (production argv) | short cache root (arm B) |
| --- | --- | --- |
| exit code | `Command failed` (non-zero) | `0`, 29.6 s, 195 output lines |
| `Invalid package cache` lines | 6 | 0 |
| lines containing `remove_all: The directory is not empty` | 7 (6 `error` + 1 `critical`) | 0 |
| `warning` / `error` / `critical` lines | 6 / 6 / 1 | 0 / 0 / 0 |
| network use | downloads required - three packages announced `will download`, and the cache's 56 package directories were written in one contiguous 38-second window | `Total download: 0 B`, `will download` 0 times |
| environment produced | none to measure - `revisions\` holds no directory, because each failed attempt removes its own revision | 16 847 files, all 81 packages of the spec linked, **0** files unreachable by plain `stat`, deepest path 220 characters |
| real computation through it | not possible | `rc=0`, 2 550 ms, empty stderr, python 3.12.16 + matplotlib 3.9.4 (Agg), PNG 6 165 bytes, CSV 272 bytes |

What this establishes: the packages, the solver and the disk are fine, and moving **only** the cache
to a short root makes the identical provisioning succeed. What it does not establish is listed in
section 10.

### 5. Expected Behavior

1. Before provisioning, the Runner should know its path budget. The cache root is derived as
   `<dataDir>\scientific-envs\provisioner\pkgs`; the channel subdirectory is already 135 characters
   on this machine, and the deepest entry path this package set creates is 143 characters, so the
   channel directory has to stay at or under 116 characters for the entries to remain addressable. A
   length pre-flight (root length plus the expected tail) would catch this before micromamba runs.
2. If the budget cannot be met, fail fast with an explicit compatibility diagnostic that prints the
   offending root, its length, the platform's long-path state and the supported remedy - instead of
   letting a package manager report individual files as missing.
3. The cache location should be short and stable by default on Windows (a machine-level short root,
   or `SCIENCE_AGENT_PACKAGE_CACHE_DIR` honoured by default rather than only when explicitly set),
   rather than inheriting an arbitrarily deep per-instance data directory.
4. Cache validation and cache removal should use the same long-path-aware access that the rest of a
   Windows deployment needs (`\\?\` / `path.toNamespacedPath`, the pattern already used in
   `packages/cas`), so that a file libmamba just wrote cannot become invisible to libmamba one step
   later.
5. A path-length condition must not be reported as "file is missing" or as a generic
   `Package cache error`. As written, the message tells the operator that the package cache is
   corrupt, which invites exactly the wrong remedy (wipe the cache and re-download, which reproduces
   the same state).
6. After an entry is invalidated in the shared cache, the Runner should be able to recover it, or
   stop using it. Today the failure path removes only the per-attempt
   `revisions/<env>` directory (`environment-store.ts:924`) and never the shared entries, and the next
   start repeats the identical `create` against that cache, so every bootstrap re-reads the same
   poisoned entries.

### 6. Actual Behavior

* Provisioning fails, first with `Invalid package cache ... is missing` and
  `Cannot find a valid extracted directory cache`, then with `remove_all: The directory is not empty`
  and `critical libmamba ...`, and the shared cache ends up with 6 unusable entries.
* The state is stable across restarts: the entries keep their gutted form, `revisions\` stays empty,
  and a second pass flags more entries than the first.
* `scientificEnvs.available=false`, `startersReady=false`, `shell.available=false`;
  `run_shell` returns `RUNNER_UNAVAILABLE` with `dispatched=false`, so no shell or Python step can
  execute for the whole instance.
* `runner.status` still says `ok`, and the only log line about it is one `WARN` whose message is
  truncated to 500 characters, so neither the UI nor `runner.log` states that the scientific
  environment is dead.
* The guidance the failure itself returns points at a remedy that cannot work against this cause:
  `Recreate or update the starter environment on the target Runner to repair managed Bash and its
  required utilities.` Re-creating the environment re-reads the same poisoned shared cache; that is
  exactly what happened here, where a later pass flagged five more entries than the first one did.

### 7. Questions for Maintainers

1. Is native Windows (host processes, no Docker/WSL) a supported runtime mode for the Runner? The
   install and quick-start documentation is what we followed; nothing in it states a path-length
   requirement for the data directory.
2. If it is not supported, should the launcher detect the platform and refuse with a clear message
   at startup, instead of booting and reporting `status=ok` while `shell.available=false`?
3. If it is supported, which fix do you prefer: (a) a short machine-level default cache root, or
   honouring `SCIENCE_AGENT_PACKAGE_CACHE_DIR` by default on Windows; (b) long-path-aware validation
   and removal of cache entries; (c) a pre-flight length check plus an explicit compatibility
   diagnostic; or a combination?
4. Could CI gain a provisioning regression test whose cache entries sit at **259, 260 and 261+**
   characters, covering create, extract, and the cleanup/`remove_all` path? The 259/260 boundary is
   where our damaged set changes character, and it is the case a "just below MAX_PATH" test misses.
5. `services/runner/src/platform/win32.ts:117-128` already substitutes `matplotlib-base` for
   `matplotlib` precisely because the qt6 tree exceeds MAX_PATH. Our data says that substitution is
   necessary but not sufficient: `matplotlib-base-3.9.4` is itself one of the six gutted entries,
   because its own `Lib\site-packages\...\__pycache__` test artefacts reach 260+ characters. Should
   the starter set be screened by measured depth rather than by known-bad package names?
6. Should an entry invalidated in the shared cache be reset automatically (with an audit record),
   given that the instance cannot recover by restarting?

### 8. Scope

This report is about **Windows native Runner environment provisioning** and its package cache.
Deliberately excluded, each with its own report: agent output truncation, MCP connector bookkeeping,
Memory Graph behaviour, and usage accounting. The 500-character log slicing in 3.5 is mentioned only
because it hides this particular error, not as a logging proposal.

### 9. Source-code references (checked against the current `main`)

* `services/runner/src/environment-store.ts:389` - `MAMBA_ROOT_PREFIX: resolve(config.root,
  "provisioner")`, which is what ties the cache to the per-instance data directory.
* `services/runner/src/environment-store.ts:390` - `CONDA_PKGS_DIRS` is exported only when
  `config.packageCacheDir` is set; `:1104-1105` - `--offline` likewise.
* `services/runner/src/environment-store.ts:540` - the only pre-flight on the cache directory is an
  existence check (`await access(...)`); there is no length check, and no `MAX_PATH`, `\\?\` or
  `toNamespacedPath` token appears anywhere in this file.
* `services/runner/src/environment-store.ts:906` and `:924` - `bootstrapStarter()` create arguments,
  and the failure path that removes only `revisions/<id>`.
* `services/runner/src/server.ts:397-398` - `SCIENCE_AGENT_PACKAGE_CACHE_DIR` is the sole override.
* `services/runner/src/server.ts:1300-1301` - `void setupManagedEnvironments().catch(...)`, one
  `WARN` on failure.
* `services/runner/src/platform/win32.ts:117-128` and `services/runner/src/platform/types.ts:80-86` -
  the existing MAX_PATH note for this starter package set.
* `services/runner/src/micromamba-releases.json:2` - the pinned provisioner version.
* `packages/operational-logging/src/redaction.ts:16` and `:40-42` - the 500-character front-slice.

### 10. What this report does not establish

* **Mechanism granularity.** That micromamba validates and deletes cache entries through
  non-extended-length paths is inferred from the message text plus the resulting on-disk state (which
  files remain, which disappear, in what order), not from libmamba's source, which is a binary here.
  The observable facts in 3 are independent of that inference.
* **`LongPathsEnabled = 1` was not tested.** Changing the registry was outside the authorised scope,
  so we cannot claim that enabling the policy would fix it; the `longPathAware` declaration in the
  binary is inert while the policy is off, and we did not verify per-call behaviour with the policy
  on.
* **Concurrency is excluded as the cause of the damage in our instance**, but for a narrower reason
  than "locks exist": downloads and extraction all fall inside one runner generation's window
  (monotone, 09:00:07-09:00:45), the previous generation had only fetched repodata,
  `enqueueMutation()` serialises mutations in-process, no second `scientific-envs` tree exists on
  this machine, and `SCIENCE_AGENT_PACKAGE_CACHE_DIR` was unset so no cache is shared between
  instances. There is **no cross-process lock** around the package cache; two Runners configured with
  the same cache root could race. We report that as a structural risk, not as part of this failure.
* **The comparison arm in 4.2 bypassed the service.** It ran micromamba directly with the equivalent
  argv; configuring `SCIENCE_AGENT_PACKAGE_CACHE_DIR` in the launcher and restarting was not
  authorised. `Total download: 0 B` also does not prove the offline seed fully served the solve, and
  `--offline` pins the package set to what was seeded, so packages beyond this spec would need the
  seed to cover them too.
* **Sample size.** Two provisioning passes in one instance, one session's run history, and the six
  entries named above. We did not survey other Windows hosts.
* **The earlier Docker observation is a user-provided history, not evidence.** Running the same
  product under Docker worked, as reported by the operator, but we have not run a same-SHA,
  same-configuration controlled comparison, so we explicitly do **not** present "Docker works" as a
  proven cause-or-cure for anything in this report.

### 11. Related items and prior search

Searched the tracker before filing, over open and closed issues, for `MAX_PATH`, `micromamba`,
`LongPathsEnabled`, `Package cache error`, `CONDA_PKGS_DIRS`, `remove_all`, `longPathAware`,
`Windows provisioning` and `scientific environment bootstrap`. No existing item covers this defect;
`LongPathsEnabled`, `CONDA_PKGS_DIRS`, `remove_all` and `longPathAware` each return zero results. The
nearest items, all distinct from this one:

* #643 - Windows runtime: native startup chain, execution routing, micromamba environments (closed) -
  the feature this report is about.
* #916 - Windows managed Shell missing base Unix tools and a diagnosable capability declaration
  (closed) - adjacent, different defect: tools absent in a *successfully created* environment.
* #583 - CAS: Windows durable-directory sync with `toNamespacedPath` (closed) - precedent that the
  long-path namespace treatment is already applied elsewhere in this project.

### 12. References

* Installation (docs site we followed): https://sciencediscovery.github.io/zh/install/index.html
* Quick start: https://sciencediscovery.github.io/zh/docs/getting-started/quick-start.html
* Mamba troubleshooting, which documents the same class of Windows path problem:
  https://mamba.readthedocs.io/en/latest/user_guide/troubleshooting.html
* Windows path limits (the 260 value that includes the terminating NUL, and the `\\?\` prefix):
  https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/windows/win32/fileio/naming-a-file
recent.title: [Windows Compatibility] Native Windows Runner provisioning fails with micromamba MAX_PATH limitations

recent.author: JinhZhao
recent.body:
## 1. Actual behaviour

The Native agent loop emits a usage figure after **every** model turn, and each of those figures is written into the run's persisted record stream. The usage ledger receives **one row per run**, and the token fields of that row are the **last main-agent turn only**.

Measured on one captured session (5 runs, 599 per-turn usage records, 5 ledger rows):

| run | ledger rows | main turns with usage | subagent streams | subagent turns with usage | sum of per-turn input tokens, all streams | input tokens in the ledger row | persisted share |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| `9ceeb1f9` | 1 | 20 | 5 | 572 | 24,023,894 | 44,952 | 0.1871 % |
| `0673152f` | 1 | 7 | 0 | 0 | 300,115 | 47,387 | 15.7896 % |
| `82036958` | 1 | 0 | 0 | 0 | 0 | `null` | n/a — no model turn ran |
| `116b288e` | 1 | 0 | 0 | 0 | 0 | `null` | n/a — no model turn ran |
| `de7527c9` | 1 | 0 | 0 | 0 | 0 | `null` | n/a — no model turn ran |

Session totals: ledger holds 92,339 input / 12,737 output / 6,592 reasoning / 7,168 cache-read tokens; the same session's streams hold 24,324,009 input / 526,865 output / 404,221 reasoning / 13,340,032 cache-read tokens. **0.3796 % of the input the provider reported for the session is in the ledger.**

Four separate things go wrong, and they compound:

1. **A per-run row carries a per-turn number.** In both runs that have tokens, the row equals one specific turn record byte-for-byte and equals no sum: the matching turn is main turn index 19 of 20 for `9ceeb1f9`, main turn index 6 of 7 for `0673152f` — i.e. the last main turn in each case.
2. **Subagent turns contribute nothing.** `9ceeb1f9` ran 5 children over 572 model turns (5,297,320 + 5,055,291 + 5,267,215 + 5,188,821 + 2,398,037 input tokens) and the ledger has 0 rows for them. 96.62 % of that run's per-turn records belong to children. No `invocationKind` exists for them, and the one `subagent.usage` event per child carries that child's *last* turn, never its sum.
3. **The row's time window and its token figures describe different scopes.** `startedAt`/`finishedAt` come from the prompt manifest (the whole run) while the tokens come from one turn: `9ceeb1f9`'s row spans 2 h 50 min 59 s (02:27:15.507Z → 05:18:14.695Z) and reports 56,382 total tokens, whose turn was recorded 0.753 s before the run closed. Any hours-of-run or cost-per-run figure derived from that row is wrong by construction, not by rounding.
4. **The input to the ledger is not reconstructable from the persisted stream.** No stream file in this session contains a single event of type `model_usage` (0 in `9ceeb1f9` main stream with its 20 model turns; 0 in `0673152f` with 7) even though the ledger value is taken from that channel — see `runs/index.ts:2387-2390` in §3, where the handler returns before publishing. An independent audit therefore cannot recompute the row from what is on disk.

What is *not* claimed here: the three rows with all-null token fields are correct as they stand. Those runs contain no `model.completed` record at all (their main streams hold only `run.queued`, `run.started`, `run.status`, `run.cancelled`/`run.failed`), so `usageStatus: "provider-not-reported"` agrees with the recorded stream. This issue is about turns that ran and were not carried into the ledger, not about inventing numbers for runs that made no model call.

## 2. Expected behaviour

1. The ledger reconciles with the provider. For a run of N main turns plus delegated children, the row set for that run must sum to (or be explicitly reconcilable to) the N + ΣM per-turn figures the provider reported and the engine already recorded.
2. Delegated work is attributable. A subagent's model turns are spend of the same run; they need their own `invocationId` and a kind that distinguishes them from the parent's `task`, so a user can answer "what did the delegation cost" — today the answer is only reachable from CAS blobs.
3. A row's figures must describe the row's scope. If one row per invocation is kept as the shape, its tokens have to be the sum over that invocation's turns with the turn count recorded (the engine already returns `turns`), so the duration window and the token window agree.
4. The channel feeding the ledger stays observable. Either the per-turn `model_usage` figures are persisted, or per-turn rows exist — one of the two must hold, so that a reviewer can recompute a stored figure without reading the internal state pool.
5. `provider-not-reported` keeps its current meaning: unknown is recorded as unknown, never as zero. The same discipline this repository already states for the evolve proxy (`evolution/llm-proxy.ts:273-275`).

## 3. Source code

Paths relative to the repository root; all quoted at main `a773942a` / `bec6399d` (identical, §8).

**The engine produces one figure per turn and keeps only the last.**

- `packages/runtime-core/src/runtime.ts:286` — `let usage: TUsage | undefined;` declared *outside* the turn loop that starts at `:296` (`for (let turn = 0; turn < this.options.maxModelTurns; turn += 1) {`).
- `packages/runtime-core/src/runtime.ts:334-337` — inside the loop, per turn:
  ```
  if (modelTurn.usage !== undefined) {
    usage = modelTurn.usage;
    this.emit({ type: "model_usage", usage });
  }
  ```
  Reassignment, not accumulation; the same pair repeats in the output-recovery retry at `:367-370`.
- `packages/runtime-core/src/runtime.ts:380-384` (normal completion), `:418-419` (suspended return), `:428-432` (turn-budget return) — every exit ships `...(usage !== undefined ? { usage } : {})`, so `AgentLoopResult.usage` is structurally the last turn's usage. `:428-430` shows the result *does* know the count it does not carry: `turns: this.options.maxModelTurns`.

**The agent wrapper forwards that single figure once.**

- `services/api/src/native-agent/index.ts:647` `let reportedModelUsage = false;`, `:700` `if (event.type === "model_usage") reportedModelUsage = true;`, `:857-858` re-emits each per-turn event upstream (`case "model_usage": emit({ type: "model_usage", usage: event.usage, usageReported: true });`).
- `services/api/src/native-agent/index.ts:715-717`:
  ```
  const usage = result.usage;
  if (!reportedModelUsage) this.emit({ type: "model_usage", ...(usage ? { usage, usageReported: true } : { usageReported: false }) });
  if (usage) this.emit({ type: "usage", usage });
  ```
  The `type: "usage"` event is the terminal, whole-agent figure — one per agent, and (see next) one turn's worth of tokens.

**The run collector holds one overwritten slot, and that slot is what gets persisted.**

- `services/api/src/runs/index.ts:1069` `let lastAgentUsage = unreportedModelUsage();` — one variable for the whole run.
- `services/api/src/runs/index.ts:2387-2390`:
  ```
  if (event.type === "model_usage") {
    lastAgentUsage = capturedModelUsage(event);
    return;
  }
  ```
  Overwrite per turn, and the early `return` means no `publish(...)` runs for this event type — which is why the persisted stream has 0 `model_usage` records while carrying 20 per-turn usage payloads.
- `services/api/src/runs/index.ts:2504` resets the slot to `unreportedModelUsage()` immediately before the run; `:2557` `const taskUsage = lastAgentUsage;`.
- `services/api/src/runs/index.ts:2591-2598` (completed), `:2653-2660` (cancelled), `:2700-2707` (failed) — the only three persistence calls on this path, each `invocationKind: "task"`, each passing the same single-slot `usage`. Repo-wide symbol search for `appendModelUsageForManifest` returns three files: its definition, `runs/index.ts` (those call sites), and `services/api/src/http/index.ts:303-306`, which is a re-export list, not a caller. There is no writer in the subagent execution path.
- `services/api/src/runs/index.ts:2109-2114` — the child bridge:
  ```
  if (event.type === "usage") {
    subagent.usage = event.usage;
    finalizeMessageStep();
    void emit({ subagentId: subagent.id, type: "subagent.usage", usage: event.usage });
  ```
  A child's whole-run figure becomes one parent-stream event and one field on the subagent record. It is never handed to `appendModelUsageForManifest`, so children cannot appear in the ledger.
- `services/api/src/runs/index.ts:3190-3210` — the other direct writer (`invocationKind: "session-naming"`), also `costUsd: null`.

**The record itself has nowhere to put turn granularity.**

- `services/api/src/model-usage/index.ts:27-35` `CapturedModelUsage` (six token fields + `usageStatus`), `:37-47` `unreportedModelUsage()`, `:49-70` `capturedModelUsage(event)` (returns the event's figures verbatim, or the all-null `provider-not-reported` shape).
- `services/api/src/model-usage/index.ts:72-83` — `appendModelUsageForManifest`'s `options` are `attemptIndex / invocationId / invocationKind / manifest / outcome / runId / usage`: no turn index, no turn count.
- `services/api/src/model-usage/index.ts:85-108` — the record built from them, with `costUsd: null` at `:89`, `finishedAt: options.manifest.finishedAt` at `:90`, `startedAt: options.manifest.createdAt` at `:105`. This is exactly the run-window-plus-one-turn mixture described in §1 item 3.
- `packages/schema/src/model-usage.ts:167-191` — `ModelInvocationUsage` has `invocationId` (`:175`) and `invocationKind` (`:176`) and no `turnId`, no `turnCount`. `packages/schema/src/model-usage.ts:152-162` — `ModelInvocationKind` is `delegation-track | evolve | paper-vision | review-correction | semantic-review | session-naming | task`: no subagent member, and repo-wide literal search for `delegation-track` returns its declaration only, i.e. no writer uses that kind. The manifests are not a workaround either: `runs/index.ts:2587` (and `:2649`, `:2696`) set `turnId: runId`, so the "turn" identifier in the manifest is the run.
- Read side is faithful to its input: `services/api/src/model-usage.ts:57-71` (`addUsageToBucket`) and `:414-448` (`summarizeModelUsageAnalytics`, which sums `usage.inputTokens` per row) and `:385-412` (`estimateInvocationCost`, per row). Nothing here mis-adds — the turns are simply absent from the input. `ModelUsageBucket.invocationCount` (`packages/schema/src/model-usage.ts:198`) counts rows, so a 20-turn run and a 1-turn run both count as 1.

**Per-call rows already exist in this codebase.**

- `services/api/src/evolution/llm-proxy.ts:126` `handleEvolveCompletion`, `:162` `const startedAt = new Date().toISOString();`, `:233` `const usage = await recordUsage(deps, grant, model, payload, startedAt);`, `:245-278` `recordUsage(...)` → `parseProviderUsage(payload.usage, …)` then one `appendModelInvocationUsage` per proxied completion, keyed `invocationId: \`evolve:${grant.runId}\`` with its own kind and the comment at `:262-263` justifying a separate kind precisely because "a search's spend is not a chat turn". The same argument applies between a parent's turns and a child's, and between turn 1 and turn 20.

## 4. Real run evidence

One captured session on the integration instance (Native executor, `invocationKind: "task"` rows). Sources: the instance data directory's `model-usage/<sessionId>.json`, `run-events/<sessionId>/<runId>/*.jsonl`, and the per-turn payloads resolved through `versioning/agent-state/blobs/sha256/` (the `payloadRef` of each `model.completed` record). Read-only instruments: `rpH7-persisted-vs-perturN.txt`, `rpH22-e6-usage-census.txt`, `rpH24-e6-usage-events.txt` under `runs/JD/TASK-001/artifacts/`. No credentials or host paths are reproduced below.

Ledger contents for the session (`model-usage/bb1d6797-1270-4bb9-a1a3-a464a5bc141e.json`, 5 rows, all `invocationKind: "task"`, all `costUsd: null`, one row per run):

```
run=9ceeb1f9 outcome=completed usageStatus=reported              in=44952 out=11430 reasoning=6282 cacheRead=3584 total=56382
             startedAt=2026-11-11T02:27:15.507Z finishedAt=2026-11-11T05:18:14.695Z manifest=63d20e49
run=82036958 outcome=cancelled  usageStatus=provider-not-reported in=null  out=null  …  startedAt=10:29:00.882Z finishedAt=10:32:45.359Z
run=116b288e outcome=cancelled  usageStatus=provider-not-reported in=null  out=null  …  startedAt=10:38:39.403Z finishedAt=10:42:15.250Z
run=de7527c9 outcome=failed     usageStatus=provider-not-reported in=null  out=null  …  startedAt=11:31:22.799Z finishedAt=11:33:44.840Z
run=0673152f outcome=completed  usageStatus=reported              in=47387 out=1307  reasoning=310  cacheRead=3584 total=48694
             startedAt=2026-11-11T11:51:15.241Z finishedAt=2026-11-11T12:03:34.525Z manifest=c2220e9c
```

Per-turn usage recorded in the streams of the same session, by stream:

```
run 9ceeb1f9
  MAIN     turns_with_usage=20   sum(in=817210  out=39005)  first(turn=0  in=24831 out=81   at=02:27:17)  last(turn=19 in=44952 out=11430 at=05:18:13.942)
  sub a426c709 turns_with_usage=128  sum(in=5297320 out=126948) last(turn=127 in=32017 out=144  at=03:09:44)
  sub c7d68122 turns_with_usage=128  sum(in=5188821 out=74992)  last(turn=127 in=44707 out=116  at=04:05:29)
  sub c59905d7 turns_with_usage=128  sum(in=5267215 out=98987)  last(turn=127 in=39699 out=461  at=04:38:24)
  sub b95116e3 turns_with_usage=128  sum(in=5055291 out=100647) last(turn=127 in=43520 out=412  at=05:12:26)
  sub ceb12354 turns_with_usage=60   sum(in=2398037 out=75464)  last(turn=59  in=41592 out=9484 at=03:28:28)
  per-turn usage records: 592 (MAIN=20, subagents=572)   sums: in=24023894 out=516043 reasoning=395528 cacheRead=13174272
  MAIN last turn in=44952 out=11430   persisted row in=44952 out=11430   EQUAL=True
  which per-turn records match the persisted row exactly: [('MAIN', 19)]      row == sum over all streams? False

run 0673152f
  MAIN     turns_with_usage=7    sum(in=300115 out=10822)  first(turn=0 in=31442 out=314 at=11:52:38)  last(turn=6 in=47387 out=1307 at=12:03:32)
  (no subagent streams in this run)
  MAIN last turn in=47387 out=1307   persisted row in=47387 out=1307   EQUAL=True
  which per-turn records match the persisted row exactly: [('MAIN', 6)]       row == sum over all streams? False
```

Which channel the ledger's own numbers arrive on, and what the parent stream holds about children (`main.jsonl` event-type census):

```
run 9ceeb1f9 main.jsonl: {"assistant.thinking.delta":309, "assistant.delta":67, "agent.record":60, "tool.started":43,
                          "tool.completed":43, "plan.updated":26, "record:model.completed":20, "subagent.updated":15,
                          "subagent.usage":5, …}
  events of type model_usage: 0        events carrying a usage dict: 5 (all type=subagent.usage)
    in=32017 out=144  -> matches child a426c709 turn 127 (its last)      matches no MAIN turn record
    in=41592 out=9484 -> matches child ceb12354 turn 59  (its last)      matches no MAIN turn record
    in=44707 out=116  -> matches child c7d68122 turn 127 (its last)      matches no MAIN turn record
    in=39699 out=461  -> matches child c59905d7 turn 127 (its last)      matches no MAIN turn record
    in=43520 out=412  -> matches child b95116e3 turn 127 (its last)      matches no MAIN turn record
run 0673152f main.jsonl: {"record:model.completed":7, "agent.record":21, "tool.started":9, …}
  events of type model_usage: 0        events carrying a usage dict: 0
```

So, in one place each: 20 and 7 per-turn figures exist for the parent and 1 survives; 572 per-turn figures exist for the children and 0 reach the ledger while 5 (their last turns) reach the parent stream; and the ledger's surviving figure never appears in the stream as a `model_usage` event, exactly as `runs/index.ts:2387-2390` predicts.

Control for the "are the nulls wrong?" question: the three null-token runs' main streams contain `run.queued: 1, run.started: 1, run.status: 2` plus `run.cancelled: 1` (or `run.failed: 1`) and 0 `model.completed` records — no turn ran, so `provider-not-reported` is accurate and those rows are not counted as losses anywhere in this report.

## 5. Trigger conditions

- **Always, on the Native agent path.** 5 of 5 runs in the captured session produced exactly one row, and 2 of 2 runs that executed model turns produced a row equal to their last main turn. Any run of more than one turn under-reports.
- **Worst exactly where the platform's value is.** A delegated research run lost 572 of 592 turn records (96.62 %) to the missing subagent rows; the more children and the closer they run to the engine's turn ceiling, the larger the blind spot. (`MAX_MODEL_TURNS = 128` at `native-agent/index.ts:102`, applied at `:656` — four of the five children here hit 128.)
- **Not provider-dependent.** The provider reported usage for every turn in these runs; the loss is between the engine and the writer, not at the wire.
- **Not platform-dependent.** No cited line branches on OS; the only Windows-specific code in the chain is unrelated.
- **Silently distorts anything derived from the ledger** — cost estimates (`estimateInvocationCost` per row, `services/api/src/model-usage.ts:385-412`), per-run spend ranking, and the run-duration pairing in §1 item 3 — because the read side trusts the row set.

## 6. Difference from existing Issues and PRs

- **#103** (closed 2026-09-21, `[Feature] Reuse JiuwenSwarm backend - sub-task: Usage`, labels `help wanted`, `priority/major`, `release/0.3.0`) is a *porting* task: bring the JiuwenSwarm backend's usage capability to this repository. It says nothing about how many rows a Native agent run writes or which turn a row describes, and its subject is the swarm gateway path — where, per the symbol search in §3, there is no ledger writer at all. This draft is about the Native executor's writer, whose whole chain (`runtime-core` → `native-agent` → `runs/index.ts` → `model-usage/index.ts`) post-dates #103's scope. **Not the same request.**
- **#304** (open PR, `fix: parse usage by protocol and keep real E2E accounting non-gating`, created 2026-10-14) changes `.ci/README.md` plus three test files (`packages/model/src/client.test.ts`, `services/api/src/agent-run/jiuwenswarm-model-gateway.test.ts`, `test/journey-basic-real-api.spec.ts`) and touches no production writer. Its stated principle — missing accounting is diagnostic evidence, not evidence of zero cost — is the same principle §2 item 5 asks this Issue to preserve, and its body explicitly notes that the protocol-aware parser already lives on main in `packages/model/src/usage.ts` (`normalizeUsage`). It resolves *how a reported figure is parsed*, never *how many figures are stored*. **Adjacent, not duplicate.**
- **#783 / #789** (closed) and **#811** (closed PR `fix(model): preserve reasoning token diagnostics`) are arithmetic/diagnostic correctness on a figure that is already in the row: cached-prompt double-charging (fixed at `services/api/src/model-usage.ts:392-398`) and reasoning-token preservation. They assume the row's token fields are the run's true counts. That assumption is what this report measures and finds false for multi-turn and delegated runs.
- **#858 / #861 / #873 / #882 / #912** (closed) and **#509 / #575** (open) concern the usage page's headers, date presets, formatting and entry points — display-layer scoping of the stored rows. Nothing proposes or performs a change to `appendModelUsageForManifest`.
- **#330** (closed, session timeline showing tokens) and **#854 / #550** (closed, subagent panel) consume the per-child `subagent.usage` figure; they establish that the child's *last-turn* number is already user-visible while the ledger holds nothing at all about children. That is the display/record asymmetry §2 item 2 asks to close, not a prior report of it.
- **#963** (closed PR, record judge tokens, session tokens and tool calls on the real-case table) writes a CI artifact in the benchmark pipeline, not `ModelInvocationUsage`.
- Searches run against the live repository index: `usage granularity` → 2 records, neither relevant; `ModelInvocationUsage` → #783, #811; `usage ledger` → #304, #963, #330, #789 among others, none about persistence granularity; `subagent usage` → no record stating that a child's model turns are absent from the usage ledger. No record proposes per-turn or per-model-call rows for the Native agent path.

## 7. Acceptance criteria

1. **Reconciliation.** For a Native run of N main turns, the stored rows for that `runId` sum to the provider-reported per-turn figures the engine emitted for it (or the difference is an explicit, named state, e.g. `turnsRecorded` vs `turnsTotal`). A test with N ≥ 3 asserts the sum, not the last value.
2. **Children are in the ledger.** A run that delegates to K subagents stores their turn spend with its own `invocationId` and a kind distinguishable from the parent's `task` — either a new `ModelInvocationKind` member or a writer for the already-declared but unused `delegation-track` (`packages/schema/src/model-usage.ts:152-162`) — plus the parent linkage that today exists only as `subagentId` on the stream event.
3. **Scope agreement.** Whichever shape is chosen, a row's token fields describe the same scope as its `startedAt`/`finishedAt`. If one row per run is retained, its tokens are the run's sums and the row carries the turn count the engine already returns (`runtime.ts:418`, `:430`).
4. **Recomputable from persisted evidence.** Either `model_usage` figures reach the run's stream (remove the pre-publish `return` at `runs/index.ts:2387-2390` or publish a distinct record) or per-turn rows exist — one of the two, so a reviewer can recompute any stored figure from the record directory alone.
5. **Unknown stays unknown.** A run with zero completed model turns keeps `usageStatus: "provider-not-reported"` with null fields, per §4's control and #304's stated policy; the fix must not materialise zeros.
6. **Derived figures follow.** With rows corrected, `summarizeModelUsageAnalytics` and `estimateInvocationCost` need no change; add a test that a 20-turn delegated run's estimated cost is roughly 20×-plus-children that of a 1-turn run, so a regression to last-turn-only persistence fails loudly.
7. **Docstring parity.** The `ModelInvocationUsage` comment space or the usage page documents what a row means after the change, since "invocation" today silently denotes "run" on one path and "call" on the evolve path.

## 8. Version this draft measured

- SD main while writing: `bec6399dc18afe8885af94080988d5e28538f4b8` (2026-11-11T12:27:01Z). Anchor baseline used for line numbers: `a773942a46a59239e5fe425fb800343086b48f43` (PR #1095 squash, 2026-11-11T11:40:15Z). Compare between them touches three files under `apps/desktop/` only.
- Blob identities (12-hex Git blob prefixes) — identical at both main SHAs *and* identical to the downstream fork the evidence was produced on (`30178fda7…`, read-only `rev-parse HEAD:<path>`):

  | file | blob at main `bec6399d` | blob at main `a773942a` | blob at the fork we run |
  |---|---|---|---|
  | `services/api/src/model-usage/index.ts` | `05ab55482858` | `05ab55482858` | `05ab55482858` |
  | `services/api/src/model-usage.ts` | `812d797dafe5` | `812d797dafe5` | `812d797dafe5` |
  | `packages/schema/src/model-usage.ts` | `3a88f4fca5d1` | `3a88f4fca5d1` | `3a88f4fca5d1` |
  | `services/api/src/runs/index.ts` | `ad02eef4fe78` | `ad02eef4fe78` | `ad02eef4fe78` |
  | `services/api/src/native-agent/index.ts` | `e243aef3821a` | `e243aef3821a` | `e243aef3821a` |
  | `packages/runtime-core/src/runtime.ts` | `16c0bc9490e8` | `16c0bc9490e8` | `16c0bc9490e8` |
  | `packages/model/src/usage.ts` | `40cc9f5d68a1` | `40cc9f5d68a1` | `40cc9f5d68a1` |
  | `services/api/src/evolution/llm-proxy.ts` | `c447143bc700` | `c447143bc700` | `c447143bc700` |
  | `services/api/src/http/index.ts` | — | — | re-export list at `:303-306` read at `bec6399d` |

  So this is upstream main behaviour, not a downstream fork difference.
- Main source files were read through the GitHub contents API pinned to each `?ref=<sha>` (the local upstream clone used earlier in this round no longer exists on disk); the fork's blobs were read with a read-only `git rev-parse HEAD:<path>` / `git show HEAD:<path>`.

## Limitations of this report

- Run evidence is one session (5 runs, 2 of them multi-turn) on a Windows host. The 1-of-N collapse and the missing `model_usage` events were reproduced in both multi-turn runs and follow directly from code with no platform branch, but we have not measured the same shape on Linux or with the JiuwenSwarm executor.
- Per-turn figures were recovered from the `payloadRef` of each persisted `model.completed` record (the agent-state CAS). We verified that the ledger row equals one of those records; we did not verify them against provider invoices, so "what the provider reported" here means "what the provider reported per turn into this pipeline".
- The instance executes the build product of the fork at `30178fda7…`. We proved the *source* blobs for every cited file match main; we did not byte-verify the compiled `dist/` of this cited module against that source.
- `costUsd` is null in every row this writer produces (`model-usage/index.ts:89`, and `runs/index.ts:3194` for the naming path). Cost is an estimate made at read time from pricing tables; the §5 claim that cost inherits the undercount is derived from that code path, not from a usage-page measurement — we did not exercise the analytics UI.
- We report that subagent turns are absent from the ledger. We do not claim a specific row-count target (per-turn vs per-invocation-with-sum-and-count): §2 and §7 state the properties, and leave the shape to the maintainers.
- The 128-turn ceiling that inflated this particular loss (four children cut at 128) is a separate finding with its own draft, and neither draft depends on the other's fix.
recent.title: [Bug]: Native agent runs persist one usage row holding the last main-agent turn — the parent's other turns and all subagent turns never reach the usage ledger
