recent.body:
**Context.** #1053 introduces a configured proxy bypass list (`ResolvedProxy.noProxy`, persisted as `proxyNoProxy`, edited via the new ProxySettingsEditor field). Reviewer @yuanzhou75 flagged on the PR that one subsystem does not honour it yet — this issue is the explicit tracking record he asked for ("Continuing the fix in a follow-up is fine by me; I only want it stated rather than dropped").

**Gap.** `services/api/src/mcp/node-client.ts` — `proxyEnvOverlay()`:

- For a `url` policy it sets all six of `HTTP_PROXY`/`HTTPS_PROXY`/`ALL_PROXY` and their lowercase forms to `proxy.url`, but builds `NO_PROXY`/`no_proxy` from `process.env` alone (`node-client.ts:129-134`).
- For an `environment` policy the overlay copies the ambient variables, which is fine, but the configured `noProxy` list is never merged either.
- Net effect: a user who fills the new `noProxy` field gets it honoured by the API's own HTTP clients, by the Runner's provisioned children and by the browser broker — but a stdio MCP child silently ignores it. That is the "configured but not applied" state #1053 exists to remove.

**Proposed fix.** When `proxy.noProxy` is set, merge it into the overlay's `NO_PROXY`/`no_proxy` (union with any ambient value so an operator-provided bypass keeps working), for both `url` and `environment` policies. Cover with a `node-client.test.ts` case asserting a stdio child's env carries the configured bypass entries.

**Scope note.** `node-client.ts` is intentionally not part of #1053's 77-file diff; keeping this out of that PR keeps its review surface unchanged.
recent.title: [Follow-up] #1053: thread the configured noProxy bypass list into stdio MCP server environments

recent.author: JinhZhao
recent.body:
## 1. Actual behaviour

An Agent calls `check_runner` and gets a green light. Nine seconds later it calls `run_shell` and is refused. Both answers describe the same Runner instance, and their embedded Runner capability blocks are **equal in every field except `checkedAt`**.

| | `check_runner` result | `run_shell` result (same Agent, 9.282 s later) |
|---|---|---|
| stream record | `tool-call_18e8130d…jsonl`, `11:52:38.996Z` | `tool-call_df9f3c68…jsonl`, `11:52:48.278Z` |
| call | `call_18e8130d…` `check_runner{"runner_id":"local"}`, `tool.completed status=completed` | `call_df9f3c68…` `run_shell{…, "cwd":".", "wait_ms":15000}`, `tool.completed status=failed` |
| wrapper | `RunnerCheckResult` (7 keys) | `RunnerBlockedResult` `{code, dispatched, instruction, operationId, runner}` |
| headline verdict | **`ready: true`**, `reason: "ready"` | **`ready: false`**, `reason: "Command failed: <micromamba.exe> --no-rc create …"` |
| embedded capability | `ready: true`, `reason: "ready"`, `sandbox: "none"`, `sandboxUsable: false`, `dependencyAvailable: true` | `ready: true`, `reason: "ready"`, `sandbox: "none"`, `sandboxUsable: false`, `dependencyAvailable: true` (identical, `checkedAt` `…48.238Z` vs `…38.951Z`) |
| shell sub-capability | `available: false`, `utilities: []`, `unavailableReason: "Command failed: …"` | `available: false`, `utilities: []`, `unavailableReason: "Command failed: …"` (equal) |
| `suggestions` | 2 items, item 0 = "…Recreate or update the starter environment on the target Runner to repair managed Bash and its required utilities." | same 2 items |
| result size | 13,987 chars | 19,423 chars |

So there are two distinct problems in the same contract.

**(a) The diagnostic verdict is route-blind.** `checkRunner` narrows its verdict to the managed Shell only when its 4th argument `requiresShell` is passed (`services/api/src/agent-run/workspace-bindings.ts:193-196`), and the tool-facing binding never passes it:

```
:415   runnerReadiness: {
:416     check: (machine, signal) => checkRunner(machine, signal),
```

so the answer an Agent receives from `check_runner` is *always* the Python-channel answer (`requiresShell = false`, `:180`), whatever the Agent intended. The same function is called with `true` from the Shell execution route (`:278`) and re-passes the blocked operation's own `requiresShell` in `wait_for_runner` (`:431`, `:446-447`). `ready` therefore has two meanings selected by a parameter the tool cannot set and the Agent is not told about. The tool's own description says it "Reports the platform, Shell, guaranteed utilities, sandbox diagnostics and repair suggestions" (`packages/workspace/src/workspace.ts:1642` at B, `:1637` at A) — but the headline field it publishes ignores the Shell probe it also publishes.

**(b) The Runner-level verdict inside the payload is a constant.** The `sandbox === "none"` branch of the probe hard-codes the answer (`services/runner/src/readiness.ts:43-45`): `ready: true, reason: "ready"`, with the failure text parked next to it in `detail`. That is why the refused call's own payload carries `ready: false` at the top and `capability.ready: true, capability.reason: "ready"` inside — one object, two verdicts, and the nested one is the Runner's official answer. Consumers that read `capability` (the `/health`-style surface, the UI) get `"ready"`; consumers that read the top-level get the truth, and which one they get depends on which code path built the object.

**(c) A closed vocabulary cannot express the state.** `RunnerExecutionCapability.reason` is typed `"ready" | "dependency-unavailable" | "incompatible" | "sandbox-unusable"` (`packages/schema/src/environment.ts:520`). There is no value for "the shell route is dead", so `"ready"` is the only permitted answer even when the probe's own sub-capability says no.

Measured across the whole capture: an object with the `RunnerCheckResult` key set occurs **194** times in the 62 stream files of this session (occurrences, not calls — see section 4 for how one call multiplies). In **194 of 194** the embedded verdict is `capability.ready: true` with `capability.reason: "ready"` (the reason text survived field bounding in 177 of them) and `capability.shell.available: false` with `shell.utilities: []`. The headline `ready` splits **76 true / 118 false** over that identical nested verdict. Zero occurrences anywhere in the capture report `shell.available: true`. So this is not an intermittent race: the Shell was unavailable throughout, the Runner probe said `"ready"` throughout, and the only thing that varied was which code path asked.

Two consequences worth separating from the diagnosis:

- A Runner that starts with a provably dead managed Shell logs nothing. `services/runner/src/server.ts:1189-1190` warns `execution_unavailable` only `if (!capability.ready)`, and `capability.ready` is the literal `true` from `readiness.ts:43` on this branch. The operator's startup log was silent for the entire 10-hour capture while the Shell was unprovisionable.
- The Agent that chooses to wait can end with no answer at all. In this capture `wait_for_runner` (`call_29c5a855…`, run `0673152f`) returned `action: "cancel"`, and the cancel branch (`workspace-bindings.ts:444-445`) returns `{action, operationId, dispatched: false, instruction}` with **no** `runner` object — so the next readiness question goes back through `check_runner` and returns `ready: true` again.

## 2. Expected behaviour

The decoupling is deliberate and we are not asking for it to be undone: PR #716's stated design is that "A missing managed shell must not block Python execution" (`services/runner/src/readiness.ts:35-37`), and that is right. What is missing is a route-scoped answer on the *diagnostic* surface, so that "is this Runner able to run my Shell command?" is answerable from the check instead of only from the refusal. Any one of the following closes it; they are alternatives, not a list to implement in full.

1. Give the tool the route it is asked about: accept `requires_shell` (or `route: "python" | "shell" | "any"`) in `check_runner`'s parameter schema and pass it to `checkRunner`. Default behaviour unchanged; the Agent's question finally determines the answer's scope.
2. Or make the verdict structural instead of caller-selected: publish route-scoped fields derived from what is already probed (for example `readyFor: { python: <ready>, shell: <ready && shell?.available !== false > }`) so every consumer reads one object and branches, and the two verdicts cannot disagree.
3. Or, minimal: never emit `reason: "ready"` when a probed sub-capability answered no. `capability.shell.available === false` should set `reason` to a new value (for example `"shell-unavailable"`) while the coarse `ready` keeps whatever meaning the Python channel needs; the union at `packages/schema/src/environment.ts:520` gains that value. This is the precedent the project already set for `sandboxNetwork` (section 6, #461/#463), whose sub-capability reports `available: false` with an `unavailableReason`.
4. Or, if the current payload is judged complete: say so where a caller reads it. `check_runner`'s description and the `RunnerExecutionCapability` doc comment should state that `ready` deliberately ignores `shell.available`, and the second suggestion should stop telling the Agent to "use check_runner" to recheck a blocker the check cannot report (`services/api/src/agent-run/workspace-bindings.ts:206`).

Whichever shape is chosen, `capability.ready`/`capability.reason` should be derived on the `sandbox === "none"` branch the way they are derived on the sandboxed branch (`readiness.ts:78-79` derives `ready` from the probe result rather than fixing it), so that the nested verdict is not a constant, and a positive test should assert that a payload reporting `shell.available: false` does not report `reason: "ready"`.

## 3. Source code

All lines read at `B:` = `a773942a46a59239e5fe425fb800343086b48f43` from the GitHub contents API (the local upstream clone is 33 commits behind main and was not used for line numbers). PR #1095 inserts 5 lines into `packages/workspace/src/workspace.ts` at `@@ -135,6 +135,11 @@`, so for that file only, `B = A + 5` at or after old line 138; both forms are given there. No other cited file shifted.

- `services/api/src/agent-run/workspace-bindings.ts` — main blob `6664fc9b1fb7`; the copy our instance runs is `8bcb6326e93f`; the two differ at **exactly one line**, `:237` (PR #1095's instruction wording), and every line cited below is byte-identical between them:
  ```
  175-178|   * `requiresShell` … `wait_for_runner` recheck and its alternative machines answer the same
             question the blocked Shell call asked. Python-only checks leave it false.
  179-180|  const checkRunner = async (machine?, signal?, refresh = true, requiresShell = false) => {
  190|        const capability = await resolveExecutionTarget(runnerId).runnerClient.executionCapability(refresh, signal);
  191-192|    // An absent `shell` field is an older Runner that cannot report it, so
            // only an explicit `available: false` narrows readiness.
  193-195|    const shellUnavailableReason = requiresShell && capability.shell?.available === false ? … : undefined;
  196|        const ready = capability.ready === true && shellUnavailableReason === undefined;
  197-199|    result = { runnerId, …, connected: true, ready, reason: shellUnavailableReason
                          || (ready ? "ready" : capability.detail || capability.reason || …), capability,
  201-206|    suggestions: ready && capability.shell?.available !== false ? [] : [ …shell repair text…,
                          "After repair use check_runner, or explicitly request user help with wait_for_runner." ]
  217-222|   * `requiresShell` blocks a Shell call when the Runner explicitly reports its managed Shell as unavailable …
            // and Python execution is never blocked by a Shell gap.
  223-239|   prepareExecutionTarget(…, requiresShell = false) → checkRunner(machine, signal, false, requiresShell)
            if (!runner.ready) throw new RunnerUnavailableError({ code:"RUNNER_UNAVAILABLE", dispatched:false, operationId, runner, instruction })
  278|       // the Shell execution route calls with requiresShell = true
  351|       checkRunner(runnerId, signal, true)
  415-416|   runnerReadiness: { check: (machine, signal) => checkRunner(machine, signal),      // <-- the tool surface
  431|         if ((await checkRunner(runnerId, signal, false, operation.requiresShell)).ready) alternatives.push(…)
  444-445|   if (decision.action === "cancel") return { action: "cancel", operationId, dispatched: false, instruction: … }   // no runner object
  446-447|   const runner = await checkRunner(…, signal, true, operation.requiresShell);
  ```
  `:196` is the defect in one line, `:416` is the reason it is invisible from the tool, and `:201` shows the function already treating `capability.shell?.available === false` as special enough to change `suggestions` while `:196` treats the same fact as irrelevant unless `requiresShell` is set.
- `services/runner/src/readiness.ts` (blob `47c678febd07`, identical in main, local upstream and the fork we run):
  ```
   21|   private readonly shellProbe?: () => Promise<NonNullable<RunnerExecutionCapability["shell"]>>,
   28|   if (!refresh && this.cached && !(this.sandbox === "none" && this.shellProbe)) return this.cached;
   34|   if (this.sandbox === "none") {
   35-39|  // [windows-desktop] … A missing managed shell must not block Python execution.
           // Shell routes check shell.available separately; sandboxUsable stays false so the
           // UI/API can still surface that isolation is absent (F6 tightens permissions to compensate).
   40|     const shell = await this.shellProbe?.();
   42-47|  return { instanceId, checkedAt, sandbox: "none",
            dependencyAvailable: true, sandboxUsable: false, ready: true,
            reason: "ready",
            detail: shell?.unavailableReason ?? "unsandboxed direct execution",
            platform: …, ...(shell ? { shell } : {}) };
   50-52|  // the sandboxed branch instead starts from ready: false / reason: "dependency-unavailable"
   78-79|  return { …, sandboxUsable: capability.sandboxUsable,
            ready: capability.sandboxUsable, reason: capability.sandboxUsable ? "ready" : "sandbox-unusable", … };
  ```
  `:43-45` is where a failure transcript and the word `"ready"` are put into one object by the same literal.
- `packages/schema/src/environment.ts:512-529` (blob `424a1559fad3`, identical in all three bases) — `RunnerExecutionCapability`: `:512` the doc comment "Reported by the Runner process, never inferred from its installation shell.", `:519 ready: boolean`, `:520` the closed `reason` union, `:521 detail?`, `:522 platform?`, `:523-528 shell?: { available; name: "bash"; utilities; unavailableReason? }`. No route dimension on `ready`. Compare `SandboxNetworkCapability` at `:506-510`, which does carry `available` + `unavailableReason`. Also `RunnerCheckResult` `:548-556` (top-level `reason: string`, `capability?`), `RunnerBlockedResult` `:558-564`.
- `services/runner/src/server.ts:1183-1188` (blob `053bc98da55c`, identical in all three bases) — the probe is wired only for Windows direct execution: `:1186` "// The managed Bash/package contract is provisioned only on Windows." / `:1187` `sandbox === "none" && process.platform === "win32" ? () => environmentStore.shellCapability() : undefined`; then `:1189-1193` the startup log gates on `!capability.ready`; and `:353-359` `SCIENCE_AGENT_SANDBOX_PROVIDER` with "[windows-desktop] Windows resolves to the direct-execution provider".
- `services/runner/src/environment-store.ts:443-466` (blob `268e0049660b`, identical in all three bases) — `shellCapability()`: `{ available: false, name: "bash", utilities: [], unavailableReason }` when the managed environment is unavailable (`:445-446`) or when the shell path is not executable (`:463-464`), and `{ available: true, utilities }` only when every `MANAGED_SHELL_UTILITIES` entry resolves (`:457-461`).
- `packages/workspace/src/workspace.ts:1638-1647` (B) / `:1633-1642` (A) — the tool definition. `parameters` accepts `runner_id` only, and `execute` calls `options.runnerReadiness!.check(params.runner_id, signal)` and returns `JSON.stringify(value)` as model-visible content, so the object in section 1 is exactly what the model receives, with no route parameter available to it.
- `services/runner/src/executor.ts:1641-1647` (blob `d0a12151eeb8`, identical in all three bases) — `directExecutionCapability()`, a *different* host-shell probe (`/bin/bash`, POSIX-only). Cited to prevent conflation: `capability.shell` is the managed Bash of the scientific environment, not the host's `/bin/bash`.

## 4. Real run evidence

One captured `integration/test` instance (Windows host, `sandbox: "none"`, DeepSeek-Flash; session `bb1d6797-1270-4bb9-a1a3-a464a5bc141e`; lead runs `9ceeb1f9-1dea-4c80-a2e5-a2eab199cb38` and `0673152f-96d2-4bce-b7ad-0f188978e6af`, plus `116b288e…`, `82036958…`, `de7527c9…`). Everything below was recomputed from the persisted `run-events` JSONL of that capture (62 stream files: 49 + 10 + 1 + 1 + 1); no task was re-run. Two counting units are used and are labelled as such — occurrences of an object are not calls, and conflating them is how a first pass on this data produced a wrong 33/33 reading.

**Calls** (`tool.started` / `tool.completed` trace events, authoritative):

| tool | run `9ceeb1f9` | run `0673152f` | recorded status |
|---|---|---|---|
| `check_runner` | 2 | 1 | all `tool.completed status=completed` |
| `wait_for_runner` | 0 | 1 | `status=completed`, `action: "cancel"`, no `runner` object |
| `run_shell` | 2 | 1 | all 3 `status=failed` |
| `request_direct_execution` | 0 | 1 | `status=failed` |
| `query_graph` | 7 | 1 | completed |

The three `check_runner` calls are at `02:28:18.996Z` and `05:15:36.278Z` (run `9ceeb1f9`) and `11:52:38.996Z` (run `0673152f`); each returned `ready: true` / `reason: "ready"`.

**Occurrences** (unit: one object whose key set is exactly `{capability, checkedAt, connected, ready, reason, runnerId, suggestions}`; the nested `capability` block is not its own unit; a single call multiplies because the result is echoed into the calling stream, the subagent step records, the parent's message history, and the `task` handoff):

| run | file kind | headline `ready` | headline `reason` | `capability.ready` / `reason` | `sandboxUsable` | `shell.available` | `suggestions` | occurrences |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| 9ceeb1f9 | subagent | false | shell failure transcript | true / "ready" | false | false | 2 | 100 |
| 9ceeb1f9 | subagent | true | "ready" | true / "ready" | false | false | 2 | 60 |
| 9ceeb1f9 | main | false | `[truncated]` | true / `[truncated]` | false | false | 2 | 9 |
| 9ceeb1f9 | main | true | `[truncated]` | true / `[truncated]` | false | false | 2 | 8 |
| 9ceeb1f9 | main | false | shell failure transcript | true / "ready" | false | false | 2 | 5 |
| 9ceeb1f9 | main | true | "ready" | true / "ready" | false | false | 2 | 3 |
| 9ceeb1f9 | tool-call | true | "ready" | true / "ready" | false | false | 2 | 2 |
| 9ceeb1f9 | tool-call | false | shell failure transcript | true / "ready" | false | false | 2 | 1 |
| 0673152f | main | false | shell failure transcript | true / "ready" | false | false | 2 | 2 |
| 0673152f | main | true | "ready" | true / "ready" | false | false | 2 | 2 |
| 0673152f | tool-call | true | "ready" | true / "ready" | false | false | 2 | 1 |
| 0673152f | tool-call | false | shell failure transcript | true / "ready" | false | false | 2 | 1 |
| **total** | | **76 true / 118 false** | | **194/194 true** | **194/194 false** | **194/194 false** | | **194** |

- Invariants across all 194 occurrences: `capability.ready: true` (194/194), `capability.sandboxUsable: false` (194/194), `capability.shell.available: false` (194/194), `shell.utilities: []` (194/194), `suggestions` length 2 (194/194). `capability.reason: "ready"` is readable in 177 and is the literal `[truncated]` in the other 17. **No occurrence reports `shell.available: true`.**
- The verdict pair from section 1: `call_18e8130d…` (`check_runner`, `ready: true`) at `11:52:38.996Z` and `call_df9f3c68…` (`run_shell`, refused with `RUNNER_UNAVAILABLE`, `dispatched: false`, `runner.ready: false`) at `11:52:48.278Z`. The two embedded `capability` blocks were compared field by field and are **equal after dropping `checkedAt`** (`instanceId` `27e38a9f-eda8-4840-814d-980216d47370` for both, `detail` equal, `shell` equal). Recorded result sizes 13,987 and 19,423 chars.
- The refusal text is the same transcript in three places inside one payload: `capability.detail`, `capability.shell.unavailableReason`, and `suggestions[0]`. Redacted opening: `Command failed: <local-root>\micromamba.exe --no-rc create --yes --strict-channel-priority --override-channels --prefix <local-root>\revisions\starter-python\rev-3fb663cf-… --channel conda-forge python=3.12 numpy=2.0 pandas=2.2 scipy=1.14 matplotlib-base=3.9 m2-bash m2-coreutils m2-grep m2-sed` … 12 further libmamba lines … `critical libmamba remove_all: The directory is not empty.`
- Both verdict classes appear inside **one** handoff object. The `task` tool's `tool.completed` records for run `9ceeb1f9` (`main.jsonl` sequence 194, 202, 214, 225, 235) carry 21 readiness-shaped objects at `details.subagent.steps[N].details` (the child's `check_runner` answers, `ready: true`) and `details.subagent.steps[M].details.runner` (the child's blocked Shell calls, `ready: false`). Example, sequence 225: `steps[18].details` has `ready: true, reason: "ready"` while `steps[13].details.runner` has `ready: false, reason: "Command failed: …"`. The lead agent therefore receives both verdicts about one Runner in one result, unlabeled and unreconciled. In 17 of those 21 the long strings had been replaced by the recorder's literal `[truncated]` marker, so neither verdict's reason is even readable there; that field bounding is a separate layer and is not part of this ask.
- Across the capture, the gate refused Shell work in **57** `RUNNER_UNAVAILABLE` payloads (52 with `dispatched: false`) and **14** `TOOL_EXECUTION_FAILED` payloads, 5 of them "Target direct shell workspace capability is unavailable". Those refusals are correct behaviour by `prepareExecutionTarget`; they are counted here only to show that the green light and the refusal describe the same Runner state in the same session, 02:27Z to 12:03Z.
- What the Agents knew and when: the four budget-stopped children's final texts open with the Shell blocker (`Shell remains blocked (micromamba package-cache corruption, shell.available: fa…`, `Shell execution is blocked on this Runner (managed Bash/env provisioning failure…`, `Shell is unavailable. Let me top up a few exact metadata lookups…`, `Shell is unavailable on this Runner (managed bash provisioning failure), so I'll…`) — they learned the state from refusals, not from the three `check_runner` calls they were told to use.

We are not claiming the underlying provisioning failure is an SD defect. Why the managed environment could not be created on this host is a separate finding (a corrupt local package cache plus a downstream environment-pool configuration). This report is only about the contract of the object that reports it.

## 5. Trigger conditions

- A Runner whose sandbox kind resolves to `"none"` **on Windows** — the default for `SCIENCE_AGENT_SANDBOX_PROVIDER=auto` on that platform (`services/runner/src/server.ts:353-359`), which is also the only condition under which the shell probe is wired at all (`:1187`). On Linux/macOS with `bubblewrap`/`seatbelt`, `ready` is derived from `sandboxUsable` (`services/runner/src/readiness.ts:78-79`), so disagreement (a) cannot arise there — though the sandboxed branch is the one that already derives its verdict from a probe, which is what section 2 item 4 asks the `none` branch to do.
- The managed starter environment must be unprovisionable at check time (here `micromamba create` failing on a corrupt package cache), so `shellCapability()` answers `available: false` with a reason (`services/runner/src/environment-store.ts:445-446` / `:463-464`). Any Shell-probe failure should do: the probe is a file/executability check plus the environment store's own creation state, and it runs no user code.
- The Agent must ask. Because `runnerReadiness.check` drops the argument (`workspace-bindings.ts:416`), `check_runner` answers the Python question whatever the Agent meant; the disagreement surfaces as soon as the Agent then takes the Shell route.
- Not required: wall-clock timeouts, model behaviour, sandbox permissions, remote Runners, the specific package-cache error. An older Runner that reports no `shell` field at all shows no contradiction — by design (`:191-192`), which is also why a fix must keep treating an absent field as unknown rather than as unavailable.
- Deterministic reproduction: run the Runner on Windows against a data directory whose starter-env revision cannot be created (or otherwise force `shellCapability()` to answer `available: false`); from one Agent, call `check_runner` and then any Shell tool, and compare `ready`/`reason` in the two results against the `capability` blocks, which will match except for `checkedAt`. A unit-level version needs a test that goes through the workspace tool registry rather than calling `checkRunner` directly, because the binding's default is the thing under test.

## 6. Difference from existing Issues and PRs

The PI ruling required checking the *actual* repair scope of #1095 and #1081 against their own patches before deciding whether E-5A is a duplicate. Both checks came out negative, so the draft stands independently.

- **PR #1095** `fix(workspace): preserve actionable shell diagnostics in model results` — merged `2026-11-11T11:40:15Z`, squash commit `a773942a46a5…`, head `c488e0b3…`, base `f61cb5e4…`. Five files: `packages/workspace/src/shell-diagnostic-view.test.ts` (new, +53), `packages/workspace/src/workspace.ts` (+5/-0), `scripts/stack-platform.test.mjs` (+16/-3), `services/api/src/agent-run/workspace-bindings.test.ts` (+2/-0), `services/api/src/agent-run/workspace-bindings.ts` (+1/-1). Its two code changes are (i) `shellExecutionModelView` gains a `diagnostic` object (`code`/`command`/`instruction`) so a *failed Shell execution result* keeps its interpretation, and (ii) one prose line at `workspace-bindings.ts:237` inside the `RUNNER_UNAVAILABLE` instruction. It does **not** touch `services/runner/src/readiness.ts`, `environment-store.ts`, `server.ts`, `packages/schema/src/environment.ts`, the `checkRunner` signature, or the `runnerReadiness.check` binding. Confirmed at blob level: main `6664fc9b1fb7` and the copy our instance runs `8bcb6326e93f` differ at line `:237` only. **In short: #1095 improved what a refused Shell call explains after the refusal; it did not change what `check_runner` claims before it.** Not a duplicate.
- **Issue #1081** `[Bug]: Readiness reports a dead provider integration as ready, because catalog.ts never probes it` — **open**, and there is no PR #1081. Same *class* as ours (a readiness verdict derived without consulting a probe), different subsystem: the plugin/provider catalog (`services/api/src/plugins/catalog.ts`), sharing no code path with Runner execution readiness. Its own framing is the expectation we rely on ("the product kept reporting ready while the download path was dead"; readiness "only reads configuration, never a probe result"). Our case is one step further along the same shape: the Runner **does** probe, **does** report `available: false`, and the headline verdict still ignores it. A fix there would not fix this, and closing #1081 would not make our payload consistent. Not a duplicate.
- **PR #716** `fix(runner): provide a managed Windows shell toolchain` — merged `2026-11-07T10:00:12Z`, head `deafeb0a…`, 24 files including `readiness.ts` (+16/-5), `environment-store.ts` (+70/-2), `workspace-bindings.ts` (+39/-12), `packages/schema/src/environment.ts` (+13/-0). This is the change that introduced the `shell` sub-capability, the `sandbox === "none"` → `ready: true` branch, and the `requiresShell` parameter — and, in the same hunk, put the failure transcript and the word `"ready"` into one object (`detail: shell?.unavailableReason ?? "unsandboxed direct execution"` added next to an unchanged `ready: true, reason: "ready"`). It threaded `requiresShell` through the execution and wait paths but not through the tool-facing `check` binding. We are not disputing its design intent (Python must not be blocked by a Shell gap); this is the residual on the diagnostic surface it left open, and its own comment at `:35-37` is the reason we expect the fix to be a route-scoped answer rather than a new block.
- **Issue #916** (Windows managed Shell missing base Unix utilities; diagnosable environment capability) — closed by #716. It asked that the capability be *reported*; `shell` now is, and the suggestions do name the repair. What it did not get is a headline verdict that reflects the reported answer.
- **Issue #461 / PR #463** `fix(runner): report egress socket path readiness` — both the bug shape and the fix shape we propose, already applied once to a sibling sub-capability: #461's title is "…so every run_shell fails **while the Runner reports ready**", and #463 made `sandboxNetworkCapability` probe its own dependency and return `{ available: false, modes: ["none"], unavailableReason: … }` so `/health` never "advertises a mode whose first command would fail". Different probe, different code, closed and verified here — cited as precedent, not as a duplicate.
- **Issue #265** (decouple sandbox readiness from installation and workbench startup; offer choices when execution is blocked) — the philosophy the `suggestions` and `wait_for_runner` card implement. Our ask stays inside it: the card is right; the headline verdict should not contradict it, and the cancel branch should not return a check-free answer into an Agent that asked for a recheck.
- **Issue #29** (dependency preflight failures should say how to fix them, not just what is missing) — satisfied: `suggestions[0]` names the repair. That is also why `reason: "ready"` next to it reads as a bug rather than as missing information.
- Repo search found no Issue or PR mentioning `shell.available` at all; `check_runner` appears only in #461, #916 and the 0.3.0-rc1 RFC #343.

## 7. Acceptance criteria

1. No model-visible `check_runner` payload may carry `reason: "ready"` (or a `ready: true` presented as an execution green light) while the same payload carries `capability.shell.available: false`, unless the payload names the route the verdict applies to. Consistency must be structural, not something a consumer recovers by parsing a nested field.
2. The two surfaces must agree about the same Runner state within a short window: a `check_runner` answer and the `runner` block of the next Shell refusal should not disagree in the headline. A test should assert that pair, since the whole defect is invisible from either object alone.
3. `capability.ready` / `capability.reason` on the `sandbox === "none"` branch must be derived from the probe the way `:78-79` derives them on the sandboxed branch, not fixed as literals — so a consumer reading `capability` is not reading a constant.
4. Whichever shape from section 2 is chosen, it must be documented where a caller reads it: the `check_runner` tool description and the `RunnerExecutionCapability` doc comment. If `ready` keeps the Python-channel meaning, the description must say that it ignores `shell.available`.
5. A test drives the **tool** path, not `checkRunner` directly: sandbox `"none"`, a `shellProbe` returning `available: false`, then `check_runner` executed through the workspace tool registry, asserting the model-visible `ready`/`reason`. Today only tests that re-implement the binding's default can pass.
6. The Runner must say so at startup. `services/runner/src/server.ts:1189` cannot fire on this branch, so a warning (or equivalent operator-visible signal) on `capability.shell?.available === false` at startup is required; the entire 10-hour capture produced no startup complaint.
7. `wait_for_runner`'s cancel/expired branch should either carry the fresh check it just performed or not tell the caller to "use check_runner" to recheck a blocker it cannot report (`:444-445` vs `:206`).
8. Duplication in the diagnostic payload should be bounded (one transcript, referenced rather than repeated in `capability.detail`, `capability.shell.unavailableReason` and `suggestions[0]`), so the verdict is not buried in a 14 KB result. Acceptance is a size bound, not a wording change.
9. Behaviour that must NOT regress: Shell gaps never block Python execution; an absent `shell` field stays "unknown", not "unavailable" (`:191-192`); the `RUNNER_UNAVAILABLE` repair instruction and the `wait_for_runner` card stay as #1095 and #265 delivered them.

## 8. Version this draft measured

- SD main when this draft was finalised: `bec6399dc18afe8885af94080988d5e28538f4b8` (2026-11-11T12:27:01Z). The one commit between it and the anchor base `a773942a46a59239e5fe425fb800343086b48f43` touches `apps/desktop/` only, and the blob ids listed below are unchanged at both, so no line number in this draft shifts.
- Line numbers were anchored at `a773942a46a59239e5fe425fb800343086b48f43` (PR #1095 squash, merged `2026-11-11T11:40:15Z`). The preceding main tip measured this round was `1d54705431ee…`; every line number above was re-read at `a773942a46a5…` from the GitHub contents API, and only the `packages/workspace/src/workspace.ts` citations shift (by 5 lines).
- Local upstream clone at the time of comparison: `d6f3b20ca2440a3dfb2eb3c922d54d22be6cdb46` (33 commits behind main); the downstream fork our instance runs is `30178fda7…`. Blob identity (main / local upstream / fork): `services/runner/src/readiness.ts` `47c678febd07` / same / same; `services/runner/src/environment-store.ts` `268e0049660b` / same / same; `services/runner/src/executor.ts` `d0a12151eeb8` / same / same; `services/runner/src/server.ts` `053bc98da55c` / same / same; `packages/schema/src/environment.ts` `424a1559fad3` / same / same; `services/api/src/agent-run/workspace-bindings.ts` `6664fc9b1fb7` / `8bcb6326e93f` / `8bcb6326e93f` (differ at line 237 only); `packages/workspace/src/workspace.ts` `11ddfadfc244` / `b85342f13264` / `b85342f13264`.
- Consequence: the capture was produced by code one prose line behind main in one file and byte-identical to main in every file that derives the verdict or runs the probe. The shape reported here is main's shape, and section 6 shows it is not closed by #1095.

## Limitations of this report

- All runtime evidence comes from one Windows host on the `sandbox: "none"` direct-execution path. We have not measured `bubblewrap`/`seatbelt` startup behaviour for this shape, and we do not claim the disagreement occurs there.
- The corpus contains no healthy-host control: every occurrence we have reports `shell.available: false`, so we cannot show from evidence what the same code prints when the Shell probe succeeds. The code says `ready: true` either way, and that is exactly what makes the field uninformative — but the "misleading on a healthy host" case is inferred from source, not observed.
- Occurrence counts (194) are a census of objects in persisted streams, not a count of tool calls (3 `check_runner`, 1 `wait_for_runner`). They are reported side by side because the ratio between them is itself a property of the capture, and because a first pass that read only one unit produced a materially wrong 33/33 claim; the corrected units are what section 1 and 4 use.
- We verified the derivation, the wiring and the tool binding at main's own blobs. We did not audit other consumers of `RunnerExecutionCapability` (UI surfaces, remote Runner targets, `/health` consumers), so we make no claim about how the contradiction renders to a human operator.
- The 57 `RUNNER_UNAVAILABLE` / 14 `TOOL_EXECUTION_FAILED` payloads are the execution gate behaving as designed; counting them next to the green lights demonstrates a disagreement, not a second defect.
- We take no position on which of the shapes in section 2 is right for the project, and we do not treat the underlying `micromamba` provisioning failure on our host as an SD defect.

### Checklist

- [x] I have searched for related issues but did not get the expected help.
- [x] This bug has not been fixed in the latest version.
- [x] Please note that if your bug description lacks corresponding environment information and a minimal reproducible demo, it will be difficult for us to reproduce and resolve the issue, which will reduce the possibility of receiving feedback, or even lead to the issue being closed.

### 🐞 Detailed Description of the Problem

**现象**：在会话里让模型「帮我打开 UniProt 这个 MCP 服务器」，模型发起 `connector.enable` 请求（scope = 本次会话，激活模式 same_run）。界面弹出「启用连接器」卡片，但正文只有一句「暂不支持，请用原版界面。」，可用动作只有「关闭」，既没有确认/拒绝，也没有跳转到设置的入口。关闭后该请求被记为拒绝，模型回复「未启用 —— 本次会话中没有打开 UniProt MCP 服务器」，并声明不会再就同一配置需求重新发起请求。

**复现步骤**
1. 新建会话，输入「帮我打开 UniProt 这个 MCP 服务器」
2. 模型调用 configuration 工具的 `connector.enable`（describe → propose）发起启用请求
3. 会话内出现「启用连接器」卡片：正文「暂不支持，请用原版界面。」，只有「关闭」按钮
4. 点击「关闭」后卡片变为「启用连接器 · 暂不配置 · 原任务已完成」，模型回复连接器未启用（`sessionEnabled=false`），整个任务中 UniProt 工具均不可用

**代码定位（main，2026-11-11）**
- 卡片正文来自 packages/configuration-ui/src/messages.ts 的 `compact.unavailable`「暂不支持，请用原版界面。」；当 compact 卡片被归为 `unsupported` 时，ConfigurationRequestCard.tsx 中 `collapsedEditor = compact?.unsupported` 为真，编辑器被收起，只留「关闭」。
- 归类逻辑在 apps/desktop/src/app/configuration-presentation.ts 的 `connector.enable` 分支：仅当 `state === "awaiting_confirmation"` 且有 `previewDigest`（即 ready），且 `enabledConnectorIds` 的 before/after 能解析为「精确新增一个 id」时才返回 `{ connectorAddition: true }`，其余一律 `{ unsupported: true }`。
- 对比：apps/web 有专门的会话内连接器卡片（ConversationalConnectorCard.tsx）可以批准；桌面端没有对应实现，而 `unsupported` 兜底文案里的「原版界面」在桌面安装包里并不存在，用户无处可点。

**期望行为**
- 桌面端支持在会话内批准 `connector.enable`（session scope / same_run），至少提供「启用 / 不启用」两个明确动作，并在启用后让本次运行拿到该连接器工具
- 若确实暂不支持，卡片应给出可操作入口（如「前往 设置 → MCP/连接器」），而不是「请用原版界面」；同时应明确提供「拒绝」，避免模型把「关闭卡片」当成用户拒绝并不再重试
- 该能力在桌面端不可用时，不应让模型发起这类请求；至少提示用户只能在设置页手动开启

### Detailed Environment Information Description

- 应用：ScienceDiscovery 桌面版（Windows x64）
- 系统：Windows 11 专业版 25H2（10.0.26200）
- 界面语言：中文
- 场景：会话内让模型启用 UniProt MCP 连接器（connector.enable，session scope，same_run）

### Additional Information

两张截图：
1. 对话中的「启用连接器」卡片：正文「暂不支持，请用原版界面。」，右下角只有「关闭」
2. 关闭后的回执「启用连接器 · 暂不配置 · 原任务已完成」，以及模型的结论：未启用，已提交的 connector.enable 请求被拒绝，UniProt 连接器保持 sessionEnabled=false

### Version Information

- 版本：0.3.0 日包（daily build）
- 构建时间：2026-11-11T00:15:34Z（安装目录 resources/version.json 的 builtAt，其中 repoCommit 为 unknown）
- 安装方式：Windows x64 安装包

### Checklist

- [X] I have searched for related issues but did not get the expected help.
- [X] This bug has not been fixed in the latest version.

### 🐞 Detailed Description of the Problem

Split out of #1049, which this issue does not replace: #1059 fixes the download path (the OA bucket locator and the misattributed "record not found"), and this issue is the other half of §5 — the readiness signal.

**What is still true after #1059.** `services/api/src/plugins/catalog.ts` never probes a provider. A configured integration can be completely dead — every call fails with a provider-side outage — and the readiness/health view still reports it as ready, because readiness only reads configuration, never a probe result. In that state the only way anyone learns the integration is down is an agent that actually calls the tool and reports the `UPSTREAM_UNAVAILABLE` guidance back to the user.

**Why it matters.** The issue that produced #1049 was found exactly this way: the failure was visible only in a run's tool result, not in the surface a maintainer would check first. §10 of #1049 repeats this: the product kept reporting ready while the download path was dead.

**Expected.** An endpoint-level failure that the gateway already classifies (`ENDPOINT_UNAVAILABLE` / `UPSTREAM_UNAVAILABLE`) should reach the readiness view, so a dead integration is visible before an agent stumbles into it. How long such a signal stays authoritative, and whether it is a probe or a last-failure timestamp, needs a decision here — the download fix in #1059 does not depend on it.

### Additional Information

The classification this issue builds on is the one #1059 lands: `services/gateway/src/sciencediscovery_gateway/http_errors.py` and the broker's `upstreamError` mapping. Readiness (`catalog.ts`) is untouched by #1059 on purpose, so the two changes can be judged separately.

recent.body:
## 🚀 Background Description

Issue #817 defined four acceptance criteria across three CI engineering capabilities: test coverage gating, CI stability, and release CI efficiency (`<5h`). Three pull requests have since landed on `main`:

- **PR #951** (`2c33bc5017`): migrated 11 previously unscheduled Playwright specs (41 case identities) onto the shared PR plan (`L2` mocked E2E) and removed the `legacy` Playwright project (`status:legacy`, `ci:e2e:legacy`, `test:legacy*`, `CI_ALLOW_LEGACY`).
- **PR #940** (`360e6b664f`): preserved `reasoning_effort: low` across Evolve and search paths, added bounded upstream transport retries (502/503/504/524 and mid-stream socket resets) for streaming model completions, and configured Nightly model and judge calls to run with `low` effort in `nightly-research` with a 75-minute research-team timeout.
- **PR #971** (`1db615cdd2`): narrowed the active BiomniBench-DA L5 execution set from 50 to 45 cases (64 total real L5 cases), pinned Biomni generator and rubric judge thinking to `enabled` with `low` effort, scaled additive resource baselines by `45/50`, and recovered `da-11-1` when a stream ends cleanly inside truncated tool-call JSON.

### Audit of #817 Acceptance Criteria on Current `main`

Measured against the latest completed `main` CI run [42968972446](https://github.com/openJiuwen-ai/sciencediscovery/actions/runs/42968972446) (`679038182e`) and recent L5 / Release runs:

#### 1. Coverage thresholds and gating
- **1.1 Coverage gate enforcement**: **Not met** — `scripts/coverage-job-summary.mjs` and `.ci/tier-policy.mjs` remain informational only (`Coverage is informational. No minimum percentage is enforced`), and the Coverage job still merges only `ut` and `st` (mocked browser E2E is not measured).
- **1.2 Whole-repo line coverage ≥80%**: **Met** — **80.82%** (`203,344 / 251,596`; Node.js `81.18%`, Python `73.93%`, up from the `73.11%` baseline at `6d3c49a`).
- **1.3 Whole-repo branch coverage ≥70%**: **Not met** — **59.86%** (`98,788 / 165,035`; Node.js `59.80%`, Python `62.06%`), **10.14 percentage points** below the `70%` target.
- **1.4 Function coverage ≥80%**: **Met (Node.js)** — **80.08%** (`13,142 / 16,411`; Python function coverage is not separately reported).
- **1.5 Statement coverage ≥80%**: **Not implemented** — `summary.json` reports `lines`, `branches`, and `functions` only.
- **1.6 New / changed code (PR diff) coverage ≥80%**: **Not implemented** — no PR diff coverage calculation, summary comment, or gate check exists in CI.
- **1.7 Per-package coverage floor ≥60%**: **Partially met** — `apps/web` (`62.89%`) and Node `services/runner` (`88.55%`) now exceed `60%`, while `packages/idea-tree` (`45.94%`), `packages/schema` (`57.89%`), and Python `services/runner` (`0%`) remain below `60%`.
- **1.8 Core-path coverage ≥90%**: **Partially met** — `services/api` (`94.84%`), `packages/sandbox-capability` (`100%`), and `packages/model` (`96.48%`) exceed `90%` line coverage, while `services/gateway` (`75.23%`) and `services/runner` (`88.55%`) are below `90%`, and no dedicated core-path gate is enforced.

#### 2. Case-level profile and module coverage
- **2.1 No case outside every profile**: **Partially met** — PR #951 eliminated all 42 `status:legacy` dead cases by moving 41 valid browser identities into the `pr` (`L2`) profile. Remaining cases outside `test/support/tagged/profiles.mjs` rules are 79 `status:external` UT/ST cases, 1 `status:quarantined` case (`test/literature-review.spec.ts`), 1 `npu:required` case, 1 `category:st + model:real` case, and 6 `os:macos` cases; `ci:catalog:check` does not yet fail on profile-unreachable tags.
- **2.2 Every module mapped to an executing gating case**: **Not implemented** — the tagged catalog does not yet carry an explicit case-to-module ownership mapping or fail when a module has no executing case.

#### 3. CI stability and flake governance
- **3.1 Automated flake identification and quarantine**: **Not implemented** — no rolling failure-rate detector, automatic quarantine transition, or tracking-issue workflow is in place.
- **3.2 Infrastructure-only retries for network/gateway faults**: **Partially met** — PR #940 and PR #971 implemented bounded transport/stream retries and clean-EOF tool-argument recovery without retrying product defects, but per-case infrastructure retry counts and gateway-outage separation are not yet surfaced in the CI summary.
- **3.3 Thinking-mode (`low` / off) A/B experiment and CI configuration**: **Partially met** — PR #940 and PR #971 pinned Nightly and Biomni L5 runs to `reasoning_effort: low` without changing product defaults, while a formal multi-run A/B pass-rate and variance comparison report remains open.

#### 4. Release CI efficiency (`<5h`)
- **4.1 L5 release CI end-to-end duration <5 hours**: **Not met** — after PR #971 landed, the `main` L5 run [42380603816](https://github.com/openJiuwen-ai/sciencediscovery/actions/runs/42380603816) (`l5 · parallel=4 · nightly-research`) ran for **15h 39m** (2026-11-07 14:13Z to 2026-11-08 05:52Z, failed); prior branch L5 runs [42340397412](https://github.com/openJiuwen-ai/sciencediscovery/actions/runs/42340397412) and [42236770100](https://github.com/openJiuwen-ai/sciencediscovery/actions/runs/42236770100) took **8h 49m** and **7h 30m**; the latest `Release` workflow run [41196686771](https://github.com/openJiuwen-ai/sciencediscovery/actions/runs/41196686771) took **25h 01m**.
- **4.2 In-pipeline duration budget tracking and over-budget alerts**: **Not implemented** — no 5-hour budget table or alert check is wired into `release.yml` or `ci.yml`.
- **4.3 Bulk data downloads managed via cache/prefetch with zero redundant downloads on cache hit**: **Not implemented** — bulk downloads across jobs are not yet uniformly cached/prefetched and timed against the budget.
- **4.4 Real-model journeys running at lowest thinking effort with latency gain recorded**: **Partially met** — `low` effort is active for Nightly and Biomni L5, but before/after per-case p50/p95 latency gain reports have not been published.

---

### Scope of Follow-up Work Tracked by This Issue

Based on the audit above, the following four deliverables require continued development:

1. **Whole-repo branch coverage ≥70% (Item 1.3)**: raise combined Node.js + Python branch coverage from the current **59.86%** (`98,788 / 165,035`) to **≥70%**, and enforce the threshold in CI.
2. **New / changed code (PR diff) coverage ≥80% (Item 1.6)**: compute diff coverage on pull requests against the merge base and enforce a **≥80%** diff coverage gate on executable changed lines/branches in CI.
3. **L5 release CI end-to-end duration <5 hours (Item 4.1)**: reduce full L5 release pipeline wall-clock duration to **<5 hours**, with per-job budget accounting and over-budget alerts in the pipeline summary.
4. **Cache/prefetch management for all bulk data downloads with zero redundant downloads on cache hit (Item 4.3)**: audit and cache/prefetch all bulk downloads in CI (JiuwenSwarm ~1.5 GB runtime and virtualenvs, pnpm/uv dependencies, benchmark datasets and fixtures, model/sidecar assets, and container/base images), record download duration separately, and eliminate repeat bulk downloads when caches hit.

## Design Ideas

1. **Whole-repo branch coverage ≥70%**:
   - Prioritize packages with the largest uncovered branch mass in `coverage/summary.json` and `coverage/python/summary.json` (such as `services/api` at `54.79%` branches, `packages/workspace` at `55.72%`, `packages/artifact-manager` at `56.63%`, `services/gateway` at `57.22%`, `services/memory-graph` at `56.95%`, and `apps/web` at `70.73%`).
   - Add targeted unit and system tests for error branches, boundary guards, and fallback paths, and wire the `≥70%` branch threshold into `scripts/coverage-report.mjs` / `.ci/tier-policy.mjs`.

2. **PR diff coverage ≥80%**:
   - Extend `scripts/coverage-report.mjs` (or add a dedicated diff-coverage step in the `Coverage` job) to intersect `git diff <base>...<head>` hunk lines with merged LCOV / JSON coverage records from Node.js (`ut` + `st`) and Python (`coverage.py`).
   - Publish a clear per-file diff coverage table in `$GITHUB_STEP_SUMMARY` and fail the `Coverage` / `merge-gate` check when changed executable lines fall below `80%`.

3. **L5 release CI end-to-end duration <5 hours**:
   - Add per-job wall-clock and phase timing (setup/download vs. execution) to the L5 summary and enforce a `<5h` (`18,000s`) end-to-end budget check.
   - Combine shard parallelism tuning, long-tail case timeout/step-budget tightening, and deduplication of overlapping lower-tier work in the release profile so the end-to-end critical path stays under 5 hours.

4. **Bulk data download caching and prefetching**:
   - Inventory every multi-hundred-megabyte download across `.github/workflows/ci.yml`, `real-e2e.yml`, and `release.yml` (JiuwenSwarm bundle and Python virtualenvs, Node/pnpm stores, benchmark datasets/fixtures, browser binaries, and Docker layers).
   - Key caches by lockfile/manifest content hashes, warm them once in an upstream setup step or shared cache entry, and log cache-hit status plus download byte/time metrics in each job summary so cache-hit runs perform zero redundant bulk downloads.

## Involved Public APIs

None. All changes are internal to CI workflows, coverage reporting/gating scripts, and test suites; no product HTTP, CLI, or SDK APIs are added or modified.

## Description of Relevance to Other Modules

- `.github/workflows/ci.yml`, `.github/workflows/real-e2e.yml`, `.github/workflows/release.yml`: coverage gating, bulk-download cache orchestration, and L5 duration budget reporting.
- `scripts/coverage-report.mjs`, `scripts/coverage-job-summary.mjs`, `.ci/tier-policy.mjs`: whole-repo branch coverage gate (`≥70%`) and PR diff coverage calculation/gate (`≥80%`).
- `packages/*`, `services/*`, `apps/*` test suites: branch coverage additions to lift whole-repo branch coverage from `59.86%` to `≥70%`.

## Test Design and Test Plan

- **Branch coverage ≥70%**: run `pnpm test:shared` with coverage enabled and `node scripts/coverage-report.mjs`; verify merged whole-repo branch coverage is `≥70.00%` and that lowering the threshold or dropping coverage causes the gate script unit tests to fail.
- **PR diff coverage ≥80%**: add unit tests for the diff-coverage calculator covering added, modified, deleted, and non-executable files, plus a synthetic PR diff below and above `80%` to verify both the step summary table and non-zero exit code on failure.
- **L5 <5h and bulk download caching**: verify on consecutive CI / L5 runs that cache-hit jobs report `cache-hit: true` with near-zero download time for JiuwenSwarm, dependencies, and datasets, that the pipeline summary outputs the job timing breakdown against the 5-hour budget, and that the end-to-end L5 run completes in `<5 hours`.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] Merged whole-repo branch coverage (`Node.js + Python` across `ut` + `st`) reaches **≥70.00%** (up from `59.86%`), and the CI coverage gate fails if whole-repo branch coverage drops below `70%`.
- [ ] Pull request CI computes diff coverage on changed executable lines against the PR base and fails the gate when PR diff coverage is below **80.00%**, with the per-file diff breakdown rendered in the job summary.
- [ ] All bulk data downloads in CI (JiuwenSwarm install and virtualenvs, pnpm/uv dependencies, benchmark datasets/fixtures, and runtime assets) are managed through content-addressed cache/prefetch steps, download duration is measured separately, and cache-hit runs perform zero redundant bulk downloads.
- [ ] The L5 release CI pipeline finishes end-to-end in **<5 hours** (`<300 minutes`) and publishes a per-job duration vs. budget summary with automatic over-budget alerting.
- Commands that must pass: `pnpm ci:l1` and `pnpm test:shared`.

Written-by: ScienceDiscovery Product Claimed-by: ScienceDiscovery Product Claim-Id: 01bed55cb4a442f0b75c584b91b8d861 Branch: dev1/fix/945-desktop-feedback-image-truncation Base: 9871f2dd537a At: 2026-11-06T00:45:51Z ## Summary The desktop shell ships its own copy of the feedback screenshot pipeline, byte-identical to the web one, so the same silent truncation happens there: one multi-select of 10 screenshots attaches only the first 8, the two dropped files disappear, and the dialog says nothing. Web is fixed separately: #942 (fix in PR #943). PR #943's `## Scope` already names this copy and leaves it out: > `apps/desktop/src/feedback/feedback-images.ts:116` carries a copy of this function with the same silent cap drop, and its own dialog has the same gap. This change is the `apps/web` face only; the desktop copy is left untouched and needs the same fix, tracked separately. This issue is that separate desktop fix. ## Where it happens (main `9871f2dd`) - `apps/desktop/src/feedback/feedback-images.ts` is the same git blob as the web file: `69a1251` (4981 bytes, sha256 `0b66e24c…` for both). Line 122 is `if (images.length >= FEEDBACK_MAX_IMAGES) break;` and line 127 returns `{ images }` with no truncation signal. - `apps/desktop/src/feedback/FeedbackDialog.tsx:304-306` — `const result = await prepareFeedbackImages(Array.from(files), images); setImages(result.images); setImageError(result.error);`; `result.error` is `undefined` on this path. - `apps/desktop/src/feedback/FeedbackDialog.tsx:476` — only `{imageError ?

{fb.images.error[imageError]}

: null}` is rendered, so nothing appears. - The cap is 8 (`packages/operational-logging/src/feedback.ts:40`). It is only stated once the add button is already disabled at the cap (`FeedbackDialog.tsx:447-452` -> `fb.images.limit(FEEDBACK_MAX_IMAGES)`), which never fires for a single over-cap multi-select. - Desktop strings are **not** the web i18n: `apps/desktop/src/text.ts:99` proxies `TEXT` over two dictionaries, and `Text` is `typeof ZH` (`apps/desktop/src/text/zh.ts:1237`). The image block is `apps/desktop/src/text/en.ts:1134-1146` (limit `:1137`) and `apps/desktop/src/text/zh.ts:1182-1194` (limit `:1185`). Entries there are function-valued (`limit: (max) => …`), so the new one must be too. ## Steps to reproduce (desktop shell) 1. Open the desktop app's feedback dialog. 2. Click "Upload image" and select 10 PNG/JPEG files in one multi-select. 3. Observe 8 thumbnails and no message; the button then reads "Up to 8 images". 4. Submit; the relayed issue carries 8 images. Expected: a visible notice naming the cap and how many files were dropped, same wording as web: "Only the first 8 screenshots were attached; 2 skipped." Actual: no notice; 2 files vanish. ## Red first (already red on the desktop module) Run through the desktop package's own runner (`apps/desktop/package.json:7` is `tsx --test tests/*.test.ts tests/*.test.tsx`), against the byte-identical copy of `apps/desktop/src/feedback/feedback-images.ts` (git blob `69a1251`, sha256 `0b66e24c…`) plus main's `packages/operational-logging/src/feedback.ts`, stubbing `createImageBitmap`/canvas/`FileReader`: ``` $ apps/desktop/node_modules/.bin/tsx --test .local/red-desktop/desktop-feedback-images.test.ts not ok 1 - desktop: ten picks at the eight-image cap report the two skipped undefined !== 2 not ok 2 - desktop: two picks under the cap report nothing skipped undefined !== 0 not ok 3 - desktop: one removed then two picked attaches one and reports one skipped undefined !== 1 # pass 0 # fail 3 ``` `images.length` assertions pass; the failing half is exactly the missing truncation signal. Proposed test file `apps/desktop/tests/FeedbackImages.test.tsx`, mirroring the web test in #943: module assertions plus a mounted-dialog assertion (desktop's `react-test-renderer` helper `apps/desktop/tests/support/dom-renderer.ts`) that the hint text appears after an over-cap pick. ## Smallest mergeable slice (Dev-1, desktop face, <= 1 week) 1. `apps/desktop/src/feedback/feedback-images.ts` — return `skipped: number` next to `images`; count files left when the cap is hit (same shape as PR #943). 2. `apps/desktop/src/feedback/FeedbackDialog.tsx` — hold `skippedImages` in state; render one neutral hint (`className="feedback-hint"`, next to the `preparing` hint at `:475`) when `> 0`, clear it on add/remove/reset. 3. `apps/desktop/src/text/zh.ts` + `apps/desktop/src/text/en.ts` — add `truncated: (max: number, skipped: number) => string` to the `images` block in both (zh first: `Text = typeof ZH`), same wording as #943. 4. New `apps/desktop/tests/FeedbackImages.test.tsx` — the three module assertions above plus the two mounted-dialog directions. No shared-contract or Worker change; web files untouched. ## Acceptance - A1 (must): picking 10 from empty attaches 8 and shows a hint containing "8" and "2" (en) / "8" and "2" (zh). - A2 (must): picking 2 under the cap shows no such hint (negative direction, so a blanket banner does not pass). - A3: with 8 attached, remove one, pick 2 more -> 8 attached and the hint says 1 skipped. - A4: the hint exists in both desktop dictionaries and disappears after a successful submit; wording matches web (#943) so the two shells read the same. ## Dedup - `search/issues` for `desktop feedback`, `feedback-images`, `desktop screenshot`, `desktop attachment`: the only feedback-truncation item is #942 (web, PR #943 open); #879/#880 are the desktop attachment **size unit** surface, unrelated. - No open PR touches any file under `apps/desktop/src/feedback/` or `apps/desktop/src/text/` (checked the desktop PRs whose text matches: #905, #814, #904). - #943's own `## Scope` states the desktop copy is deliberately left out, so this is the tracked follow-up rather than a duplicate. ## Notes - No PR is opened with this issue now: today's new-PR budget is already spent on #941/#943, so the desktop PR queues behind whichever lands on main first. - Opened without labels (our token gets 403 on label writes); triage labels need a maintainer. - Environment: desktop face (`apps/desktop`), no API/base change; base main `9871f2dd537a6f3e3a94a7eb7b5bc67ef717d363`.

## What

`services/gateway/tests/test_architecture_boundaries.py:156` (`GeneratedWorkspaceBoundaryTests`, added by #915) pins only one direction of the walk: both new cases assert that something is **not** reported. Nothing asserts that a violation still **is** reported after the ignore list changed.

## Trigger

`IGNORED_DIRECTORIES` is widened again, or `_files()` is narrowed, so that a real source root (`services/api`, `packages`, `apps/web`, `test/api`) stops being walked. Every current case still passes:

- `test_a_generated_workspace_is_not_walked` and `test_a_workspace_file_removed_after_listing_is_skipped` assert absence only;
- `test_node_and_browser_sources_use_only_product_names` asserts `failures == []`, which a walk that sees nothing also satisfies.

The boundary test then silently stops policing the Gateway boundary with no red test anywhere.

## Fix

Add the mirror case in `GeneratedWorkspaceBoundaryTests`, reusing the `mock.patch.object(sys.modules[__name__], "_files", ...)` plumbing already present at `:162`:

- have the patched walk yield a path under `services/api/src` (for example `services/api/src/probe-boundary-<pid>.ts`) whose content contains a vendor token;
- assert `_node_boundary_failures()` returns that path, as `path: <relative>` or `content: <relative>`.

Three lines in the test file. No production code changes.

## Why it is worth a line

Measured at `f99cc8a24495544988045699b9e5c2429553e332` (review comment on #915): a fabricated `services/api/src/probe-zz-deerflow-boundary.ts` does produce `['path: services/api/src/probe-zz-deerflow-boundary.ts']`, and with the pre-change ignore set a probe in `services/api/.tmp` produces `['content: services/api/.tmp/probe-manual-537457.ts']`. The guard works today; only its regression direction is untested.

Found while reviewing #915 and tracked here so the review thread can be closed without losing the gap.

### Checklist

- [X] I have searched for related issues but did not get the expected help.
- [X] This bug has not been fixed in the latest version.
- [X] Please note that if your bug description lacks corresponding environment information and a minimal reproducible demo, it will be difficult for us to reproduce and resolve the issue, which will reduce the possibility of receiving feedback, or even lead to the issue being closed.

### 🐞 Detailed Description of the Problem

**What the user sees.** The mocked E2E suite is `87/88` and the one red case fails not on product behaviour but on a browser console error raised by the suite's own teardown:

```text
Error: no console/page errors expected, got:
[error] Failed to load resource: the server responded with a status of 404 (Not Found)
  @ http://127.0.0.1:4410/api/projects/3abde864-e853-4350-aa53-5ccc1a6fafa6/research-package/preview?sessionId=6bcfc3e0-...
```

Case: `test/agent-run-componentization.spec.ts:380` — `S2b subagent 首个受控工具的权限卡也出现在主对话最外层`. Job `Gate / L2 E2E (mocked, standard-journeys)` (job id 130151439627) on Nightly run [42907916462](https://github.com/openJiuwen-ai/sciencediscovery/actions/runs/42907916462), sha `4bb737c2`.

**Evidence.** The mocked stack's `stack.log` (in `mocked-e2e-results-standard-journeys`, artifact id 13807782121) shows the request arrives **after** the project was deleted by teardown:

```text
GET  /api/evolve/status HTTP/1.1 200 OK
DELETE /api/projects/3abde864-e853-4350-aa53-5ccc1a6fafa6 HTTP/1.1 200 OK
POST /cleanup/project HTTP/1.1 200 OK
DELETE /api/models/4eea8f0a-... HTTP/1.1 200 OK
GET  /api/projects/3abde864-e853-4350-aa53-5ccc1a6fafa6/research-package/preview?sessionId=6bcfc3e0-...&defaults=1 HTTP/1.1 404 Not Found
```

The same log carries **59** such `404` responses on `research-package/preview`, and in another case the deleted Session is still polled directly:

```text
GET /api/sessions/c6603f8c-e86e-46dd-a455-b87ff206c4fd/runs HTTP/1.1 404 Not Found
GET /api/sessions/c6603f8c-e86e-46dd-a455-b87ff206c4fd/agent-activity HTTP/1.1 404 Not Found
```

So the panel keeps polling a project/session that teardown has just removed. The browser logs every 404 as a console error, and the journey's "no console errors" assertion turns that into a failed case.

**Expected.** One of these, whichever the team prefers:

1. A mounted panel stops polling once its project/session is deleted (listen for the deletion the test performs, or cancel the poll on unmount).
2. The preview read treats "project gone" as a normal end of polling and does not surface it as a console error (checked request + handled 404, instead of an unhandled resource load).
3. The assertion is scoped to the case's own session being alive.

(1) is the honest fix: the product should not keep asking the API about a project it has removed.

### Detailed Environment Information Description

- Repository: `openJiuwen-ai/sciencediscovery`, `main` at `4bb737c2fccc8b55471dfd08f4f58754c5981cb3`.
- Mocked E2E (`profile: daily`, `L2 E2E (mocked, standard-journeys)`), 88 planned / 87 passed / 1 failed; run started 2026-11-10T21:44:15Z (2026-11-11 05:44 CST).
- Stack: adapter 4410 → Node API 4510, runner 4411, memory-graph 17774; no real model calls in this job.

### Additional Information

This is a harness/teardown race rather than a user-facing delivery failure, but it reds the mocked gate on its own. It is unrelated to the four real-E2E failures on the same run (see the linked issues).

### Version Information

- `main` @ `4bb737c2fccc8b55471dfd08f4f58754c5981cb3`
- Nightly run 42907916462; job 130151439627; artifact `mocked-e2e-results-standard-journeys` (13807782121)

recent.body:
## Background and environment

During a source installation on a Debian 13 cloud desktop on 2026-10-11, using main commit `5ddaa38bd68a84e4e20b14116d91880fe87bdd08`, two problems required manual investigation:

1. The desktop terminal did not inherit the outbound proxy environment. The initial managed micromamba download failed with `ECONNREFUSED`; an installation environment with the required network configuration could complete the download.
2. When the adapter inherited a SOCKS proxy configuration, it failed to start because `socksio` was missing, affecting access to the application.

The first observation is an environment-triggered failure, not proof of a downloader implementation defect. The second has a concrete dependency declaration gap.

## Conditions and observed behavior

### A. Different proxy environments across installation and runtime entry points

- External access required a proxy, but the terminal initiating scientific-environment preparation did not inherit the corresponding configuration.
- The micromamba connection was refused and scientific-environment preparation could not complete.
- Installation succeeded through an official download/install path with the necessary network configuration, retaining the pinned version and SHA-256 verification.
- The scientific environment subsequently became ready, with Python 3.12, NumPy, pandas, SciPy, and Matplotlib available.

### B. SOCKS configuration prevents adapter startup

- Create a clean adapter environment from the declared project dependencies and start it with a valid SOCKS proxy configuration.
- During HTTP client initialization, the missing socksio dependency prevents adapter startup.
- In this installation, adding socksio from official PyPI to the adapter's isolated environment restored startup; API health and page HTML checks then passed.

Source references:
- [Adapter declares plain httpx](https://github.com/openJiuwen-ai/sciencediscovery/blob/5ddaa38bd68a84e4e20b14116d91880fe87bdd08/services/adapter/pyproject.toml#L19-L25).
- [HTTP clients are constructed during startup](https://github.com/openJiuwen-ai/sciencediscovery/blob/5ddaa38bd68a84e4e20b14116d91880fe87bdd08/services/adapter/src/sciencediscovery_adapter/app.py#L47-L63).

## User impact

- Users may have already installed the source and other dependencies, yet still be blocked at first startup or scientific-environment preparation, preventing access to the workbench or relevant computations.
- Users must investigate differences between terminal and child-process proxy environments, and may need to install undeclared dependencies manually.
- A component-level failure can look like a failed installation of the entire application, leading to unnecessary reinstalls. This is not evidence that micromamba itself is unsuitable or unavailable.

## Expected behavior and proposed improvements

1. Unify installation/startup preflight checks: inspect the actual child process's proxy configuration, connectivity to required download sources, and dependencies for the selected proxy protocol. Report redacted status, never credentials.
2. Declare and lock SOCKS support, for example through `httpx[socks]`. Define the proxy boundary between loopback service calls and external requests, including correct `NO_PROXY` handling.
3. Identify the failing component, stage, underlying cause, and actionable next step. After configuration is corrected, allow retrying the failed step while reusing verified tools and caches.
4. Report Web entry point, adapter, and scientific-environment readiness separately instead of treating partial readiness as an all-or-nothing result.

The repository already has [download retry and cache mechanisms](https://github.com/openJiuwen-ai/sciencediscovery/blob/5ddaa38bd68a84e4e20b14116d91880fe87bdd08/scripts/fetch-managed-micromamba.mjs#L179-L295), as well as [classified errors and mirror/preinstalled-tool recovery guidance](https://github.com/openJiuwen-ai/sciencediscovery/blob/5ddaa38bd68a84e4e20b14116d91880fe87bdd08/services/runner/src/environment-store.ts#L1138-L1173). The goal is to connect these capabilities into a coherent first-run experience, not to replace the downloader.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] A clean adapter environment starts with HTTP/SOCKS proxy configurations without manually installing undeclared dependencies.
- [ ] Missing or incorrect proxy configuration produces redacted, actionable diagnostics while retaining the underlying error.
- [ ] Correcting configuration allows retrying the failed step and reusing verified artifacts, without clearing all data or reinstalling.
- [ ] Version pinning and hash verification remain enforced; recovery does not disable TLS verification.
- [ ] Tests cover no proxy, HTTP/SOCKS proxies, unreachable download sources, and successful retry after correction; installation documentation is updated.

Related: #29 (actionable dependency preflight), #213 and #229 (onboarding feedback). This issue focuses on the observed proxy-related failures and first-install recovery experience.

recent.body:
### 🚀 Background Description

Exporting a session works today, but the dialog is still shaped like a developer tool rather than a user task. Everything a user needs in order to decide *what* they are handing off, *how big* it will be, and *what happened* to the last export is either missing, misleading, or only reachable by reopening a modal. This is the session-export UI design work, desktop first.

The save flow itself was fixed in #986 / PR #999 (native save dialog, automatic save, per-export tracking) and the capability is specified in #803, so this issue is not about those. It is about the presentation of scope, size, progress and outcome.

Observations from the current desktop UI (`apps/desktop/src/views/ResearchPackage.tsx`, main 2026-11-09) and from a real export of a session with evolve runs and scientific memory (build `c95f080a`):

| What the user sees | What is actually true | Why it misleads |
| --- | --- | --- |
| 预计大小（未压缩）**910.6 MiB** on the 完整导出 card | the saved `.sdresearch` was **19.2 MiB** (20,161,641 bytes) | one number, 46× the real file; it is `estimateKind: "uncompressed"` and the label is the only hint |
| no size limit anywhere in the dialog | the archive cap is **512 MiB**, checked against the *compressed* archive (`packages/research-package/src/index.ts:15`, `:231`) | the one size shown cannot be compared with the limit that decides success |
| 完整导出 + 包含完整轨迹详情 + 包含完整科学记忆图谱 → packaging runs, then fails | `Research package exceeds the archive size limit`, in **English**, inside a zh-CN UI | minutes of packaging for an outcome that was predictable, plus an untranslated, unactionable message |
| 正在计算范围与大小… forever, primary button disabled | `EXPORT_PREVIEW_PENDING`, retried every 1.5 s with no cap and no explanation (`ResearchPackage.tsx:217-227`) | no reason, no retry, no cancel, no way to know whether waiting helps (#1018) |
| a single line `N 个导出进行中`, expandable to filenames | phases (packaging / saving) and destination are known to the client but not shown | the user cannot tell "still packing" from "packed, now writing to disk" |
| cancelling your own export | `pushFlash("error", t.exportCanceled)` — a red error (`:152`, `:271`, `:350`) | a deliberate user action is reported as a failure |
| 已保存的会话包 list inside the export modal | the list is component state only; the shell persists just `lastExportDir` (`win_desktop/src/export-state.ts`) | after restarting the app the history is gone, and "打开文件位置" cannot be used for an earlier package |
| 导出会话 only in the session row menu (`Sidebar.tsx:210`) | — | a first-class task is buried three levels down |
| import dialog: title, object count, `omissions` | per-dimension content is unavailable (`PackageInspection` has no counts) | the user cannot see what will be restored before committing; this is also how evolve runs disappear silently (#1019) |

### Design Ideas

**1. Make the choice about content, not about jargon.** Replace the two profile cards' taglines with a per-dimension table for the selected profile — 会话 / 消息 / 产物 / 产物版本 / 工作区文件 / 执行记录 / 任务 / 科学记忆节点 / 关系 — and render the two optional switches nested under 完整导出 with their *delta* shown on the same table and on the size line. The server already computes these numbers (`countExport`, with Chinese labels in `services/api/src/research-snapshots.ts:444`); the preview payload simply does not expose them yet.

**2. Show two honest numbers and the limit.** `未压缩 ≈ 910.6 MiB` is useful for disk planning; `归档 ≈ 19.2 MiB` is what the user copies around and what the cap applies to. Show the archive limit as a meter, and once a package exists show its real archive size. Before packaging, if the selection is over the limit, say so on the card and offer the fix (drop 完整轨迹 / 完整记忆图谱, or switch to 必要导出) instead of starting a task that must fail.

**3. A durable export center instead of a transient modal.** Turn the export surface into a panel/sheet with two blocks: the scope form above, a persistent list below (filename, archive size, time, state, destination, 打开文件位置, 重新保存). The list must survive closing the panel and restarting the app, and `已取消` must be a neutral state, not a red error. Keep the modal as the confirmation step if a modal is still wanted; keeping state in component memory is what loses it.

**4. Explain blocked and pending states.** When the preview cannot settle, say why in user terms ("该会话有一个执行停在恢复流程，导出范围暂不可确定" is the #1018 case), and offer 重试 / 取消 / 查看该执行. A disabled primary button with a spinner is not a state.

**5. Give the task a first-class entry.** A 导出 button in the session header (`SessionBar`), with the row-menu item kept as a shortcut. Import stays where it is.

**6. Localize and make failures actionable.** Server errors reach the UI untranslated (`task.error` is rendered raw at `:321` and flashed at `:153`). Map known failures (archive limit, changed revision, missing task, preview pending) to zh-CN copy with a next step; keep the raw string behind a details disclosure, consistent with the failure-alert principle in #846.

**7. Import side, same information standard.** Show the same per-dimension counts from the package manifest in the inspect step, plus an explicit "不会恢复" block (this is where an evolve omission must appear, #1019), so the user decides before importing rather than discovering an empty Evolve panel afterwards.

Alternatives not selected: restyling the existing modal without changing what it shows; auto-selecting 完整导出; removing the size estimate entirely (users need it for disk planning); moving export into the settings page.

### Involved Public APIs

Additive only, no breaking change:

- `GET /api/projects/{projectId}/research-package/preview` — add `counts` (same shape as `countExport`), `archiveLimitBytes`, and if a cheap estimate is acceptable `estimatedArchiveBytes`. Keep `estimateKind` so a client never mistakes the two.
- `POST .../research-package/exports` and `GET .../exports/{id}` — expose the finished archive size (`archiveBytes`) so the list can show it without a download.
- `POST .../research-package/inspect` — expose the manifest `counts` already present in the package manifest.

`apps/web` and `apps/desktop` share `apps/desktop/src/api/research-package.ts` shapes, so both must keep working; web keeps the browser-download destination, desktop keeps the token-bound native save.

### Description of Relevance to Other Modules

| Module | Responsibility |
| --- | --- |
| `apps/desktop/src/views/ResearchPackage.tsx` | Scope form, counts table, size meter, export center, localized failures |
| `apps/desktop/src/views/SessionBar.tsx`, `Sidebar.tsx`, `App.tsx` | Entry point and panel wiring |
| `apps/desktop/src/styles/research-package.css`, `text/zh.ts`, `text/en.ts` | Layout and copy, both languages |
| `win_desktop` (`export-state.ts`, `preload.ts`, `main.ts`) | Persisted export list, destination tokens, reveal-in-folder |
| `services/api` (`research-snapshots.ts`) | Preview payload, counts, limit, archive size |
| `packages/research-package` | `MAX_TOTAL_BYTES`, manifest counts, omission strings |
| `apps/web` | Same view; parity required but not the focus |

### Test Design and Test Plan

- Component tests for the new blocks: counts table renders server counts; the size block shows both numbers and never labels the archive size as the estimate; an over-limit selection warns before `startExport` is called; cancel renders neutral; unknown server errors fall back to the raw string behind details.
- E2E on the desktop build with the real local stack, using a session that has evolve runs and scientific memory (the fixture from #1019):
  - 必要导出 and 完整导出 each round-trip to a saved `.sdresearch`, and the counts shown in the dialog match `POST .../inspect` of the produced package.
  - 完整导出 with both switches on the oversized session shows the pre-flight warning instead of a late English failure.
  - restart the app: the export list still shows the saved package and 打开文件位置 works.
  - cancel during packaging and during saving: neutral state, no error flash.
  - preview blocked (session with a stuck execution): the dialog explains the reason and offers retry/cancel.
- Import: inspect shows counts and the explicit not-restored list; compare against the live imported session.
- Commands: `pnpm --filter @sciencediscovery/desktop typecheck`, `pnpm --filter @sciencediscovery/desktop test`, `pnpm --filter @sciencediscovery/desktop build`, `pnpm ci:l1`. Screenshots of the export panel (necessary, complete with switches, over-limit warning, export list after restart) go in the PR body for the owner's visual approval, per the UI review rule.

### Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] The export scope step shows per-dimension counts for the selected profile, and the two optional switches show their effect on those counts and on size.
- [ ] The size block shows the uncompressed estimate and the archive size/limit distinctly; no single number is presented as the file the user will copy.
- [ ] A selection that cannot fit the archive limit is reported before packaging, with the fix offered on the card.
- [ ] Progress shows per-task state (packaging / saving) and destination; the export list survives closing the panel and restarting the app, and 打开文件位置 works for earlier packages.
- [ ] Cancelling a self-initiated export is neutral, not an error; known failures are localized with an actionable next step, raw text only behind details.
- [ ] A blocked preview names its cause and offers retry/cancel.
- [ ] Import inspection shows the same per-dimension counts and an explicit "will not be restored" list.
- [ ] Both zh-CN and en copy exist; `pnpm --filter @sciencediscovery/desktop typecheck|test|build` and `pnpm ci:l1` pass.
- [ ] The owner has seen the screenshots in the PR body before approval.

### Additional Information

Related: #803 (feature scope), #986 (save flow, closed by PR #999), #846 (localized, non-redundant failure presentation), #1018 (a session whose preview never settles — the blocked-state copy is a product decision there), #1019 (evolve runs absent from the package — the import "will not be restored" block must state it), #995 (import opens two sessions), #801 (desktop scientific memory), #798 (desktop evolve).

Measured numbers quoted above come from one real session on build `c95f080a`: 完整导出 preview 933,095,424 bytes uncompressed → saved archive 20,161,641 bytes; 完整导出 with both switches → `Research package exceeds the archive size limit`. The failure is not reproduced by any test in this issue description; it was observed by hand.
