stale.body:
## Context

Since July 2026 an open-source "science workbench" category has formed, triggered by Anthropic's Claude Science launch (2026-06-30). Three direct open-source alternatives appeared the same week and are now at scale: [synthetic-sci/openscience](https://github.com/synthetic-sciences/openscience) (~3.6K★), [aipoch/open-science](https://github.com/aipoch/open-science) (~4.2K★), and [ai4s-research/open-science](https://github.com/ai4s-research/open-science) (~1.7K★). Having compared ScienceDiscovery against them (and against the autonomous-scientist systems: Sakana AI-Scientist, InternScience/InternAgent + MLEvolve), here is a strengths/gaps assessment in the hope it helps prioritization. Facts below are from public repo data collected 2026-09-15.

## Strengths (keep — and communicate)

1. **Sandbox-first security model.** Fail-closed Bubblewrap/Seatbelt execution, operator-scoped NPU chip passthrough, opt-in Broker with fixed entry points and `shell: false`. None of the three competitors communicates a default-isolation story; the highest-engagement technical question on a competitor's launch thread was literally *"are the skills executed within a secure, containerized sandbox by default, or does the user manage isolation?"* — this repo already answers that question, but almost nobody knows it does.
2. **Provenance depth.** CAS with pinned-asset drift rejection, review checks, cross-session/SubAgent citation chains. The strongest provenance story in the category.
3. **Search-camp RSI engine.** The evolve sidecar (flat-PUCT tree + OpenEvolve MAP-Elites, discriminability probe, explicit "no model training, no search-rule modification") is a clean, honest scope with a real cousin in [InternScience/MLEvolve](https://github.com/InternScience/MLEvolve) (#1 on MLE-Bench).
4. **Ascend NPU path.** 910B sandbox passthrough + allowlisted workloads (Protenix/MindScience) is unique in the category and extends machine-verifiable research to device-scale workloads.
5. **Engineering discipline beyond repo age.** Bilingual doc set, CI tiers (UT/ST/mocked E2E), self-documented limitations (e.g., Idea Tree scores are model judgments, not experimental evidence).

## Gaps (ordered by leverage)

1. **Installation/onboarding.** No binaries in Releases — #1 (open since 08-19, rated 1/5) is the only organic user feedback this repo has received, and it is someone who *could not install the product*. All three competitors ship desktop installers and a <10-minute quickstart. This pairs directly with the first-experience goal in #22.
2. **No community surface.** All merged PRs are bots; there are zero human external PRs. For comparison: aipoch merges 6+ human PRs/day; ai4s-research power users file bugs *and* land the fixes (e.g., their stall-guard for looping agents came from a user). A "good first issue" ladder + a contributor guide + weekly maintainer RFC triage would start the flywheel.
3. **Category invisibility + an unverifiable benchmark claim.** 58★ vs 1.7–4.2K for peers; one promotion event found (Sina Finance 2026-08-16) whose headline claim (BiomniBench-DA "业界SOTA") is dual-claimed by aipoch's README badge on the same benchmark. Without published methodology/splits, the claim reads as marketing and hurts credibility with scientists — either publish the eval or drop the superlative.
4. **Adoption levers validated by competitors, still missing here:** headless CLI / task API (repeated cross-repo demand — researchers want CI and agent-to-agent use, not only a GUI), model-provider onboarding (subscription reuse, connectivity-test friction), Windows parity.
5. **Cross-model skill consistency.** The single most-validated complaint in the category: *"one flag switches the model, not whether the skill actually works"* (prompts tuned on one model degrade on smaller/local models). A per-skill model-compatibility matrix or a cross-model smoke-test suite for the 300+ skills would directly differentiate.

## Suggested next steps

- [ ] Ship Linux binaries + a 10-minute quickstart (pairs with #22)
- [ ] Publish evolve/idea-tree efficiency metrics (per-node token cost, CAS reuse rate, surviving-node quality on an independent benchmark) — the pruning+reuse efficiency story is genuinely differentiating and no competitor tells it
- [ ] Benchmark-claim triage: methodology for BiomniBench-DA or remove the SOTA wording
- [ ] Community ladder: CONTRIBUTING good-first-issues + a maintainer-reserved RFC-triage day

Happy to help flesh any of these out.
stale.title: [Feedback] Strengths and gaps vs. the 2026 open-source science-workbench landscape

items.author: yuanzhou75
items.body:
Closes #1109.

A Native run persisted **one** usage row, and its token fields were the **last main-agent turn**; the parent's other turns and every subagent turn never reached the ledger. Measured on the reported session: 5 runs, 599 per-turn figures, 5 rows, and 0.3796 % of the input the provider reported for the session.

## Owner

**PR-bot-2号** (`@yuanzhou75`). The account is shared by the team's Bots, so the author line cannot distinguish them; this line is for the ownership register.

## The shape this implements

The maintainer chose **one row per invocation, with subagents as their own rows**, and **no backfill of existing rows**. Both are recorded on the issue; this is what they mean in code.

| row | `invocationKind` | tokens | window |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| the run | `task` | the **sum** over the run's main-agent turns, with `turnsRecorded` | the run's manifest, as before |
| each delegated child | `delegation-track` (declared in `packages/schema/src/model-usage.ts` and, until now, written by nobody) | that child's own sum, with `turnsRecorded` | the child's `createdAt` → its `usage` event |

So a row's token figures now describe the same scope as its `startedAt`/`finishedAt`, which they did not before: the old row paired the whole run's window with a single turn's tokens.

## What changed

**`packages/runtime-core/src/runtime.ts`** — the loop emitted one figure per turn and kept only the last (`usage = modelTurn.usage`). It cannot add `TUsage` itself — the loop is generic and does not know the shape — so it takes an optional `accumulateUsage(previous, next)`. With it, `AgentLoopResult.usage` is the run's total and the result carries `turnsWithUsage`; without it, `usage` keeps its old meaning, so no other caller changes behaviour.

**`packages/model/src/usage.ts`** — `addUsage`, the shape-aware adder: counts add, and a field the provider never reports stays `null` rather than becoming `0`.

**`services/api/src/model-usage/index.ts`** — `addCapturedModelUsage` for the persisted shape (unknown stays unknown; a turn that reported nothing leaves the total untouched), `turnsRecorded` on the record, and `appendDelegatedModelUsage` for the child row with its own window.

**`services/api/src/runs/index.ts`** — the run collector's single overwritten slot becomes a running total plus `modelTurnsRecorded`; each `model_usage` is now also **published to the run's stream** (it used to be consumed and dropped by an early `return`, which is why no `model_usage` record existed in the capture); the three persistence sites pass `turnsRecorded`; each child's `usage` event writes its `delegation-track` row.

**`packages/schema/src/session.ts`** — `model.usage` as a run-stream event: per-turn figures are persisted so a stored row can be recomputed from the record directory alone (criterion 4).

## Consequences, stated rather than discovered later

- A run that delegates now contributes **1 + K rows** instead of 1, and the parent's row grows from one turn's worth to the run's total. `ModelUsageBucket.invocationCount` and per-run spend will step up accordingly — that is the point of the change, and it is why the numbers on any dashboard will look different after this lands.
- **No historical backfill** (the maintainer's decision): existing rows are left exactly as written. They are distinguishable because they carry no `turnsRecorded`. An audit reader can tell which shape a row came from.
- Nothing materialises zeros: a run with no completed model turn keeps `provider-not-reported` and null fields.

## Verification

- `packages/model/src/usage.test.ts` — a new case sums two turns (400/60/460 from 100+300, 20+40, 120+340) and asserts a never-reported field stays `null` and that the first turn is the total. **Mutation check:** replacing the summation with the last turn turns it red (`actual: 300, expected: 400`).
- `services/api/src/model-usage.test.ts` — sums turns into a run row, keeps `provider-not-reported` when no turn reported, and does not count an unreported turn as zero.
- Both files are tagged `os:linux`; I ran them with the tag relaxed to `os:windows` on this Windows host (14/14 and 25/25) and left the tag as committed.
- `tsc --noEmit` clean for `packages/runtime-core`, `packages/model`, `packages/schema`, `services/api` and `tsconfig.tests.json`.
- What I did not run: the full `runs/index.ts` suite and any real session. The row-per-invocation path is covered at the writer level; the end-to-end effect on a real delegated run is CI's and a live session's to show, and I am not claiming a measured reconciliation against provider invoices here.

## Not fixed here

The 128-turn ceiling that inflated this particular loss (four children cut at 128) is a separate finding with its own draft; `MAX_MODEL_TURNS` is untouched.

items.title: fix(api): persist a run's summed usage and give delegated spend its own row

Closes #264
Supersedes #285 (thanks @zy95-12 for the original work — the core of this PR is inherited from it, with `Co-authored-by` trailers preserved on the inherited commits)

## What this does

Takes over the remaining scope of #264 by inheriting the valuable parts of #285 (its author stopped development) and adding the unclaimed win_desktop increment.

### Inherited from #285 (cleanly applied, 46 files)

- **`packages/network`** (new, dependency-free): `resolveRoute` / `proxyProcessEnvironment` / `redactNetworkError` / `withProxyFetch` — manual redirect handling, HTTPS-downgrade refusal, cross-origin credential stripping, scoped undici Agent lifecycle
- **`services/api` proxy connectivity**: user-initiated diagnostic `POST /api/proxy/test` (HEAD probe to the micromamba release host, 10s timeout, redacted output)
- **`services/runner`**: `AsyncLocalStorage`-scoped per-operation proxy policy; subprocess environments built via `proxyProcessEnvironment` (micromamba/conda/pip children inherit the proxy instead of hanging on unreachable mirrors); setup errors redacted
- **`scripts/fetch-managed-micromamba.mjs`**: downloader defaults to `withProxyFetch` (fixes Node fetch ignoring proxy env) + `redactNetworkError`
- **data-source / model / executor**: `resolveRoute` delegation (net −21 lines in `env.ts`), proxy-aware transports
- **Web UI**: staged-draft editing for proxy settings (entries staged in the dialog, persisted on Save), URL redaction in list display, "Network and proxy" grouping, WebSearch single entry point
- **Docs** (en + zh): installation/preflight/recovery guidance for proxy environments
- **`test/journey-proxy-settings.spec.ts`**: user-perspective E2E journey

### New in this PR (win_desktop increment, the #264 gap #285 did not cover)

The Windows desktop shell previously skipped the registry's `socks=` entry when mirroring the system proxy ("v1: direct beats half-broken"). Both stack consumers now speak SOCKS5 natively — undici 8.12.2 `ProxyAgent` (verified end-to-end: SOCKS5 greeting on the wire) and `httpx[socks]` in the adapter — so the mirror is no longer half-broken:

- `socks=host:port` → `ALL_PROXY=socks5://host:port` (+ lowercase), per-scheme `http=`/`https=` entries still win for their schemes, loopback `NO_PROXY` bypass preserved in every mirrored form
- Docs updated (undici 8.9 → 8.12 note + Windows mirror behaviour)

### Conflict resolution vs main@b2a4906 (6 files, manual merge)

- `fetch-managed-micromamba.mjs`: kept main's newer `maxRetryDelayMs`/`sleep` retry parameters, threaded through the new `withProxyFetch` default
- `adapter/app.py`: `InternalClient` consolidation kept main's `legacy_limits` keepalive fix (Node idle-close race) — `InternalClient` gained a `limits` passthrough, guarded against passing an explicit `None` to httpx (its default is a live `Limits` object)
- `test/issue-143-proxy-settings.spec.ts`: adapted to the new labels/staged-draft flow while keeping main's E2E-META annotations and drawer handling
- `http/index.ts`, `environment-store.ts`, `api/package.json`: straightforward unions of both sides

## Testing (local, Windows)

| Suite | Result |
| --- | --- |
| win_desktop full suite | 223/223 |
| win_desktop proxy (flipped socks assertion + mixed-config case) | 7/7 |
| api server / store / proxy-connectivity | pass (server suite covers the new `/api/proxy/test` route) |
| runner environment-store / server | pass |
| data-source / model / executor / schema | pass |
| apps/web ProxySettingsEditor | pass |
| typecheck (api, runner, data-source, model, executor, web) | pass |
| adapter `test_network.py` via `uv run --extra test` | 9/9 (after the limits guard fix) |
| adapter full suite | 273 passed, 10 failed — all environmental on Windows (Unix `0o600` permission assertions, live gateway/LLM cases tagged `os="linux"`); unrelated to this change |

Not verifiable locally: the Linux CI matrix, the Playwright journeys (`@os:linux`), and Python-side integration — left for CI.

Fixes #1117: the `llm-wiki` bridge and its TypeScript connector rejected Wiki page paths using Windows `\` separators, so a `search` `page_id` could not be passed to `get_page`/`get_pages`, although the connector already folds `\`→`/` on results.

Development was requested with `bot-develop`. Goal: fold `\`→`/` once, before every existing check, at each layer's single path-validation entry point, weakening no rule.

- `services/gateway/src/sciencediscovery_gateway/llm_wiki_mcp.py`: new `_fold_separators`; `_page_path` folds before the length/char/segment checks, so both tools share one rule. `get_pages` builds that list once and uses it for the request body and the `omitted_paths` comparison, and compares the provider's `pages[].path`/`missing[]` in the same folded form, so an echo of the Windows spelling is not reported as omitted.
- `packages/mcp-sources/src/llm-wiki.ts`: new `normalizePagePath`; `isPagePath` folds before validating and `validateInput` returns the folded `path`/`paths`, so the broker's forwarded body, cache key and permission strings see one spelling.

Tests: the backslash-rejection case became acceptance in both suites, plus search→`get_page`+`get_pages` round trips with verbatim Windows `page_id`s, a provider-echo case and an accept/refuse parity table. Reverting the source fix fails the new tests.

items.author: yuanzhou75
items.body:
Closes #1108.

`check_runner` used to answer a question the Agent had not asked: the tool binding dropped the route (`workspace-bindings.ts:416`), so an Agent got the Python-channel verdict (`requiresShell = false`, `:196`) whatever it was about to run — and the Runner's own payload fixed `ready: true, reason: "ready"` on the `sandbox === "none"` branch (`readiness.ts:42-47`) even when the probe beside it said `shell.available: false`. This makes the verdict route-scoped structurally, per the maintainer's choice of §2 option 2.


## The contract

`RunnerExecutionCapability` gains an optional `readyFor: { python: boolean; shell: boolean }`, and `reason` gains `"shell-unavailable"`:

| field | meaning |
| --- | --- |
| `ready` | unchanged: the Python channel (a Shell gap never blocks it — PR #716's design is kept) |
| `reason` | derived from the probe on the `none` branch instead of fixed at `"ready"`; says `"shell-unavailable"` when the managed Shell is dead |
| `readyFor.python` | sandbox and dependency usable, Shell plays no part |
| `readyFor.shell` | `python` **and** the managed Shell usable; an absent `shell` field stays unknown, not false |

`check_runner`'s result now carries the same `readyFor`, and its headline `reason` is never the bare word `"ready"` while the same object reports a dead Shell. The parameter schema did **not** grow a route option: no new caller knowledge, and no new probe — `shellCapability()` already ran in the same probe, the answer was just discarded.

## What changed, file by file

- `packages/schema/src/environment.ts` — `readyFor` on `RunnerExecutionCapability`, `"shell-unavailable"` in the `reason` union, `readyFor` mirrored on `RunnerCheckResult`. Optional, because an older Runner cannot report it (same treatment as `shell?`).
- `services/runner/src/readiness.ts` — the `none` branch derives `reason`/`readyFor` from the probe; the sandboxed branch reports `readyFor` from its own sandbox verdict; the initial `report` literal carries `{python: false, shell: false}`.
- `services/api/src/agent-run/workspace-bindings.ts` — `checkRunner` computes both routes from `readyFor` when present and falls back to `ready` + `shell.available` for an older Runner; a Shell caller gets the Shell verdict and its real reason.
- `services/runner/src/server.ts` — startup now warns when the managed Shell is dead. The existing `if (!capability.ready)` could never fire on that branch, which is why the 10-hour capture in the issue produced no startup complaint.
- `services/runner/src/environment-store.ts` — the provisioning transcript is bounded (1200 chars + a pointer to the Runner log) so one failure does not put a 14 KB libmamba dump into a model result.
- `services/api/src/agent-run/workspace-bindings.ts` — the advice no longer repeats that transcript (it was in `capability.detail`, `capability.shell.unavailableReason` **and** `suggestions[0]`), and the `wait_for_runner` cancel branch no longer sends the caller to `check_runner` to recheck a blocker the check could not report.
- `packages/workspace/src/workspace.ts` — the tool description says what `ready` covers and to read the route you intend to use.

## Verification

- `services/api/src/agent-run/workspace-bindings.test.ts` — new case drives the **tool-facing binding** (`runnerReadiness.check`, which is what `check_runner` calls) with `{ready: true, reason: "shell-unavailable", readyFor: {python: true, shell: false}}` and asserts: the model-visible JSON carries `readyFor` naming both routes, `reason` is not `"ready"`, `capability.reason` is `"shell-unavailable"`, and the advice does not repeat the transcript. It also pins that the binding takes only two parameters — the reason the verdict has to be structural rather than something a caller passes in.
- `services/runner/src/readiness.test.ts` — the `none` branch now asserts `reason: "shell-unavailable"` and `readyFor: {python: true, shell: false}` while `ready` stays `true`; the repaired probe asserts `{python: true, shell: true}`; the no-probe case asserts `{python: true, shell: true}` with `shell` still absent (unknown ≠ unavailable).
- Mutation check: putting `reason` back to the literal `"ready"` turns the runner case red.
- Direct probe on this head with `shellProbe → available: false`: `{ready: true, reason: "shell-unavailable", readyFor: {python: true, shell: false}}`; with `available: true`: `{ready: true, reason: "ready", readyFor: {python: true, shell: true}}`.
- `tsc --noEmit` clean for `packages/schema`, `packages/workspace`, `services/runner`, `services/api` and `tsconfig.tests.json`.
- **`services/runner/src/readiness.test.ts` cannot run on this machine (POSIX dependency)** — its bubblewrap/seatbelt cases spawn a shell script, one asserts `platform === "linux"`, and several remove a temp directory that SQLite still holds on Windows. Its result here is therefore not a verdict on this change either way, and **CI covers it**. The route-scoped assertions I added are independently evidenced by the direct probe above and by the API-side case. The same host limitation makes 3 cleanup cases in `workspace-bindings.test.ts` fail with `EBUSY`, before and after this change alike.

## Not changed on purpose

- Python execution is never blocked by a Shell gap (criterion 9): `ready` keeps the Python meaning and `prepareExecutionTarget(..., requiresShell = false)` still reads it.
- An absent `shell` field still means "unknown", not "unavailable".
- The `RUNNER_UNAVAILABLE` repair instruction and the `wait_for_runner` card delivered by #1095 and #265 are unchanged; only the cancel branch's closing sentence changed, as criterion 7 asks.
items.head: fix-1108-route-scoped-readiness
items.title: fix(runner): make the readiness verdict route-scoped so check_runner cannot contradict run_shell

items.author: yuanzhou75
items.body:
Closes #1081

## What was wrong

Readiness was configuration-only. `statusFor()` (`packages/data-source/src/catalog.ts`) compares the tools an MCP server advertises with the manifests and never asks a provider anything, so a connector whose every call failed still read `ready`. The only way anyone learned an integration was down was an agent that called it and reported the `UPSTREAM_UNAVAILABLE` guidance back — which is how #1049 was found, and what §10 of that issue repeats. (The issue names `services/api/src/plugins/catalog.ts`; readiness actually lives in `packages/data-source/src/catalog.ts`.)

## Change

**A memory of provider outages** (`packages/data-source/src/source-outage.ts`)

The broker records the last provider-level failure per source and the catalog reports it beside the status it already computes.

**The predicate is the reviewer's — provider-level only.** `recordedOutage` judges the attempt the way admission does: a declared endpoint scope (`failureScope === "endpoint"`), or a `transport-error` / `server-error`. Nothing else is recorded. This matters because `upstreamError()` falls back to `UPSTREAM_UNAVAILABLE` for any attempt status it does not map, and the node client classifies a tool-reported `isError` as `semantic-error` — so an invalid query or a DOI the provider cannot resolve used to record a ten-minute outage and render `Last upstream outage: SEMANTIC_ERROR`. `SourceHealth` already treats those as request-specific; readiness no longer contradicts it.

**The endpoint code is preserved.** A declared endpoint scope is recorded as `ENDPOINT_UNAVAILABLE`, not as the tool-level `SEMANTIC_ERROR` it used to inherit. That is the one endpoint-level signal that exists today (the 406 refusal in `http_errors.py`), and it stays distinguishable from a request-scoped rejection. A transport/server failure records `UPSTREAM_UNAVAILABLE`.

**Advisory by construction.** `getStatus()` attaches `lastOutage` and changes nothing else: `status`, `error` and `missingTools` are exactly what configuration says. That is deliberate — `status !== "ready"` is a gate at three call sites (`http/index.ts:3133`, `:3172`, `:4704`), so a signal that flipped it would disable a working-but-flaky connector on a transient error. The record expires after ten minutes, which is unrelated to the broker's 30–120 s cooling windows: cooling governs admission, this only governs what readiness says.

**One explicit instance.** The bootstrap constructs a single `SourceOutages` and passes it to both the catalog and the broker, instead of the two sides reaching the same module-level default by accident.

**Visible where a maintainer looks** (`packages/mcp/src/connector-picker.tsx`, `apps/web/src/i18n/messages.ts`, `apps/web/src/styles/conversation.css`)

The composer's connector picker draws the line next to the readiness line it already has, in both locales, and takes the recorded provider message as its tooltip rather than shipping `detail` unused. It now has its own rule: without one it inherited `label small` (`nowrap` + `ellipsis`), so the sentence was clipped at the popover's 340 px width in the muted colour instead of the warning colour. It reuses the theme variable and the same treatment as `.connector-picker-status`.

## Screenshots

Real component (`renderToStaticMarkup`), with the real stylesheet inlined (`apps/web/src/styles/{tokens,base,primitives,conversation}.css`) and the popover rendered open in both locales. The Chinese line is the long one — `最近一次上游故障：ENDPOINT_UNAVAILABLE（2026/11/11 21:00:00）` — and it wraps onto two lines rather than truncating, in the warning colour.

![Recorded upstream outage shown in the connector picker, zh-CN and en](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/yuanzhou75/sciencediscovery/screenshots-1081/docs/screenshots/1081/connector-picker-last-outage.png)

Not an Electron window and not a live app session: this is renderer-level, which is what the change is. Stated so it is not read as more than it is.

## Tests

`packages/data-source/src/source-outage.test.ts`:

- the record survives to the last second of the window and is forgotten after it, per source;
- `getStatus` returns the outage **and** `status: "ready"` unchanged, with `availableTools` untouched;
- **new** — a tool-level rejection, a rate limit, a broker cooldown and a record-scoped 404 record **nothing**;
- **new** — a transport failure records `UPSTREAM_UNAVAILABLE`; a 406 endpoint refusal records `ENDPOINT_UNAVAILABLE` with the provider's message, and is what `getStatus` then reports.

`apps/web/tests/ConnectorPicker.test.tsx`: a `ready` connector with a recorded outage renders the line, and the status is asserted to stay `ready`.

## Verification

- `tsc --noEmit` clean for `packages/schema`, `packages/data-source`, `packages/mcp`, against the exact files this PR pushes.
- `source-outage.test.ts`: **4/4**. The suite declares `os:linux`, so the tagged collector no-ops on this Windows host; I ran the same file with the platform forced to the declared one.
- `services/api`: one error remains, `platform.ts(495) readText not in ProposalDeps`. It is a stale-checkout artifact, not this change: the same error is produced by `main`'s `platform.ts` with my three lines stripped, and none of them touch that line. CI is authoritative for that package.
- `apps/web` type-check is not usable as evidence here either (pre-existing errors from the older checkout); the picker compiles clean in `packages/mcp` and the change is one rule plus three attributes.

items.body:
## What the failing case actually did

`test/agent-run-componentization.spec.ts` > `S2b` failed on `no console/page errors expected`. Its `trace.zip` has exactly **two** `research-package/preview` requests, both 404, and the two bodies are different:

| time (UTC) | body | cause |
|---|---|---|
| 21:51:21.978 | `{"error":"File not found"}` | an `ENOENT` mapped to 404 at `services/api/src/http/index.ts:4381` |
| 21:51:35.966 | `{"code":"EXPORT_PREVIEW_RESOURCE_DELETED"}` | the preview was aborted because the Project was deleted (`research-export-previews.ts:197-213`) |

The same `stack.log` (artifact `mocked-e2e-results-standard-journeys`) shows the wider pattern on a Session that no longer exists: `GET /api/sessions/<id>/runs`, `/agent-activity` and `/execution-blocks` answered 404 over and over, because the page stayed mounted and every poller kept asking. The preview poll alone accounts for 56 of the 404s in that run.

## What this changes

1. **The API answers a preview poll of a deleted scope with `200 { state: "deleted" }`.** The panel is only asking "how big is the export for the Session I am showing"; once that Project or Session is gone, there is nothing to preview, and a 4xx here is what the browser turns into a console error. A preview aborted by that same deletion answers the same way. A **download** of a package whose Project is gone keeps its 404: that request is a mistake worth reporting, a poll is not.
2. **The export dialog stops offering actions on a gone scope.** Its own 3-second poll receives the same answer; from then on the estimate and file list stay on screen as the pre-deletion snapshot while **both export buttons are disabled**, and the alert says so instead of claiming nothing is left to preview.

   (An earlier version of this PR also stopped a `ResearchPackagePreviewMonitor` on that answer. `main` deleted that component in `63f20d9e`, and my rebase had carried it back in as a new file; it is deleted again here. Re-mounting it would reverse that commit and is a maintainer decision, not part of this fix.)
3. **The agent-activity panel stops asking too.** On `Session not found` it keeps the message it already renders and clears its list, instead of re-reading `/agent-activity` every 2 seconds forever.

The client turns the `deleted` answer into an `ApiRequestError` carrying `EXPORT_PREVIEW_RESOURCE_DELETED` (`apps/web/src/api/plugins.ts`), so both callers recognise it without parsing text.

The journey assertion in `test/agent-run-componentization.spec.ts:443` is **not touched** - no skipped console errors, no scoping by session, no filtered stream.

## What this does not fix

The first 404 of that case is `File not found`, an `ENOENT` inside a preview of a **live** Project: it precedes the delete and comes from the generic `ENOENT ? 404` mapping, not from the deletion. This PR only converts such an error when the Project or Session is in fact gone. Naming the failing read is separate work, now tracked in **#1099**; it is not claimed here.

## Scope of the API change

Only the polling shape ends quietly. `GET /api/projects/{id}/research-package/preview?sessionId=…&defaults=1` — the request a mounted panel repeats every 3 s — answers `200 {"state":"deleted"}` once its Project or Session is gone, and so does a preview aborted by that same deletion. A one-shot preview read (`?level=…` without `defaults`) keeps its `404 EXPORT_PREVIEW_RESOURCE_DELETED`, because there the caller asked once and the answer is worth reporting, and a package download keeps its 404 as well.

`services/api/src/research-package-http.test.ts` > `preview deletion ends the poll quietly while shutdown and the one-shot read keep their status` pins that split: poll `200 {"state":"deleted"}`, one-shot 404, `503` still 503 for both shapes. Without the route change the same case fails with `actual: 404, expected: 200`.

## Verification

- `apps/web`: `tsc -p tsconfig.json --noEmit` clean on this head.
- `apps/web/tests/ResearchPackageGonePolling.test.tsx`: **1/1** — the file keeps only the `AgentActivityPanel` case, because `main` deleted the preview monitor in `63f20d9e`.
- `apps/web/tests/AgentActivityPanel.test.tsx`: 8/8 with the changed panel, including the existing "session miss does not stick" case.
- `services/api/src/research-package-http.test.ts`: 20/20 on this head, including the poll-200 / one-shot-404 / 503 split.
- **Not measured locally:** the mocked journey. This machine has no working pnpm install for the API workspace (the shared tree sits at a different commit), so that half is CI-confirmed.

## Screenshots — both deleted-scope states, in the export dialog

Captured on **`e7065e89`**: the web app served from this head's own source, with the real API running from the same head against a fresh data directory. The sample Session and its 15 workspace files are real; the Project is deleted through `DELETE /api/projects/{id}`, so the dialog learns about it only from its own poll — the case this PR fixes. No network mocking: the two states differ only in *when* the deletion lands.

**State A — the dialog was open with a snapshot, then the Project was deleted.**
The same 4742.5 KiB estimate and 15 files stay on screen, and the sentence points at them *above*, with both export actions disabled.

**State B — the Project was already gone when the dialog was opened.**
No cached snapshot exists, so the estimate and both scope cards read `—` instead of "Calculating size…", and the sentence says there is no size any more rather than claiming a snapshot.

**zh-CN — A before / A after / B after**

![zh-CN A before: estimate 4742.5 KiB, both export actions live](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/yuanzhou75/sciencediscovery/screenshots-1074/docs/screenshots/1074/head-e7065e89/zh-A-before.png)
![zh-CN A after: 预计 4742.5 KiB kept, alert 该项目或会话已不存在；上方为删除前的大小，已不能导出。, 后台导出 and 立即导出 disabled](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/yuanzhou75/sciencediscovery/screenshots-1074/docs/screenshots/1074/head-e7065e89/zh-A-deleted.png)
![zh-CN B after: estimate and both cards read —, alert 该项目或会话已不存在，已无法再读取大小。](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/yuanzhou75/sciencediscovery/screenshots-1074/docs/screenshots/1074/head-e7065e89/zh-B-deleted.png)

**en — A before / A after / B after**

![en A before: Estimated 4742.5 KiB, both export actions live](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/yuanzhou75/sciencediscovery/screenshots-1074/docs/screenshots/1074/head-e7065e89/en-A-before.png)
![en A after: Estimated 4742.5 KiB kept, alert This Project or Session no longer exists. The last known sizes are shown above; exporting is disabled., Background export and Immediate export disabled](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/yuanzhou75/sciencediscovery/screenshots-1074/docs/screenshots/1074/head-e7065e89/en-A-deleted.png)
![en B after: estimate and both cards read —, alert This Project or Session no longer exists; there is no size to show any more.](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/yuanzhou75/sciencediscovery/screenshots-1074/docs/screenshots/1074/head-e7065e89/en-B-deleted.png)

What the capture script printed, read from the DOM rather than from the images:

```
A  STRONGS=["必要导出","完整导出","预计 4742.5 KiB"]  ALERT="该项目或会话已不存在；上方为删除前的大小，已不能导出。"
   BUTTONS 后台导出=disabled 立即导出=disabled          ERRORS=[]
B  STRONGS=["必要导出","完整导出","—"]                ALERT="该项目或会话已不存在，已无法再读取大小。"
   BUTTONS 后台导出=disabled 立即导出=disabled          ERRORS=[]
en A  ALERT="This Project or Session no longer exists. The last known sizes are shown above; exporting is disabled."
en B  ALERT="This Project or Session no longer exists; there is no size to show any more."
```

One caveat, stated rather than hidden: after a deletion the **other** session-scoped pollers (`/runs`, `/agent-activity`) still answer 404 and raise the app's "Session not found" toast. That is outside this diff and is not what is claimed here — the preview poll this PR converts is answered `200 {"state":"deleted"}`, which is why the dialog stops.

Screenshots live on the `screenshots-1074` branch, not in the diff.

## Acting on the review of `f29c77f6` (F6)

The review's two points, both in `e7065e89`:

**The sentence now follows what is actually on screen, not `preview` alone.** `preview` is cleared when a file selection changes, while `necessarySize`/`completeSize` keep coming from `defaults` and survive the gone answer — so in that window the two scope cards showed "1.0 KiB" while the alert said there was no size. The sentence is chosen from `preview !== undefined || necessarySize !== undefined || completeSize !== undefined` (`ResearchPackageActions.tsx:225`), and a new case selects a file, leaves the custom preview unanswered, lands the gone answer, and asserts the sentence admits the sizes the cards still show.

**The evidence and the description are from this head.** The captures above are `e7065e89`, in both locales and both states; the alt texts and the F4 bullet below now quote the current wording, and this section is the F6 item.

## Acting on the review of `0e226467`

Two items came out of that review; both are in `82c9a75c`.

**The gone answer now belongs to the scope that asked for it** (the unresolved thread on `ResearchPackagePreviewMonitor.tsx:40`). The monitor stays mounted across a conversation switch, so a rejection from the previous scope that landed after the switch marked the *new* scope gone, both effects returned early, and its 3 s poll was never re-armed. Each request now captures its scope and compares it with the current one before setting `gone`. Pinned by a case that mounts on one conversation, switches while the request is in flight, then lets it answer `gone` and asserts the new scope still polls.

**A gone scope can no longer be exported** (F2, the `[Needs a person]` item). The dialog's own 3 s poll receives the same `deleted` answer; from that answer on, both export buttons are disabled. The last estimate and file list stay on screen as the pre-deletion snapshot rather than being cleared, which is the maintainer's decision: the dialog is only reachable while the scope exists, so this state comes from a concurrent deletion (another tab or another client), and a snapshot beside a disabled action reads better than an empty dialog. The paragraph above that described the preview as gone was wrong about this and is corrected.

Note on scope: `apps/desktop` is unaffected — its export dialog lost this option entirely in #1082.
## Acting on the review of `8eede370`

- **F5 (must-fix, rebase artifact):** the monitor `main` removed in `63f20d9e` is deleted again, and its three test cases went with it. The test file keeps only the `AgentActivityPanel` case, which covers a component `App.tsx` really mounts.
- **F4 (copy):** the alert describes the retained snapshot instead of denying it. Its wording was corrected again in F6 — en "…The last known sizes are shown above; exporting is disabled." / zh "该项目或会话已不存在；上方为删除前的大小，已不能导出。" — because the first version said "below" while rendering after the estimate.

Both threads are answered and resolved. `tsc -p tsconfig.tests.json --noEmit` is clean; the kept agent-activity case and the dialog case both pass.

Closes #1100. Requested: 「桌面端支持在会话内批准 `connector.enable`（session scope / same_run），至少提供「启用 / 不启用」两个明确动作」

The desktop 「启用连接器」 card showed only 「暂不支持，请用原版界面。」 plus one 「关闭」 button, which is recorded as a refusal. Past ten enabled connectors `domain-adapters.ts` summarizes the `enabledConnectorIds` diff as `"<N> connectors: <first 10 IDs> …"`, and `configuration-presentation.ts` refused every summarized diff.

## Change
`connector.enable` now also recognises that summarized diff: the adapter builds an enable as `[...new Set([...current, target])]`, so a real addition repeats the visible baseline unchanged and is one ID longer. When the ten visible IDs equal the baseline or its summary prefix, the count grows by one and the target is not visible, it is a `connectorAddition` and the card offers Confirm/Cancel. Exact lists and reversals keep their paths; unproven shapes still return `{unsupported: true}`.

New fixture `test/fixtures/configuration-connector-summarized-addition.json` is a real 11-connector proposal; the new api integration test replays it through the real store and framework, and the en/zh desktop tests cover the card.

## Validation
`cd apps/desktop && pnpm test` 1140 pass/0 fail; `cd services/api && node --import tsx --test src/configuration/*.test.ts` 418 pass/0 fail; `npx tsc -p tsconfig.tests.json`, package typechecks, `check-architecture.mjs`, `pnpm ci:catalog:check` clean; the new desktop tests fail pre-change. Not run: no browser/desktop E2E and no screenshots, and `architecture:check`'s scripts suite has 7 host failures (jiuwenswarm setup), identical at base.

## Risk and gates
Desktop surface: needs the maintainers' `UI` label and zh/en screenshots from a person. Residual: a summarized diff proves the adapter's append shape, not identities past the tenth ID, so a hand-built `restoreConnectorIds` proposal netting +1 could read as an addition; `framework.ts` rejects values starting with `restore`.

Release category: release:fix

Tests: cd apps/desktop && pnpm test
Reported by the agent; not rerun by the control plane.

items.body:
Fixes #945

## What changes

`apps/desktop` carries its own copy of the feedback screenshot pipeline (the same blob web had before #942). One multi-select of 10 screenshots attaches the first 8 and the other 2 vanish: `prepareFeedbackImages` stops at `FEEDBACK_MAX_IMAGES` and returns only `{ images }`, while the dialog can render an unsuccessful pick (`imageError`) but not a partially successful one.

This PR counts what the cap drops and says so in both desktop dictionaries:

1. `apps/desktop/src/feedback/feedback-images.ts` — `prepareFeedbackImages` returns `skipped: number`; every pick past the cap is counted (`continue` rather than `break`) so a multi-select is reported as a whole.
2. `apps/desktop/src/feedback/FeedbackDialog.tsx` — `skippedImages` state, rendered as one neutral `feedback-hint` beside the existing `preparing` hint when it is above zero, cleared on open, on remove, and after a successful submit.
3. `apps/desktop/src/text/en.ts` and `text/zh.ts` — `images.truncated: (max: number, skipped: number) => string`, function-valued like the `limit` entry beside it, with the wording #943 used for web so the two shells read the same.
4. `apps/desktop/tests/FeedbackImages.test.tsx` — three module assertions and two mounted-dialog assertions (10 picks and 2 picks, en and zh).

## Red first

The test landed before the implementation, and the readings below are that pair — the same three cases, run with and without the change:

```
$ node_modules/.bin/tsx --test tests/FeedbackImages.test.tsx
# before the implementation
not ok 1 - the desktop dialog counts the screenshots the eight-image cap drops
    undefined !== 2                      (also undefined !== 0 and undefined !== 1)
not ok 2 - an over-cap pick says how many screenshots were skipped, in English and Chinese
    actual: []                           (no feedback-hint for a ten-file pick)
ok     3 - a pick under the cap says nothing about skipped screenshots
# pass 1 / fail 2

# at this tip
ok 1 / ok 2 / ok 3
# pass 3 / fail 0
```

`skipped` was `undefined` before the change, so a ten-file pick could not report anything and the dialog had nothing to render. The third case passes in both states on purpose: the notice has to describe a dropped file, and a blanket banner would fail it.

## Ran / Not run

Ran:
- `apps/desktop` → `node_modules/.bin/tsx --test tests/*.test.ts tests/*.test.tsx` — **982 tests, 0 fail** (699 subtests, 123 suites).
- `apps/desktop` → `tsc -p tsconfig.json --noEmit` — clean.
- The red/green pair above.

Not run: `apps/web` (its own suite is untouched by this diff) and the desktop E2E journey, which needs the packaged shell.

This PR addresses intermittent failures in the token onboarding journey and the artifact tool bridge without adding test randomness. It keeps artifact reads concurrent while making transient read-only bridge failures recoverable.

## Changes

- Make the zh-CN startup-token journey consume the persisted token after reload and exercise invalid-token recovery through the mounted app's hashchange path.
- Give the HTTP response-error test a single teardown owner so shutdown cannot race outstanding response-drain work.
- Retry only idempotent `read_artifact` bridge calls after transport errors or HTTP 502/503/504 responses, using bounded fixed delays; write tools are never replayed.
- Add deterministic adapter tests covering transport recovery, concurrent reads, and the no-retry rule for write operations.

## Validation

Local tests were not run during PR preparation, as requested.

Before rebasing this change set onto the upstream `main`, the existing local validation was:

- Adapter focused tests: 73 passed.
- Full adapter suite: 300 passed; 9 external gateway/real-model tests were blocked because their services and credentials were unavailable.
- The final rebased commit was not rerun locally.

## E2E user journeys

BLOCKED — not run during PR preparation, as requested.

- Tested SHA: `516ec48b`.
- Browser journey `journey-local-token-onboarding`: the invalid-token hashchange and persisted-token reload scenarios were not rerun locally.
- API/adapter bridge behavior: the affected live stack journey was not rerun locally.
- Counts: passed 0, failed 0, blocked 2, skipped 0.

## Release

Release category: release:fix

User impact: startup-token recovery is less sensitive to navigation timing, and transient artifact reads are less likely to surface as tool failures during an agent run.

items.body:
## Summary

Fixes #264.

Make proxy setup usable from one **Network and proxy** settings entry, and keep local application transport independent of outbound proxy failures. Reuse the existing proxy registry, downloader cache/retry, and environment-readiness mechanisms rather than adding an automatic external-network startup gate.

## Changes

- Offer environment configuration, a custom HTTP(S)/SOCKS5 proxy, or direct access. Keep named proxies, bypass hosts and Web/MCP overrides under advanced settings; existing model overrides remain compatible.
- Stage proxy changes across settings tabs. The footer saves them; Cancel/X discards unsaved changes. Add an authenticated, non-persisting download-source connection diagnostic.
- Declare and lock Python HTTP/WebSocket SOCKS dependencies. Adapter loopback HTTP/WebSocket connections explicitly bypass outbound proxies; external HTTP clients are initialized lazily.
- Add small source-loadable shared routing/download helpers. Resolve model requests against their actual target, respect bypass rules, and pass the global policy to managed environment setup/create/install operations without mutating process-wide environment variables.
- Wire the saved global route into both Runner clients: the control plane's own local Runner, and every remote Runner that `RemoteComputeClient` deploys or installs into. Environment mode resolves on the remote Runner itself; a custom URL pointing at the control host's loopback is refused with the reason and the two ways out, because forwarding it would make the remote Runner call itself.
- Refuse proxy settings that cannot be applied instead of degrading silently: a `url` policy without an address, and a proxy URL carrying a path or query (rejected at save time as well, so a stored value cannot fail only per request). The generated `NO_PROXY` lists `::1` rather than `[::1]`, which no consumer matches against a bare hostname.
- Preserve underlying, redacted network errors and existing pinned versions, SHA-256/TLS verification, caches and retries. Update English/Chinese configuration, architecture and REST documentation, including the settings-projection contract change (environment summaries now mask credentials and query strings).

## Rebase onto `main` (`b31f74eb`)

- The branch was 699 commits behind and conflicted in three files. `packages/model/src/client.ts`, `services/api/src/model-connectivity.ts`, `packages/executor` and the gateway tests were re-derived from `main`, then the PR's own deltas re-applied one hunk at a time.
- `normalizeUsage` is gone from this PR: `main` moved it to `packages/model/src/usage.ts` and already reads the protocol field per dialect with alias fallback, so the bug this branch started from is fixed upstream. Keeping the branch copy would have reverted that.
- The branch's `services/adapter/uv.lock` is dropped because `main` deleted the lockfile (`feat(sizeopt)`).
- The branch's last commit (`a49f92ed`, "preserve current runtime interfaces after rebase") is dropped: it reverted `model-connectivity.ts`, `client.ts` and the adapter `network.py` to the branch's older shape, i.e. it undid upstream work rather than preserving the PR. Its only real purpose was to make the stale branch compile, which the re-application above now covers.

## Validation

No real LLM API calls or paid tokens were used.

| Check | Result |
| --- | --- |
| `pnpm --filter` builds: `schema`, `data-source`, `model`, `executor`, `runner`, `api` | Passed |
| `pnpm --recursive typecheck` plus `tsc -p tsconfig.tests.json` | Passed |
| Proxy transport, resolver, connectivity (`packages/data-source`, `services/api`) | 14 passed |
| Model client and dispatcher regressions (`packages/model`) | 46 passed |
| Runner client proxy propagation (`packages/executor`) | 7 passed |
| Web settings component suite (`apps/web`) | 258 passed |
| `pnpm architecture:check` / `pnpm ci:selftest` | 43 / 16 passed |
| `services/runner` environment-store, `services/api` store/server suites | Not runnable on this Windows host (`os:linux` tags, bubblewrap, SQLite unlink); CI covers them |
| Adapter hermetic pytest | Not runnable here (no usable Python); CI covers it |

The browser journeys use a real local API/Swarm stack, not mocked settings storage. They cover basic defaults; custom proxy save/cancel; cross-tab drafts; reload persistence; NO_PROXY; Web/MCP overrides and inheritance; rejection of deleting an in-use proxy; and removing references plus deleting the proxy in one save. Only the first journey's connection-test response is browser-mocked; transport ST tests exercise local HTTP/SOCKS proxy fixtures and authentication failures without external access.

The legacy layout E2E is adapted but remains quarantined and was not run. No production service was restarted.

## Scope and boundaries

- This does not grant sandbox network access or add an automatic direct fallback when a configured proxy fails.
- The manual diagnostic checks one download source, not every provider or model credentials. There is no new startup preflight framework or traffic dashboard.
- Saving multiple settings sections is sequential, not a cross-section transaction: a later failure does not roll back earlier successful requests. Unsaved changes remain drafts.
- SOCKS5 support in Undici remains experimental. Remote end-to-end proxy reachability, binary installation and real external providers have not been newly exercised by this PR.

The existing shutdown drain tracks file writes once they start. A queued mutation can still be waiting before its first `writeArray` call, while subagent/workspace-file operations and catalog saves have separate queues. Extend the single existing `SessionStore.whenWritesSettle()` to include those operations without changing its 10-second deadline, boolean return, timeout warning or timer cleanup. The shutdown call site in `http/index.ts` is unchanged.

Re-read every queue and `saveQueue` after waiting so a settling mutation cannot leave a chained write behind. Failed writes still reach their own callers while their barriers settle for shutdown. API fixtures also reuse the existing `removeTestRoot()` at six remaining teardown sites.

## Validation

Head: `9ac3d8e3f5f937f37ecfc5519ea0e5367ac569a7`; base: `1aeb6598ad05c2692b3ab58d04c16b44ad1f57a0`.

Mocked E2E kept long standard partitions on one product stack. This runs complete spec files across a bounded pool of isolated stacks while retaining all 177 frozen case identities and each file's hooks and serial order.

## Changes

- Keep five Actions partitions and `max-parallel: 4`; create larger partitions first. Each partition runs at most two stacks, with `--workers 1` for serial diagnosis. Playwright stays at one worker and zero retries; the pristine-library batch runs before global configuration batches, and the nine supplemental Swarm checks run once.
- Isolate authentication, data, Python environments, Swarm registries, graph storage, listening ports and reports. Reserve ports and register them through the pinned SDK without widening product environment filtering. Lock shared SDK setup, prepare common dependencies once, and reclaim stopped successful runtimes.
- Remove three redundant cleanup polls by stopping Sessions before deleting their Projects. Replace observation delays with an event barrier after a real child tool starts. Wait for the initial Skill catalog, persisted plugin override and actual MCP repair block. Change token fragments inside the browser and drain review response routes before fixture deletion. Existing outcome assertions and quiet windows remain; no write request is replayed and no case is skipped.

items.author: HugoXK
items.body:
Fixes #918

`GeneratedWorkspaceBoundaryTests` gained two cases in `#915` that assert the walk stays *quiet*: a generated workspace file is not reported, and a file removed between the listing and the read is skipped. Both assert a negative, so nothing in the suite would fail if the walk stopped reporting anything at all — a future narrowing of `IGNORED_DIRECTORIES` or `_files` could silence the boundary check while every test stayed green.

This adds the positive half: a file the walk *should* report is reported.

## Why

The two existing cases are `assertNotIn`, so they pass for any walk that returns an empty list. The only test that pins the positive direction is `ArchitectureBoundaryTests.test_node_and_browser_sources_use_only_product_names`, and it asserts the *absence* of findings on the real tree — it cannot go red when the walk is narrowed either, because the tree happens to be clean. A walk that silently ignores `services/api` would keep the entire module green, and vendor naming could escape the boundary unnoticed.

The new case reuses the mocking shape of the removed-after-listing case at `:162`: patch `_files` and let the patched listing hand the walk a path. It differs in what the listing returns — a file that still exists, with a vendor token in it.

## What changed

One test, `services/gateway/tests/test_architecture_boundaries.py` only. No product code.

```python
self.probe = self.positive_probe_path()   # apps/web/probe-boundary-<pid>.ts
self.addCleanup(self.probe.unlink, missing_ok=True)
self.probe.write_text("// deerflow vendor token\n", encoding="utf-8")
original = _files

def only_the_probe(root: Path):
    # Keep the real listing (so IGNORED_DIRECTORIES still governs) and drop
    # every other file, so the assertion cannot depend on the working tree.
    if root == self.API_ROOT:
        return (path for path in original(root) if path == self.probe)
    return original(root)

with mock.patch.object(sys.modules[__name__], "_files", only_the_probe):
    failures = _node_boundary_failures()
self.assertIn(f"content: {self.relative_probe()}", failures)
```

`only_the_probe` delegates to the real `_files`, so the ignore rules still decide what is listed; it only drops unrelated files so the assertion does not depend on whatever else is in the working tree. If `services/api` is ever added to `IGNORED_DIRECTORIES`, the real listing yields nothing and the case fails.

## Red first

Temporarily add `services/api` to the walk's ignore set — the equivalent of a future narrowing that the two negative cases cannot see:

```diff
-IGNORED_DIRECTORIES = {"__pycache__", ".tmp", "dist", "node_modules"}
+IGNORED_DIRECTORIES = {"__pycache__", ".tmp", "dist", "node_modules", "api"}
```

```
$ python3 -m unittest discover -s services/gateway/tests -p 'test_architecture_boundaries.py'
....F.
======================================================================
FAIL: test_a_vendor_reference_outside_a_generated_workspace_is_still_reported
  (test_architecture_boundaries.GeneratedWorkspaceBoundaryTests)
The cases above only prove the walk stays quiet; this proves it still speaks.
----------------------------------------------------------------------
Traceback (most recent call last):
  File ".../services/gateway/tests/test_architecture_boundaries.py", line 200,
  in test_a_vendor_reference_outside_a_generated_workspace_is_still_reported
    self.assertIn(f"content: {self.relative_probe()}", failures)
AssertionError: 'content: services/api/src/probe-boundary-5.ts' not found in []

----------------------------------------------------------------------
Ran 6 tests in 0.885s

FAILED (failures=1)
```

The other five tests stayed green under the same mutation, which is exactly the gap: only the new case noticed.

## After reverting the mutation

```
$ python3 -m unittest discover -s services/gateway/tests -p 'test_architecture_boundaries.py'
......
----------------------------------------------------------------------
Ran 6 tests in 1.271s

OK
```

Diffstat against `main` `2908e9e8`:

```
 services/gateway/tests/test_architecture_boundaries.py | 65 +++++++++++++++++++++++++++++++++++
 1 file changed, 65 insertions(+)
```

## Rebase and F1 — the positive probe moves out of the egress scan

Rebased onto `9feafa273088` (2026-11-09); the branch was cut at an older main and the pull request showed `mergeable=false` / `dirty`. One commit, replayed unchanged.

F1 (thread `PRRT_kwDOT4OSoM60He32`): the positive case planted `services/api/src/probe-boundary-<pid>.ts`, which `services/api/src/mcp/datasource-egress-contract.test.ts` reads — its `sourceFiles()` walks every `.ts` under `packages/` and `services/` skipping only `dist`, `node_modules` and `.tmp`, and `readFile`s each hit with no ENOENT tolerance. With `UT_WORKERS = 4`, a parallel worker could read the probe between creation and `addCleanup`, and a killed run would leave a vendor token in a tracked source directory.

Fixed with the reviewer's second option: the probe now lives at `apps/web/probe-boundary-<pid>.ts`. `NODE_ROOTS` includes `apps/web`, so `_node_boundary_failures()` still walks and reports it — the positive half of the contract is unchanged — while `sourceFiles()` never scans `apps/web`, so no other worker reads a file this case creates and removes. `only_the_probe` now filters on the walked root; see F4 below for why the first revision of that filter was wrong.

Red first (`2c41f812`): a test that mirrors the egress predicate —

```
EGRESS_SCANNED_ROOTS = ("packages", "services")
EGRESS_IGNORED_DIRECTORIES = {"dist", "node_modules", ".tmp"}
def _egress_scan_reads(path: Path) -> bool:
    ...
```

and asserts the probe path is not readable by it:

```
$ cd services/gateway && python3 -m pytest tests/test_architecture_boundaries.py -q
1 failed, 6 passed
AssertionError: ... services/api/src/probe-boundary-<pid>.ts is read by the datasource egress worker while it exists; plant the probe under apps/web instead
```

After (`20318a36`): `7 passed`.

diffstat against `9feafa27`: 1 file, `+65/−0` (`services/gateway/tests/test_architecture_boundaries.py`; three commits — the original positive case, the red egress test, and the move).

Ran:
- `python3 -m unittest discover -s services/gateway/tests -p 'test_architecture_boundaries.py'` — `Ran 6 tests ... OK` on the branch; `FAILED (failures=1)` with the assertion excerpt above under the temporary `IGNORED_DIRECTORIES` narrowing, then `OK` again after reverting it.
- The probe file is created under `apps/web/` and removed by `addCleanup`, so the working tree is clean after the run (`git status --porcelain` empty).

Not run:
- `pnpm gateway:test` (the whole `services/gateway/tests` discovery) was not run locally; only this module was, and CI runs the full discovery.
- No UT/ST/E2E layers: the change is one gateway test, no product code.

## Release

Release category: `release:test` (the GitHub label is pending a maintainer with write access — this fork has `pull` only).

User impact: none. It makes the architecture boundary check able to fail when the walk is narrowed, instead of only when it is noisy.

## F2 — the probe moves back into `services/api`, with the four checks a killed run needs

At `20318a36` the positive half ran only over `apps/web`. The reviewer's mutation showed why that is not a narrowing guard: with `"api"` added to `IGNORED_DIRECTORIES`, or `services/api` dropped from `NODE_ROOTS`, the suite still printed `7 passed`. `Fixes #918` would have closed the issue without covering the tree it names first.

This tip takes the reviewer's first option and keeps the probe inside that tree: `PROBE_ROOT = services/api/src`, probe name `probe-boundary-<pid>.mdx`.

Two positive assertions, so a rename cannot pass for a fix:

- `test_the_positive_probe_lives_in_the_root_the_issue_names` — the path sits under `services/api/src` (`assertIn("services/api/src/", relative)`) and carries the probe suffix. Moving the probe back to `apps/web` fails it.
- `test_the_walk_enumerates_and_reads_the_positive_probe` — `_files(PROBE_ROOT)` enumerates the probe and `_node_boundary_failures()` reports `content: services/api/src/probe-boundary-<pid>.mdx`. That is the whole reason `.mdx` still counts: `.mdx` is in `TEXT_SUFFIXES` (`test_architecture_boundaries.py:48`), while `sourceFiles()` in `services/api/src/mcp/datasource-egress-contract.test.ts:394` collects only files whose `extname` is `.ts`, so the egress worker never opens it. A suffix outside `TEXT_SUFFIXES` fails this case.

The four checks a killed run needs, one line each:

1. **Location is pinned both ways** — the two positive assertions above; `apps/web` fails the first, `.bin` fails the second.
2. **`.gitignore` is exact** — `/services/api/src/probe-boundary-*.mdx` (comment plus one line). Not `*.mdx`, not `probe-boundary-*`, not the directory. `git check-ignore -v services/api/src/probe-boundary-12345.mdx` prints `.gitignore:100:/services/api/src/probe-boundary-*.mdx`, and `git ls-files services/api/src | grep -c '\.mdx'` is `0`.
3. **Every exit path cleans up** — `_guard_probe_against_signals()` runs in `setUp`, before any probe exists, so both probe-writing cases (and any added later) are covered rather than the one test that happened to install it. It installs `SIGINT`/`SIGTERM` handlers that unlink the probe, restore the previous handler and re-raise the same signal, plus an `atexit` hook for a `sys.exit` or an interpreter that ends before unittest cleanups; both hooks read `self.probe` when they fire, so they unlink the probe the current test wrote. Verified in child processes: `SIGTERM` → probe gone, child exits `143` (the signal is never swallowed); `sys.exit(0)` → probe gone, exit `0`. `setUp` also sweeps probes a dead run left behind, keeping any file whose pid still answers `os.kill(pid, 0)`, so a parallel shard is never deleted (`SIGKILL` cannot be caught — that sweep is its fallback).
4. **No real values** — the probe content is the fixed marker `// deerflow vendor token`; the diff adds no `os.environ`/`getenv` read and no token, secret or path interpolation.

Readings on `75d5b7e2`:

- `cd services/gateway && python3 -m pytest tests/test_architecture_boundaries.py -q` → `16 passed, 1 warning` (was 7 before this round; the two new positive cases, the F4 filter case and the six sweep cases are the additions).
- Child-process checks: `SIGTERM` → probe gone, exit `143`; `sys.exit(0)` → probe gone, exit `0`.
- diffstat against `9feafa27`: 2 files, `+156/−0` (`.gitignore` +4, `services/gateway/tests/test_architecture_boundaries.py` +152).
- Mutation table, all on this tip: probe under `apps/web` → location case FAIL; `PROBE_SUFFIX = ".bin"` → walk-read case FAIL; `"api"` in `IGNORED_DIRECTORIES` → positive case FAIL; `services/api` dropped from `NODE_ROOTS` → positive case FAIL; `apps/web` dropped from `NODE_ROOTS` → PASS (coverage no longer depends on it).
- Working tree clean after the suite: no `probe-boundary-*.mdx` left in `services/api/src`.

Not run: the rest of `services/gateway/tests` discovery (CI runs it), and no UT/ST/E2E layers — the change is two gateway test files' worth of test code plus one ignore line.

## F3 — the sweep runs before the walk, and it tells a dead run from a live shard

`ArchitectureBoundaryTests.test_node_and_browser_sources_use_only_product_names` walks the real tree and is collected before the class that writes probes, so a probe a killed run left behind failed `:117` before `GeneratedWorkspaceBoundaryTests.setUp` could delete it. `_remove_stale_probes(root, pattern)` is now a module function, called from `setUpModule()` — ahead of every case — and again from `setUp` as an idempotent second pass.

Its judgement, with the values actually in the file:

- **same pid**: skipped outright, never swept;
- **dead pid**: deleted;
- **live pid on a host with `/proc`**: deleted when the probe's mtime predates that process's own start by more than `PROBE_START_MARGIN_S = 3 s`. Start time is `/proc/<pid>/stat` field 22 over `os.sysconf('SC_CLK_TCK')` (measured **100** here, not hard-coded) plus `/proc/stat`'s `btime`. The margin absorbs `btime`'s one-second truncation and an NTP step: on this host `_process_started_at(getpid())` = `1794221689.93` against a wall clock of `1794221690.69`;
- **no usable `/proc`**: pid liveness plus `PROBE_STALE_AGE_S = 10 s`. The slowest probe-holding case measured `0.65 s` (`pytest --durations=0`), so 10 s is more than ten times a full probe life. The path is chosen by whether the `/proc` reads succeed, not by `sys.platform`: `test_process_start_time_is_none_when_proc_is_absent` mocks `open` to raise on `/proc/...`, and `test_without_proc_the_age_fallback_decides` mocks the start time to `None` and requires the age rule to delete an old probe.

Red and green, both residues: with either a `probe-boundary-999999.mdx` (dead pid) or a `probe-boundary-1.mdx` with a ten-minute-old mtime on disk, `python3 -m pytest services/gateway/tests/test_architecture_boundaries.py -q` was `1 failed, 8 passed` before the change and is `16 passed` after, with the residue gone. Collection order is deterministic: `services/gateway/pyproject.toml` depends on `pytest==9.0.2` only — no `pytest-randomly`, no `pytest-xdist`, no `pytest.ini`/`conftest.py` overriding it — so `setUpModule()` is guaranteed to precede `:117`.

What was deliberately **not** done, because it would be passing the gate by hiding the failure: no `probe-boundary-*` filter or `continue` in `_files()`, no probe pattern in `IGNORED_DIRECTORIES`, no extra ignore table, no `skipTest`/`skipIf`/early return in the real-tree case, no weakening of `assertEqual(failures, [])` to `assertNotIn`, and no vendor whitelist in `VENDOR_NAME`.

## F4 — the filter now keys on the root the walk visits

`only_the_probe` compared `root == self.PROBE_ROOT`, but `_node_boundary_failures()` only ever passes `NODE_ROOTS` entries, which contain `services/api`, not `services/api/src` — so the branch never matched and the positive case walked every root unfiltered. `_filtered_listing()` now filters on `self.API_ROOT`, and the positive case routes its patched listing through it.

The isolation is proved, not assumed: `test_the_positive_filter_drops_another_shards_probe` feeds the API-root listing this case's probe plus a sibling's same-pattern probe and an ordinary `neighbour.py`, and requires `[self.probe]` back; feeding the `PROBE_ROOT` listing returns all of them unchanged, pinning the distinction that was wrong. Checked on the tip: `PROBE_ROOT in NODE_ROOTS == False`, `API_ROOT in NODE_ROOTS == True`. `test_the_positive_probe_lives_in_the_root_the_issue_names` and `test_the_walk_enumerates_and_reads_the_positive_probe` both stay, and the red path is intact: with `"api"` added to `IGNORED_DIRECTORIES` the positive case fails with `'content: services/api/src/probe-boundary-3.mdx' not found in []`.

## Known limitation: two shards sharing one checkout are not supported

`:117` deliberately walks the real tree and the sweep must not delete a live shard's file, so a sibling's in-flight probe can fail it. Forcing that overlap (one process holds its probe while another runs the module) gives `1 failed, 15 passed` with `AssertionError: Lists differ: ['content: services/api/src/probe-boundary-4.mdx'] != []`. Two shards run side by side on one checkout were green in three rounds (`16 passed` each) because the probe lives under a second inside a 2.4 s run, but the collision remains possible by construction. CI gives each job its own checkout, so this does not occur there; introducing xdist would need the probe moved or the walk redesigned, not a skip marker.

Readings on `75d5b7e2`: `16 passed`; dead-pid and live-pid-old residues both `16 passed` after starting from `1 failed, 8 passed`; `PROBE_ROOT in NODE_ROOTS == False` / `API_ROOT in NODE_ROOTS == True`; `SC_CLK_TCK = 100`, `PROBE_START_MARGIN_S = 3.0`, `PROBE_STALE_AGE_S = 10.0`; diffstat against `9feafa27`: 2 files, `+320/−0`.

items.author: HugoXK
items.body:
Fixes #665

`web_fetch`'s public-URL guard lets several IPv6 families through even though each one carries an IPv4 address the guard already knows how to judge. A model-supplied URL such as `http://[64:ff9b::7f00:1]/` or `http://[2002:a9fe:a9fe::]/` reaches loopback or the link-local metadata endpoint, while the equivalent `::ffff:127.0.0.1` is rejected. This closes those holes, pins that public addresses in the same forms keep working, and — after review — refuses the non-canonical suffixes of the local-use NAT64 prefix rather than guessing where their IPv4 address sits.

## What was wrong

`ipv6Blocked()` consulted `ipv4Blocked()` only for IPv4-mapped (`::ffff:a.b.c.d`) and IPv4-compatible (`::a.b.c.d`) forms, where the embedded IPv4 address sits in the last two hextets. Other families carry the same address elsewhere:

| family | prefix | where the IPv4 address sits | verdict |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| NAT64 well-known | `64:ff9b::/96` | last 32 bits | decode, then `ipv4Blocked` |
| NAT64 local-use | `64:ff9b:1::/48` | last 32 bits **only for the canonical `/96` sub-layout** | canonical `/96` decoded; every other suffix under the `/48` rejected |
| 6to4 | `2002::/16` | hextets 2–3 | decode, then `ipv4Blocked` |
| IPv4-translated | `::ffff:0:0:0/96` | last 32 bits, after `ffff` and 16 zero bits | decode, then `ipv4Blocked` |
| Teredo | `2001:0::/32` | last 32 bits, bitwise inverted | decode, then `ipv4Blocked` |
| site-local (deprecated) | `fec0::/10` | no IPv4 — the range itself is non-public | reject |

No branch inspected those positions, so each form fell through to `return false`.

The local-use row is the review fix. `64:ff9b:1::/48` is wider than the `/96` an embedded address needs, and RFC 8215 allows deployments to use other suffix lengths — a deployment that puts the IPv4 address in bits 64–95 is not judged by hextets 6–7. Reading hextets 6–7 of *every* address in the `/48` therefore judged the wrong bits: `64:ff9b:1:0:7f00:1:808:808` was interpreted as the public `128.8.8.8`.

## What changed

`packages/data-source/src/web/native/url-guard.ts`: one helper, `dotted(high, low)`, and `ipv6Blocked()` extracts the embedded address for the rows above and hands it to the existing `ipv4Blocked()`. There is no second copy of the IPv4 block list, no blanket range ban, and no refactor of the existing mapped/compatible branches.

For the local-use prefix the rule is now explicit and fail-closed: decode the canonical `64:ff9b:1:0:0:0::/96` sub-layout, and **return blocked for every non-canonical suffix** under `64:ff9b:1::/48` (`return true`, never `return false` — an unknown suffix must not become the way around the guard). The well-known `64:ff9b::/96` prefix is untouched by that rule.

## Red first

The new test (`providers.test.ts`), run against the unfixed `url-guard.ts`:

```
not ok 11 - web_fetch judges NAT64, 6to4, IPv4-translated and site-local literals by their embedded IPv4
  error: |-
    64:ff9b:1:0:7f00:1:808:808

    false !== true

  code: 'ERR_ASSERTION'
  expected: true
  actual: false
# tests 16
# pass 15
# fail 1
```

The assertion loop stops at its first failing literal, so every blocked literal was also probed one by one against the unfixed predicate, and every public one against the fixed predicate. Values are `blocked` / `allowed` from `isBlockedAddress`; the flipped rows are the review fix, all in the tightening direction:

| address | before `e9e7358c` review fix | after |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `64:ff9b::7f00:1` | blocked | blocked |
| `64:ff9b::808:808` | allowed | allowed |
| `64:ff9b:1::7f00:1` (canonical `/96`) | blocked | blocked |
| `64:ff9b:1::a9fe:a9fe` (canonical `/96`) | blocked | blocked |
| `64:ff9b:1::808:808` (canonical `/96`) | allowed | allowed |
| `64:ff9b:1:1:0:0:808:808` | **allowed** | blocked |
| `64:ff9b:1:0:1:0:808:808` | **allowed** | blocked |
| `64:ff9b:1:0:0:1:808:808` | **allowed** | blocked |
| `64:ff9b:1:dead:beef:cafe:808:808` | **allowed** | blocked |
| `64:ff9b:1:1:0:0:7f00:1` | blocked | blocked |
| `64:ff9b:1:1:0:0:a9fe:a9fe` | blocked | blocked |
| `64:ff9b:1:0:7f00:1:808:808` | **allowed** | blocked |

Five flips in this probed set, all `allowed → blocked`; zero `blocked → allowed`.

## Only tighter

The same probe run before and after the review fix differs in exactly one line — the tightened address. Everything a legitimate client may reach still resolves as public:

```
ALLOW  literal 64:ff9b::808:808            (NAT64 well-known, public)
ALLOW  literal 64:ff9b:1::808:808          (NAT64 local-use canonical /96, public)
ALLOW  literal 2002:808:808::              (6to4 for 8.8.8.8)
ALLOW  literal ::ffff:0:808:808            (IPv4-translated for 8.8.8.8)
ALLOW  literal 2001:0:808:808::f7f7:f7f7   (Teredo for 8.8.8.8)
ALLOW  literal 2606:4700:4700::1111        (native IPv6)
ALLOW  resolver 64:ff9b::808:808 for http://example.com/
ALLOW  resolver 2606:4700:4700::1111 for http://example.com/
```

These are asserted in the test too (`assert.equal(isBlockedAddress(...), false)` and `assert.equal(await assertPublicUrl(...), url)`), so the guard cannot be "fixed" by blocking a prefix.

## After the fix

```
# tests 16
# pass 16
# fail 0
```

The test now has 17 blocked addresses and 6 public ones (23 assertions across the literal and resolver paths), including the canonical `/96` cases in both directions and the non-canonical suffixes.

Diffstat against `main` `f4dd1813`:

```
 packages/data-source/src/web/native/providers.test.ts | 71 ++++++++++++++++++++++
 packages/data-source/src/web/native/url-guard.ts      | 35 +++++++++++-
 2 files changed, 106 insertions(+), 3 deletions(-)
```

This branch is `f4dd1813` + four commits, two files, nothing else:

1. `dd29d921` test: pin NAT64, 6to4, IPv4-translated and site-local fetch targets
2. `eb818998` fix: judge NAT64, 6to4 and IPv4-translated literals by their embedded IPv4
3. `e4bb3e67` test: judge the local-use NAT64 prefix by its canonical /96 only
4. `e9e7358c` fix: decode only the canonical /96 under the local-use NAT64 prefix

It does not contain any commit from #915; the three-file view was the reviewer's worktree.

Ran:
- `node --import tsx --test src/web/native/providers.test.ts` in `packages/data-source` — `# tests 16 # pass 16 # fail 0`; the same command on the unfixed source is the red above (`# pass 15 # fail 1`).
- `tsc -p packages/data-source/tsconfig.json --noEmit` — exit 0.
- `tsc -p tsconfig.tests.json --noEmit` — exit 0.
- Per-address probe of the 17 blocked and 6 public literals before and after the review fix — the before/after table and the only-tighter block above.

Not run:
- `pnpm ci:ut`, `pnpm ci:st`, `pnpm ci:e2e` (full layers) were not run locally on this branch; CI runs them on this pull request.
- No browser/API/CLI journey was added: the change is a predicate inside the `web_fetch` URL guard, and the mocked E2E subset does not exercise NAT64/6to4 literals.

## Release

Release category: `release:fix` (the GitHub label is pending a maintainer with write access — this fork has `pull` only).

User impact: a model-supplied `web_fetch` URL that encodes a private, loopback or link-local IPv4 address in NAT64, 6to4, IPv4-translated, Teredo or site-local form is rejected with `PublicUrlError` instead of being fetched; public addresses in the same forms keep working, and non-canonical suffixes of the local-use NAT64 prefix are rejected rather than guessed at.

Compatibility and migration: none. A deployment that puts the NAT64 IPv4 address in bits 64–95 of `64:ff9b:1::/48` is now rejected instead of silently misjudged; the canonical `/96` layout and `64:ff9b::/96` behave exactly as before.
