items.body:
This PR exports the existing main-agent/independent-worker Issue-to-PR workflow as opt-in contributor tooling. Scheduling decisions stay with the main agent rather than a script-driven queue controller. It does not modify ScienceDiscovery's research agent runtime, CI policy, repository settings or the operator's running pipeline.

## Scope

- Add `.agents/skills/repo-issue-pipeline` with the coordination policy, worker contract and operational guidance: claim before admission, reproduce before implementation, full accepted-scope delivery, original-thread resume, change-driven discussion/CI/conflict maintenance, independent main-agent review and explicit human/authority boundaries.
- Export a portable one-turn Codex SDK transport with an optional executable override instead of a machine-specific CLI path. Requests explicitly acknowledge full host access; per-session locks prevent concurrent hosts, saved threads resume in their original worktree, and private session/events/final/failure records survive handoff. An incomplete or failed stream cannot be reported as successful.
- Add 16 hermetic tagged tests to the existing `scripts/*.test.mjs` discovery path, without introducing a second CI definition or requiring model tokens.
- Add English/Chinese developer overviews and contributor navigation, plus a setup guide covering private ledgers, configurable repositories/concurrency/inspection interval, resource and cost limits, continuation, systemd examples, recovery and raw-log sensitivity.

## Deliberate boundaries

This is an opt-in developer tool, not a product background service or automatic installer. No real task ledger, account, credentials, logs, host-specific services or legacy migration code are included. Cloning/installing the skill starts nothing. Workers have explicitly authorized full host access, so this must not be attached to untrusted PR/webhook execution. Worktrees are not sandboxes. Raw private logs can contain tool secrets and must not become public CI artifacts.

Periodic wake-up is documented but must be configured and verified on the target host. Completion-event wake-ups and a cross-platform daemon installer are not implemented. The main agent, not the host script, enforces the task-pool cap and repository authority. Successful SDK turns and green CI do not establish full Issue acceptance. Merging/enqueueing/releases/settings/secrets/gate changes and paid real-model tests need separate matching authority.

## Validation

- `node --test --experimental-test-coverage scripts/repo-issue-pipeline.test.mjs`: **16 passed, 0 failed, 0 skipped**. Host line coverage **97.64%**, branch coverage **96.00%**, function coverage **50.00%** in this direct Node report. Do not interpret these as repository-wide coverage.
- Coverage gaps: the real SDK dynamic import/constructor and CLI signal callback wiring were not exercised through a live Codex process. CLI child-process coverage is not merged into the parent report. Factory injection verifies start/resume/options/event/failure behavior, but does not prove account/CLI compatibility or model scheduling quality. No paid Codex smoke, actual OS-signal integration or service-manager installation test was run.
- Skill metadata validation, JavaScript syntax check, architecture check and CI catalog check passed.
- Markdown lint: **0 issues**. Documentation links: **141 tracked Markdown files checked**, no broken targets.
- Full local UT/ST/browser E2E are **not claimed passed**. The clean checkout has not been provisioned with all package-local dependencies/build outputs: shared UT collection stopped at missing `react` in an existing web test. Initial pnpm entry-point checks also encountered dependency-layout verification; no shared dependency tree was purged. The host's serialized heavy-test lock was occupied by an existing worker, so this PR does not interrupt that task or start competing full-stack runs. Full CI remains pending.

## E2E user journeys

ScienceDiscovery product E2E: **not applicable to the changed product path**, because there is no application UI/API/agent-runtime behavior change. Full browser-suite execution is nevertheless unverified as noted above. The new contributor tool is covered by offline request-to-session/output tests; a real Codex-account-to-fork-PR journey remains an explicit integration gap and must not be represented as a mocked product E2E pass.

## Release

Release category: release:internal

User impact: optional contributor tooling only; no automatic process or new application dependency.

items.body:
ScienceDiscovery's issue, review and CI queues need explicit handoffs: the next actor, the missing evidence and the condition that permits progress. This proposal adds an operator-invoked development-loop skill and guide, linked from CONTRIBUTING.

## What changes

- Three queues: issue implementation, PR review, and CI/acceptance.
- Seven decision points: requirement claim, design/dependencies, implementation, source review, CI repair, real acceptance and release sign-off.
- Role-separated contributor/reviewer/maintainer TODOs, verified versus suggested ownership, release impact and recheck triggers.
- Exact-head review history, current readiness refreshes, pagination/error coverage and duplicate-request prevention.
- ScienceDiscovery's PR L1/L2, merge-group L3, daily L4 and release L5 stay distinct. Fix commits first reuse the automatic synchronize run; pending runs do not invite duplicate reruns.

Related: release tracker #249 and source-review skill proposal #231. This complements source review and does not adopt an unmerged proposal as trusted policy. Magpie is credited for unified agent/model routing and instruction-library inspiration; this is not represented as an imported upstream PR-loop skill.

## Scope and rollout

Documentation and agent instructions only. No scheduler, workflow, paid research, credentials or repository settings are installed or changed. Maintainers must separately approve deployment cadence, quotas, notifications and write actions. Keep this PR draft until the proposed handoffs and rollout choices are reviewed.

## Validation

- Skill frontmatter validator: passed.
- Relative links in new files: 11 targets verified against the pinned upstream tree and proposed files.
- `git diff --cached --check`: passed.
- Repository markdownlint configuration: 128 files checked, 0 issues.
- Repository documentation-link checker: 127 Markdown files passed.
- `node --test .ci/research-policy.test.mjs`: 9 passed, 0 failed, 0 skipped.
- Independent read-only review: four manual scenarios checked (new head/new CI attempt, changed state before publication, incomplete screenshot evidence, PR versus merge-group gates); no blocking findings. These are reasoning checks, not an executed scheduler or production effectiveness measurement.
- Base inspected: `cc974a14468cbdfd66c76f2720ebd751aefb1cdd`.
- Full application UT/ST/E2E and live-model journeys have not been executed. No product/runtime files changed. CI policy tests establish routing invariants, not product or scientific correctness.

## E2E user journeys

Not applicable to the product: this change adds contributor/agent workflow documentation with no user-observable runtime path. The eight dry-run acceptance scenarios describe checks required before future automation deployment; they do not claim that a loop has been deployed or tested end to end.

## Release

Release category: release:internal
User impact: developer-facing review and queue coordination guidance.
Compatibility and migration: none.
GitHub release label: pending verification/application.

AI assistance: Codex drafted the guidance and performed the checks listed above.

recent_closed_unmerged.body:
Part of #897 — the P0 item the #834 review identified as the merge-blocking follow-up: any interruption of a mirror-mode `uv sync` in `scripts/start-stack.mjs` could leave `uv.lock` dirty with its backup already deleted — unrecoverable, and the next start froze the dirt as the "pristine" baseline.

## The defect (three parts, per the #897 discussion)

1. `runStep()` spawned `uv sync` without registering it in `children`
2. `cleanup()` restored the lockfile backup **before** killing the children, and `restoreActiveLockfile()` deletes the backup as part of the restore
3. The SIGINT/SIGTERM handlers `process.exit` immediately after `cleanup()`, never awaiting uv

So a SIGTERM delivered only to the launcher: restored + deleted the backup, exited, and the still-running uv rewrote `uv.lock` with mirror-resolved content → dirty lock, nothing to save it. The desktop's normal shutdown route (`taskkill /PID … /T /F` in `win_desktop/src/stack.ts`) never runs the handlers at all — half the fix exists for that path.

## Two complementary halves

**A (handlers run: POSIX SIGTERM / terminal Ctrl-C)**
- `runStep` registers every child (uv included) in `children`, removes it on exit
- `cleanup()` kills first, restores after; on POSIX it waits synchronously (bounded, SIGKILL escalation) for the children to die — the handler cannot await, and a mere SIGTERM delivery followed by `process.exit` would re-open the same rewrite window

**B (no handler ever runs: desktop `taskkill /T /F`, power loss, OOM)**
- a residual `uv.lock.stack-backup` at startup is healed back over `uv.lock` (with a log line) before the build block can freeze the dirt as the baseline — as discussed in #897, the "self-heal at startup" proposal alone is not enough; both halves are needed

**Also:** corrects the `stack.ts` stop() comment that claimed `taskkill /T` runs "each service's own cleanup" — `/F` is TerminateProcess; nothing runs, which is exactly why half B exists.

## Tests

`scripts/start-stack-interrupt-safety.test.mjs` (new, all-platform tags — no host skips):
- shape assertions pinning both halves (registration, kill-before-restore, heal-before-build-block)
- a behavioural run of the sliced-out heal helper against a dirty-lock + pristine-backup workspace
- mutation-verified: reverting half A, half B, or the cleanup ordering (each individually) turns the suite red

Existing `start-stack-lock.test.mjs` (6 tests) untouched and green — its static invariants (handler ordering, finally shape) still hold.

## P1 decision points (from the #897 bot analysis — for the owner)

This PR deliberately contains **only P0**. The remaining #897 items need decisions before code:

| Item | Decision needed |
| --- | --- |
| §2 first-run completeness guard | (a) subject: `.py` count vs `.pyc`; (b) behaviour: assemble hard-fail vs bootstrap named log; (c) manifest location (`version.json` has no runtime reader today) |
| §3.1 locale-trim hardening | remedy for the silent early-return: fail the build (matches `assemble-backend.mjs` `fail()` style) vs actually create the dir + copy 2 paks |
| §3.2 stale doc refs | 6 confirmed locations (docs zh/en, launcher comment, `build-payload.sh` ×3 — the last three are the issue's omission) — no decision needed, ready to go once P0 lands |

## What changes

The run timeline's "N papers returned" line and the persisted tool trace each carried their own list of three source names (`arxiv`, `pubmed`, `europe-pmc`). bioRxiv and medRxiv return records in exactly the same gateway envelope (`sourceId`, `toolId: "search_preprints"`, `records`) and are already registered as paper producers, but neither site recognised them: a 25-record preprint search showed a truncated text preview and was indistinguishable from a search that returned nothing countable.

Both sites now take the answer from the **tool graph registry** — is `mcp__<sourceId>__<toolId>` registered with `product: "paper"` — through one shared helper in `@sciencediscovery/schema`:

- `services/api/src/runs/index.ts` — `completedToolEvidence`, the persisted trace.
- `apps/web/src/timeline/research-label.ts` — `returnedPaperCount`, the tool card and group summary (plus `Orchestration.tsx` for the subagent step).

No name list is extended: the registry is already the single source of truth for what a tool produces, and it lists `mcp__biorxiv__search_preprints` and `mcp__medrxiv__search_preprints` beside the three older sources. A newly registered literature tool counts with no edit here, and registered non-literature tools (`uniprot` search, `pdb` search_structures) plus a non-search tool (`biorxiv` read) stay uncounted. Existing behaviour is preserved: provider `total` estimates and non-array `records` still yield no count, and 0 records still counts 0.

## Scope

Only the two count sites change. The **desktop frontend never renders that line and never reads `paperCount`** — the consumers are the old web timeline (`RunTimeline.tsx`, `Orchestration.tsx`) and the trace the API persists. I did not touch the frozen `apps/web` UI beyond the count function.

## Carried from Dev-2

The two test files are carried unchanged from the Dev-2 branch `dev/1028-biorxiv-medrxiv-paper-count` at tip `2b8ee95f` ("test(web,api): expect a paper count for biorxiv and medrxiv preprint searches"); that branch has no PR. This is the work the Lead's comment of 2026-11-09 11:01 assigned to Dev-2 (`Claimed-by: ScienceDiscovery Lead (assigning ScienceDiscovery Dev-2)`), so the review of this PR covers it rather than a second parallel one.

## Verification

On the merged `main` content (`a773942a`), linux/amd64:

| Check | Result |
| --- | --- |
| `node --import tsx --test services/api/src/runs/index.test.ts` | 23/23 PASS (22/23 with the fix reverted — `not ok 17 completed traces retain bounded authoritative evidence…`) |
| `node --import tsx --test apps/web/tests/ResearchLabel.test.tsx` | 3/3 PASS (2/3 with the fix reverted — `not ok 3 paper counts use returned search records…`) |
| `typecheck` for schema, api, web | 3/3 PASS |
| `apps/web` full test suite (`tsx --test tests/*.test.ts tests/*.test.tsx`) | 1333/1333 PASS |
| `pnpm ci:l1` | 4 planned / 4 executed / 4 passed |

Both suites pin the acceptance cases: 25 records → 25, empty `records` → 0, `uniprot`/`pdb`/`read` → `undefined`.

E2E is not run locally: the change is a pure count decision plus its existing render site, with no desktop surface involved.

## UI evidence

The only rendered surface is the old web timeline's `timeline.papersReturned` line, which this PR now reaches for preprint searches instead of falling back to `evidencePreview`. There is no desktop before/after to show — the desktop timeline does not render this line at all. `apps/web` has no local screenshot harness (no browser or visual test setup in the package), so this PR carries the rendered-string assertions instead of images; if the maintainers want a screenshot from a live web timeline, say so and I will produce one from a running stack.

Fixes #1028

recent_closed_unmerged.body:
Fixes #1070.

Both real-E2E evolve journeys clicked send and then waited for a Run that was never asked for. An `/evolve-design` send does not leave on the composer's submit: it stores the draft and returns, and the **"confirm evolution settings"** dialog's own button is what sends it. The journeys never answered that dialog, so the message was never posted — the shard `stack.log` contains no `POST /api/sessions/<id>/messages` at all.

## This is the test that changed, not the product

The dialog is intended behaviour. I read both clients before picking a direction:

| client | where | what happens |
| --- | --- | --- |
| web | `apps/web/src/App.tsx:3770-3781` | `submitMessage` calls `setEvolveSubmission(...)` and returns for any `/evolve-design` input; only the dialog's `onConfirm` reaches `sendComposerMessage({ algorithm, direction })` |
| desktop | `apps/desktop/src/views/Composer.tsx:920-932` | `submit()` calls `setDirectionDraft(...)` and returns; only the dialog's `onSend` reaches `sendDraft` |

Two clients implementing the same gate independently, with a dialog that carries the algorithm choice, the checkpoint pace, a custom JSON scope, direction generation and the retry carry-over, is a designed interaction rather than an oversight. The journeys were written before it landed and were never taught to answer it.

## What changed

- **`test/helpers/journeys.ts`** — `isEvolveCommand()` and `confirmEvolveDirectionDialog(page)`: wait for the dialog by its accessible name, press its confirm button, wait for it to close. `sendUserMessage` calls it only for an evolve command, so every ordinary journey is untouched.
- **`test/helpers/desktop-evolve.ts`** — the same pair for the desktop dialog. It also answers the no-sandbox `--allow-direct` alert, in the same shape the srbench journey already used (`:299-305`), so a Windows host behaves as before. `sendMessage` calls it only for an evolve command.
- **`test/evolve-compression-real.spec.ts`** — the local `send()` does the same, guarded by the prefix. That matters because the same `send` is called twice: once with the command, once replying to a design checkpoint with an ordinary sentence (`:117`), and that second call must not wait for a dialog that will not open.
- **`test/desktop-evolve-srbench-real.spec.ts`** — answers the dialog between pressing Enter (`:315`) and `waitForNewRun` (`:317`).

`test/journey-evolve-initialization.spec.ts` also contains `/evolve-design`, but it asserts the draft stays unsent and never submits — I read it and left it alone.

## Why two component tests

The journeys select the dialog by its accessible name and press it by its label. If either is renamed, the real-E2E case breaks again in exactly the same silent way (no request, a timeout, and a green-looking journey report). So the words are pinned where they can be checked cheaply:

- `apps/web/tests/Evolve.test.tsx` — the `DirectionDialog` confirm step renders 确认演进设置 and 开始演进, labelled by its heading.
- `apps/desktop/tests/evolve-ui.test.tsx` — the same for `EvolveCreateDialog` in `submission` mode, and the create step's own 开始设计 is absent there.

## Verification

- `tsc -p tsconfig.tests.json --noEmit`: clean (real dependency tree installed for this snapshot, not the stale one from another checkout).
- The two new component tests pass: `apps/web/tests/Evolve.test.tsx` 28/28, `apps/desktop/tests/evolve-ui.test.tsx` 37/37 (both run with the platform tag relaxed for this host, and reported as such rather than as a CI-green run).
- **Mutation-checked, four ways:** renaming the confirm title or the confirm button to anything else turns the matching test red, in both clients. Restored, both are green.

**What I could not run:** `evolve-compression-real.spec.ts` and `desktop-evolve-srbench-real.spec.ts` are `@real @tier:l4 @sandbox:bubblewrap` and need Linux with bubblewrap, the full local stack and a real model. This host is Windows, so the honest statement is that the two journeys are verified by the **Nightly** run that owns them, not by me. What is verified here: the types compile, the selectors match the dialogs the specs now drive (asserted in the component tests), and the confirm step's control flow is the one the existing srbench case already used for the same alert.

recent_closed_unmerged.body:
## Changes

- Simple Desktop cards use a short title, target/scope, one value and Confirm / Cancel. Remove repeated explanations and the long collapsed details. Actions are right-aligned, content-width and 32px tall on fine-pointer desktops, with 44px coarse-pointer targets. Scalar edits preview automatically without applying them.
- Before navigation, complex supported cards show their title and **Open settings**. After opening the original settings page, the conversation keeps a confirmation card asking whether the user has finished the change. **Changed / Not changed** both release the bound original task. Only after that answer does the card collapse into the existing small receipt, showing the specific settings destination and the user's answer. Opening settings alone never completes the request. The original settings page stays unchanged.
- Keep session-model selection inline. Unsupported cards can be closed. Existing `model.metadata` requests no longer expose an inline editor, clear-facts action or settings fallback because the new UI has no complete matching editor.
- Preserve genuine backend security consent, revision/target binding, visible active auto-apply countdowns and cancellation. Never replace or auto-accept a required consent statement to shorten the card.
- Preserve editable drafts during delayed preview, serialized revisions, poll-first reconciliation, IME protection and confirmation gating.
- Add a revision/state-version-bound `settings-confirmation` endpoint and durable user-report receipt. Both answers continue through the existing Native/checkpoint or live-tool wait. The confirmation writes no settings, runs no verification, grants no security consent and does not claim that manually changed settings are effective. Preserve the old Web full editor and historical connector records.

## Scope and dependencies

This PR contains the shared frontend and the no-write manual-settings confirmation protocol. Backend PRs #770, #773, #763 and #734 still need version-matched combination validation; not every backend capability is offered in Desktop. Long/complex security and network requests without a complete original-page fallback remain unsupported. Simple provider/MCP proxy selection and safe resource renaming can remain inline. `model.metadata` has no new-UI editing or navigation fallback.

No changes to paused #826, backend approval policy or runtime proxy resolution. The separate adaptation guide is not committed. The plugin-save timing fix is now in main. recent_closed_unmerged.body: ## Scope Conversation support is limited to the operations supported by the new UI: - Rename an existing shared proxy resource. The backend rejects creation, deletion, type changes and URL replacement. The new UI's fixed metadata fields may be echoed only unchanged; the transactional writer accepts only an ID and name. - Select an existing provider's proxy policy or an existing MCP server's proxy policy: inherit, none, or a registered proxy ID. Existing activation and connection/permission boundaries are unchanged. Removed `proxy.default` from the adapter registry, public capability schema, Agent metadata, discovery, settings-confirmation destination, conversation writer, UI and store snapshot branches. Removed resource CRUD/credential handling from the conversation adapter. Replaced obsolete CRUD/default tests with absence/rejection, rename, stale-state, rollback, repeat, refusal and continuation regressions. The unreleased adapter/schema version stays at 1 to match #1017; the apply path still validates rename-only input. Existing main settings APIs still create/edit/delete proxies and edit the deployment default. Removed the unused security-consent subsystem introduced by this PR, including its schema, UI, route, authorizer and table initialization; no current adapter produced a security-consent plan. Main endpoint authorization, credential storage, safety settings and runtime transport are retained. Shared settings-confirmation and receipt behavior remain for supported capabilities. No historical development-data compatibility is added. No #1017/#758/#826 changes are included. Authenticated settings reads may return a decrypted custom URL to their settings editor, as on main. Conversation discovery and rename use metadata only, never decrypt or collect URLs. Saving a provider/MCP policy neither probes a proxy nor grants destination, private-network or execution permission, and does not prove live routing. ## Revision Head: `8271b4f1228a6060631bdd89765c5eccd0c3d009`, after rebasing and resolving conflicts. One squashed commit with parent `1aeb6598ad05c2692b3ab58d04c16b44ad1f57a0` (distinct from moving main). Author and committer: `wangyuheng16@huawei.com`. ## Validation Pre-rebase cleanup validation at `7764dcbc` (not a rerun at current head `8271b4f1`): - 301/301 configuration and connection-update tests passed, including endpoint authorization, proxy rename/provider/MCP, continuation and atomicity. A focused run passed 110/110. - Full Web tests passed 1267/1267 in the final serial run. Configuration card tests passed 50/50, including English/Chinese receipts for a supported capability. - API and Web type checks, repository test type checking, TypeScript package builds and the Web production build passed. - Regression checks verify that the removed security-consent route returns 404 without changing endpoint authorization and that a fresh store does not create its unused table. - Architecture boundaries passed. Scripts passed 112/113 initially; the remaining RACE-contract test passed separately after using a writable uv cache. Initial local proxy-environment and resource-pressure failures were rerun successfully; no product workaround was added. - Full repository UT/ST/L2, browser visual validation and real model/proxy transport are not claimed passed. Current-head CI is tracked separately; these local results are not a full CI pass. Earlier version-alignment validation showed framework-generated rename cards for system, environment and custom URL proxies passing the #1017 `318efca8` classifier at schema version 1, with provider projection also passing. That earlier check is not new-head browser evidence. ## Architecture and overlap This change owns stored proxy choices and the finite conversation adapters, not a second runtime route resolver. #285 remains the transport/resolver overlap in `services/api/src/store.ts`, `packages/network`, model and Runner clients. Proposed order remains this PR before #285, subject to maintainer agreement; whichever lands second must rebase and keep one resolver. Shared UI/continuation prerequisites from #738, #746 and #757 remain included; see #756 for those common fixes. Supersedes #732, #752, #753 and #751 only within the narrowed scope above. Design documents, HTML, private evidence and unfinished MCP URL work remain excluded. Maintainer architecture/security ownership and approvals are still required. ## Release Release category: `release:feature`. User impact: existing proxy rename and provider/MCP route selection in conversation. Compatibility: existing settings APIs and encrypted storage remain; removed conversation operations are no longer advertised or executable. Activation timing and actual transport verification remain distinct. Refs #820 ## Rename UI captures: `7764dcbc` + `318efca8` Real UI captures from #734 API `7764dcbc` paired with #1017 UI `318efca8`, at 1180 × 757. These captures predate the rebase to current head `8271b4f1`; they are not current-head browser validation. The local source checkouts matched these commits without tracked changes. These screenshots use an isolated synthetic session and cover only the rename card before confirmation and its saved receipt. They are not a full E2E pass: no real model/task run, task resumption, live proxy reachability, provider/MCP policy flow, refusal case or narrow-layout validation is claimed here. The Chinese-locale pending card still contains the English scope label **Proxy display name** and English synthetic resource/session names; this is not evidence of complete localization. ### Rename before confirmation (Chinese locale) ![Rename card before confirmation, Chinese locale](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/wyhohyw/sciencediscovery/f5f6005387c9e6149a70afbba3f1cbe3d847edbe/01-zh-rename-pending.jpg) ### Rename before confirmation (English locale) ![Rename card before confirmation, English locale](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/wyhohyw/sciencediscovery/f5f6005387c9e6149a70afbba3f1cbe3d847edbe/02-en-rename-pending.jpg) ### Saved receipt (English locale) ![Rename saved receipt, English locale](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/wyhohyw/sciencediscovery/f5f6005387c9e6149a70afbba3f1cbe3d847edbe/03-en-rename-saved.jpg) ### Saved receipt (Chinese locale) ![Rename saved receipt, Chinese locale](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/wyhohyw/sciencediscovery/f5f6005387c9e6149a70afbba3f1cbe3d847edbe/04-zh-rename-saved.jpg) Both saved receipts explicitly show that there is no task to resume. ## MCP proxy selection drafts: `7764dcbc` + `318efca8` Additional real UI captures from the same #734 API `7764dcbc` + #1017 UI `318efca8` isolated synthetic session (Chinese locale, 1180 × 757). These captures also predate the rebase to current head `8271b4f1`; they are not current-head browser validation. These show draft selection states only. No route was applied or saved in these three captures, and no connection or live transport was tested. English option/scope labels and synthetic names remain visible, so complete localization is not claimed. Provider policy, refusal cases and full E2E coverage remain outside this evidence. ### Direct connection: pending confirmation ![MCP direct connection selected, pending confirmation](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/wyhohyw/sciencediscovery/6d3f66a27d04767076bc6ae8540edfcba0dbad40/05-zh-mcp-direct-pending.jpg) ### Inherit deployment default: already the current value The card shows **已是此值** and the confirmation button is disabled; this is not a new save. ![MCP inherited policy selected, already current and confirmation disabled](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/wyhohyw/sciencediscovery/6d3f66a27d04767076bc6ae8540edfcba0dbad40/06-zh-mcp-inherit-draft.jpg) ### Registered proxy: unsaved selection ![Registered MCP proxy selected, not saved](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/wyhohyw/sciencediscovery/6d3f66a27d04767076bc6ae8540edfcba0dbad40/07-zh-mcp-explicit-draft.jpg) ## Historical images These original images are preserved unchanged. They predate this scope reduction and are not evidence that removed functionality is supported. Earlier CI/test results in PR history are not acceptance evidence for this head.

Consolidates the existing MCP settings work into one module: metadata, call timeout, enable/disable, removal of saved HTTP/SSE header groups and STDIO environment overrides, custom-server deletion, and replacement of existing credential header values. Connection-cache and credential-redirect fixes remain included.

## Scope of this revision

- Supersedes #764, #765, #766, #767, #768, #769, #771 and #772. One squashed commit with parent `578a9505e24bffefe2a0e3ec61d25a356f791669`.
- Neo4j is deferred for this release. Removed `memory.credential`, its adapter, schema/registry/discovery/UI entries, Memory-only journeys, and changes to the pre-existing Memory settings API. The existing main-branch Memory behavior is unchanged; its legacy password writer still trims surrounding whitespace.
- Preserved the shared exact encrypted-draft mechanism because MCP credential-header replacement requires it. Destination consent, target binding, manual confirmation, finite fields, CAS, durable external receipts and resolve-only recovery remain.
- Added regressions that the deferred capability is neither advertised nor accepted, and that the existing Memory writer retains its old normalization. The production HTTP registry still requires all seven MCP capabilities.
- This diff is 64 files, +2966/-72.

Saving does not probe a server, start a process or grant execution permission. Existing connections can keep old settings until normal reconnection. New MCP URLs, server creation, OAuth and arbitrary header/environment editing are outside this PR. MCP HTTP/SSE requests reject all redirects, including same-origin redirects; use the final server URL.

## Validation

Published head: `5d981b8e67186cc044d75b2ce2d4afad2bc9d2b6`. Validated local commit: `b1928a8673c20fd7d026081aa147b545fce137d4`; source tree: `266628f6862e81d398ebf0c75328d152b2136614`. The published tree is verified identical after fetching it back.

- Full `pnpm build` and `pnpm typecheck`: passed with workspace concurrency 1. Initial concurrent attempts were terminated with exit 137; the successful serial runs tested this same tree.
- API configuration/MCP suites: **434 passed, 0 failed, 0 skipped**, run serially from `services/api` with `node --import tsx --test --test-concurrency=1 src/configuration/*.test.ts src/mcp/*.test.ts`.
- Web configuration card/client tests: **58 passed, 0 failed, 0 skipped**.
- Legacy Memory normalization regression: **1 passed, 0 failed**.
- Local L1: **4 planned, 4 executed, 4 passed**.
- Local full UT: **incomplete**, blocked during Node collection; no full-UT pass claimed.
- Local ST: **51 planned, 43 executed, 36 passed, 7 failed, 8 unexecuted**. Unmodified main `578a9505` reproduced the same seven failed identities (five sandbox process-adapter cases, Evolve distribution/runtime, and Swarm SDK contract); both local runs were incomplete because a worker terminated. This does not establish a full ST pass.
- Local mocked browser E2E: **blocked** by missing pinned Chromium. The run was stopped after confirming browser launch failures. No browser assertion or screenshot is credited.

Host HTTP/HTTPS/ALL/NO proxy variables were unset for isolated test processes. No assertion was relaxed and no sandbox or browser substitute was used. The [CI run for this exact published head](https://github.com/openJiuwen-ai/sciencediscovery/actions/runs/42606079680) is pending. The previous head’s successful CI does not validate this tree.

## E2E user journeys

**8 isolated public-API journeys, 32/32 steps passed** on the actual compiled API from the validated source tree:

- All seven `test/api/configuration-mcp-*.mjs` journeys: metadata, timeout, availability, header removal, environment removal, header credential replacement and deletion.
- `test/api/mcp-credential-redirect-boundary.mjs`.

Each used its documented `E2E_*_ISOLATED=1` flag, owned loopback fixtures and synthetic credentials. They verify persisted outcomes and the credential/redirect boundary. Browser options were not enabled. These are separate API journeys, not a combined browser or real-vendor/model journey. Windows/WSL and real-service/model authentication remain unverified.

## Compatibility and migration

The encrypted custom-MCP store retains the legacy plain-map shape while its operation journal is empty. The first journaled settings edit can write encrypted v2; the first deletion writes v3, and the store stays v3 afterward. Older binaries cannot read either envelope. Settings and receipts remain one atomic encrypted write. There is no automatic downgrade: restore the pre-upgrade file, or start with an empty store and re-add servers. The English/Chinese MCP setup and protocol docs describe recovery; regressions cover the legacy shape, the permanent v3 boundary, full-journal rejection and unreadable-row recovery.

There is deliberately no migration-specific warning or recovery UI. Version detection happens in the encrypted custom-MCP store; a load error propagates during API startup. There is no migration/recovery UI screenshot to attach.

## UI evidence

Real WSL Desktop captures pair this backend `5d981b8e` with published shared UI #1017 `3f7b14b8`. The metadata path is unchanged in the current `882b6f0c` UI: the relevant presentation diff only adds the same original-MCP-settings fallback for `mcp.timeout`. Images below retain their actual capture version rather than being relabeled.

These original, unedited 1440 × 900 zh-CN captures use a real `mcp.metadata` API proposal and a fresh isolated local data directory. The custom MCP fixture is disabled and loopback-only. Clicking **前往设置** opens the unchanged original MCP settings page. Escape returns to the conversation; clicking the existing **已打开设置** disclosure expands its setting name and navigation-only explanation. No metadata was applied, no model was configured or called, and no Run was submitted. This is basic navigation evidence, not the credential/destructive-flow acceptance matrix or a runtime-transport pass.

recent_merged.body:
Closes #1106, Closes #1107


## Why one pull request for two issues

Both issues are the same handoff contract seen from two sides: what stopped the child (#1106) and what the parent is given when it did (#1107). They share `packages/workspace/src/workspace.ts` — the envelope is built there — so two parallel PRs would collide and break the repository's "one in-flight PR per file" rule. Two commits, one reviewable change, both issues closed.

## #1106 — one turn budget, and a stop that says so

The configured child budget never reached the engine. `NativeAgentOptions` had no turn-budget field, so `composeRuntime` always received the hard-coded `MAX_MODEL_TURNS = 128`: a child declared with 300 turns stopped at 128, the exhaustion path called `transition("completed")`, and the parent was told `completed / stopReason=completed / turnCount=128` with no field naming a budget. The observer that checks the configured value runs after the engine has already stopped, so `maxTurnsExceeded` stayed `false` and the `turn_capped` vocabulary was unreachable.

- **One authoritative bound.** `packages/runtime-core` now owns `MODEL_TURN_CEILING` and `effectiveModelTurns(configured)`, so the number a caller is told about and the number the loop enforces cannot drift apart. `create-agent-run` forwards `profile.budget.maxModelTurns`; the loop runs `effectiveModelTurns(configured)`.
- **Which bound won is stated.** A caller may ask for fewer turns. Asking for more than the ceiling is accepted but does not raise it, and the record now carries `effectiveMaxTurns` beside `maxTurns`; the handoff carries `subagent_turn_budget: { configured, effective }`.
- **A spent bound is a stop, not a completion** (per the maintainer's decision): the loop raises `Agent exceeded maxTurns=N`, `classifySubagentFailure` recognises that shape, and the existing `timed_out` → `turn_capped` vocabulary carries it to the parent. Budgets inside the ceiling keep using the observer path; both paths now agree on what counts as a budget stop.

## #1107 — a partial handoff that says it is partial

A `task` result shipped the child's last assistant output cut at 20,000 characters with **no marker**, and `subagent_result_sha256` hashed the *uncut* text — so a consumer that verified the envelope against its own integrity field failed on a handoff reported `completed`. The same body was written into `brief`, `finalText` and `subagent_result_brief`, which tripled an oversized handoff past the tool-output projection bound and made it unparseable on the way to the model.

- **The cut is visible:** `subagent_result_truncated`, `subagent_result_chars { delivered, full }` and `subagent_result_ref`, published only when content was left out.
- **The hash describes what was delivered**, so the integrity field and the payload agree.
- **The rest is reachable:** the full text is stored through an injectable `saveSubagentResult` sink and its ref published, so `read_tool_output(ref, offset, limit)` — the channel that already exists — reaches the remainder.
- **One body, not three:** `brief` and `subagent_result_brief` are removed; `finalText` carries the text.
- **The delivery contract is stated:** `finalText` is the child's *last contiguous run of assistant output* (adjacent streamed fragments merged), documented in both locales, so callers stop reading it as a summary of the whole delegation.

## Tests

- `packages/runtime-core/src/runtime.test.ts`: the three cases that encoded "exhaustion completes" now assert the bound is reported, and the boundary case additionally asserts the loop still paired every assistant tool call with its result and ended in `failed` rather than `completed`. **23/23.**
- `packages/workspace/src/workspace.test.ts`: the envelope expectation drops the two duplicate keys, hashes the delivered text, and pins `subagent_turn_budget`; a new case drives a 20,105-character child result and asserts `delivered: 20_000 / full: 20_105`, the ref, the delivered-text hash (and that it differs from the uncut hash), the absence of both duplicate keys, and both bounds. **68 pass, 2 fail** — and the two failures are the pre-existing host-dependent shell cases (`a command written with the workspace's host path…`, `run_shell executes an existing workspace script…`), which fail identically on the unmodified test file in this checkout.

## Verification

- `tsc --noEmit` clean for `packages/runtime-core`, `packages/schema`, `packages/workspace`, `packages/specialist`.
- `services/api` reports **one** error, `bootstrap/platform.ts(495) readText is not in ProposalDeps`. It is a stale-checkout artifact, not this change: the same error is produced by `main`'s `platform.ts` with my lines stripped, and none of my edits touch that line. CI is authoritative for that package.
- The two suites above declare `os:linux`; the tagged collector no-ops on this Windows host, so both were run with the platform forced to the declared one.

## What this does not change

The wall-clock budgets remain the primary guard (`runTimeoutMs` / `runIdleTimeoutMs`); the turn bound is still a runaway safety net. Raising a configured budget above the ceiling does not raise the ceiling — it is reported, not honoured, which is what the maintainer chose.

recent_merged.body:
Closes #1063.

The issue's "How to close this" names four things: (a) an explicit heap budget on every launch path, (b) a memory signal so a near-limit run is visible before the process dies, (c) at least one measured long run showing the headroom, and (d) either a bounded trajectory build or a documented decision that its response may stay unbounded. All four are in this PR, (d) as a real bound — and measuring it turned up a hard failure that the bound also removes.

## (a) The heap budget is explicit on every launch path

`SCIENCE_AGENT_API_MAX_OLD_SPACE_MB`, default **3072 MiB**, read and applied by every path that starts the API process:

| Launch path | How the budget reaches Node |
| --- | --- |
| `services/api` `start` / `dev` | `node --max-old-space-size=3072 …` (npm scripts cannot read a variable portably, so they carry the number; the other paths carry the same one) |
| `scripts/start-stack.sh` | `api_command=(node --max-old-space-size="$api_heap_budget_mb" …)` in all three modes (local source, locked, docker), with range validation |
| `scripts/start-stack.mjs` | `spawnService(process.execPath, [\`--max-old-space-size=${apiHeapBudgetMb()}\`, apiEntry], …)` |
| `services/launcher/src/serve.ts` (packaged/binary) | `args: [\`--max-old-space-size=${apiHeapBudgetMb(baseEnv)}\`, apiEntry]` |
| docker | goes through `start-stack.sh --mode docker`, so it inherits the same flag |

`scripts/api-heap-budget.test.mjs` fails if those paths ever disagree on the variable name or the number, and if any of them launches the API without a flag — the failure mode being guarded is precisely a path that quietly falls back to V8's default, which is what the 46-minute run in #1011 died of.

The local-source mode of `start-stack.sh` previously ran `pnpm api`, i.e. the package script and its own working directory. It now launches `services/api/dist/server.js` directly like the other modes, so one budget applies everywhere; the two settings that existed because of that working directory are still exported explicitly, and the comment there says so.

## (b) The signal that did not exist

The API now states, once, the budget it really runs under, and samples the heap every 30 s (`services/api/src/memory-watch.ts`, started in `startApiServer` and stopped when the server closes — a server created by a test gets neither):

```
INFO [api] event=api_heap_budget budgetMb=3072 explicitMb=3072 envMb=unset effectiveLimitMiB=3264
INFO [api] event=api_memory_sample rssMiB=248.1 heapUsedMiB=73.5 heapTotalMiB=123.7 externalMiB=17.3 heapRatio=0.023 budgetMb=3072
```

Those two lines are from a real local API started with `node --max-old-space-size=3072 --import tsx src/server.ts` on this head.

`api_memory_pressure` is logged once at 75 % of the limit and `api_memory_critical` once at 90 %, each with the ratio, the budget and what to do about it. The ratio is `heapUsed / v8.getHeapStatistics().heap_size_limit`, not against `heapTotal`: the committed heap makes the ratio meaningless (a 1.6 GB heap with a 1.6 GB commit would read 100 %).

A process that received no flag logs `api_heap_budget_implicit` with the effective limit instead of silently running on the default, and an override that a launcher ignored (`SCIENCE_AGENT_API_MAX_OLD_SPACE_MB=4096` but `--max-old-space-size=3072`) is reported too.

## (d) The trajectory build is bounded — and it no longer throws

`sessionTrajectory` (`services/api/src/trajectory.ts`) used to append every event of every Run, of every agent stream and every `tool-<id>` stream into one array and hand the whole thing to `openSessionTrajectory` — the same shape #1061 removed one layer down, still there one layer up. It now keeps at most `SCIENCE_AGENT_TRAJECTORY_MAX_EVENTS` (default **120000**) recorded events, dropping the oldest as newer ones arrive, and the trajectory index carries a warning naming how many were left out:

```
Only the newest 120,000 recorded Run events are shown; 80,000 older events were left out to keep this view within its budget. Raise SCIENCE_AGENT_TRAJECTORY_MAX_EVENTS to include more.
```

That string travels in `index.warnings`, which the viewer already renders under "Recording completeness", so a bounded view cannot be mistaken for a short session. What the index is built from — committed Steps, event segments, journals, contexts — is read from CAS rather than from this array, so it is unaffected.

**The crash.** While measuring, a 200k-event Session without trimming did not merely use more memory: it threw

```
RangeError: Maximum call stack size exceeded
    at openSessionTrajectory (packages/trajectory/src/server.ts:318)
    → entries.splice(0, entries.length, ...ordered);
```

`...ordered` is one argument per entry, and V8 refuses the call once a long Session has more entries than the argument limit. So on main the trajectory read of a large Session fails outright, whatever the heap budget. `packages/trajectory/src/server.ts` now assigns element by element; with that, 200k entries build in 87 s and return a normal index. This is a separate defect from the memory question, and it is why "document the response as unbounded" was not an acceptable answer for (d): the unbounded path was already broken at the size the issue is about.

## (c) Measurement

`scripts/measure-trajectory-memory.mjs` builds a Session of the requested size through the real `SessionStore` (no HTTP, no model calls), then runs `sessionTrajectory` while sampling `process.memoryUsage()` every 25 ms:

```
node --import tsx scripts/measure-trajectory-memory.mjs --runs 50 --events-per-run 4000 [--max-events N]
```

Measured on this head, Windows host, Node 24:

| Session | Kept events | Peak heap used | Peak RSS | Time |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| 100k events, no trimming | 100,000 | 211.3 MiB | 431.0 MiB | 97 s |
| 200k events, no trimming | 200,000 | 390.4 MiB | 581.7 MiB | 87 s |
| 200k events, budget 120k | 120,000 | 341.7 MiB | 532.1 MiB | 122 s |
| 600k events, budget 120k | 120,000 | 376.0 MiB | 543.9 MiB | 480 s |

Read the last two rows together: a Session three times larger keeps the same 120,000 events, and its peak heap moves from 341.7 to 376.0 MiB instead of following the Session. The unbounded path grows with every event and was already past the argument limit at 200k.

Two honest limits on that table. The sessions are synthetic, not the 46-minute real one from #1011 (whose per-event payloads are larger, so its footprint per event is higher), and the unbounded comparison stops at 200k because that is where it stops working rather than where it stops mattering. The other cost this does not claim to fix is time: the builder still walks every event and its ordering is a k-way merge over streams, so 600k events took 8 minutes to produce a 120k-event view. Bounding the array bounds memory; it does not make the read fast, and that is a separate change.

## Decisions this PR makes, because the issue asks for a person

The issue lists three operational decisions; each is one line here, reversible through the same variable, and written up in `docs/{en,zh}/developer-docs/session-trajectory.md`:

1. **Cap value 3072 MiB, set at the launch paths** rather than in the API or in deployment manifests. The abort happened at 4126.5 MiB (V8's default old space on that runner); a budget below it is only safe together with the bound in (d), which is why the two changes ship together. Raising the cap alone would only move the abort.
2. **The trajectory default is a tail, not an error and not "unbounded".** A long Session keeps its newest 120k recorded events and says so; the index still lists every committed Step and its details. The alternative — refuse to render above the budget — would make the trajectory viewer useless exactly when it matters.
3. **`--heapsnapshot-near-heap-limit=1` is not enabled.** A snapshot is hundreds of MiB written at the moment the process is dying, which needs a storage and retention decision of its own; the sampled timeline plus the two warnings answer the question the issue asks ("visible before the process dies") without it.

## Owner

**PR-bot-2号** (`@yuanzhou75`). The account is shared by the team's Bots, so the author line cannot distinguish them; this line is for the ownership register.

## Acting on the review of `4901c64d`

**P1 was real and is fixed.** The budget block in `scripts/start-stack.sh` was committed with the `case` subject empty — `case "" in` instead of `case "$api_heap_budget_mb" in` — and both messages had lost the value (`got ''`, `got .`). Every launch mode matched the empty alternative, printed the integer error and exited 2 before starting anything; `--help` was the only path that survived, and `bash -n` and the regex in the guard test both pass on it.

Fixed in `7192f229`:

- `case "$api_heap_budget_mb" in`, and both messages interpolate `$api_heap_budget_mb` again;
- `scripts/api-heap-budget.test.mjs` gained the behavioural case the review asked for: it extracts the committed block, runs it through `bash -c`, and asserts that `3072`, `4096` and an unset variable continue (an unset one via the `${VAR:-3072}` default), while `abc` and `1` exit 2 with the refused value in the message. Mutating the subject back to `case "" in` turns that case red (`status: 2`, `got '3072'`), so the guard now fails on the exact slip that produced this P1.

Run directly on this host: `bash -n` clean; the block continues with 3072/4096 and exits 2 for `abc` (`got 'abc'.`) and `1` (`between 256 and 32768, got 1.`).

**`Binary release (aarch64)` on the previous head was an apt/DNS flake, not this diff:** the log ends with `E: Failed to fetch http://ports.ubuntu.com/ubuntu-ports/pool/main/b/bubblewrap/bubblewrap_0.9.0-1ubuntu0.3_arm64.deb  Temporary failure resolving 'ports.ubuntu.com'` → `Process completed with exit code 100`, while the rest of the job had already resolved its indexes with warnings. The new head re-runs it.

## Verification

- `tsc -p services/api/tsconfig.json --noEmit`, `tsc -p services/launcher/tsconfig.json --noEmit` and `tsc -p tsconfig.tests.json --noEmit`: clean.
- `services/api/src/heap-budget.test.ts`, `memory-watch.test.ts`, `trajectory.test.ts` and `scripts/api-heap-budget.test.mjs`, `services/launcher/src/serve.test.ts`: **run here with the `os:linux` tag locally relaxed to `os:windows`** (this machine is Windows; the tag otherwise skips them, which is exactly the silent-zero trap from #1042). 12/12, 2/2 and the launcher suite pass; tags are restored to `os:linux` in the diff.
- Mutation checks, both reverted afterwards: disabling the trajectory trim turns `trajectory.test.ts` red (`20 !== 6`, the whole stream instead of the tail); changing the launcher's default from 3072 to 4096 turns `scripts/api-heap-budget.test.mjs` red.
- `bash -n` on `start-stack.sh`; `node --check` on `start-stack.mjs`, `stack-platform.mjs`, the measurement script.
- The 200k-event reproduction above: `RangeError` on the old assembly, a normal 200k-entry index after it.
- One launcher case, `serve fail-startup preserves ownership and cleans up on shutdown or interrupted startup`, cannot run on this host: it creates a symlink and Windows refuses it (`EPERM`). That is a host limitation, not this change; it is CI's to run.
- Not claimed: a real 46-minute Session, and the Nightly shard that produced the abort. The numbers above are synthetic and labelled as such.

recent_merged.author: yuanzhou75
recent_merged.body:
Closes #1049 — this fixes the download path (the retired locator and the `NOT_FOUND` misattribution). The readiness half of §5 was split out on purpose and is tracked by #1081, so that part is not claimed here.

## What was broken

Two defects behind one symptom: `europe-pmc_prepare_paper_download` / `pubmed_prepare_paper_download` could not produce a PDF candidate at all, and the failure reached the agent as "this record does not exist".

1. **Retired locator.** `config/external-urls.json` still pointed `data_sources.ncbi.pmc_oa` at the PMC OA Web Service (`…/oa.fcgi`), which NCBI retired in 2026, and `_pmc_pdf_candidate()` had no other route. A provider retirement therefore removed the whole download capability instead of degrading it.
2. **Flattened attribution.** `http_errors.py` refined `failureScope` only for `406`, so the resulting `404` was recorded as `unknown`; `node-client.ts` then derived the model-facing code from the message text (`"404"` → `NOT_FOUND`), and `broker.ts` passed `NOT_FOUND / retryable:false` on. An agent reads that as a statement about the literature, not about the service.

## Change

**Locator — read the supported OA package bucket instead of the retired service** (`public_biomed_mcp.py`, `config/external-urls.json`)

`_pmc_pdf_candidate()` lists the PMC OA package bucket with `prefix=<PMCID>.` and `list-type=2`, walks `NextContinuationToken` to the last page, and builds the candidate from a key matching `PMC<id>.<n>/PMC<id>.<n>.pdf` — preferring that article basename over a supplement and taking the largest integer version. Consequences:

- the PDF URL is composed from the configured bucket, never from a provider-supplied `href`;
- a key that leaves the record's own version directory never becomes a candidate;
- a record with no package keeps the existing **record-scoped** `ValueError("PMC OA record does not provide a PDF")`;
- a bucket that answers with an HTTP failure propagates as an **endpoint** failure through `raise_for_status`.

`pmc_oa` is replaced by `pmc_oa_package_bucket`, and the bucket host is added to the `pubmed` and `europe_pmc` connector host allowlists. Nothing else referenced the retired key (the issue's repository-wide search matches what I see).

**Attribution — say "the service is gone" when it is** (`http_errors.py`, `node-client.ts`, `broker.ts`)

- `404` / `405` / `410` classify as `failureScope: "endpoint"` only when the caller passes `fixed_endpoint=True` (the bucket listing, the PubMed eLink, the Reactome search). A record-scoped URL (e.g. `data.rcsb.org/rest/v1/core/entry/<id>`) keeps `failureScope` unset and stays `NOT_FOUND`.
- `node-client.ts` reports `ENDPOINT_UNAVAILABLE` when the provider said the scope is endpoint-wide, instead of deriving `NOT_FOUND` from the status digits.
- `broker.ts` maps that to `UPSTREAM_UNAVAILABLE`, `retryable: false`, `upstreamCode: ENDPOINT_UNAVAILABLE`, with guidance stating it is an outage and not a gap in the literature.
- A record-scoped `404` keeps `NOT_FOUND`.

`upstreamError` is exported from `broker.ts` so the mapping can be tested directly; it is a pure function and its behaviour is unchanged apart from the new branch.

## Tests

`services/gateway/tests/test_public_biomed_mcp.py`:

- preferring the article PDF over a supplement (`srep32040-s1.pdf`) in the same directory;
- selecting the largest integer version (`PMC123.10` beats `PMC123.2`);
- walking a truncated listing with a continuation token and refusing a truncation without one;
- asserting the request carries `list-type=2` and `prefix=PMC123.` on every page;
- a listing without a PDF key raises the record-scoped error, and a key that leaves the bucket is discarded;
- a `fixed_endpoint` 404/405/410 produces `failureScope: "endpoint"`; a record-scoped 404 stays unclassified; `503` stays `unknown`.

`packages/data-source/src/broker.test.ts`:

- an attempt carrying `ENDPOINT_UNAVAILABLE` maps to `UPSTREAM_UNAVAILABLE` (not `NOT_FOUND`) with guidance;
- an attempt carrying `NOT_FOUND` still maps to `NOT_FOUND`.

## Verification

- `tsc -p packages/data-source/tsconfig.json --noEmit` and `tsc -p services/api/tsconfig.json --noEmit`: clean.
- `broker.test.ts`: 15/15 locally.
- **Gateway suite:** `pytest services/gateway/tests/test_public_biomed_mcp.py` reports **39 passed** at this head, run independently twice — by zhaozhaozz (`2026-11-11T05:43Z`) and by the repo's review bot (`2026-11-11T07:09Z`) — so the suite is not resting on CI alone. It still cannot run on my machine: the local Python has neither `pytest` nor `httpx`, so those two runs are the evidence, not a local one.

## Not done

`catalog.ts` still reports the connector `ready` without probing the provider, so a dead endpoint leaves readiness green. That is a readiness design change rather than part of this defect, and the issue asks for it separately; happy to do it in a follow-up.

recent_merged.body:
## What changes

`GET /health` and `/api/health` on the API, and `GET /health` on the Runner, answer ahead of the token gate on purpose — the container health checks have no token. They returned the Runner's whole record to everyone who could reach the port: platform, Runner version, execution user, sandbox egress allowlist, workspace quotas, scientific-environment and NPU capabilities. A default install binds `127.0.0.1`, but a deployment published with `SCIENCE_AGENT_PUBLISH_HOST=0.0.0.0`, or a Runner on another machine for remote execution, exposed exactly the reconnaissance an attacker of the sandbox wants first.

The routes stay public and the unauthenticated answer shrinks to liveness:

| route | without a valid token | with one |
| --- | --- | --- |
| API `GET /health`, `/api/health` | `{service, liveness}` | the full record as before |
| Runner `GET /health` | `{status}` | the full record as before |

A missing token and a wrong token both get liveness only, so the route no longer tells a caller whether it guessed a credential.

## Readers that follow the contract

- `RunnerClient.health()` sends its token. It is still the first call on a connection, so the clock offset is still learned from the same response before anything is signed; an older Runner that answers the detail regardless keeps working.
- The desktop self-check reads the detail through the client it already authenticates, and its tip says what the credential unlocks instead of presenting liveness as an incomplete stack.
- The Docker deployment-contract job generates a job-scoped token, forwards it as `SCIENCE_AGENT_AUTH_TOKEN` and uses it for the diagnostic read; the public liveness poll, and the Runner status/sandbox assertions, are unchanged.
- The shared real-E2E helpers and the desktop L3 suite (`apps/desktop/e2e-real/support.ts`, added after the first attempt at this change) send the configured token. That suite used to read `runner.status` off the public answer; it now reads it authenticated, and when a stack answers liveness only it tells a wrong credential (a failure) from a missing one (a skip) on an authenticated route.
- English and Chinese REST documentation states the public key set.

## Route shape

This keeps the detail on the same route with a token-dependent payload, which keeps the container checks token-free and needs no second URL. The alternative the issue left open — a separate authenticated route — would leave `/health` always liveness-only; say so in review if that is preferred and I will redo it that way instead. Merging this is the decision that the token-dependent shape is the owner.

## Desktop surface

The user-visible difference is one tooltip string and one dot state in the first-run self-check, plus the packaged wizard now reading the Runner through the authenticated route instead of the public one:

| where | before | after |
| --- | --- | --- |
| SetupWizard self-check, Runner row, English tip | `Not checked` | `Not checked (token required)` |
| same, Chinese tip | `未检查` | `未检查（需要令牌）` |
| SetupWizard self-check, Runner row dot when the browser probe gets an answer that carries a Runner which is not ready | green `✓` | `✗` |
| packaged first-run wizard (`win_desktop/src/wizard-api.ts`) Runner readiness | anonymous probe of the Runner port, `execution.ready` | `GET /api/health` with the token, `runner.execution.ready` |

No before/after screenshot is attached, and I would rather not attach a made-up one. The tip is the `<span class="boot-dot">` element's native `title`, so the page bitmap is identical before and after: the row is still a `–` glyph, and a browser screenshot cannot contain a native tooltip. The state that produces the new string is a skip, which by definition paints nothing else differently. Capturing it would need a real OS-level hover capture of a state that an isolated stack did not reach: without a credential the wizard stops on the credential screen, and with one the Runner row is checked and green (`selfCheckTip` is only reached for a skipped row).

What can be checked instead, on this head:

- `selfCheckTip(key, state, runnerNeedsToken)` is exported so the decision lives in one place, and `apps/desktop/tests/boot-screens.test.tsx` covers all three branches: a token-required Runner row yields `Not checked (token required)`, any other skip yields `Not checked`, a checked row yields no tooltip — 8/8 PASS.
- `win_desktop/test/wizard-api.test.ts` answers public liveness without a token and the full detail with one — 7/7 PASS; with the pre-change body restored, 3 of them fail.

## Verification

Recorded at `396ee89d`; the current head `234144cd` differs from it by two contract comments and one optional field declaration. linux/amd64, WSL-hosted build tree with bubblewrap available, and the API file compared against a clean worktree on the PR base `a773942a`:

| Check | Result |
| --- | --- |
| `services/api/src/server.test.ts` | 118 planned / 116 passed / 2 failed — the base is 116 / 114 / 2 with the same two cases |
| `node test/api/health-visibility-journey.mjs` | PASS, 4 steps, 0 failed |
| `apps/desktop` unit suites | 126 suites, 1137 tests, 1137 passed |
| `win_desktop` unit tests | 224 tests, 220 passed, 4 failed — the Linux-only cases below |
| `pnpm ci:l1` | 4 planned / 4 executed / 4 passed |
| `pnpm build`, `tsc -p tsconfig.tests.json --noEmit`, `typecheck` (api, runner, executor, desktop) | PASS, PASS, 4/4 |
| `services/runner/src/server.test.ts` 54/56, `runner-client.test.ts` 7/7, `remote-compute.test.ts` 25/25, `sandbox-network.test.ts` 7/8 | failures reproduce on unmodified `main` or need real egress |

Neither api failure is this change's: `PDF upload extracts full text and tables into the session workspace` needs the `services/paper` environment this worktree does not have (`spawn …/services/paper/.venv/bin/python ENOENT`), and `API runs one observable subagent through task and keeps nested task denied` diffs `reasoningTokens: null` in the expectation against an object without that key. Both reproduce on the base. The four `win_desktop` failures are Linux-only platform cases (`bootstrapPackaged` twice, the repo-root default, `killStackTree`'s spawned pid); the file this branch touches, `wizard-api.test.ts`, is 7/7, and 3 of those fail with the pre-change body restored. The Runner's two long-socket-path egress cases and `sandbox-network`'s real-egress case need a container `main` does not have either.

The previous push's UT failure was mine: two reads in the managed-recovery test still took the Runner's health detail without a credential (the pre-submission capabilities check and the restarted server's identity), so they saw liveness only. Both now send the token, like every other health read in that file, and the unauthenticated route keeps its own case. The same head also rebases onto the merged #1044/#935 work, so `specialistErrorStatus` stays exported beside the health gate.

Production HTTP journey, `node test/api/health-visibility-journey.mjs` — **PASS, 4 steps, 0 failed**, recorded against this commit:

1. Isolated production API and Runner listening on ephemeral loopback ports.
2. Six unauthenticated responses (missing and wrong token, both API routes and the Runner) are HTTP 200 with exactly the public key set and no deployment detail.
3. Three authenticated responses keep their diagnostic fields, including the API's aggregation of the Runner.
4. With the Runner stopped, public liveness stays HTTP 200 and the authenticated diagnosis names the unavailable Runner.

Not run locally: the mocked and real browser E2E suites, and the Docker/binary/macOS startup paths. The desktop L3 change is typechecked but not executed — it needs a real stack and a real model. PR-profile CI skips the distribution jobs, so the deployment contract needs the merge-queue run.


## Self-check evidence (first run, desktop web UI)

Rendered from this head against a local stack (API + Runner + desktop dev server), Chinese and English, 1008x1000 pane and a 480x146 crop of the self-check list.

| State | Chinese | English |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Runner row ready | ![](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/HongyeZhou/sciencediscovery/evidence/267-selfcheck/docs/images/health-selfcheck/zh-selfcheck.png) | ![](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/HongyeZhou/sciencediscovery/evidence/267-selfcheck/docs/images/health-selfcheck/en-selfcheck.png) |
| Runner stopped | ![](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/HongyeZhou/sciencediscovery/evidence/267-selfcheck/docs/images/health-selfcheck/zh-fail-selfcheck.png) | ![](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/HongyeZhou/sciencediscovery/evidence/267-selfcheck/docs/images/health-selfcheck/en-fail-selfcheck.png) |

Full panes: [zh](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/HongyeZhou/sciencediscovery/evidence/267-selfcheck/docs/images/health-selfcheck/zh-pane.png), [en](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/HongyeZhou/sciencediscovery/evidence/267-selfcheck/docs/images/health-selfcheck/en-pane.png), [zh, Runner stopped](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/HongyeZhou/sciencediscovery/evidence/267-selfcheck/docs/images/health-selfcheck/zh-fail-pane.png), [en, Runner stopped](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/HongyeZhou/sciencediscovery/evidence/267-selfcheck/docs/images/health-selfcheck/en-fail-pane.png).

The third state in the review — "token required" — has no capture because the shipped wizard cannot reach it:

- with no token, ^Gpps/desktop/src/App.tsx (the 	oken === "" branch) renders AuthScreen and the wizard never mounts;
- with a token the server refuses, the 401 on /api/settings runs onAuthRejected, which clears the token, so the app is back on AuthScreen before a self-check list exists.

health.runner === undefined therefore only happens in a version mismatch — a new app against an old API — and 
unnerNeedsToken is defence for that, not a state the UI can show today. The skipped row is captured on the model row instead: – with 	itle="未检查" / "Not checked".

Both skip reasons paint the same –; only the 	itle differs, and a native tooltip cannot appear in a bitmap. Those three tooltip cases are pinned in ^Gpps/desktop/tests/boot-screens.test.tsx (selfCheckTip: the token reason, a skip for any other reason, and no tooltip once a row was checked).

Not captured: the packaged Windows shell's wizard self-check rows (zh-CN and en, ready and not-ready) — a Windows build of the shell is not available here. The readiness source for that row changed (anonymous probe of the Runner port → `runner.execution.ready` read out of the authenticated `/api/health` detail), but the row's rendering and its two dot states are the same code path as the desktop wizard's, captured above; `win_desktop/test/wizard-api.test.ts` pins the two answers that drive them (7/7, and 3 of them fail with the pre-change body restored). The rows are therefore unchanged in every state I have seen, and what they paint now comes from the credential the wizard already holds.

Fixes #267

recent_merged.body:
Closes #1083

## Root cause

`hydrateTrajectory` (in `services/api/src/research-snapshots.ts`) awaited `view.detail(entry.id)` for every index entry with no guard. The trajectory reader throws `ENOENT` when an index entry points at a record that was pruned, not yet published, or is being written by a live run, and a reader with no entry for an id raised a plain `Error` instead. Under the preview route the uncaught `ENOENT` becomes `404 {"error":"File not found"}`; the plain `Error` became a 500.

That matches the reported matrix exactly: `level=complete` with `includeFullTrajectory=1` hydrates the entire index, while `necessary` hydrates a filtered subset and `complete` without the flag hydrates nothing — so only one of the five rows in the report's table reaches `detail()` for the whole index.

## Change

**Guarded read** (`services/api/src/research-trajectory-detail.ts`, new)

`readTrajectoryDetail` keeps the entry's identity in an omission line — `trajectory:<session>:<entry>:<reason>` — and returns `undefined` so the caller skips it, the way this builder already treats an unreadable artifact version, CAS object, workspace file or memory graph. A cancelled export still propagates: the abort is re-thrown before anything is recorded, so a cancellation never becomes a quietly thinner package.

**Index and details stay 1:1** — the review's blocker

Skipping the detail while leaving its index entry produced a package that exported fine and then failed to import: `validatePackageTrajectory` requires `details.length === entries.length` (`research-package-trajectory.ts:109`) and `restorePackage` maps a violation to `400 Invalid research package trajectory`. The 404 would simply have become an unusable artifact.

`hydrateTrajectory` now collects the ids whose detail it retained and filters `entries`, `untimedEntries` and `historicalEntries` to them through `filterTrajectoryIndex`, so all three lists agree with `details`. A fully readable export is untouched — the filter is a no-op when nothing was dropped.

**Bounded receipt**

The per-entry omission list is capped at five named entries plus one summary line. A session whose trajectory store is unavailable would otherwise add one line per entry to the receipt *and* to the preview payload.

## Coverage of the whole report, not just one URL

The guard sits in the shared hydration, so it covers the explicit `preview?level=complete&includeFullTrajectory=1` request the report names, the **export** path (`buildResearchPackageInput` → the same `hydrateTrajectory`), and **both clients** — the desktop export dialog sends this exact query too, so the fix does not depend on #1082 landing.

## Evidence for `Closes`

@HongyeZhou asked for evidence that the reported request answers, rather than for one possible cause to be removed. Two things, both checkable in the tree:

1. **The reported request already has a green assertion on `main`.** `research-package-http.test.ts:86-99` imports a session that carries the trajectory fixture, then loops `level ∈ {necessary, complete} × includeFullTrajectory ∈ {0,1} × includeFullMemoryGraph ∈ {0,1}` and asserts that each `preview` answers and that the corresponding export round-trips through `importResearchPackage`. `complete` + `includeFullTrajectory=1` on a session with trajectory content is therefore covered, and it was already passing CI before this PR.

2. **What this PR adds is the unreadable-record case inside that same request.** The new tests pin both directions against the real import gate: the unfiltered shape (`2` index entries, `1` detail) is rejected with `Invalid research package trajectory`, and the filtered shape passes `validatePackageTrajectory` with the same inputs.

So: the request answered before for readable records, and the one remaining way it could fail — a record the reader cannot open — now degrades to a named omission instead of a 404. The failure mode the report describes cannot reach the client from this path any more.

Honest limit: the two 404s in the original trace were `?defaults=1` polls (the triage established this from the job log), and that shape was already fixed by `a7ff1333`; the explicit `?level=` path is what #1103 covers. I could not re-run the reporter's session end-to-end — the `research-package-http` harness does not transform on this Windows host, so its result comes from CI, not from me.

## Tests

`services/api/src/research-trajectory-omission.test.ts`:

- an `ENOENT` from `detail()` yields `undefined` plus `trajectory:session-1:pruned:ENOENT: …` and does not throw;
- a `detail()` that returns nothing gets the same treatment (`trajectory detail is not available`) — this was the 500 case;
- a readable entry is returned and records no omission;
- an already-aborted signal rejects and records **no** omission;
- **new:** the unfiltered shape is rejected by `validatePackageTrajectory`, and `filterTrajectoryIndex` makes the same package pass with `details.length === entries.length` on all three index lists;
- **new:** filtering a healthy package is a no-op.

## Verification

- `tsc -p services/api/tsconfig.json --noEmit`: clean, against the exact files this PR pushes.
- `tsc -p tsconfig.tests.json --noEmit`: clean.
- The new test file passes **4/4**. Its suite declares `os:linux`, so the tagged collector no-ops on this Windows host; I ran the same file with the platform forced to the declared one.
- `research-package-http.test.ts` needs the full fixture harness and does not transform on this host; CI's UT gate is its evidence.

recent_merged.body:
Closes #1099

## Root cause — named, not guessed

`services/api/src/research-export-previews.ts` already knew this state and already had an answer for it:

```ts
if (deferWhileRunning && isMissingPreviewFile(error)) {
  throw new ApiStatusError(409, "Export preview is pending", "EXPORT_PREVIEW_PENDING");
}
```

`isMissingPreviewFile` is `code === "ENOENT"`. The mapping was gated on `deferWhileRunning`, i.e. it applied only to the `?defaults=1` warm path, and the comment above it said so on purpose: *"Explicit previews keep the original error semantics."*

That is the seam the issue is about. An `ENOENT` escaping an explicit preview reaches the route's error handler, which maps any `ENOENT` to `404 {"error":"File not found"}` (`http/index.ts`). A browser logs a bare 404 as a resource error, and the journey's `no console/page errors expected` assertion counts it. That matches the trace: the **21:51:21.978** entry is this one, and the **21:51:35.966** entry — `EXPORT_PREVIEW_RESOURCE_DELETED` — is the deletion case #1074 owns.

## Which read throws it

Several, and that is why the answer is the contract rather than one patch: the preview reads messages, runs, run streams, trajectory details, CAS objects and workspace files. Of those:

- the trajectory-detail read is handled separately and specifically by #1101, which turns an unreadable record into an omission instead of failing the request;
- the CAS/version/workspace-object reads already record omissions rather than throwing;
- the remaining stores read through `SessionStoreHttpError` for "no such session/project", which is not an fs error and is unaffected by this change.

So the residual case is "a file the run has not published yet", for which the repository already has a client-facing contract. Pinning one read would leave the other stores answering the bare 404.

## Change

`isMissingPreviewFile` now maps to `409 EXPORT_PREVIEW_PENDING` for **both** paths — the warmed defaults and the explicit preview. The comment no longer claims an exemption that #1099 asks to remove.

What is deliberately *not* changed:

- a genuinely deleted project/session still answers `EXPORT_PREVIEW_RESOURCE_DELETED` (it is an `ApiStatusError`, not an fs error, so it never passes through this branch);
- `?defaults=1` behaviour is identical to before;
- opt-in clients still get `202` with `Preference-Applied: respond-async` when they send `Prefer: respond-async`; clients that do not send it now get the 409 that `apps/web` already handles by retrying.

## Tests

`services/api/src/research-export-previews.test.ts` — one case is **rewritten**, because it encoded the old contract: *"explicit previews preserve missing-file errors"* asserted that the raw `ENOENT` escapes. It is now *"explicit previews answer the pending contract when a run races file publication"* and asserts `409 / EXPORT_PREVIEW_PENDING`. The neighbouring case for the warmed path is unchanged and still passes.

## Verification

- `research-export-previews.test.ts`: **19/19** pass, including the rewritten case. The suite declares `os:linux`, so the tagged collector no-ops on this Windows host; I ran the same file with the platform forced to the declared one.
- `tsc -p services/api/tsconfig.json --noEmit` and `tsc -p tsconfig.tests.json --noEmit`: clean, against the exact files this PR pushes.
- No HTTP-level expectation depended on the old behaviour: the http suite's preview status table pins `EXPORT_PREVIEW_RESOURCE_DELETED` and `EXPORT_PREVIEW_SERVICE_CLOSED`, never a 404 for a missing file.

## Not claimed

This does not make the missing file appear — it makes the answer honest: a client retries instead of the browser recording a resource error. Publishing or waiting per read remains the other option the issue allows, and it is what #1101 does for the trajectory records it can name.
